[v1 chat: unify stop propagation and robust tool-call handshake for streamed responses]
description:
Motivation: customers using the /v1/chat.completions compatibility layer reported inconsistent stop handling and truncated toolcall exchanges when streaming responses and falling back across model variants. This PR unifies parameter normalization for stop arrays/sentinels, ensures logprobs and stop signals are propagated deterministically through streaming envelopes, and introduces a resilient tool-call handshake/resume protocol to avoid lost tool outputs in intermediate reconnections.

What this changes (single continuous description): canonicalize v1 chat params: introduce a single param-normalizer that accepts legacy stop formats (string, array, special tokens) and produces an internal stop-set representation used by both batch and streaming paths; coerce role aliases and preserve role metadata when mapping between adapter layers; implement stop-propagation: stops are now evaluated at token-generation and stream-framing layers with consistent precedence (explicit stop list > stop weight heuristics > model-inferred EOS) so clients see matching stop points between sync and streaming responses; logprobs envelope: add compact logprob delta messages emitted on the stream with clear token indices and an explicit final logprob frame for non-streamed fallback; tool-call handshake/resume: new two-way preflight step in the stream (TOOL_HANDSHAKE / TOOL_ACK) plus a resume token so downstream tool runners can rehydrate partial tool outputs after connection blips; streaming stability: introduce heartbeat sentinel frames and backoff-aware fragment coalescing to reduce duplicate fragments and improve reassembly across proxies.

Files changed (high level): api/compat/v1/param_normalizer.py (new) — canonicalization and migration shims; serving/streaming/framer.go — stop evaluation and heartbeat frames; runtime/tooling/handshake.go — tool handshake and resume token state machine; tests/compat/test_chat_stops.py — coverage for stop formats and streaming parity; tests/streaming/test_resume_reassembly.js — fuzz tests simulating partial reconnects; docs/openapi/v1_chat_compat.md — updated compatibility notes and migration guidance.

Commits (summary):
- 4f92d5d: add param normalizer and adapter glue;
- 9c1b3a7: implement streaming stop evaluation + heartbeat frames;
- a6e4b2f: tool handshake/resume protocol and runtime state;
- 2b7f113: tests, docs and CI flakiness fixes.

Backward compatibility and migration notes: existing clients should continue to work unchanged. Edge cases fixed: stop arrays passed as comma-separated single strings (legacy client bug) are normalized; stop handling differences between non-streamed and streamed codepaths are eliminated. Tool runners that rely on implicit stream termination should adopt the new handshake ACK semantics to avoid missing final fragments — see docs/openapi/v1_chat_compat.md for example pseudocode. No breaking API changes were made; developers wanting to opt into stricter stop-prioritization can set the new parameter "stop_mode=strict" (opt-in).

Tests and CI: added unit and integration tests that exercise mixed-mode streaming and reconnects; included a small synthetic latencies harness that revealed an off-by-one stop fence which was fixed. CI: build/test/lint all pass on main matrix except a transient macOS flake that required a rerun. Final CI status: pass.

Review thread (condensed): Reviewer Liam asked for clearer separation between param-normalizer side effects and request telemetry; I split the telemetry emission into a separate tracing hook as requested. Sofia requested an additional fuzz test for tool reassembly under packet reorder; added test case in tests/streaming/test_resume_reassembly.js. Eliot flagged a potential race in the resume token garbage collection; I added a bounded TTL and unit test. After two rounds of changes reviewers approved and marked ready.

Deployment notes: staged to canary and exercised against dedicated workloads; observed 0.4% p99 latency increase under large stop lists but 18% reduction in duplicate stream fragments. No rollout blockers.

Related work: references ENG-9384 (streaming parity effort) and ENG-9422 (tool-runner reliability). Links: internal design doc at /docs/design/chatv1-stop-tool-handshake.md and migration examples in docs/openapi/v1_chat_compat.md.

Release notes: "Improve v1 chat compatibility: consistent stop handling for streamed and sync responses; robust tool-call handshake with resume support to avoid lost tool outputs during reconnects; streaming stability improvements (heartbeat, fragment coalescing) and logprob envelope frames for clearer token-level diagnostics."

Liam Chen: clarify telemetry side-effects -> moved telemetry to tracing hook; Sofia Rodriguez: add fuzz case for packet reorder -> added; Eliot Brooks: race on resume GC -> added TTL and tests; approvals after changes (LGTM x3).

Improve v1 chat compatibility: deterministic stop propagation across streaming and sync paths; resilient tool-call handshake with resume tokens; streaming stability fixes and compact logprob frames.

[chat-v1 compatibility polisher: function handoff & structured response parity]
description:
Motivation: polish remaining edge-cases in our /v1/chat.completions compatibility shim so customers using OpenAI-style params see consistent behavior when using streaming, functions, and structured outputs. This PR focuses on three practical gaps discovered during a PLG customer migration: role aliasing when clients send nonstandard role labels, stop-array coalescing with mixed encodings (bytes vs strings), and a graceful logprob fallback when models do not provide exhaustive token logprobs during framed streaming.

What this change does: normalizes alias roles (system/meta -> system, usr/user -> user), coalesces stop sequences at both the adapter and runtime stream boundary to avoid double-truncation, and introduces a logprob-fallback path that synthesizes stable per-token probability hints (not full logprobs) when upstream models return partial data. Additionally this PR refines the function-call handshake in the stream envelope: we now emit a preflight "fncap" delta to indicate function schema acceptance before tool payloads arrive, and when a function is invoked we ensure the framed JSON body uses the same structured-shape negotiated by the v1 adapter.

Compatibility notes: preserves existing Redwood streaming framing for native clients; changes are gated behind the chatv1 compatibility flag and a runtime toggle so we can roll back quickly if there are regressions. Unit and integration tests added; a small e2e with the Python SDK demonstrates parity with OpenAI's behavior for the customers' test prompt set.

[Cross-role Tool Access Governance and Self-Service Handbook]
Summary:

This handbook defines the governance model, operational runbook, and self-service flows for granting, reviewing, and revoking access to Redwood’s internal tools across roles and teams. It is intended for people-ops, engineering managers, security reviewers, and tool maintainers. The goal is to make tool access predictable, auditable, and fast while minimizing over-permissioning.

Key Principles:
- Least privilege by default: users receive the minimum role required to do their job.
- Role-driven access: we prefer role-based assignments with ephemeral exceptions.
- Self-service first, manual oversight when necessary: automate safe, common grants.
- Clear ownership: every tool has an owner and an escalation path.
- Auditable lifecycle: provisioning, reviews and deprovisioning are tracked centrally.

1) Scope and Definitions
- Tool: any internal SaaS, self-hosted service, or repo that requires explicit credentials or permissions (examples: AWS consoles, Jira admin groups, prod Grafana, CI pipelines).
- Role: a named collection of permissions (e.g., developer-readonly, infra-operator).
- Access Request: a request submitted to the Access Portal for a role or tool-specific permission.
- Exception: temporary access outside standard roles; must have an expiration and approver.

2) Ownership and Responsibilities
- Tool Owner (team-specified): maintains the role catalog, documents required permissions, defines safe self-service gates, and responds to escalations.
- People Ops: owns onboarding/offboarding orchestration, periodic review cadence, and highest-level policy.
- Security: defines acceptable exception policies, approves high-risk tools, and performs audits.
- Manager (requester approver): verifies business need and ties access to role/mission.

3) Access Model (high level)
- Role Catalog: canonical list of roles for common tools; stored in the Access Portal.
- Self-Service Roles: low-risk roles that can be assigned instantly (examples: docs-edit, ci-reader)
- Request-and-Approve Roles: medium-risk roles requiring manager approval (examples: staging-deploy, metrics-writer)
- Manual Approval Roles: high-risk roles requiring security review (examples: prod-admin, billing-admin)

4) Standard Provisioning Flow (Self-Service preferred)
1. User initiates request via Access Portal (or CLI).
2. For self-service roles: immediate grant recorded in audit log; user notified.
3. For manager-approval roles: manager receives approval email and must respond within 48 business hours; if approved, provisioning executes automatically.
4. For security-approval roles: security reviewer staged; expected SLA is 3 business days.
5. All grants include metadata: requester, approver, justification, expiration (if exception), and ticket ID.

5) Approval Matrix (sample)
| Tool Category | Example Tools | Typical Role Name | Approval Path | Max SLA for Approval | Expiration Policy |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Low risk | Docs, Internal Wiki | docs-edit | Self-service | Instant | Persistent (attached to employment) |
| Medium risk | Staging CI, Dev DB | staging-deploy | Manager | 48 business hours | 90 days (auto-renew) |
| High risk | Production infra, Billing | prod-admin | Manager + Security | 3 business days | 7 days (explicit extension only) |

6) Exception and Emergency Access
- Emergency access (e.g., incident mitigation) uses the Fast-Track Exception flow:
  1) Requester files an incident-tagged access request with justification and incident ID.
  2) On-call approver (manager or designated incident commander) may grant a 4-hour temporary token via the Access Portal.
  3) Security must be notified within 1 hour and will follow up to convert to a formal exception or revoke.
- All emergency grants are logged and retroactively reviewed as part of the incident postmortem.

7) Deprovisioning and Offboarding
- Standard offboarding timeline:
  - Day 0: account disabled for interactive access within 4 hours of HR offboarding signal.
  - Day 1: short-lived API tokens invalidated; persistent service accounts rotated if necessary.
  - Day 7: cloud console roles removed; scheduled backup of any outstanding owner responsibilities.
- Manager responsibility: reassign ownership before final removal.
- Audit: people-ops runs weekly deprovisioning reports, security runs monthly verification.

8) Periodic Access Reviews
- Quarterly review for all high-risk roles.
- Biannual review for medium-risk.
- Annual review for low-risk.
- Review process: automated report produced by Access Portal -> owner validates or initiates deprovisioning -> people-ops enforces changes within 7 business days.

9) Tool Onboarding Checklist (for Tool Owners)
1. Identify required roles and map to least-privilege sets.
2. Document roles in the Role Catalog section of the owner page.
3. Define which roles are self-service vs require approval.
4. Provide an onboarding runbook with contact points and SLOs.
5. Register tool owner and escalation email in the Access Portal.
6. Provide a test account and verification steps for the access flow.

10) Technical Integration Patterns
- Recommended: integrate tool with SSO and SCIM for group sync.
- Fallback: if SCIM unavailable, implement an API-based provisioning endpoint with scoped tokens and change tracking.
- Example access request payload (JSON):
{
  "requester": "user@redwood.com",
  "tool": "grafana-prod",
  "role": "viewer",
  "justification": "Oncall rotation",
  "expires_at": "2026-02-28T23:59:00Z"
}
- Example CLI (Access Portal CLI):
$ rwd-access request --tool grafana-prod --role viewer --justification "oncall"

11) Monitoring, Auditing and KPIs
- KPIs to track: time-to-provision (median), percent self-service, number of active exceptions, time-to-deprovision after offboard.
- Reporting cadence: weekly provisioning dashboard, monthly audit exports (CSV) to security vault.
- Audit checks: verify no more than 5% of production-admin grants are older than 30 days without re-approval.

12) De-Escalation and Dispute Resolution
- If a manager or user disputes a grant or removal, escalate to people-ops with the ticket ID. People-ops will convene: manager, tool owner, and security to adjudicate within 5 business days.

13) Sample Runbook: Granting Prod-Read Access (Manager-Approved)
1. Manager submits request in Access Portal with business justification.
2. Portal routes to tool owner notification and manager approval.
3. On approval, provisioning job runs (SCIM or API).
4. Access granted; audit log written; notification sent to requester and manager.
5. After 90 days, system creates a renewal task for the manager.

14) Implementation Roadmap (next 18 months)
- Q2 2026: Complete SCIM integrations for top 10 tools.
- Q3 2026: Launch delegated team-admin roles for large product groups.
- Q4 2026: Build exception analytics dashboard and automatic expiration nudges.

15) Appendix: Common Role Examples
- developer-readonly: view-only GitHub repos, dev dashboards.
- ci-builder: CI pipeline trigger and artifact write to staging buckets.
- infra-operator: deploy to staging, manage infra-as-code prs.
- prod-admin: full production console access (high-risk).

Contact and Escalation
- People Ops team: people-ops@redwood.com
- Security on-call: security-oncall@redwood.com
- Tool owner contact: listed on each tool owner page in the Access Portal

[Ops Pocket Guide: Controls, Change, Data, Procurement & Templates]
Summary
-------
This pocket guide consolidates Redwood-wide controls and step-by-step processes for access and permissions, change management, data governance, procurement and expenses, vendor management, travel exceptions, and packaged internal templates. It is intended as a single-stop reference for team leads, people-ops partners, engineering managers, finance approvers, and security reviewers.

Scope
-----
Applies to all company employees, contractors, and third-party vendors that interact with Redwood systems and data. Exceptions must be documented and approved by the owning team and Security.

1) Access and Permissions Lifecycle
----------------------------------
Goal: Ensure least-privilege, auditable access provisioning and timely deprovisioning.

Key services and tools
- Redwood IAM (central identity store; SSO + SCIM provisioning)
- Jira Service Desk (access request and approvals)
- Okta for SSO and MFA enforcement
- Vault (secrets management)

Roles and responsibilities
- Requester: Submits access request and justification.
- Manager: Verifies business need and signs approval (within 72 hours).
- Resource Owner: Grants or denies access, documents duration and justification.
- Security: Performs periodic audit and exception reviews.

Standard request flow (numbered)
1. Requester files access request in Jira Service Desk using template "Access Request - Role/Resource".
2. Manager approves in Jira within 72 hours. Auto-escalate to skip-level after 96 hours.
3. Resource Owner assigns role and logs entitlement in the Access Log.
4. SCIM provisioning applies role in Redwood IAM; Okta pushes group membership to services.
5. After 90 days, access expires unless renewed via a Renewal Request.

Temporary access and emergency access
- Temporary access (duration <= 14 days) requires manager approval and must specify start/end dates.
- Emergency access (breakglass) is permitted only when a production incident requires immediate work. Broken-glass sessions must be opened in the Breakglass Tracker and reviewed within 48 hours by Security.

Periodic audits and attestations
- Quarterly entitlement review by Resource Owners.
- Access attestation cadence: Engineering and Product: quarterly; Finance and Legal: biannually.
- SLO: 95% of stale access remediated within 30 days of detection.

2) Change Management (Service & Configuration Changes)
-----------------------------------------------------
Purpose: Coordinate changes to services and infra to reduce risk and ensure rollback capability.

Change types and approval matrix
- Standard changes: Low-risk, pre-approved templates (e.g., routine config refresh). No CAB required; change owner posts in #changes Slack channel 24h prior.
- Normal changes: Non-emergency changes that may impact availability or behaviour. Require change ticket in Jira, risk assessment, and CAB sign-off if risk level >= medium.
- Emergency changes: High-priority fixes for active incidents. Notify SRE and Security, document post-facto, and schedule a post-incident review.

CAB (Change Advisory Board) composition and cadence
- Weekly CAB meeting: SRE lead, Release Manager, Product Ops, Security representative, and an affected service owner.
- Ad-hoc CAB for high-severity normal changes.

Change process (high level)
1. Create Jira change ticket with: description, risk rating, rollback plan, monitoring playbook, and expected impact window.
2. Run canary deploys in staging and execute smoke-tests.
3. Submit to CAB at least 48 hours before planned change (unless emergency).
4. Post-deploy: update runbook, close ticket only after 24h stability window.

Required artifacts for every normal change
- Runbook link
- Rollback steps (exact CLI/commands or job id)
- Impact matrix (services impacted and owners)
- Observability checklist: dashboards to monitor and alerts to mute

3) Data Management & Classification
----------------------------------
Objective: Protect data according to sensitivity and legal requirements while enabling productive access.

Classification levels (table-style text)
- PUBLIC: Information safe for public disclosure (docs, marketing website).
- INTERNAL: Company information intended for internal use only; minimal risk if leaked.
- CONFIDENTIAL: Contains PII, contract terms, customer-provided data with restrictions. Requires encryption at rest and in transit, and RBAC-enforced access.
- RESTRICTED: Highest sensitivity (regulated data, keys, or production secrets). Access only to explicitly approved individuals and logged via Vault.

Retention and deletion guidelines
- Default retention: product telemetry 365 days; aggregated metrics: indefinitely.
- PII: retain only as necessary for business purpose; default retention 2 years unless customer contract requires longer.
- Data deletion: Data owners must create a Deletion Request in Jira with a data inventory and deletion proof (screenshot or deleted object IDs).

Encryption and key management
- All CONFIDENTIAL and RESTRICTED data at rest must be encrypted with keys managed in KMS/HSM.
- Access to key material is permissioned via Vault policies.

Data access request flow
1. Submit Data Access Request (Jira) including dataset name, columns, justification, and duration.
2. Data Steward reviews within 5 business days.
3. If approved, access provisioned in query environment (read-only) or via extract with minimized fields.

4) Procurement & Expenses (Buttons to buy the right things)
----------------------------------------------------------
Principles: Centralize vendor spend, enforce approvals by spend tier, and preserve audit trail for reimbursements.

Procurement thresholds and approvers (table-style text)
- <$1,000: Manager approval (use expense reimbursement).
- $1,000-$25,000: Manager + Finance approver.
- $25,000-$250,000: Manager + Finance + Legal review.
- >$250,000: VP approval + Legal + Procurement committee.

Preferred vendor platforms
- SaaS procurement: Coupa (ProcureFlow) for contract and purchase order lifecycle.
- Hardware/Capital: Request via "HW Request" template in Jira and route to IT Asset Management.

Procurement process (numbered)
1. Fill the procurement request template in Coupa or Jira (item, justification, cost center, expected contract term).
2. Finance verifies budget and assigns GL codes within 3 business days.
3. Legal performs contract review for spend >= $25k or if data handling clauses exist.
4. Procurement issues PO and routes to vendor.
5. Receipts and invoices: upload to Expense system and tag to PO.

Expense reimbursement rules
- Use corporate card for approved recurring SaaS or travel.
- Expense submission window: within 30 days of spend. Late submissions require People Ops review and may be denied.
- Per diem: follows regional brackets on the Travel Matrix (see Travel policy section).

5) Vendor Management & Onboarding Checklist
-----------------------------------------
Objective: Ensure vendors meet security, privacy, and contractual standards before granting access or engaging financially.

Vendor onramp checklist (each item required for medium/high risk vendors):
- Business case and owner assigned.
- Security questionnaire completed (SSQ) and reviewed by InfoSec.
- Contract with data processing addendum (DPA) and SLAs if applicable.
- Classification of vendor data access (scope & least privilege).
- Insurance and compliance evidence (ISO/ SOC reports) if handling CONFIDENTIAL or RESTRICTED data.
- Vendor access provisioning tickets and least-privilege roles created in Redwood IAM.
- Quarterly vendor risk review scheduled for ongoing vendors.

Vendor offboarding steps
1. Raise Offboard ticket in Jira with last date of work.
2. Revoke all credentials and rotate shared secrets.
3. Confirm data return/deletion per contract and document with proof.
4. Close vendor account and archive contract in procurement system.

6) Travel Policy & Exceptions
-----------------------------
Standard travel policy highlights
- All business travel requires pre-approval via Travel Request form and alignment with cost center.
- Travelers must use approved booking vendors for airfare and hotels.
- Travel insurance for international trips above 7 days is required.

Expense caps (examples)
- Domestic lodging cap: $250/night (regional exceptions require pre-approval).
- International lodging cap: $350/night.
- Meals: per diem follows published regional table in Travel Matrix.

Exceptions and approval workflow
- Exceptions to policy (e.g., upgraded seat class, additional nights) must be requested 7+ days in advance and require manager + Finance approval.
- Emergency extension: manager approval and post-trip expense justification required.

7) Internal Templates & Artifacts Index
--------------------------------------
The following templates are pre-approved and available in the Templates Library (Confluence):
- Access Request - Role/Resource (Jira template id: AR-2025)
- Change Ticket Template (CT-std) with rollback checklist
- Data Access Request (DAR-1)
- Vendor Onboarding Checklist (VENDOR-ON-2024)
- Procurement Request Form (PROC-REQ)
- Travel Request & Expense Form (TRV-REQ)
- Incident Breakglass Report (BGR-1)

8) Escalation Paths & Contacts
------------------------------
- Security incidents: PagerDuty -> Security on-call; also open Security Incident ticket.
- Procurement exceptions: Finance Manager -> Head of Finance.
- Access disputes: People Ops -> Security -> Legal if contractual.

9) Compliance, Reporting, and KPIs
----------------------------------
Suggested metrics to track (examples)
- Average time to provision new access: target <= 48 hours.
- Percentage of change tickets with complete rollback plans: target 100%.
- Vendor onboarding SLA (from request to contract signing): target <= 20 business days.
- Data access request median turnaround: <= 5 business days.

Reporting cadence
- Monthly operations dashboard for execs: spend by cost center, outstanding procurement requests, vendor risk summary.
- Quarterly compliance report: access attestation results, audit findings, and remediation status.

10) Exceptions and Continuous Improvement
---------------------------------------
- Exceptions must be documented in Jira with a Business Justification and expiry date, reviewed by Security and People Ops.
- We will run an annual controls retrospective to refine thresholds, templates, and automation points.

Related pages
-------------
- Confluence: policies-and-process/company-operations-reference-2025 (for budget links)
- Confluence: security-and-compliance/audit-logging (for audit procedures)
- Confluence: eng-infra/terraform-and-iac (for hardware procurement standards)

  curl -X POST https://iam.redwood.internal/api/v1/revoke -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"user":"alice@example.com","group":"infra-admins"}'

[Access-to-Award: Company-wide Playbook for Access, Change, Procurement and Vendor Workflows]
Overview

This playbook, "Access-to-Award", defines the end-to-end company policies and prescriptive procedures for: access and permissions, change management, data handling, procurement and expenses, vendor management, travel approvals, and the set of canonical internal templates. It is intended for all employees, hiring managers, procurement requesters, and approvers.

Scope

Applies to: all Redwood employees, contractors with corporate accounts, and any supplier integrations that interact with Redwood infrastructure or corporate data.

Objectives

- Reduce time-to-approve for common procurements to <= 5 business days for requests under $10k.
- Centralize access requests with auditable approvals and 90-day revalidation cycles.
- Ensure vendor onboarding includes a standardized risk assessment and an assigned contract owner.
- Minimize unapproved configuration changes by enforcing change windows and pre-deployment checklists.

Key Roles and Responsibilities

- Requester: Submits the procurement or access request and provides business justification.
- Approver: Team manager or cost center owner who validates business need.
- Procurement Owner (Finance): Reviews supplier terms, price reasonableness, and tax/compliance checks.
- Security Reviewer: Assesses data access, required controls, and required legal addenda.
- IT/Cloud Ops: Implements access and provisioning tasks.
- Contract Owner: Maintains the vendor contract and renewal calendar.

Section 1 — Access and Permissions (Access-to-Award phase A)

Policy statements:
- Principle of least privilege enforced by default. Access is granted for a defined purpose and expiry.
- All privileges that allow data egress, escalation, or production writes require a business justification and Security approval.

Process (Steps):
1) Requester files an Access Request via the Access Portal (access.redwood.internal). Include duration, scope, and justification.
2) Manager approves or rejects within 3 business days.
3) Security performs risk review for sensitive scopes (PII, Billing, Secrets).
4) IT provisions access with a time-limited role and records audit entry.
5) Revalidation reminder triggered at 60 days, mandatory reapproval at 90 days.

Access tiers and examples:
- Tier 0: Public docs; no request required.
- Tier 1: Internal non-sensitive services (read-only dashboards). Manager approval.
- Tier 2: Sensitive systems (billing, PII). Manager + Security approval.
- Tier 3: Privileged operations (deploy write access, infra admin). Manager + Security + SRE approval.

Section 2 — Change Management

Change types:
- Routine: Configuration changes that are reversible, low risk. No CAB required if change < 15 min impact and tested in staging.
- Scheduled: Feature releases, infra scaling with >15 min expected impact — requires standard CAB review.
- Emergency: Outage mitigation — documented post-facto to CAB within 24 hours.

Change windows and SLA:
- Normal change window: Mon–Fri 09:00–17:00 UTC for non-critical services. Night/weekend windows are reserved for scheduled infra changes with pre-approved rollback plans.
- Rollback capability must be demonstrable in <= 30 minutes for any change classified as Scheduled.

Pre-deployment checklist (required):
- Link to runbook and test results.
- Smoke test plan and rollback steps.
- Impacted services and owners listed.
- Performance and observability queries included.

Section 3 — Data Management

Data classification categories: PUBLIC, INTERNAL, CONFIDENTIAL, RESTRICTED. All datasets must be labeled in the data catalog.

Handling rules (high level):
- RESTRICTED: Encryption at rest + in transit, limited to named principals, storage audited monthly.
- CONFIDENTIAL: MFA enforced for access, export controls applied.

Data retention & deletion:
- Default retention for logs: 90 days (hot), 2 years (cold).
- Sensitive PII: retention only as long as required by the business process; data owner must document retention justification.

Data sharing with vendors:
- Data sharing requires: Data Processing Agreement (DPA), approved SOC/ISO evidence, and a Data Access Justification form. No PII is shared without encryption and contractual protections.

Section 4 — Procurement and Expense Approval (Access-to-Award phase B)

Onboarding checklist (must be completed before production access):

[Enterprise Operations Playbook: Access, Change, Data & Procurement]
Overview
This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference’s company-wide operational policies and reusable templates for: access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel, and internal templates. It is intended for people managers, engineers proposing changes, procurement requesters, security reviewers, and finance approvers. Use the checklists and templates in the final section when beginning a request.

Principles and governance
- Principle: Least privilege by default. Access is granted at the minimum level required and reviewed quarterly.
- Principle: Segregation of duties for procurement and change approvals where feasible.
- Principle: Data classification drives retention, access controls, and encryption requirements.
- Principle: Risk-based change management — low-risk operational changes may be expedited; high-risk, customer-impacting changes require formal approvals and rollback plans.

1) Access & permissions (high level)
Purpose: Define how to request, approve, and revoke access to internal services, cloud accounts, and sensitive datasets.
Key roles and responsibilities:
- Requester: Employee submitting the access request.
- Manager: Verifies business justification and endorses.
- Owner (service/data owner): Grants final approval for resources they manage.
- IAM Team: Executes the access change and records the ticket.
- Security: Periodic auditor for privileged roles.

Access tiers and examples:
- Tier 0 — Privileged administrative: root cloud accounts, KMS/HSM admin, production database admin. Approval: Director+ and Security. Review cadence: monthly.
- Tier 1 — Production service operators: deployment writers, runtime admins. Approval: Service owner + Engineering Manager. Review cadence: quarterly.
- Tier 2 — Internal tooling and analytics: dashboards, non-sensitive logs. Approval: Team manager. Review cadence: semi-annually.
- Tier 3 — Public/non-sensitive access: marketing tools, public docs. Approval: Team manager. Review cadence: annually.

Standard request process (numbered):
1. Requester files an access request via /tools/iam-requests (use template below). Include justification, duration (if temporary), and resources.
2. Manager endorses within 48 business hours.
3. Service/data owner reviews and approves or rejects within 3 business days.
4. IAM team implements and posts the ticket update with artifact of permission change (IAM policy diff, Terraform plan snippet).
5. For temporary access, IAM sets an expiration. Expired grants are auto-revoked and generate a compliance log.

Emergency access (break-glass):
- Process: Pager duty to on-call identity engineer + security notify channel. Emergency grants must be requested with a post-facto justification and will be audited. Any break-glass grant must be short-lived (max 24 hours) and converted to a controlled access path if needed longer.

2) Change management (standardized flow)
Scope: Applies to infra, runtime, networking, and customer-impacting application changes. Software-only feature flags that do not change infra are exempt if covered by automated test gates and SLO guardrails.

Change categories and approval matrix:
- Standard change: Pre-approved routine changes with documented playbooks (e.g., routine config tweak). Approval: No additional approvals required; must follow runbook.
- Minor change: Low-risk code or infra change. Approval: Team lead + automated CI green. Implementation window: standard maintenance hours.
- Major change: Any change affecting production latency, availability, or data model. Approval: Service owner + SRE + Product manager + go/no-go meeting. Requires written rollback plan and canary plan.
- Emergency change: Pushed outside formal schedule for incident mitigation. Retrospective required within 72 hours and RCA if customer impact.

Change request (CR) template (fields to include in the ticket):
- Title, owner, change type, business justification, impact analysis, roll-forward steps, rollback steps, test plan, monitoring/alerting adjustments, scheduled window, approvers, related incidents, preconditions.

Pre-deployment checklist (must be completed for Major changes):
- Unit + integration tests green.
- Load and perf tests run against representative data (target latencies within 10% of baseline).
- Monitoring dashboards prepared (new panels if needed).
- Alert thresholds defined and tested.
- Canary plan: traffic percentage, duration, metrics to evaluate, abort criteria.

Rollout and rollback guidance:
- Canary for 5–10% for at least 30 minutes under normal load before increasing.
- Abort criteria: error rate > 0.5% for 5 minutes above baseline, p95 latency increase > 30% for 5 minutes, or any customer-visible failures.
- Rollback action: execute documented rollback steps and open an incident.

3) Data management (classification, retention, and handling)
Data classification (three tiers):
- Confidential — customer PII, secrets, audit logs with identifiers. Controls: encryption at rest and in transit (AES-256 + TLS1.3), strict RBAC, additional DLP scans, retention policy 1–7 years depending on contract. Access requires Tier 0/1 approvals.
- Internal — internal telemetry, non-identifying logs, internal docs. Controls: RBAC, encrypted at rest, retention 1 year default.
- Public — marketing assets, public docs, open-source artifacts. Controls: public by default.

Retention and deletion policy (summary table described in text):
- Core customer records: retention 7 years unless contract specifies otherwise. Deletion requires data owner sign-off and a documented deletion runbook.
- Audit logs: retention 3 years for security logs, 90 days for operational logs unless investigation ongoing.
- Temp artifacts (scratch buckets): auto-delete after 30 days.

Data handling requirements:
- All Confidential data must never be stored in personal devices or unapproved cloud storage.
- Use approved ETL pipelines for moving data; ad-hoc exports require manager + security approval and must be tracked in the Data Export Registry.
- For datasets used in evals or research, apply anonymization steps (hashing, token removal) and document transformation steps in the dataset manifest.

Breach and suspected exposure process (high level):
1. Immediate containment: remove access to affected systems, rotate related credentials.
2. Notify Security immediately and open a breach incident (critical).
3. Begin forensic capture following Security runbook; notify Legal and Customer Success as required by contracts.
4. Communicate to impacted customers per contract SLAs and regulatory obligations.

4) Procurement & expenses (practical thresholds and templates)
Procurement approval levels:
- Micro purchases (< $1,000): Team manager approval. Use corporate card or expense tool.
- Standard purchases ($1,000–$25,000): Department head + Finance approval. Requires vendor record creation if new.
- Capital / Contracted services (> $25,000): Procurement + Legal + Finance + Director-level sign-off; requires vendor SLA and security questionnaire.

Vendor onboarding and expense flow (numbered):
1. Requester fills the Purchase Request form (template below) with justification, cost center, and preferred vendor.
2. Procurement validates vendor (existing vendor? security & compliance questionnaire).
3. Finance reserves budget and issues PO if required.
4. Legal reviews contract terms if > $25k or if vendor handles confidential data.
5. Procurement completes purchase and records vendor in Vendor Registry.
6. Post-purchase: submit receipts/ invoices to expenses@redwood.com and mark invoice against PO.

Travel policy highlights (for traveler convenience):
- Booking: Use company travel tool; all international travel must be pre-approved by manager + People Ops for visa/insurance coordination.
- Class: Domestic economy for flights under 4 hours; premium economy or business only with Director approval for flights > 8 hours or medical/crew exceptions.
- Per diem and accommodation: Follow rate card in Travel Template. Higher-cost options require justification and manager approval.
- Expenses: Submit receipts within 10 business days. Unreported expenses after 60 days may be rejected.
- Safety: Employees traveling to high-risk regions require manager and Security sign-off and must register itineraries with People Ops.

Expense approval matrix (in text):
- Manager approves up to $1,000/month per employee.
- Dept head approves $1,000–$5,000.
- Finance approves $5,000–$25,000.
- Director-level and Procurement for > $25,000.

5) Vendor management and security integration
Vendor risk tiers:
- Tier A — Highly sensitive (handles Confidential data or infra access). Requirements: full security questionnaire, penetration test results or SOC2 Type II, encryption controls, contractual SLAs, and periodic reviews every 6 months.
- Tier B — Moderate risk (SaaS with no customer-identifiable data). Requirements: standard security questionnaire and annual review.
- Tier C — Low risk (marketing, office supplies vendors). Requirements: minimal record in Vendor Registry.

Vendor lifecycle checklist (short):
- Initial intake: business case, procurement form, vendor questionnaire.
- Security assessment: Security + Product review for data handling capability.
- Contract negotiation: Legal + Finance. Include termination rights and data return/destruction clauses.
- Onboarding: Enter vendor into Vendor Registry and configure payments.
- Quarterly/annual review: performance, SLA compliance, security posture.

6) Internal templates and artifacts (copy & use)
Included templates (use verbatim and attach to tickets):
- Access Request Template (fields: requester, resources, justification, duration, manager)
- Change Request Template (fields: title, owner, type, rollback steps, canary plan)
- Purchase Request Template (fields: budget code, vendor, line items, approvers)
- Travel Request Template (fields: trip reason, dates, approver, estimated cost)
- Vendor Onboarding Checklist (fields: risk tier, questionnaire link, contract ID)

{ "requester": "<name>", "email": "<name@redwood.com>", "resource": "<service-or-bucket>", "level": "Tier 1", "justification": "<business-need>", "duration_days": "30", "manager": "<manager-name>" }

  - kubectl rollout status deploy/service-x -n prod

Compliance, audit, and reporting
- Quarterly access certification: managers receive an automated list of direct reports’ privileged access and must certify or revoke.
- Procurement spend reporting: Finance publishes monthly departmental spend summaries and flags any single-vendor concentration > 30% of category spend.
- Change audits: All Major changes must attach a CR and monitoring snapshots; SRE will randomly audit 10% of Major changes each quarter.

Escalation and exception process

[Procurement: Legal Risk Triage & Escalation SOP]
Overview
This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) describes Redwood Inference's end-to-end triage for procurement items that require legal review or cross-functional escalation. The goal is to reduce cycle time, ensure appropriate risk controls for contracting and billing, and provide clear ownership and SLA targets for each review tier.

Scope
- Applies to all vendor engagements, SOWs, license purchases, hardware leases (including GPU reservations), SaaS subscriptions, and professional services agreements initiated via Procurement.
- Excludes low-value purchases that follow the corporate purchasing card (P-card) policy (see Finance policy: /confluence/finance-and-legal/procurement/p-card-guidelines).

Definitions
1) Low-risk procurement: Purchase value <$25k, no data access, vendor uses standard market terms, no cross-border data transfer.
2) Medium-risk procurement: $25k–$250k, includes limited data access (non-sensitive), or requires limited bespoke terms (payment schedules, warranty clarifications).
3) High-risk procurement: >$250k, access to customer data or models, on-prem or network connectivity required, escrow/KMS requirements, change to indemnity/limitation clauses, or vendor requested data residency exceptions.
4) Contracting Owner: Procurement lead assigned to the purchase.
5) Legal Triage Owner: Commercial counsel assigned to initial review.

Decision Matrix (quick reference)
| Value band | Data access | Special clauses requested | Initial path | SLA (initial review) | Escalation
| --- | --- | --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| <$25k | None | Standard T&C | Procurement approval | 2 business days | Procurement Manager
| <$25k | Non-sensitive | Minor clarifications | Procurement + Legal FYI | 3 business days | Legal (if changes requested)
| $25k–$250k | Non-sensitive | Payment / warranty edits | Legal triage | 5 business days | Senior Counsel
| >$250k or any sensitive data | Any | Any bespoke confidentiality / KMS / escrow | Legal + Security + Finance | 10 business days | GC + Head of Procurement + Security

Procedure (step-by-step)
1. Procurement Request Intake
   a. Requestor opens a PR in the Procurement system (Jira/Workday) with required attachments: vendor quote, SOW, standard T&C, and vendor risk questionnaire.
   b. Procurement Owner tags the request with one of the risk bands and assigns Contracting Owner.
2. Automated Pre-checks (Procurement)
   a. Validate vendor is in the approved vendor list and has completed KYC.
   b. Run vendor risk scan (third-party risk tool) — attach report.
3. Legal Triage (Commercial Counsel)
   a. Counsel performs 3-screen review: (1) identify material exposures (indemnity, liability caps, warranty, IP, data access); (2) verify billing & rev-rec implications (see RevRec checklist below); (3) recommend standard redlines.
   b. Counsel applies template responses from the Clause Library for common items (data transfer addendum, limited indemnity, software license grant).
4. Cross-functional Review (when required)
   a. Security: Required for any network connectivity, data access, KMS/escrow, or on-prem deployments. Security lead must sign off within 3 business days of assignment.
   b. Finance: Required for contracts with atypical billing cadence, revenue-sharing, or subscription modifications; Finance must verify revenue recognition implications and billing trigger alignment.
   c. Product/Platform: Required for technical SOW accuracy and operational acceptance criteria for managed services.
5. Negotiation & Approval
   a. Procurement leads negotiations on non-legal commercial terms; legal negotiates legal language.
   b. For high-risk contracts, the final approval requires sign-off from Head of Procurement, Commercial Counsel, and Director of Finance.
6. Execution & Post-signature Controls
   a. Store executed contract in the contract repository (DocuSign + ContractDB) and tag with metadata (see Contract Metadata section).
   b. Trigger supplier onboarding checklists: finance onboarding (AP routing), security onboarding (vulnerability scan), and ops onboarding (service acceptance).

Contract Metadata (required fields stored in ContractDB)
- contract_id: unique Redwood identifier (e.g., RDW-CTR-2026-000123)
- vendor_legal_name
- purchasing_owner: "team/person"
- commercial_owner: "Procurement lead"
- legal_owner: "Commercial counsel"
- start_date / end_date / renewal_terms
- not_to_exceed_value / committed_spend_line_items
- billing_trigger: invoicing cadence and event that triggers rev-rec (see billing examples)
- data_classification_and_controls: none | non-sensitive | regulated | restricted
- kyc_status: complete | incomplete
- escrow_or_kms_required: yes | no
- confidentiality: internal | restricted | customer-only
- signed_copy_link: internal URL to storage

Revenue Recognition & Billing Checklist (Finance items to confirm before legal approval)
- Identify performance obligations and the billing trigger for each (e.g., access to API endpoints vs. delivery of physical hardware).
- Confirm whether contract changes the timing of revenue recognition (advance payments, non-refundable fees, milestone billing).
- Map invoicing cadence to subscription terms; attach billing examples: 
  Example 1: Monthly subscription — bill in arrears on 1st of following month; revenue recognized ratably over month.
  Example 2: Annual prepay — bill at execution; revenue recognized ratably over 12 months.
  Example 3: Hardware + installation SOW — hardware recognized at delivery; installation revenue recognized over acceptance period (SOW acceptance).

Service Level Targets for Reviews
- Procurement initial intake validation: 1 business day.
- Legal initial triage (see Decision Matrix): 2–10 business days depending on band.
- Security review when required: 3 business days.
- Complete negotiated contract to signature for medium-risk: target 15 business days; high-risk: target 30 business days.

Escalation Contacts
- Procurement Manager: Maya Thompson — procurement@redwoodinference.com — primary for intake issues.
- Legal: Diego Morales — diego.morales@redwoodinference.com — commercial counsel.
- Senior Counsel / GC: Eleanor West — eleanor.west@redwoodinference.com — escalations for policy exceptions.
- Finance RevRec: Priya Singh — priya.singh@redwoodinference.com — billing/revrec edge cases.
- Security: Jin Park — jin.park@redwoodinference.com — data and network escalations.

Exception Handling & Emergency Procurement
- Emergency procurement (e.g., critical hardware replacement) may be approved by Head of Procurement + Head of Finance with retroactive legal review. Document the emergency rationale and complete a post-facto risk assessment within 5 business days.
- For multi-year commitments with budget implications, Procurement must coordinate with Budget Owners and FP&A to surface commitment in the next forecast cycle.

Template Clauses (common redlines and recommended language)
1) Limitation of Liability (recommended cap): "Except for willful misconduct or breach of confidentiality, liability shall not exceed the greater of (i) USD 1,000,000 or (ii) the fees paid in the 12 months preceding the claim."
2) Data Processing Addendum (DPA) pointer: "Attach DPA described in Appendix A; vendor must support EU SCCs and provide KMS integration details for customer-managed keys where required."
3) Escrow/KMS: "For on-prem or model-hosting arrangements where customer datasets or model weights may be subject to e-discovery or regulatory requests, vendor must provide an escrow arrangement or KMS integration documented in Schedule 3."

Audit & Reporting Requirements
- Quarterly procurement compliance report to Finance and Legal: list of executed contracts > $100k and any deviations from SOP.
- Monthly aging report of contracts in negotiation (by risk band).
- Post-mortem on all high-risk negotiations that exceeded 30 business days: root cause and action items.

Appendix A: Sample Legal Redline Checklist (for counsel)
- Verify IP ownership and license grants.
- Check indemnity and carve-outs for open-source dependencies.
- Confirm limitation of liability and insurance obligations.
- Ensure confidentiality duration and return/destruction procedures.
- Confirm termination for convenience and transition assistance obligations.

Appendix B: Example CLI snippet to tag a contract in ContractDB (internal tool)
$ contractdb tag add --id RDW-CTR-2026-000123 --label "data:non-sensitive" --field billing_trigger="monthly_in_arrears" --owner procurement/maya.thompson

Related Documents & References
- Procurement playbook (sourcing to recognition): /confluence/finance-and-legal/procurement/sourcing-to-recognition-control-catalog-and-procurement-playbook-2025
- Contract clause inventory: /confluence/finance-and-legal/contracts-and-legal-process/contract-clauses-escrow-kms-data-residency-2026
- RevRec examples and policy: /confluence/finance-and-legal/revrec-and-billing/subscription-billing-cutover-and-revenue-timing-policy-2027

Change History
- 2025-11-12: Initial draft by Aisha Patel.
- 2025-12-08: Added Decision Matrix and revrec checklist (review by Priya Singh).
- 2026-01-09: Published after Security review and updated SLA targets.

Owners & Maintenance
- Document owner: Head of Procurement (Maya Thompson).
- Document steward for updates: Commercial Counsel (Diego Morales).
- Review cadence: annual or on material policy change.

This SOP is the authoritative procedure for procurement legal triage and escalation. Any deviations must be documented as an exception and approved by the GC and Head of Finance.

[Contract Sourcing, Pricing Clauses, and Billing SOP — Contract-to-Revenue Alignment]
Summary:
This document defines the standard operating procedures (SOP) for sourcing customer contracts, standardizing pricing and SLA clauses, and mapping contract events to billing and revenue recognition triggers. It is intended to reduce contract review cycles, ensure consistent accounting treatment, and create clear handoffs between Sales, Legal, Finance, and Procurement.

Scope:
- Applies to all new commercial contracts (hosted API, Dedicated, Private) and amendments to existing accounts where contract value >= $10,000 ARR or multi-year commitments are proposed.
- Excludes internal vendor procurement (see procurement SOP) and non-revenue master service agreements (MSAs) under $10k ARR.

Objectives:
1. Standardize clause language for pricing, billing triggers, and SLAs to minimize legal variability and simplify RevRec decisions.
2. Define an approval matrix for discounts, custom payment terms, and data residency addenda.
3. Ensure automated mapping of contract milestones to billing and revenue recognition events.
4. Reduce contract review cycles to <= 5 business days for standard deals.

Definitions:
- Billing Trigger: a contract event that causes Finance to invoice and/or recognize revenue (examples: service activation, delivery milestone, subscription start date).
- Deferred Revenue Event: money received before the service is delivered and recognized under ASC 606.
- Enterprise Commit: a reserved-capacity contract with fixed monthly committed spend.

Roles & Responsibilities:
- Sales (Deal Owner): complete Deal Intake Form in Salesforce, select pricing template and expected billing trigger.
- Legal: review non-standard language, insert approved clause variants from Clause Library, sign MSA.
- Finance (Revenue Accounting): confirm RevRec impact, map billing triggers to revenue schedules, advise on contract language.
- Procurement (Customer-side bill-of-materials or HW): handle purchase orders and supplier-side flows.
- Contracts Ops: upload final fully executed contract to Contract Repository and tag metadata.

Approval Matrix (summary):
| Decision | Threshold | Required Approvals | SLA for approval |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| Standard pricing & MSA template | Any | Sales + Auto-apply | 2 business days |
| Discount > 20% | > $50k ARR | Sales Manager + Finance Director | 3 business days |
| Custom billing cadence / Net-90 or more | Any | Finance Director + Legal | 5 business days |
| Data residency / On-prem deployment addenda | Any | Legal + InfoSec + Finance | 7 business days |
| Enterprise commit with holdback/penalty language | > $500k total contract value | VP Sales + Head of Finance + Legal | 10 business days |

Contract Clause Standardization (examples):
- Pricing header: "Customer agrees to pay Redwood Inference the fees set forth in Exhibit A. Fees are non-refundable except as stated in Section 5 (Credits & Refunds)."
- Billing Trigger sample snippets: 
  - Subscription: "Billing commences on the Subscription Start Date defined as the date the Service is provisioned to Customer and confirmed by Redwood via email."
  - Enterprise Commit: "Customer will be billed monthly in advance for committed capacity. Usage beyond committed capacity will be billed monthly in arrears at the overage rate set forth in Exhibit A."
- SLA penalty language (template): "If average 30-day availability falls below the SLA threshold (99.5%), Customer is eligible for service credits equal to X% of monthly fees as specified in Exhibit B. Credits are Customer's sole remedy for SLA failures."

Mapping Contract Events to Billing & RevRec (process):
1. At contract signature, Contracts Ops adds metadata fields: contract_value, billing_trigger_type, subscription_start_date, commit_term_months, is_deferred.
2. Finance runs a RevRec pre-check: 
   - If billing is in advance for a future period, flag as deferred revenue and create schedule per ASC 606 (monthly or daily recognition).
   - If billing is milestone-based, link milestone IDs to revenue recognition tasks and estimate percent-complete when applicable.
3. For Enterprise Commits: create a committed revenue schedule and an overage revenue stream; reconcile usage records daily and invoice monthly.

Examples (common scenarios):
- Standard monthly subscription (prepaid): invoice on Subscription Start Date for month 1 in advance -> Recognize revenue ratably across that month.
- Annual prepaid contract: invoice on Start Date for 12 months -> Defer revenue and recognize monthly over 12 months.
- Multi-year Enterprise Commit with ramp: commit fees billed quarterly in advance -> Recognize ratably across quarter, with evidence of performance for ASC 606 satisfied.

Procurement Handshake & PO Flow (when customer issues PO):
1. Sales attaches PO to Deal in Salesforce.
2. Contracts Ops validates PO matches signed MSA/Order Form (customer legal name, billing address, payment terms).
3. If mismatch, Contracts Ops returns issue to Sales with a clear remediation checklist.
4. Once matched, Finance issues invoice per payment terms and logs PO number in ERP for reconciliation.

Contract Variance Checklist (must be confirmed before Legal approval):
- Is pricing template changed? (yes/no)
- Is there non-standard refund or credit language? (yes/no)
- Is there a data residency or encryption change? (yes/no)
- Are there third-party transfer/subprocessor clauses? (yes/no)
- Is there an unusual indemnity or liability cap? (yes/no)
- Does the customer request Net-90 or invoice holdback? (yes/no)

Quick Decisioning Rules (for Sales to self-serve):
- If all answers are "no" on the variance checklist and total ARR < $250k, apply standard e-sign template and route for auto-execution.
- If any "yes" and < $50k ARR, route to Legal Ops for expedited review (48–72 hours).
- If any "yes" and >= $50k ARR, require Legal + Finance manual review.

Clause Library & Templates:
- Location: Contract Repository -> /templates/2026/Standard-MSA-v3.1, Order-Form-Subscription-v2.0, Enterprise-Commit-Addendum-v1.2
- Naming convention: template-type_version_date (example: MSA_v3.1_20260201)
- Maintain a changelog in the template directory and tag releases with the release manager's name.

Operational Playbook (day-of-signature to revenue recognition):
1. Contracts Ops uploads fully executed PDF to repository and populates metadata.
2. System webhook triggers Finance: create billing schedule and set initial invoice.
3. Finance flags RevRec task; revenue accountant confirms recognition schedule and posts deferred revenue journal entries.
4. Billing system sends initial invoice and records receivable.
5. Monthly close: revenue team validates recognition vs usage and posts adjustments before period close.

Automations & Integration Points:
- Salesforce -> Contracts Repository webhook: on contract status = Executed, push PDF + metadata to repository.
- Contracts Repository -> ERP: create contract record with invoicing cadence and PO linkage.
- Usage pipeline -> Billing: daily usage records to compute overage billing for Enterprise commits.

Escalation Paths:
- Time-sensitive commercial negotiations (deadline < 72 hours): Sales flags as "urgent" in Deal Intake Form, Leads from Legal & Finance are paged for triage.
- Accounting disputes: Finance Lead allocates a ticket in the RevRec queue and informs Sales and Customer Success within 24 hours.

Metrics & Targets:
- Contract review cycle time (standard deals): target <= 5 business days.
- Percentage of deals using standard templates: target >= 85% by end of quarter.
- Accuracy of RevRec schedules at initial posting: target >= 98% (measured monthly).
