[Brand-Isolated Interaction Color Ramps for Dark Console (charts, tables, buttons)]
description:
Problem: Brand accents bleed in dark mode when used across interactive micro-states (hover, focus, active) and data overlays (table row highlights, chart series glows). Current token set uses a single accent ramp per brand that assumes a light background; when placed on deep surfaces it loses contrast or oversaturates adjacent UI elements.

Goal: Define a brand-isolated interaction ramp and a small set of scoped component overrides that produce predictable, accessible micro-interaction colors across dark console surfaces. The solution should: produce consistent perceived brightness across different brand hues, preserve text and icon contrast against interactive surfaces, avoid color contamination in adjacent grayscale surfaces, and be computationally light to generate at build/runtime.

Scope: buttons, pill badges, table row highlights, table cell selection, chart series fills/glows, small focus rings and hover states. This ticket covers token definitions and a reference Figma kit and a PRD for the frontend implementation; engineering work to wire tokens into runtime will be a follow-up linked as dependencies.

Deliverables:
- Token spec: new token names and mapping rules (brand isolation ramp tokens + semantic aliases).
- Figma component kit with annotated dark-surface variants and visual QA for 6 brand hues.
- Frontend override guidance: CSS var mapping, component API flag (useIsolatedAccent: boolean), and suggested fallbacks for older browsers.
- Accessibility acceptance criteria (contrast ratios and motion-friendly transitions).

Design decisions and approach:
1) Isolation via desaturated overlay method: generate ramps by compositing a desaturated overlay layer + small luminance adjustment rather than purely adjusting hue saturation/lightness. This preserves chroma information while providing predictable perceived darkness on deep surfaces.
2) Per-component semantic aliases: define tokens like token.interaction.brandAccent.surfaceHover/active/focus; components map to semantic tokens rather than raw brand color tokens.
3) Small, deterministic algorithm for runtime: start from brand base color (hex), compute a neutral-desaturate factor and blend with surface-luminance anchor to yield three micro-state colors. This allows runtime compatibility when brands are customer-provided.
4) Chart-specific treatment: chart glows should use a single-channel alpha overlay of the brandAccent with a blurred gaussian mask and a tuned luminance delta to avoid overwhelming axes/labels.

Acceptance criteria:
- Hover/Active/Focus for primary and subtle buttons maintain WCAG AA text/icon contrast (>=4.5:1 for any icon/text on that surface).
- Table row highlight and chart series glow do not reduce neighboring text below AA when applied at default opacity.
- Figma QA for six selected brand hues (red, green, blue, purple, orange, teal) shows consistent perceived lightness across examples.

Notes on trade-offs:
- Using a desaturated composite increases maintenance compared to hand-tuned ramps but scales to many brand hues and supports customer-provided brand colors.
- Slight chroma loss for very low-saturation brand tokens is acceptable; we will document a recommended minimum brand saturation for reliable results.

Next steps / Implementation plan:
- Deliver Figma kit and annotated token spec (this ticket).
- Frontend engineering ticket (ENG-98412) to implement runtime generator and component flagging; will be dependent.
- QA pass with accessibility team and solutions engineers for customer-provided brand tests.

- Design PRD: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/CONSOLE/Brand+Isolated+Interaction+Ramps
- Reference research doc on perceived lightness: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1XyZ-research-studies

[Consistent spinner overlay and label behavior for button loading/disabled states]
description:
Standardize how the Button component shows progress and disabled states across variants (primary/secondary/tertiary/icon-only) and themes. Deliver a token-driven spinner layout that avoids layout shift, preserves focus order, communicates state to assistive tech, and remains theme-aware (dark/high-contrast). This replaces several ad-hoc patterns that caused visual regressions during last release and inconsistent behavior between icon-only and label buttons.

acceptance_criteria:
Buttons show an inline overlay spinner without layout shift for all size variants
Icon-only buttons display a centered spinner and maintain a visible hit target and accessible name
When loading, visible label either shows microcopy (e.g., 'Saving...') or remains visually present per variant rules; screen readers receive an appropriate aria-live update
Focus order and keyboard activation remain consistent while a button is loading/disabled
Spinner and spacing use design tokens (spinner-size, spinner-gap, button-spinner-opacity) and respect reduced-motion and high-contrast settings
No new regressions in button hover/active/focus visual states across themes (light/dark/high-contrast)
Automated visual snapshot tests and accessibility checks (axe/voiceover) pass for new behavior

tasks:
Design: produce token spec for spinner size and gap (xs/sm/md/lg) and token mapping for each button size
Design: create visual comps for Primary, Secondary, Tertiary, and Icon-only with loading overlay and inline label variants
Engineering: implement CSS+React changes to support overlay spinner and token usage
Engineering: add aria-live announcements and ensure icon-only buttons surface accessible names
QA: regression test existing button interactions and run visual diffs across themes
Docs: update component doc with migration notes and examples for legacy consumers

decisions:
Use an overlay spinner that sits on top of the button content (semi-transparent layer) to prevent layout shift across different label lengths
Maintain the visible label for non-icon buttons when loading but switch copy to developer-provided 'loadingLabel' if supplied; otherwise fall back to original label with aria-live announcement
For icon-only buttons, replace icon with spinner but keep aria-label present and expose loading state via aria-busy=true on the button
Spinner sizing and gap values will come from new tokens so runtime can map to quantized CSS values for consistent pixel snapping

tradeoffs:
Overlay prevents layout shift but increases CSS complexity and requires z-index discipline across nested containers
Keeping the visible label reduces surprise for users but may conflict with compact UI requirements; offering 'loadingLabel' provides opt-in succinct messaging
Replacing the icon in icon-only buttons is visually clean but requires careful attention to hit target and screen reader names to avoid regressions

[Reduce loading jitter: adaptive spinner, text-preserving states, and theme-aware motion]
description:
Problem: Users and telemetry show that button interactions feel unstable when network latency varies: the loading spinner appears too quickly on short waits, causes text shift when replacing label content, and different themes (dark vs light/high-contrast) expose poor contrast or invisible spinners. Additionally, reduced-motion and a11y settings are not respected consistently across icon-only buttons. This ticket defines a design spec for adaptive loading affordances that preserve label width, respect reduced-motion and color tokens, and provide an escape path to cancel long waits. Goals: (1) avoid visual jitter by deferring and crossfading loading indicators rather than snapping; (2) maintain layout stability by reserving label width and optionally overlaying spinner without replacing text; (3) ensure spinner/icon contrast meets WCAG in all themes; (4) add a micro-interaction pattern for icon-only buttons where spinner substitutes with a subtle pulse instead of large motion; (5) document token changes and provide developer acceptance criteria and test cases for regressions.

acceptance_criteria:
Default primary and secondary button components reserve label width so enabling loading does not shift layout unless explicitly configured.
Loading indicator appears after a 200ms debounce for normal buttons and 120ms for icon-only buttons (configurable via token).
When loading replaces actionable text, crossfade over 120ms with preserved baseline alignment; an alternative 'overlay' mode shows a spinner on top of the label without removing text.
Spinner and pulse accent colors are token-driven and pass 4.5:1 contrast against the current surface in both light and dark themes (design provides token suggestions).
Reduced-motion preference disables crossfades and uses instant appearance plus a static spinner glyph or color change; animations must be <50ms where motion is required.
Icon-only buttons use a scale-preserving micro-pulse (20% subtle scale) instead of large spinner rotation when reduced-motion off; when reduced-motion on, use a static filled circle with a visible ring.
Design tokens added/updated and documented: button.loading.debounce, button.loading.mode (replace|overlay), button.icon.loading.style (pulse|spinner), button.loading.transition-duration, button.loading.color-token, and reduced-motion behavior notes.
Design handoff artefacts: Figma components with three variants (idle, delayed-loading, overlay-loading), a short video showing micro-interactions, and a Confluence page with dev QA checklist.
Regression tests created in Storybook and Playwright that assert no layout shift on toggle, accessible contrast checks, and reduced-motion behavior under OS preference emulation.

tasks:
Audit current button tokens and gather failing examples from product pages (Console, Hosted API flow, Dedicated setup).
Create Figma component variants: idle, loading-replace, loading-overlay, icon-pulse, icon-static.
Propose token values and fallback rules for light/dark/high-contrast themes and circulate for review.
Produce motion specs (timing, easing, crossfade) and reduced-motion alternatives.
Developer handoff: prepare a single-page spec, export components, and attach sample CSS/JS usage patterns.
Work with ENG to implement token names and default values; iterate on accessibility edge cases.
Add Storybook stories and Playwright visual tests; mark as required for release sign-off.
Run a small regression sweep across 3 critical pages and log findings.

design_notes:
Prefer width-preserving approach: measure label width and reserve using inline min-width to avoid reflow; theme tokens should supply padding-scale so min-width calculation is predictable.
Introduce 'overlay' mode for cases (e.g., destructive actions) where retaining label is more important than visual cleanliness; overlay uses semi-opaque surface token with spinner tint token.
Spinner color token should default to button.fg.inverse on solid variants; on ghost/transparent variants use button.fg.primary with subtle drop shadow for contrast in dark mode.
For icon-only buttons, the pulse must be anchored on the icon center and limited to 8–12ms per frame—use 2-frame pulse at 60fps for subtlety; fallback to static filled circle if reduced-motion is enabled.
Document how to opt a route into a more aggressive loading UX (immediate spinner) for flows where instant feedback is required (search-as-you-type disabled).
Provide a short paragraph for engineering explaining cost/benefit of reserving width vs. overlay (performance, complexity, localization implications).

[Button skeleton placeholder + optimistic UI announcement pattern for intermittent network latency]
description:
Background: Product teams continue to see edge regressions where a button transition from idle -> loading is visually abrupt during high-latency paths (mobile networks, cold caches). In several bug reports, users perceived actions as unregistered when the spinner appeared late; accessibility reviewers also flagged lack of timely ARIA live announcements for optimistic UI updates. This ticket proposes a design pattern: a lightweight, theme-aware skeleton affordance that appears immediately on tap/click for network-bound actions, paired with a short ARIA announcement and a stable layout strategy so buttons don't shift when content changes.

Scope: Design specs, token adjustments, and component guidance for: primary/secondary/ghost variants, icon-only and split buttons, text length changes, and dark/light theming. Include motion timing for skeleton fade and fallback behavior for interrupted requests (cancel/undo).

Goals:
- Reduce perceived latency by showing immediate tactile feedback without introducing new layout shifts.
- Ensure screen readers receive concise updates (eg. "Sending" -> "Sent" -> "Failed") without verbosity or repetition.
- Keep token surface area minimal: color/opacity/height tokens updated where necessary; avoid adding many new tokens unless justified.

Non-goals: Full redesign of button sizes or introducing new component variants. This ticket focuses on affordance + accessibility announcements and regression fixes for existing variants.

acceptance_criteria:
Design spec (Figma) with skeleton state for all button variants: primary, secondary, ghost, icon-only, and split. Includes token references and motion timing.
Accessible announcement pattern documented: ARIA live region example markup/snippet, debounce rules to avoid repeated announcements, and guidance for screen reader verbosity.
Prototype (Figma & HTML/CSS) demonstrating no layout shift when switching to skeleton, with visual regression screenshots across themes (light/dark/high-contrast).
QA checklist: keyboard focus preserved, icon buttons announce action name + status, interrupted/canceled requests revert affordance cleanly and show error microcopy where applicable.
Design sign-off from Accessibility SIG and Product (comments resolved in PR).
Linked Engineering ticket created and dependency recorded for runtime changes required in button component library.

[Implement press-resilience and theme-coalescing for floating action buttons]
description:
Refactor the floating action / icon-only button surface to use a small set of new, token-driven press-state properties and introduce a cancelable-loading affordance for long-running actions. Goal: reduce flicker/regression across themes, improve press resilience when users abort gestures, and centralize theme coalescing so variants behave consistently across light, dark, and high-contrast modes.

background:
We have recurring regressions where floating icon buttons shift size or lose contrast when a loading spinner is shown. Mobile teams reported that long-press cancellation and accidental double-taps are resulting in ambiguous visual feedback. Current styles are duplicated across components and don't expose a simple press/cancel contract to the runtime. This ticket consolidates tokens and prescribes behavior (press, cancel, deferred-loading, motion-reduced) specifically for floating/icon-only buttons.

acceptance_criteria:
Introduce three tokens: --btn-press-opacity, --btn-press-elevation-offset, --btn-cancel-threshold (defaults and theme overrides) and document them in the tokens page
Floating/icon-only buttons use token values and render no layout-shift when entering a cancelable-loading state
Press state persists until either a successful action resolution or an explicit cancel gesture within cancel-threshold; accidental taps must show a reversible micro-state
High-contrast and dark themes pass color-contrast checks for pressed and loading states (WCAG AA)
Design system stories (Chromatic) for: default, pressed, long-press-start, canceled, loading->success, loading->error
Unit/regression visual tests added and passing in CI; a short playbook describing how to triage related regressions is attached
Implementation docs and migration notes for engineering outlining token fallback rules and runtime expectations

tasks:
Draft token spec and fallback strategy
Update Figma components and export updated tokens
Add CSS variables and documentation in DS site
Implement cancelable-loading overlay pattern in component library
Add unit and visual regression tests
Coordinate with mobile design lead for parity notes
Write rollout plan and backwards-compatible flags

decisions_and_tradeoffs:
We choose token expansion (3 tokens) instead of separate variants per theme to limit combinatorial complexity; increases runtime responsibility to coalesce tokens
Cancelable-loading uses a non-blocking micro-spinner anchored inside the button rather than replacing label so there is zero layout shift; tradeoff: slightly more complex CSS positioning
Motion reduction: when user-level reduced-motion is on, the pressed elevation becomes a subtle opacity change only to maintain accessibility
We will default --btn-cancel-threshold to 350ms but allow customers to override in Dedicated/Private via runtime config

notes:
Tie telemetry event 'button.cancel' and 'button.loading' to an observability dashboard so we can catch regressions in customer flows. There's an outstanding conversation about whether the micro-spinner should be considered part of token surface or an implementation detail; decided to keep it implementation-scoped but documented.

[Simplify button loading transitions and normalize icon scaling across themes]
description:
Problem: Multiple regressions and inconsistencies have surfaced after the recent token migration: icon-only buttons visually shift during loading, dark-theme outlines bleed on focus, and the loading spinner timing conflicts with small button press feedback. This ticket scopes a focused design cleanup: simplify loading transitions, define a consistent icon scaling strategy so icons don't reflow when a spinner appears, ensure motion respects prefers-reduced-motion, and produce updated specs for engineering and QA.

acceptance_criteria:
1) When a button enters a loading state the overall component width must remain stable (no layout shift) across size variants (compact/regular/large). 2) Icon buttons should swap the icon for a spinner using absolute positioning / overlay rather than replacing DOM size to avoid reflow. 3) Loading animation timing harmonized: spinner fade-in at 80ms, full rotation begin at 220ms; immediate feedback on press remains. 4) All motion disabled when prefers-reduced-motion is set. 5) Dark and high-contrast themes must preserve focus outline without bleed into spinner. 6) Updated CSS tokens and migration notes provided for frontend owners. 7) QA checklist produced with automated visual regression snapshots and a small Playwright test matrix.

design_notes:
- Use overlay technique: keep icon in flow with visibility:hidden when spinner active; spinner is absolutely positioned centered. This keeps button width constant. - Introduce a new semantic token: button.loading-opacity (default 0.0 -> 0.0 to avoid double layering). - Define scale-preserve rule for icon assets: SVGs must have viewBox-preserve and use vector-fit:contain fallback. - Create two spinner silhouettes: spinner-compact (12px) and spinner-regular (16px) with same center anchor. - Motion timings chosen to reduce perceived input latency while avoiding jank. - Edge case: when label truncation occurs (ellipsis) ensure spinner overlays the right edge, not the label, to avoid content shift.

[Shadow Experiments — E2E Test Plan (Console + APIs)]
Purpose
Validate end-to-end functionality for Shadow Experiments (Console + backend APIs) with emphasis on: (1) experiment creation and lifecycle, (2) correctness and stability of results/deltas, (3) permission boundaries and auditability, and (4) degraded-mode behavior (fail-open, backpressure, scoring lag) without impacting user response path.

Scope
In-scope (beta/GA path):
- Console UI: create experiment, list experiments, detail page (deltas, confidence bands where available), drilldown into sampled examples, export.
- Console backend APIs: CRUD, query aggregates, query examples, filters/pagination.
- Rollouts integration: attaching an experiment to a canary/A-B rollout; linking in rollout timeline.
- RBAC: org/tenant scoping, project/workspace scoping (where applicable), read vs write roles, admin-only actions.
- Audit logs: create/update/delete actions and policy changes.
- Degraded mode: shadow target errors/timeouts, telemetry ingestion lag, scoring queue backlog, circuit breaker triggers; Console behavior under partial data.

Out of scope (explicit non-goals for v1):
- Full offline replay of arbitrary historical traffic beyond retention.
- Customer-managed custom eval code execution inside Redwood.
- Private deployment air-gapped scoring beyond “simulated” tests in this plan.

Test environments / prerequisites
Environments
- staging: primary for E2E automation. Must include routing + shadow mirroring enabled, telemetry ingestion, scoring workers, and dashboards.
- dogfood/internal tenant: for realistic traffic. Use only synthetic prompts approved for storage.
- dedicated-sim: optional environment with tenant-level retention/redaction overrides to validate config knobs.

Feature flags
- shadow_experiments_api: gates API endpoints.
- shadow_experiments_console: gates UI navigation and pages.
- shadow_mirroring_dataplane: gates routing mirroring.
- shadow_scoring_pipeline: gates scoring queue/worker.
Notes: E2E should explicitly cover flag OFF behavior (hidden UI, 404/403 API semantics as decided).

Seed data / fixtures
- Tenant A (internal): roles
  - admin_user (Org Admin)
  - eng_user (Editor/Developer)
  - readonly_user (Viewer)
- Tenant B (external-like): to validate tenant isolation.
- Routes:
  - route_chat_prod (streaming enabled)
  - route_chat_non_stream (non-stream)
  - route_embeddings (should be blocked for v1 if not supported; validate correct UX/error)
- Variants:
  - control: model=rw-open-llama-70b:v3, quant=fp16
  - shadow1: model=rw-open-llama-70b:v4, quant=fp16
  - shadow2: model=rw-open-llama-70b:v3, quant=int8 (quantization profile variant)
- Prompt corpus: synthetic, non-sensitive; include intentional “format contract” tasks (JSON schema output), refusal/safety prompts, and instruction-following prompts.

Observability hooks required for E2E
- Ability to query scoring lag (p50/p95) and ingestion lag in test env.
- Ability to force/simulate:
  - shadow target 5xx
  - shadow target timeout
  - ingestion throttling
  - scoring worker pause
  - circuit breaker open
(If we lack toggles, coordinate with SRE/Platform to add test-only knobs.)

Pass/Fail criteria
- Pass: all P0 scenarios pass; no P0 regressions; no evidence of user-path latency impact in staging canary run (measured via existing route latency metrics) when shadowing is enabled at <=1% sampling.
- Fail: any P0 scenario fails; any cross-tenant data leakage; any role bypass; any case where enabling shadowing changes the user response payload; any audit log omissions for create/update/delete.

Risk areas / known sharp edges (track during QA)
- Cardinality: example drilldown filters might introduce high-cardinality dimensions; ensure backend does not emit unsafe labels.
- Partial data windows: scoring results are async; deltas should show “insufficient data” not misleading zeros.
- Streaming semantics: mirrored streaming requests may be partial; ensure UI explains partial capture and scoring eligibility.
- Retention/redaction: example payloads must be redacted/truncated per policy; ensure UI never displays raw prompt when redaction applied.

Test matrix
Legend: P0 = must pass for beta; P1 = should pass before GA; P2 = nice-to-have.

A) Experiment creation flow (Console)
A1 (P0) Create experiment — minimal valid fields
- Preconditions: shadow_experiments_console=ON; user=admin_user; route_chat_non_stream exists.
- Steps:
  1) Navigate: Console → Rollouts/Quality → Shadow Experiments → Create.
  2) Select route=route_chat_non_stream.
  3) Set sampling=1%.
  4) Add 1 shadow target: shadow1.
  5) Save.
- Expected:
  - Experiment created with status=Active (or Created→Active depending on lifecycle).
  - UI shows experiment ID, created timestamp, owner.
  - A “data pending” state is shown until results present.
  - No client-side console errors.

A2 (P0) Validation errors and inline guidance
- Steps:
  - Try sampling=0, sampling>max allowed, missing route, duplicate shadow targets.
- Expected:
  - Clear error messages.
  - Save disabled until valid.
  - Matches backend validation errors (no divergence between UI and API).

A3 (P1) Create experiment with multiple shadow targets (fan-out)
- Steps:
  - Add shadow1 + shadow2; set per-target timeout if supported.
- Expected:
  - Experiment saves and UI clearly lists both targets.
  - Later results show per-target deltas.

A4 (P1) Create experiment from a Rollout (attach)
- Preconditions: existing canary rollout object for route_chat_non_stream.
- Steps:
  - Rollout detail page → “Attach shadow experiment” → create new.
- Expected:
  - Experiment linked in rollout timeline.
  - Clicking link opens experiment detail with context back-link.

A5 (P1) Idempotency/duplicate submit
- Steps:
  - Click Save repeatedly / refresh during save.
- Expected:
  - Exactly one experiment created.
  - UI recovers gracefully and navigates to created experiment.

B) Experiment lifecycle operations (Console + API)
B1 (P0) Pause/Resume experiment
- Preconditions: experiment active.
- Steps:
  - Pause; confirm; then Resume.
- Expected:
  - Status transitions reflected in UI and API.
  - Mirroring stops/starts accordingly (validated via event counts not increasing while paused).

B2 (P0) Update sampling rate
- Steps:
  - Change sampling 1% → 5%.
- Expected:
  - Audit log entry created.
  - Backend enforces max sampling per tenant.
  - UI warns about cost/overhead.

B3 (P1) Update shadow target set
- Steps:
  - Add/remove a shadow target.
- Expected:
  - New target appears; old target retains historical results (if supported) or clearly resets.
  - UI indicates boundary (“configuration changed at T”).

B4 (P0) Delete experiment
- Steps:
  - Delete; confirm.
- Expected:
  - Experiment no longer listed.
  - API returns 404 (or tombstone) depending on decision; ensure consistent.
  - Audit log entry present.

C) API contract E2E (Console backend)
C1 (P0) Create experiment API
- Endpoint: POST /shadow-experiments
- Validate:
  - 201 with experiment_id
  - server-side validation errors are stable and documented
  - feature flag OFF => 404 or 403 per spec (verify)

C2 (P0) List experiments API with pagination
- Endpoint: GET /shadow-experiments?page_size=…&cursor=…
- Expected:
  - Stable ordering (by created_at desc)
  - Cursor roundtrips; no duplicates

C3 (P0) Get aggregates API
- Endpoint: GET /shadow-experiments/{id}/aggregates?window=1h|24h
- Expected:
  - Returns control vs shadow metrics with explicit “n” sample sizes
  - If insufficient data: explicit state, not zeros
  - No high-cardinality fields present (no raw prompt_id unless hashed/allowed)

C4 (P1) Get examples API with filters
- Endpoint: GET /shadow-experiments/{id}/examples?outcome=regression|improvement&limit=…
- Expected:
  - Examples are redacted/truncated
  - PII-safe fields only
  - RBAC enforced (see section D)

C5 (P1) Export API (if present in beta)
- Endpoint: GET /shadow-experiments/{id}/export
- Expected:
  - Export contains only allowed fields; respects retention window

D) Permissions, RBAC, and tenant isolation
D1 (P0) Role-based access — Viewer
- Preconditions: readonly_user has Viewer role.
- Expected:
  - Can view list + detail + aggregates.
  - Cannot create/update/pause/delete.
  - UI hides write actions AND API returns 403 if called.

D2 (P0) Role-based access — Editor/Developer
- Preconditions: eng_user (Editor).
- Expected:
  - Can create/pause/resume/update sampling.
  - Delete restricted to Admin (if that’s the policy) OR validated against the chosen policy.

D3 (P0) Admin-only retention/redaction overrides (if exposed)
- Expected:
  - Non-admin cannot change retention/export settings.

D4 (P0) Tenant isolation
- Steps:
  - Using Tenant A credentials, attempt to access Tenant B experiment ID.
- Expected:
  - 404 (preferred) or 403 per security policy.
  - No metadata leakage (title, existence, timestamps).

D5 (P0) Audit logs
- Validate audit entries for:
  - create experiment
  - update config (sampling, targets)
  - pause/resume
  - delete
- Expected fields:
  - actor, tenant, timestamp, action, resource_id, diff summary.
- Note: confirm entries appear in audit log UI and via audit export path (if available in env).

E) Results correctness and statistical sanity checks
Goal: verify that what we render in the Console matches the underlying scoring outputs and aggregation logic, and that we handle async timing without misleading users.

E1 (P0) Control response unaffected
- Method:
  - Run baseline request to route_chat_non_stream with shadow enabled.
  - Compare response payload to shadow disabled (same input, same control model pinned).
- Expected:
  - Identical control output (within expected nondeterminism bounds if temp>0; for test set use temp=0).
  - No added latency beyond acceptable jitter; shadow failures do not bubble to user.

E2 (P0) Aggregates reflect known synthetic regression
- Setup:
  - Use a prompt set where shadow2 (int8) is known to occasionally violate JSON format.
- Steps:
  - Run enough synthetic traffic (or replay job) to exceed minimum sample size.
- Expected:
  - Format adherence metric decreases for shadow2 vs control.
  - UI flags regression (color/label) and shows sample size and time window.
  - Confidence interval shown only when computed; otherwise show “CI unavailable” not fake bounds.

E3 (P1) Metric version/rubric version pinning displayed
- Steps:
  - Run experiment across a rubric version bump (if possible in staging) or simulate by creating experiment pinned to v0 vs v1.
- Expected:
  - UI displays rubric version used.
  - Aggregates are not compared across incompatible versions without explicit warning.

E4 (P1) Example drilldown matches aggregate counts
- Steps:
  - Filter examples by “format_violation=true”; count returned examples should be consistent with aggregate rate (within sampling limits).
- Expected:
  - No examples outside retention window.
  - Example payloads show redaction markers.

E5 (P2) Segment filters
- If segmentation by region/model-route exists:
  - Validate that segment filters do not explode cardinality; UI uses allowed enums/buckets.

F) Degraded-mode behavior (must be boring)
F1 (P0) Shadow target timeout (data plane)
- Steps:
  - Force shadow target to time out (e.g., firewall rule or test knob).
  - Send production-like traffic.
- Expected:
  - User response path succeeds.
  - Telemetry indicates shadow_error=timeout.
  - UI shows increased shadow error rate; no crash.

F2 (P0) Shadow target 5xx
- Expected:
  - Same as timeout; no retries that impact user path.

F3 (P0) Telemetry ingestion lag
- Steps:
  - Throttle ingestion (test knob) so events arrive late.
- Expected:
  - UI shows “data delayed” banner with last ingested timestamp.
  - Aggregates window queries are explicit about data completeness.

F4 (P0) Scoring queue backlog
- Steps:
  - Pause scoring workers; generate shadow events.
- Expected:
  - UI shows scoring lag increasing.
  - No false “quality is stable” conclusions; should show “pending scoring”.
  - When workers resume, metrics backfill; UI updates.

F5 (P0) Circuit breaker open
- Steps:
  - Induce sustained shadow failures to trigger breaker.
- Expected:
  - Mirroring disables automatically (or reduces) per policy.
  - User path unaffected.
  - UI surfaces breaker state and guidance (“shadowing temporarily disabled due to errors”).

F6 (P1) Partial outages: examples endpoint unavailable
- Steps:
  - Simulate examples storage outage while aggregates still work.
- Expected:
  - Detail page loads aggregates; examples panel shows error + retry; no full page failure.

F7 (P1) Rate limiting / quotas
- Steps:
  - Exceed allowable example fetch or export limits.
- Expected:
  - Proper 429 and UI message; no infinite spinners.

G) Streaming-specific E2E
G1 (P0) Streaming request mirrored without user-visible changes
- Steps:
  - Use route_chat_prod with streaming.
- Expected:
  - Streaming chunks delivered identically with and without shadowing.
  - Shadow capture rules honored (partial capture allowed but must be flagged).

G2 (P1) Shadow streaming stops early
- Steps:
  - Force shadow target to be slow mid-stream.
- Expected:
  - User stream continues.
  - Shadow stream may be terminated at timeout; recorded as partial.
  - Scoring either skips partials or uses partial policy; UI indicates.

H) Redaction/retention and sensitive data handling
H1 (P0) Redaction applied before display
- Steps:
  - Include synthetic prompt containing a redaction trigger pattern.
- Expected:
  - Stored/displayed prompt is redacted per rules.
  - UI indicates redaction occurred.

H2 (P1) Retention window enforced
- Steps:
  - Set retention short in dedicated-sim; wait/advance time if tooling allows.
- Expected:
  - Examples older than retention not retrievable.
  - Aggregates may remain (if aggregates retained separately); ensure it matches policy.

I) Regression tests / compatibility
I1 (P0) Backwards compatibility on existing Rollouts UI
- Ensure Shadow Experiments nav and components do not break existing latency/cost rollout dashboards.

I2 (P1) Browser compatibility
- Validate Chrome + Firefox latest; Safari best-effort.

I3 (P1) API versioning
- If API is versioned, ensure old clients get sane errors; SDK behavior aligned.

Automation plan
- Cypress/Playwright for UI flows (A, B, D, partial E).
- API tests (Postman/newman or pytest) for C, D, F.
- Load test (small) for “user-path unaffected”: run 1–5% shadow sampling and compare p50/p95/p99 vs baseline; store results as CI artifact.
- Scheduled nightly: degraded mode F3/F4 (can be flaky; mark as quarantine until test knobs stable).

Test data management
- Do not use real production prompts.
- For dogfood tests: ensure “prompt logging for shadow artifacts” is set to minimal retention; confirm redaction.
- Ensure all screenshots/log exports used in bug reports redact any payloads.

Bug triage and severity definitions
- Sev0: user response changed or user-path errors increased due to shadowing.
- Sev1: cross-tenant data access, RBAC bypass, missing audit logs.
- Sev2: incorrect aggregates/deltas, misleading UI states, export leaks.
- Sev3: cosmetic issues, copy, minor UI alignment.

Open questions / items blocking final sign-off
- Final policy: who can delete experiments (Admin only vs Editor)? Need explicit decision so tests align.
- Feature flag OFF semantics: 404 vs 403 (security preference is 404 to avoid discovery).
- Minimum sample sizes for “regression” labeling (Applied ML to provide thresholds); otherwise use “insufficient data” gating.
- Streaming partial scoring policy: skip vs score-partial; UI copy depends.

Owners for follow-ups
- Test knobs for degraded-mode simulation: Sean Gallagher / Platform SRE.
- Rubric version display and compatibility behavior: Jonas Weber / Selene Huang.
- RBAC policy confirmation + audit log fields: Marcus Lin / Kevin Osei.
- UI copy for “data delayed/pending scoring”: Kenji Nakamura + Elliot Price.

Change log
- 2026-02-10: Added degraded-mode tests for scoring backlog + ingestion lag after dogfood queue incident.
- 2026-02-18: Added streaming-specific cases based on routing semantics review.
- 2026-02-24: Updated RBAC test expectations to match latest Console backend checks (pending final policy decision on delete).

[Incident snapshot — collapsible panels proposal]
Goal: design a compact, scannable incident snapshot view for the Console that makes error triage faster for engineers and SREs. Focus on timeouts, 5xx responses, and model-level errors (OOM, decoding failures, invalid logits). The view should be lightweight (fast to open), keyboard friendly, and provide actionable quick-paths (re-run, switch model, escalate, open trace).

Notes-to-self / design constraints:
- Primary persona: platform engineer / on-call SRE doing quick triage; secondary persona: product engineer debugging a user-reported failure.
- Should open from many entry points: alert link, request search result, trace timeline, log lines.
- Keep initial payload small: fetch summary fields first, lazily fetch heavy artifacts (token heatmaps, full response bodies).
- Avoid duplicating existing Trace UI; this is a fast, focused snapshot for one incident/request.
- Permission gating: sensitive payloads masked if not in project scope; show redaction banner.

Proposed layout (collapsible panels):
[Top bar] single-row header with: request id | timestamp | route | status badge (timeout/5xx/model-error) | quick-actions (re-run, copy request, escalate)

Main body: vertical stack of collapsible panels (collapsed by default except Summary):
1) Summary (expanded by default)
  - Short error blurb (e.g., “Inference timeout after 4.0s — backend worker saturated”).
  - Probable cause ribbon (low-confidence estimates based on heuristics): CPU saturation / model runtime / network / bad prompt. (Small pill UI with % confidence; tooltip explains heuristics.)
  - Quick health check row: model variant, GPU type, host region, queue length at time, latency p50/p95 for route in last 5m.

2) Request payload (collapsed)
  - Request metadata (user id, api key id, tags).
  - Prompt snippet (first 1–2k chars) with TLDR auto-summarization if >1k chars.
  - Link to full payload in blob store (lazy fetch).

3) Response samples (collapsed)
  - If partial response available, show side-by-side: actual vs expected (expected from golden set or previous successful run if available).
  - When model returned decoder errors, highlight first invalid token position and raw error.

4) Infrastructure timeline (collapsed)
  - Mini sparkline timeline showing CPU/GPU utilization for the node (10s resolution around event).
  - Network latency spikes and queue depth overlay.
  - Click expands to load full SRE timeline view.

5) Trace links & logs (collapsed)
  - Links to full trace view, span ids, and the log line that triggered the alert.

6) Reproduction & Quick fixes (collapsed)
  - Small inline sandbox: run a replay with editable parameters (model, max_tokens, timeout). Default pre-filled with original request.
  - Quick actions: retry same route, switch to fallback model (dropdown), throttle tokens, run with quantized variant. Each action logs an audit record and shows before/after diff of cost estimate.

7) Root-cause hints (collapsed)
  - Heuristic bullets e.g., "High queue length + p95 token time -> backpressure". Items link back to telemetry queries.

Interaction details / microcopy:
- Keyboard: press R to open Reproduction panel, C to copy request id, F to open full trace. Tooltips on badges show last 3 related incidents.
- State: panels remember user open/close per-session (local storage).
- Errors masked: if request contains PII, show masked prompt snippet and button "View (audit)" which opens sponsor-approved payload view.

Wireframe notes (visual priorities):
- Compact header, dense rows. The snapshot is not a full debugger but must be scannable in <7s.
- Use color-coded badges: red (5xx), orange (timeout), purple (model error). Badges have accessible labels "High priority" etc.
- Panels use low-contrast separators, slight elevation for Summary.

Backlog / grooming items (candidate tickets):
- PROD-UX-101: Basic snapshot frame + header + Summary panel (MVP). Estimate: 3 pts. Owner: Riley. Acceptance: open from alert -> shows header + summary + basic quick-actions.
- PROD-UX-102: Request payload panel + prompt snippeting + TLDR summarizer. Estimate: 5 pts. Owner: Samir. Acceptance: prompt >1k truncated w/ TLDR and link to blob.
- PROD-UX-103: Reproduction sandbox (server-side replay) + quick-actions. Estimate: 8 pts. Owner: Jules. Security review required. Acceptance: user can run replay and see result in inline panel.
- PROD-UX-104: Heuristic RCA ribbon (probability score). Estimate: 5 pts. Owner: Avery. Acceptance: Ribbon appears with at least 3 heuristic rules and tooltip linking to the rule definition.
- PROD-UX-105: Telemetry mini-timeline and expand-to-trace. Estimate: 5 pts. Owner: SRE lead. Acceptance: sparkline shows util and queue data for 1m window.

Open questions / risks:
- How to surface confidence for heuristic RCA without being misleading? Need input from applied-ML on model error classification.
- Security: replay could leak secrets if not sandboxed; add enforcement to strip api key headers.
- Performance: ensure snapshot API is <200ms for summary payload to keep it snappy. We may need a denormalized incident snapshot store.

Design alternatives considered (brief):
- Modal vs. full-page: modal felt lighter but has limited space for timeline; decided on side-drawer style if opened from trace, full page if opened from alert landing.
- Single long scroll vs collapsible panels: chose collapsibles to reduce cognitive load and network fetch.

Acceptance criteria for MVP:
- Snapshot can be opened from alert link and request list in under 300ms (summary data).
- Summary panel contains error blurb, probable cause ribbon, and 3 quick-actions (retry, copy id, open trace).
- Reproduction sandbox is stubbed (runs in async mode and returns a simulated response).
- All UI elements pass basic accessibility checks (keyboard focus, labels).

[Suggestions API performance budget (beta) — latency, payload, rate limits, caching]
Doc intent
- Capture performance + scale budgets for the Console “Optimization suggestions” beta API.
- This is a constraints doc for engineering: if we can’t meet these numbers, Console UX (table + drawer) will feel sluggish and we’ll get pageload regressions.

Scope
- Suggestions list endpoint + (optional) details endpoint.
- Beta scope = batching + caching suggestions only.
- Org/project scoped, RBAC enforced. No cross-tenant access.

Non-goals
- Real-time per-request inference; suggestions are batch computed and served from storage.
- Guaranteeing “savings accuracy” (handled separately); this doc is about runtime performance and availability.

Assumptions / traffic model (beta)
- Primary UI path: Console loads Suggestions view once per user session; user may sort/filter/paginate; opens 0–5 drawers.
- Expected “active beta orgs”: 10–30 orgs initially, scaling to 100–200 orgs during expanded beta.
- Concurrent interactive users: 1–10 per org during working hours (spiky), with occasional demos.
- Background job compute cadence: hourly default (can be daily if compute pressure), but serving layer must tolerate stale data.

API endpoints (working contract)
- GET /optimize/suggestions
  - Query params: org_id, project_id (optional), environment (optional), route_id (optional), model (optional), region (optional), suggestion_type (batching|caching), sort, order, page_size, cursor
  - Returns: list of suggestion summaries, next_cursor, stale_as_of, request_id
- GET /optimize/suggestions/{suggestion_id}
  - Returns: the full details payload used by the drawer (why/explanation, assumptions, guardrails, links)

NOTE: If details endpoint is too expensive, we can embed “drawer-lite” content in list response for top N, but that likely increases payload size and hurts perceived speed on the main view.

Performance targets (server-side, excluding client rendering)
Table legend:
- p50/p95 measured at API gateway for 200 responses
- payload size is gzip’ed (over-the-wire) unless stated otherwise
- “cold” = cache miss at service cache layer; “warm” = cache hit

Table: latency + payload budgets
| Surface | Scenario | Target p50 | Target p95 | Hard ceiling p95 | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| GET /optimize/suggestions (list) | warm cache | 80 ms | 180 ms | 300 ms | Primary table load + filter/sort changes |
| GET /optimize/suggestions (list) | cold cache | 140 ms | 300 ms | 450 ms | Cold allowed but should be rare in interactive paths |
| GET /optimize/suggestions/{id} (details) | warm cache | 60 ms | 150 ms | 250 ms | Drawer open should feel instant |
| GET /optimize/suggestions/{id} (details) | cold cache | 120 ms | 250 ms | 400 ms | Drawer tolerates slightly higher; still keep tight |

Table: payload budgets
| Response | Target (gzip) | Hard ceiling (gzip) | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| list page (<= 50 rows) | <= 35 KB | 60 KB | Prefer page_size default 25; 50 max |
| details payload | <= 20 KB | 40 KB | Avoid giant “explanation” blobs; link to docs when needed |
| error payload | <= 2 KB | 5 KB | Keep errors structured, don’t dump stack traces |

Page size / pagination budget
- Default page_size: 25
- Max page_size: 50 (server-enforced)
- Cursor-based pagination required for stable ordering + performance at scale.
- Sorting should be backed by indexed columns; forbid unindexed sorts.

Rate limits (beta)
Rationale: prevent accidental UI loops / eager refresh from hammering backend; keep headroom for compute pipeline + other Optimize traffic.

Table: rate limits
| Principal | Endpoint | Limit | Burst | Window | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| per-user | list | 60 req/min | 20 | 60s | Filter/sort + pagination should be within this |
| per-user | details | 120 req/min | 40 | 60s | Drawer opens can be chatty; still bounded |
| per-org | list | 600 req/min | 200 | 60s | Demos + multiple users |
| per-org | details | 1200 req/min | 400 | 60s | |
| per-IP (fallback) | all | 3000 req/5min | 500 | 300s | DDoS-ish guardrail |

Client guidance to reduce request volume
- UI should debounce filter changes (>= 250–400ms).
- Use “Apply filters” button if we see over-fetching.
- Cache list pages client-side for 30–60s keyed by (org, project, filters, sort, cursor).

Caching strategy
Goals:
- Keep list endpoint p95 < 300ms reliably.
- Avoid repeated DB hits for identical list queries during active usage.
- Support multi-tenant correctness (cache keys must include org_id + project scope + RBAC context).

Proposed layers
1) CDN / edge caching: NOT recommended for beta
- Reason: RBAC + org scoped data; cache fragmentation and security risk.

2) Service-level cache (recommended)
- Cache store: Redis (or equivalent) in-region with the service.
- Cache key inputs (must include): org_id, project_id (or “all”), environment, route_id, model, region, suggestion_type, sort, order, cursor/page boundary, page_size, and a “rbac_scope_hash”.
- TTL:
  - list pages: 60s default (tunable 30–180s)
  - details: 5m default (tunable 2m–15m)
- Invalidation:
  - Passive TTL is fine for beta.
  - Optional: invalidate org keys when new suggestion batch is published (publish event emits org_id + generation timestamp).

3) DB query caching (not primary)
- Avoid relying on DB-level cache; we want deterministic performance with predictable memory pressure.

Staleness behavior
- API must return: stale_as_of timestamp for the dataset used to generate suggestions.
- Console should show “Updated X hours ago” and avoid auto-refresh loops.
- If stale_as_of > 48h (configurable), show warning state but still serve data.

DB / storage performance requirements
- The list endpoint must be implementable as:
  - 1 query for suggestions page (plus possibly 1 query for related route/model metadata), i.e., avoid N+1.
  - Use pre-joined or denormalized summary fields for the list view.
- Required indexes (high level):
  - (org_id, project_id, suggestion_type, sort_key, suggestion_id)
  - (org_id, project_id, route_id)
  - (org_id, project_id, model)
  - (org_id, project_id, region)
- Store “summary” vs “details” separately if needed to keep list thin.

Response shaping (keep the list light)
List response should include only what the table needs:
- suggestion_id (stable)
- suggestion_type (batching|caching)
- target: route_id + route_name (or route display label), model, region/environment (as applicable)
- estimated_savings_usd_per_day (and percent)
- estimated_latency_delta_ms_p50 / p95 (or a compact representation)
- risk_level (Low/Medium/High)
- confidence (e.g., High/Medium/Low or numeric band) — keep small
- stale_as_of (top-level)
- “why_short” (1 sentence max) optional; longer copy belongs in details

Details response can include:
- why_long (bulleted reasons)
- assumptions (tokens priced at X, cache hit uplift assumptions, etc.)
- guardrails / “when not to apply”
- deep links to config pages

Error/timeout budgets
- Gateway timeout: 2s (hard)
- Service internal timeout for DB: 400ms (list), 300ms (details)
- Service internal timeout for cache: 30ms
- Retries:
  - No client retries on 4xx.
  - At most 1 retry on idempotent 5xx at gateway, with jitter; avoid thundering herd.

Availability targets (beta)
- Service SLO (beta): 99.5% successful responses (2xx/3xx) over 7 days.
- Error budget: 0.5% (note: beta; revisit for GA).

Observability requirements (for enforcing budget)
Golden signals (per endpoint)
- request rate (RPS), error rate (4xx/5xx), p50/p95/p99 latency
- cache hit rate (service cache), cache latency, cache errors
- DB query time distribution + query count per request (detect N+1)
- payload size distribution (gzip + raw)
- top offenders by org_id (rate + latency)

Dashboards/alerts (minimum)
- Alert: p95 list latency > 300ms for 10m (burn rate style)
- Alert: 5xx rate > 1% for 5m
- Alert: cache hit rate drops below 60% (investigate TTL/invalidation)
- Alert: compute lag > 2x cadence (data freshness)

Security/RBAC considerations that affect caching
- Cache must not “bleed” across users if RBAC differs. Options:
  A) include rbac_scope_hash in cache key (preferred)
  B) only cache org-level if all users share identical view permissions (not true)
- Safer approach for beta: cache at org+project level AND require permission to “view optimize suggestions” at that scope; still, users may have project exclusions, so hash is needed if we support mixed access.

Proposed rbac_scope_hash inputs
- user_id + org_id + list of allowed project_ids (or a role id)
- permission: optimize:suggestions:read
- NOTE: if this becomes too low hit-rate, revisit RBAC model to make permissions less granular for beta.

Load shedding / degradation behavior
- If DB is slow or cache is down:
  - Prefer serving stale cached responses if within TTL-grace (e.g., allow 5m stale-while-revalidate).
  - If neither available, return 503 with a specific error code that Console maps to a friendly error state.
- If payload too large (unexpected explanation bloats):
  - Truncate server-side with a “truncated: true” flag (string field in response) OR move fields behind details endpoint only.

Open questions / TODOs
- Do we need /optimize/suggestions/summary endpoint for “top opportunities” card elsewhere in Console? If yes, define separate budget.
- Should list endpoint include confidence bands (min/max savings) in beta? If yes, measure payload impact.
- Confirm default TTLs with Console team to avoid confusing “why did it change” in UI while user is browsing.
- Decide whether details endpoint is required for beta launch or can be deferred.

Revision history
- 2026-02-07: initial draft (Logan)
- 2026-02-12: tightened p95 ceilings; added payload budgets after early UI perf testing (Chloe/Felix)
- 2026-02-19: added RBAC cache key notes + stale-while-revalidate recommendation (Allison/Aisha)


[Compact debug sparkline prototypes]
body:
Purpose:\nThis note captures a light-weight, high-density wireframe + interaction proposal for surfacing and triaging error behaviors (timeouts, 5xx, model-level errors) in the Console error list without forcing users into a full trace explorer. Aim is to give engineers a fast signal->action loop for recurring or high-impact failure modes.

body_addendum:
Design constraints and assumptions:\n- Primary user: engineer on-call or feature owner doing quick TTR (time-to-resolution) work.\n- Console list view is busy; we want an at-a-glance heatmap for recent regressions and a tiny inline timeline for each route/session.\n- Should be keyboard-friendly and cheap to render (SVG sparklines and simplified badges).\n- Must link to deep-dive (existing failure replay) but default flow should allow patching a rule/rolldown from the list.

proposal_summary:
Core idea: compact sparkline + error fingerprint card per route/flow\n- Each row in the error table includes a 48x12 sparkline showing failure rate over the last 48 hours (30m buckets).\n- Overlaid on the sparkline are tiny markers for distinct error fingerprints (color-coded: red=5xx, orange=timeout, purple=model-error) with hover tooltips.\n- A micro-metric stack to the left: instantaneous 95th latency, token-rate per second, and error percent as tiny numeric chips.\n- Expand-in-place: pressing Enter or clicking mini-chevron expands a thin panel (max 160px height) that shows the top 3 sample traces, a short hypothesis line, and 2 quick-actions: "Reroute to fallback model" and "Create rollback/patch".

visual_notes:
Wireframe notes for the 1-row compact card: \n- Left: route name + model badge + small muted description (one-line).\n- Mid: sparkline 48x12 with faint grid, black baseline = success, colored markers for fingerprint peaks. Hover shows time window and sample count.\n- Right: chips: [err% 3.4%] [p95 320ms] [tokens/s 120] and an action kebab.\n- Expand panel: two columns. Left column: 3 ranked trace snippets (timestamp, short error message, model-version, quantization-profile). Right column: small quick-fixes and triage checklist (assign, postmortem link, mark as transient).\nASCII mockup for row (compact):\n[route-name] [m:rw-4] | ▁▁▂▃▅▂▁▁◉▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁ | [err% 4.2] [p95 420ms]  •  ⋮\nExpand ->\n-----------------------------------------\n| sample 1 | 2026-02-26 11:12 | 504 gateway | model-v2-q4 | quick-action: reroute |\n| sample 2 | 2026-02-26 10:58 | timeout 30s  | model-v2-q4 | quick-action: increase-timeout |\n-----------------------------------------

interaction_patterns:
Micro-interactions and keyboard flows:\n- Row focus with up/down arrows; Enter toggles expand; 'c' opens create-issue modal pre-populated with selected fingerprint and top traces.\n- Hover on sparkline shows a tiny tray with aggregated counts and a link "Open session replay".\n- Right-click kebab offers: ignore-fingerprint (rule), mute-route-for-1h, create-issue, pin-sparkline (promote to dashboard).\n- Expand panel has two-state quick-actions: preview (simulate reroute against last 1k requests) and apply (apply policy to live routing). Preview is always safe and non-destructive.

data_model_notes:
What must backend provide per row (minimal):\n- time-series vector (48 buckets, counts success/fail)\n- fingerprint ids + short label + sample count\n- top-3 sample traces (timestamp, short message, request-id)\n- route metadata (model version, quantization profile, region)\n- simple pre-computed metrics: p50/p95, err%\nThese are intentionally compact to support cheap list rendering.

heuristics_and_prioritization:
How to rank rows in the table by default:\n1) weighted score combining absolute errors in last 24h + delta compared to baseline + severity (5xx > timeout > model-error).\n2) user pinned routes always first.\n3) Option to switch to 'regression-only' mode (shows top deltas).\nTagging heuristics: group fingerprints if same message AND same top-2 stack frames OR same model-version+token-threshold.

accessibility_considerations:
- Sparkline markers must have hover text and keyboard focus equivalent.\n- Color choices must pass contrast for badges; use patterns or dot shapes if colorblind.\n- All quick-actions accessible by keyboard and screen-reader friendly labels.

acceptance_criteria:
MVP acceptance (product + eng):\n- List view renders 1000 rows with sparklines without jank on typical SRE machine.\n- Expand panel fetches top-3 samples in <300ms.\n- Quick-action preview returns simulated reroute metrics within 1s.\n- Users can create triage issue with prefilled fingerprint + traces via keyboard-only flow.\n- Feature controlled behind a feature-flag and rollout toggle.

backlog_and_next_steps:
Backlog items (ranked):\n- [P0] API endpoint: aggregated 48-bucket timeseries + fingerprint map (ENG-1229)\n- [P0] Frontend component: tiny sparkline svg with marker overlay (PR: console-prototypes#78)\n- [P1] Quick-action preview simulation service (ENG-1344)\n- [P1] Create rule modal integration (policy service)\n- [P2] Accessibility pass (a11y QA)\n- [P3] Dashboard pinning + alert subscription UX\nOwner tasks for next week:\n- Design: produce hi-fi sprite for 48x12 sparkline and marker hover states (Asha)\n- FE: implement basic sparkline component and keyboard nav (Miguel)\n- BE: prototype timeseries aggregator endpoint + sample trace fetch (Evan)

open_questions_and_risks:
Open questions:\n- How do we dedupe fingerprints across routing fallbacks? (risk: duplicate noise)\n- What retention should backend assume for 48-bucket aggregates? (storage/cost tradeoff)\n- Preview simulations may leak PII in traces — need scrub rules.\nRisks:\n- Overloading list with microvisuals could increase cognitive noise; plan to gate behind analytics experiment and gradual rollout.

notes_to_reviewers:
Please review focusing on:\n- Are the quick-actions appropriate and safe to expose (preview vs apply)?\n- Does the ranking heuristic match on-call workflows?\n- Anything missing that would prevent safe rollouts (compliance/audit hooks)?\nAdd comments inline in the Confluence doc or drop notes in Slack #console-ux.

references_and_inspo:
- Example: Datadog sparkline rows, but we favor single-trace quick-preview rather than full flamegraphs.\n- Internal: ties to `failure-replay-and-trace-ux-notes` and `triage-quickstart-canvas` (see linked artifacts).\n- Research: quick look at mental model for sparklines in lists, Nielsen Norman Group notes on microvisualizations.

final_remark:
This is intentionally lightweight: target first iteration is 'useful and cheap' rather than exhaustive. If core heuristics and the tiny sparkline give immediate reductions in time-to-detect/triage during the experiment, expand to richer inline diagnostics.

[Suggestions View (Console) — Frontend Implementation Plan (Beta)]
Context
We’re shipping the beta “Optimization suggestions” experience in the Redwood Console. Scope is strictly batching + caching suggestions surfaced via Optimize Suggestions service.

This doc is the concrete frontend implementation plan for the Suggestions page: routing, component breakdown, data fetching/caching, pagination/sorting, and error/empty-state handling. It’s written to align with the backend API contract (stable IDs, cursor pagination) and the design spec (table list + details drawer).


0) Assumptions / inputs
- Feature flag: Suggestions view is gated per-org (and potentially per-project) via OptimizeSuggestionsBeta flag.
- Access control: Users also require RBAC permission optimize:suggestions:read. If flagged on but permission missing, show a clear access denied state (do not fall back to “no data”).
- API: GET /optimize/suggestions supports filtering, sorting, and pagination (cursor-based), returns stable suggestion IDs and stale_as_of timestamp.
- Design: Primary UI is a table-like list with filter chips + sort, and a right-side details drawer on row click.
- Telemetry: We emit impression/expand/dismiss/apply-click events with required properties (org_id, project_id, route_id, model, suggestion_id, suggestion_type, risk, confidence).


1) User journeys to support (MVP for beta)
1) Discover suggestions
- Entry point: Console left nav → Optimize → Suggestions (or deep link).
- Default query: last 7 days telemetry window (server-defined) and sort by estimated_savings_usd_per_day desc.

2) Inspect a suggestion
- Click a row to open details drawer.
- Drawer includes “Why we recommend”, assumptions, savings estimate ranges if provided, risk explanation, and “How to apply” deep link(s) to config.

3) Dismiss / apply
- Dismiss (UI-only action; record dismissal event; backend persistence optional in beta—see “Known gaps”).
- Apply: CTA opens relevant config page with query params pre-filled; we track “apply_click” (NOT auto-apply).

4) Handle no results / no telemetry / not enabled
- If API says insufficient telemetry or returns “eligibility reason”, show the corresponding empty state with setup CTA.


2) Routing + page composition
Routes
- New route: /console/:orgSlug/:projectSlug/optimize/suggestions
- Optional deep link to open drawer: /optimize/suggestions?suggestion_id=<id>
  - Behavior: page loads list; after list resolves, if suggestion_id is present and found, open drawer.
  - If suggestion_id not found in first page, attempt a direct fetch-by-id only if backend supports it; otherwise show toast “Suggestion not found or no longer available” and do not loop.

Feature flag guard
- Route-level guard: If org not enabled for OptimizeSuggestionsBeta, show “Beta access required” empty state with link to request access.
- If enabled but RBAC missing, show “Access denied” empty state with support/internal request link.


3) Component breakdown (proposed structure)
Page-level
- <SuggestionsPage />
  - Owns: URL state ↔ query state sync, data fetching orchestration, top-level empty/error rendering, and page-level telemetry (impression).
  - Children:
    - <SuggestionsHeader /> (title, subtitle, help link, staleness chip if needed)
    - <SuggestionsFiltersBar /> (filter chips, search, sort dropdown)
    - <SuggestionsTable /> (virtualized list, row actions, loading skeletons)
    - <SuggestionDetailsDrawer /> (open/close, fetch detail if needed)
    - <SuggestionsFooter /> (pagination controls + “results per page” only if we decide to expose limit)

Shared components
- <RiskBadge />: already implemented in shared UI library (uses design-approved colors + tooltip copy).
- <ConfidenceBadge />: simple pill, likely “High/Medium/Low” (copy from design spec).
- <MoneyDelta />: $/day + % formatting.
- <LatencyDelta />: p50/p95 delta formatting with “ms” and sign.

Data models (frontend types)
- SuggestionListItem
  - suggestion_id (stable)
  - suggestion_type (batching | caching)
  - route_id / route_name
  - model
  - estimated_savings_usd_per_day
  - estimated_savings_pct
  - latency_delta_p50_ms / latency_delta_p95_ms
  - risk_level (low | medium | high)
  - confidence_level (low | medium | high)
  - stale_as_of (timestamp)

- SuggestionDetails (for drawer)
  - includes all list item fields plus:
  - why_recommended (bullets)
  - assumptions (bullets)
  - guardrails (bullets)
  - recommended_config (human-readable + link targets)
  - inputs_snapshot (optional, if included by API; we will not render raw metrics unless designed)


4) Data fetching strategy (caching, pagination, debouncing)
Library
- Use existing Console standard data layer (React Query). If we’re already on TanStack Query v4, stick with it.

Query keys
- List query key should include org_id, project_id, filters, sort, and cursor.
  - suggestions:list:{org}:{project}:{filtersHash}:{sort}:{cursor}

Pagination
- Cursor-based pagination per ADR. Use React Query useInfiniteQuery unless design requires explicit page numbers.
- Proposed UX: “Load more” (infinite) OR paginated table with Next/Previous.
  - For beta, prefer Next/Previous with a visible cursor model to reduce surprise and keep row counts stable.
  - Implementation detail:
    - Keep “current cursor” in URL (e.g., ?cursor=<token>) only if required for shareability.
    - Otherwise keep cursors in memory to avoid leaking opaque cursor tokens into shared links.

Sorting
- Sort options per design ticket (expected):
  - Savings ($/day): desc (default), asc
  - Risk: low→high (or high→low; confirm)
  - Confidence: high→low
  - Latency impact p95: asc
- Sorting triggers a full list refetch; reset cursor.

Filtering
- Filters (beta baseline):
  - suggestion_type (batching/caching)
  - risk_level
  - route (multi-select, optional)
  - model (multi-select, optional)
  - region (only if supported by API; otherwise omit)
- Filter changes are debounced (300ms) for text search; immediate for chip toggles.
- Filter state is mirrored to URL query params for shareability.

Caching
- Stale time: 60s for list. This avoids refetching on quick nav or drawer open.
- Refetch on window focus: disabled for this page (we don’t want background refetch to reorder table while user is reading). Provide manual refresh button in header.
- Manual Refresh
  - Button: “Refresh” → invalidates list query and refetches.
  - If API includes stale_as_of, we display “As of <time>” and update on refresh.

Drawer data
- Option A (preferred): list response includes enough detail for drawer (why/assumptions) so drawer doesn’t need a second request.
- Option B: drawer fetches details on open via /optimize/suggestions/{id}.
  - If we don’t have a details endpoint in v0, keep it all in list response.
  - If details endpoint exists, we still pass list item into drawer immediately (optimistic render), then hydrate extra fields.


5) Table rendering + performance
- Use row virtualization if >100 rows is common; otherwise keep it simple for beta.
- Use skeleton rows while loading.
- Row click opens drawer; provide secondary actions in kebab menu (Dismiss) to avoid accidental dismissal.
- Accessibility
  - Table must support keyboard navigation: arrow keys optional; tab to row; Enter opens drawer.
  - Drawer trap focus; Esc closes drawer.
  - Risk badge tooltip accessible via keyboard.


6) Empty states and how we determine them
We need to disambiguate:
A) Feature not enabled
- Condition: flag false for org/project.
- UI: “Optimization suggestions beta is not enabled for this org.” CTA: “Request access” (link to internal form or docs).

B) Access denied (RBAC)
- Condition: API returns 403 with known error code OR permissions endpoint indicates missing optimize:suggestions:read.
- UI: “You don’t have access to view suggestions.” CTA: “Request access” (link to internal support/INT ticket form).

C) Insufficient telemetry / not eligible
- Condition: API returns 200 with eligibility_status = insufficient_telemetry OR empty list + reason.
- UI: “Not enough telemetry yet” with:
  - what signals are required (QPS, cache metrics, latency histograms)
  - typical time to populate (e.g., “within 24 hours after enabling telemetry”)
  - CTA to telemetry setup page.

D) No suggestions available (healthy)
- Condition: API returns 200, eligible, but suggestions list empty.
- UI: “No suggestions right now” with explanation (“We didn’t find safe batching/caching changes with meaningful savings.”) and link to docs.

E) Backend error
- Condition: 5xx / network errors.
- UI: error panel with retry, status page link, and error request id (if present).

F) Stale estimates
- Condition: stale_as_of older than threshold (e.g., >48h) OR compute lag flag.
- UI: show warning banner “Estimates may be out of date (as of …).” Provide refresh; do not block.


7) Error handling details
- If list fetch fails:
  - Render error state at page level.
  - Include “Retry” button.
  - Log error to client error reporting with route, org/project ids, HTTP status, request id.

- If drawer hydration fails (Option B):
  - Keep drawer open; show inline “Couldn’t load full details” with Retry.
  - Still allow Apply CTA if we have enough info.

- If apply deep link destination not available (config page missing or route disabled):
  - Fallback: open docs page and show toast “Couldn’t open settings automatically. See docs.”


8) URL state (shareable + stable)
Query params (proposed)
- type=batching|caching (multi allowed: type=batching&type=caching)
- risk=low|medium|high (multi allowed)
- model=<string> (multi allowed)
- route_id=<id> (multi allowed)
- sort=savings_usd_per_day_desc (enum)
- suggestion_id=<id> (for drawer)

Rules
- Changing filters/sort clears suggestion_id to avoid stale drawer state.
- Closing drawer removes suggestion_id from URL.


9) Telemetry instrumentation (frontend)
Events (names per taxonomy doc; final names owned by Telemetry team)
- suggestions_view_impression
  - fired once when page renders and flag+rbac allow view.
  - props: org_id, project_id, default_sort, filters_applied_count

- suggestions_row_open
  - fired on drawer open (not on mere row focus).
  - props: suggestion_id, suggestion_type, route_id, model, risk_level, confidence_level, rank_position

- suggestions_dismiss_click

Unit/integration (React Testing Library)

- RBAC denied state renders on 403.

E2E (Playwright; aligns with Leila’s checklist)
- Flag off → beta access empty state.
- Flag on + RBAC missing → access denied.
- Eligible + results → list loads, drawer opens, apply click navigates.
- Eligible + no results → “No suggestions right now”.

- Pagination: next/prev returns stable results; no duplicate keys; scroll position preserved.

- Page and components behind feature flag; do not ship nav entry to all users until flag rollout.

2) Implement query param state model (filters/sort/suggestion_id).

description:
Customer report (Northbridge AI Platform, enterprise):

Issue summary:
- Beginning ~2025-11-21 09:05 PT, customer observed elevated streaming disconnects for chat completions in us-east.
- Impacted traffic was primarily streaming (SSE). Non-streaming responses were reported as “mostly OK” with intermittent latency.
- Public status page showed all components operational during the impact window; customer is asking why the incident was not communicated and requesting per-capability visibility (Streaming vs non-streaming).

Customer impact:
- Customer’s end users experienced partial responses / dropped connections while waiting for streamed tokens.
- Customer’s app retries increased significantly; they estimate ~6–10% of sessions required a user refresh.

Environment:
- Prod
- Region: us-east

Customer notes / evidence:
- “We see spike in `ERR_STREAM_CLOSED` / client disconnects between 09:05–09:40 PT. Status page stayed green; support macros told us to check status page first and it wasn’t helpful.”
- Example request details provided by customer (redacted): request_id prefixes `nb-9f2*`, `nb-a31*`.

Requested outcome:
1) Confirm whether Redwood had a known incident in us-east affecting streaming.
2) Clarify whether this should have been on the status page.
3) Provide guidance/workaround and expected prevention.
4) Improve status page granularity so streaming-only failures are communicated clearly.

Internal notes (initial triage):
- Likely a streaming-specific failure mode (disconnects at gateway or websocket/SSE path) that doesn’t manifest as elevated 5xx for non-streaming requests.
- Current public component grouping is too coarse (Hosted API rolled up), and current status signal is primarily error-rate based; streaming disconnect counters are not part of the status signal source-of-truth today.

[Progressive stream deceleration followed by silent cutoff during KV checkpointing on long chats]
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports streaming chat responses that gradually slow token delivery over ~10-40s and then stop without an explicit 5xx. The client eventually sees a socket close after its internal timeout. Impact: several long-running conversational sessions with >8k token histories for the customer experience silent pauses then disconnects.

Impact:
- Intermittent but reproducible for this customer on prod us-east-1 for long-context chats.
- Affects users on both web client and SDK behind corporate VPNs.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted API (prod) region us-east-1
- Customer uses enterprise tenant with Dedicated routing to shared pool
- Observed with redwood-1-large and gptx-like-13b model variants

steps_to_reproduce:
1) Start a streaming chat session via SSE with a long prompt/history (>8k tokens).
2) Continue a back-and-forth for several messages until total context length >~10k tokens.
3) Observe generated tokens streaming for ~20-60s; notice per-token latency creeping up from ~80ms to >600ms.
4) After a period of slow delivery there is a ~5-15s silence and then client-level socket close due to application timeout.
5) Repeat; issue occurs more frequently when autoscaling or worker compaction runs concurrently.

logs:
Selected logs/timestamps pulled from customer session (redacted):
- 2026-03-09T14:12:31.109Z request-id=req-9f8a stream-start tokens_sent=0
- 2026-03-09T14:12:39.194Z req-9f8a token-100 latency=85ms
- 2026-03-09T14:12:55.721Z req-9f8a token-600 latency=430ms
- 2026-03-09T14:13:05.102Z req-9f8a token-900 latency=780ms
- 2026-03-09T14:13:12.980Z WARN serving-runtime: starting kv-cache-checkpoint compaction (worker=wn-34)
- 2026-03-09T14:13:17.311Z req-9f8a stream-silence duration=12s client-timeout=15s
- 2026-03-09T14:13:29.872Z connection-closed by client socket-err=ECONNRESET
Diagnostic links:
- Console trace: https://console.redwood.ai/trace/req-9f8a
- Logs: https://logs.redwood.ai/query?request=req-9f8a

investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: progressive token latency tied to a backend compaction/checkpoint operation causing worker-side write stalls and backpressure that reduces token emission bandwidth. Edge proxy (Fastly/our edge) was also observed to coalesce small chunked responses occasionally resulting in silence from the client perspective.

What we checked:
- Worker traces show KV checkpoint tasks trigger within the same worker's scheduling window causing CPU spikes and brief network stall.
- No 5xx from runtime; stream remained open but tokens were not flushed to socket.
- Edge proxy config set to buffer up to 32KB per chunk for TLS reassembly; combined with client TCP delayed-ACKs on some VPNs, small incremental token chunks were coalesced into longer pauses.
- Autoscaler events correlated: new worker warmup and concurrent checkpoint compaction increased host load.

Hypotheses refined:
1) KV checkpoint compaction triggered synchronous writes/locks that inhibited async token flushes on affected workers.
2) Edge buffering + small chunk emission pattern created client-observable silence during those spikes.

Evidence supporting root cause:
- Correlation between 'starting kv-cache-checkpoint compaction' log and immediate latency spike to >500ms and then silence.
- Reproduced in a controlled staging run by forcing checkpoint compaction while streaming a long conversation; observed same token deceleration then silence.

comments:
2026-03-10 09:42 - Ana Patel (Support): Customer reported repeated occurrences after a long call at 08:30 UTC. Customer supplied session IDs and agreed to try a staging test with us.
2026-03-10 11:05 - Liam O'Connor (SRE): We reproduced the behavior in staging. When we trigger a KV checkpoint compaction on the same worker as the stream, token emission stalls though runtime does not return 5xx. Opening edge/worker traces now.
2026-03-10 15:22 - Priya Menon (Runtime Eng): Observed that checkpointing currently takes a CPU-bound path that can preempt token-flushing coroutine. Proposing: make checkpointing cooperative and add periodic non-token heartbeat writes to keep edge from coalescing.
2026-03-11 02:14 - Edge Team (Fastly integration): Confirmed edge config was set to coalesce small chunked writes. We prepared a config tweak to disable coalescing for API hostnames for an initial rollout.
2026-03-11 13:40 - LearnWave Labs (customer): Can confirm after our test with the patch we saw steady token flow and no disconnect for sessions that previously failed. Thanks!
2026-03-12 09:01 - Liam O'Connor (SRE): Deployed runtime change to make KV checkpoint compaction cooperative + added 5s keepalive token emission during long generations. Edge config updated to reduce chunk coalescing for streaming endpoints. Monitoring in progress.
2026-03-12 17:50 - Ana Patel (Support): Marking resolved after customer validation. Created postmortem page and follow-up task to add telemetry for checkpoint-stream interference.


resolution:
Fixes applied: 1) Runtime: checkpoint compaction reworked to use non-blocking cooperative coroutines and yield to token-flushing path. 2) Runtime: periodic keepalive SSE comment tokens emitted if no tokens for >4s. 3) Edge: disabled aggressive chunk coalescing for streaming endpoints. Rollout: staged to prod us-east-1 on 2026-03-12 08:00 UTC, monitored for 48 hours. Customer validated with long-context sessions; no reproductions afterward.

Follow-ups:
- Add a metric 'streaming-pauses-during-checkpoint' and alert if rate > 1/hr per tenant.
- Backfill mitigation to ensure dedicated pools run checkpointing on separate worker threads by default.
- Postmortem: https://confluence.redwood.ai/postmortems/SUP-846215-postmortem

notes_for_handback:
If customer reports recurrence: request affected request-id and timestamps; check worker for concurrent 'kv-cache-checkpoint' log entries; verify edge coalescing flags and runtime keepalive emission. Escalate to Runtime Eng and Edge team if pattern matches.

[Streaming chat sessions disconnect or stall mid-generation for users on intermittent mobile networks]
description:
Issue summary: Multiple customers (notably ByteFlow Analytics) report that SSE/WebSocket-based streaming chat responses either disconnect abruptly or stall indefinitely during mid-generation when the user is on spotty mobile networks. Impact: Partial responses are being delivered, the finalization event ("response.complete") is missing in many cases leading to client-side timeouts and retries. Several customers report increased error rates starting after the 2026-03-12 midnight UTC deploy to streaming-proxy. Environment: Production (us-west primary), affected across us-west and eu-central customers, primarily on circuits with high jitter and intermittent packet loss.

steps_to_reproduce:
1) Use the hosted chat API with streaming enabled (SSE or WebSocket) and model=redwood-chat-1.
2) Simulate an intermittent mobile network (high jitter, small packet loss) using network throttling (e.g., tc/netem or a mobile device with flaky signal).
3) Send a multi-paragraph prompt that triggers multi-chunk streaming (> 3 chunks).
4) Observe connection behavior and whether 'response.complete' or final event is received by client within expected timeframe.

observed_behavior:
Clients report connections either dropping with upstream errors (502/504) or streams freezing with no new events for >30s while server-side logs show partial chunk writes. In some cases the client eventually reconnects and receives duplicated tokens from server-side retries.

expected_behavior:
Streaming connections should deliver all chunks followed by a final completion event. On transient network blips the server should keep the stream alive long enough for client reconnection or gracefully terminate with a clear error so client can retry deterministically.
