[Intermittent WAN Degradation — Operator Runbook for Private Deployments]
Summary:\n\nThis runbook describes detection, mitigation, and post-incident steps for intermittent WAN degradation affecting Redwood Private deployments (VPC-connected or on-prem control plane bridges). It focuses on preserving SLOs, minimizing model-serving disruption, safe traffic steering, and safe rollback/upgrade behavior when WAN links fluctuate.\n\nScope:\n- Applies to private deployments with hybrid control planes (VPC+edge), air-gapped bridges, and VPC-peered tenant topologies.\n- Covers symptoms related to intermittent increased latency, packet loss, asymmetric routing, and short network partitions (seconds to minutes).\n- Not intended for full datacenter failure: see Disaster Recovery runbooks for regional failover.\n\nOwner & escalation:\n- Primary owner: eng-private-deployments / Field Operations (oncall: #pod-privops)\n- Secondary owner: eng-sre (oncall: #sre-oncall)\n- Pager: +1-555-0102 (privops)\n- If customer impact > 10% of tenant requests or SLA breach suspected, escalate to Engineering Manager (Elena Martinez) and Customer Success lead (Ravi Kumar).\n\nSLOs and impact thresholds (operational):\n- Healthy: control-plane request p95 <= 250 ms, tokenized inference p95 <= 400 ms.\n- Degraded: sustained >20% increase above baseline latency OR packet loss >3% for >= 60s.\n- Critical: sustained packet loss >10% or periodic disconnects causing >1% of requests to error for >= 5 min.\n\nSignals & detection (alarms):\n1) Automated alerts:\n   - Telemetry: control-plane RPC error-rate spike, model-serving tail-latency increase, and KV-cache miss storm.\n   - Network sensors: BGP flaps, interface errors, RTT jump, interface input errors.\n   - Ingest: increased retransmits and TLS session resets reported by edge proxies.\n2) Customer reports: elevated 5xx errors, streaming timeouts.\n3) Synthetic checks: cross-region / tenant health checks failing intermittently.\n\nImmediate triage checklist (first 10 minutes):\n1) Confirm alarm: check telemetry dashboards (Redwood Console -> Private Deployments -> Tenant X -> Latency & Errors).\n2) Verify scope: identify affected tenants, control-plane nodes, and AZs. Use redwood-ctl status --tenant <id> --scope network to list impacted routes.\n3) Capture artifacts:\n   - redwood-ctl trace capture --duration 120s --include=network,proxy,kv\n   - tcpdump on affected interface: sudo tcpdump -i <iface> -w /tmp/wan-issue.pcap (rotate after 2 min)\n4) Check provider signals: cloud provider network health dashboard, router BGP peer status, WAN provider NOC bulletins.\n\nTiered response (action matrix):\n- Tier 1 (Transient blips, <60s): monitor and annotate incident. Increase sampling on traces but avoid changing config.\n- Tier 2 (Degraded, 60s–10m): apply graceful traffic throttles and reroute noncritical traffic. Notify CS for impacted tenants.\n- Tier 3 (Critical, >10m or SLA risk): execute traffic steering to alternate control-plane region or enable degraded-mode serving. Consider controlled rollback of recent changes.\n\nImmediate mitigations (playbook):\n1) Reduce noisy background traffic:\n   - Apply egress rate limit for telemetry-heavy collectors to 20% of baseline: redwood-ctl policy apply --path /telemetry/ingest --egress-cap 20%\n   - Temporarily disable scheduled large-model preloads (model prefetch) via config flag: set config.model_prefetch=false for affected clusters.\n2) Prefer local inference paths:\n   - If model artifact exists locally on edge nodes, shift routing to local-only mode: redwood-ctl route set --tenant <id> --prefer-local true\n   - Confirm KV cache hits: redis-cli -h <kv-host> INFO and check keyspace hits/misses.\n3) Reroute control-plane to alternative region (safe fallback):\n   - Only for tenants with fallback allowed in config.json: if fallback_enabled == true then execute: redwood-ctl failover start --from-region A --to-region B --tenant <id>\n   - Use canary traffic percentage (start 5%) and watch error rates for 3 minutes.\n4) Switch to degraded-mode policy for latency-sensitive endpoints:\n   - Replace full response streaming with chunked summary responses (low-bandwidth fallback).\n\nSafe traffic steering checklist (detailed):\n1) Authorization & customer consent: verify tenant contract allows cross-region steer and notify CS with template (see templates section).\n2) Capacity check: ensure target region has at least 1.5x measured peak qps reserved for tenant during failover window. Use capacity query: redwood-ctl capacity query --region B --reserve 1.5x --tenant <id>\n3) Consistency considerations: model versions pinned? If target region runs a quantized variant, enable quality guardrail: redwood-ctl quality-check --model <model-id> --baseline <tenant-prompt-set>\n4) KV cache warmup: pre-warm top-1000 keys with redwood-ctl cache prewarm --keys-file top_keys.txt --region B\n5) Monitor: increase tracing to p100 sampling for the tenant during steer.\n\nModel-serving and KV cache considerations:\n- Avoid simultaneous model hot-swap during network instability. Hot-swap increases remote fetches and can amplify traffic.\n- If large model layers are fetched over WAN, defer model downloads; prefer fallback quantized variants located locally.\n- KV cache eviction policy: if eviction storms occur, throttle write-back via circuit breaker config: set config.kv.circuit_breaker_window=30s\n\nUpgrade & rollback safety guidance (when WAN is unreliable):\n- Postpone planned upgrades for control-plane or model hot-swap until link stability >= 30 min.\n- If an upgrade caused the issue: perform incremental rollforward to previous stable build per the orchestrated-rollforward-and-customer-safeguards playbook.\n- Rollback checklist:\n  1) Verify stored artifacts and signatures: gpg --verify <artifact>.sig <artifact>\n  2) Initiate controlled rollback targeting 10% of nodes as canary: redwood-ctl deploy rollback --target-percent 10 --reason \"WAN_degradation\"\n  3) Monitor service-level metrics for 5 minutes before widening.\n\nCustomer communication templates (shortened):\n- Initial alert (CS -> customer): \"We are investigating intermittent network disruptions affecting inference latency for your tenant. Our team has applied traffic isolation measures and will notify you with updates every 15 minutes.\"\n- Failover notification: \"We are proactively steering traffic to an alternative control plane in <region>. You may observe brief consistency artifacts for pinned model versions. Estimated mitigation time: 30–45 minutes.\"\n\nPost-incident actions (before incident close):\n1) Collect all artifacts: pcaps, redwood-ctl traces, probe results, BGP logs, provider tickets.\n2) Conduct a 30-min blameless incident review within 72 hours. Include: timeline, mitigation effectiveness, customer impact, and recommended preventive work.\n3) Recommended follow-ups (backlog items):\n   - Implement adaptive telemetry sampling to prevent noisy collectors from amplifying WAN saturation.\n   - Add health-check that tracks asymmetric packet loss and route divergence.\n   - Create automation to prewarm KV cache for tenants with fallback flags.\n\nRunbook validation tests (quarterly):\n- Synthetic scenario: inject 5% packet loss on control-plane interface for 5 minutes and validate:\n  - automated alert triggers,\n  - runbook mitigations complete without human-only steps within 10 minutes,\n  - customer notification template is sent by CS automation.\n- Chaos test: scheduled WAN flaps (BGP withdraw/announce) in staging for 3 AZs. Validate canary failover and rollback timeline.\n\nAppendix: sample troubleshooting commands and expected outputs:\n- Quick health checks:\n  - redwood-ctl status --verbose --tenant <id>\n  - curl -sS https://private-ctrl.<region>.internal/health | jq .\n  - iperf3 -c <peer> -t 10 (target throughput / latency)\n- Adjust iptables to drop 1% traffic for test: sudo tc qdisc add dev eth0 root netem loss 1%\n- Capture example edge proxy error: tail -n 200 /var/log/redwood/edge-proxy.log | grep \"upstream reset\"\n\nCustomer requirements summary (minimums for predictable private behavior):\n| Category | Minimum requirement | Rationale |\n|---|---|---|\n| WAN SLA | 99.95% with jitter < 30 ms p95 | Stable link reduces transient failovers |\n| Layer 2/3 MTU | 1450–9000 (consistent across path) | Avoids fragmentation for model artifact streaming |\n| BGP | Static or BGP with eBGP timers >= 3s and graceful restart | Prevents rapid flaps that trigger control-plane failover |\n| KMS latency | <= 150 ms p95 to KMS endpoints | Key operations should not be intermittently slow |\n| Local storage | 400 GB free on edge nodes (per model pool) | Allows local model replica and cache warmup |\n\nOwnership and contacts:\n- Field operator lead: Aisha Patel (aisha@redwood.ai)\n- SRE escalation: Mateo Rivera (mateo@redwood.ai)\n- Customer Success: Ravi Kumar (ravi@redwood.ai)\n- Playbook reviewers: Elena Martinez, Priya Singh\n\nRelated artifacts and links:\n- See: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/day-2-ops/kv-cache-consistency-chaos-validation-and-rollback-matrix-2028\n- See: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/deployment-guides/private-deploy-onboarding-and-failover-runbook-2026\n\nRevision history:\n- 2025-01-14: Created by Aisha Patel\n- 2025-06-12: Expanded steering checklist and added model-serving KV cache guidance (reviewers: Ravi Kumar, Elena Martinez)\n\nEnd of runbook.

[Contract Survivability and Degradation Test Plan]
Summary
This page defines the Contract Survivability and Degradation Test Plan: a standardized, automated validation and exercise suite for verifying that service contracts (API request/response schemas, streaming semantics, model-variant compatibility) survive realistic failure and degradation modes, and that graceful-degradation policies keep downstream applications safe.

Purpose and scope
- Purpose: Ensure changes to APIs, model variants, runtime kernels, or infra do not cause silent client breakage or unacceptable user-facing quality regressions when the platform degrades (capacity loss, quantization fallbacks, network partitions, high tail latency).
- Scope: Applies to: Redwood public REST/streaming API endpoints, model-serving runtime variants (fp16, int8, quantized kernels), routing/fallback policies, and platform-side contract transforms (stream chunking, partial result checkpointing). Excludes: third-party managed endpoints and external partner SDKs.

Key definitions
- Contract survivability: The ability of a client and service to continue to communicate successfully (with defined semantics) despite service degradation, version differences, or partial failures.
- Graceful degradation: Controlled reduction of service fidelity (e.g., shorter max tokens, fallback to smaller model, send partial results) instead of outright failures.
- Degradation threshold: A measurable limit (latency, error rate, quality metric) that triggers a degradation policy.

Goals and non-goals
- Goals:
  1) Provide a runnable test matrix that exercises all supported compatibility modes and failure profiles.
  2) Verify observability coverage (telemetry, logs, traces) for each degraded path.
  3) Declare pass/fail criteria tied to SLOs, quality delta limits, and error budgets.
  4) Integrate tests into CI gating and canary pipelines for releases and infra upgrades.
- Non-goals: This document does not specify model retraining, per-customer contractual SLAs, or security certification steps.

Test strategy overview
- Three layers of validation:
  1) Contract unit checks: static schema validation + golden response matching. Fast, runs on PR.
  2) Survivability scenarios: synthetic fault injection (GPU drain, quantization fallback, kernel failover, partial KV cache loss) executed in staging clusters. Medium time-to-run.
  3) Degradation chaos+load: long-running experiments under realistic traffic mixes (chat, embeddings, reranking) to measure quality drift, latency tail behavior, and cascading effects.

Compatibility and test matrix
- Dimensions to cover (matrix columns): client API version, streaming vs non-streaming, response schema version, model binary variant (float16, int8, bfloat16), kernel family, region, and tenant isolation mode (hosted/dedicated/private).
- Example matrix rows (textual table):
  | Scenario | Client v1 | Streaming | Model var | Kernel | Failure injected | Expected survival behavior |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | Short-circuit fallback | v1 | streaming | fp16 -> int8 | fused-attn-v2 | quantize fallback during generation | Continue streaming with truncated tokens + warning header |
  | Partial KV loss | v2 | non-stream | bfloat16 | kv-cache-v1 | KV cache eviction on half of shards | Fall back to recompute prefix with <=30% latency penalty; maintain correctness |

Pass/fail criteria and thresholds
- Latency SLOs (staging baseline vs experiment):
  - 50th percentile: not > 1.25x baseline
  - 95th percentile: not > 1.5x baseline
  - 99th percentile: not > 2.0x baseline or absolute 5s (whichever is lower)
- Error budget and rates:
  - Service errors (5xx): experiment must not exceed 0.2% absolute increase over baseline in a 30-minute window.
  - Client-visible schema errors: zero tolerated for contract-major-mode changes.
- Quality delta (for generative outputs):
  - Automated evals on canary prompt set: BLEU/ROUGE/Hallucination proxy delta must be <= 5% relative degradation for critical prompt subset; for non-critical prompts allow up to 10% with explicit stakeholder signoff.
- Observability completeness:
  - All degradations must emit a structured event: event_type=degradation_experiment, failure_mode, affected_model_variant, request_id. Missing events are a hard fail.

Test cases (representative)
1) Quantize-Fallback-Stream-Test
Preconditions: staging cluster with both fp16 and int8 model families deployed behind routing policy.
Steps:
   1. Start a 10-min steady streaming workload (chat prompts at 50 req/s) using streaming client v1.
   2. Mid-run, trigger quantization fallback by toggling node-level kernel preference (simulate degraded GPU memory).
   3. Monitor stream continuity, chunking headers, and final truncation messages.
   Expected result: clients receive valid stream chunks, final message contains a header 'x-degradation-warning: quantize-fallback' and token truncation does not exceed configured limit (default: 128 tokens).

2) KV-Cache-Partial-Evict-Test
Preconditions: KV cache warm with repeated prefix workloads.
Steps:
   1. Run synthetic repeat-prefix traffic at 200 rps for 20 minutes.
   2. Evict KV cache on 40% of serving shards.
   3. Measure latency delta and validate correctness via deterministic checksum of first 64 tokens on a reserved prompt set.
   Expected result: deterministic checksum match, p95 latency within threshold, eviction logged per-shard.

3) Streaming-Edge-Chunk-Reassembly
Steps:
   1. Induce network jitter and drop 1 in 50 stream packets at the edge proxy.
   2. Verify client resume semantics: partial-result-checkpointing token offsets allow resumption without reissuing entire prompt.
   Expected: successful resume in <= 2s and no duplicate tokens.

Automation and CI integration
- Unit contract checks: run as part of PR pipeline via 'make contract-unit-checks'. Fail fast.
- Survivability smoke: nightly GitHub Action suite running core scenarios (quantize fallback, KV eviction) against ephemeral staging clusters. Tag results and publish to the release dashboard.
- Release gating: any change to routing/fallback policy or kernel family must run the full survivability scenarios in the release canary phase. A failed scenario blocks rollout by automated policy in the deployment pipeline.

CI snippets and examples
- Example CI job (YAML):
  jobs:
    survivability-smoke:
      runs-on: ubuntu-latest
      steps:
        - name: Run quantize fallback smoke
          run: ./tools/survive/run_quantize_smoke.sh --cluster staging --duration 600

- Example curl for schema validation (non-streaming):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
    -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" 
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
    -d '{"model":"rwd-7b-fp16","prompt":"What is the capital of France?","max_tokens":32}'

Observability and telemetry requirements
- Telemetry events must include the following structured fields: service, request_id, client_version, model_variant, kernel_family, failure_mode, degradation_policy, latency_ms, snippet_hash.
- Trace spans: experiments must produce a top-level span named 'degradation-experiment' that includes child spans for 'routing', 'cache-lookup', 'kernel-select', and 'fallback-action'.
- Dashboards and alerts: Create a dedicated dashboard 'Contract Survivability' with panels: p95 latency by scenario, quality-delta heatmap, structured event rate by failure_mode. Alert rules: when structured event missing for >10 runs raise severity P2.

Rollout, canaries and rollback policy
- Canary policy for runtime/kernel changes:
  - Stage 1 (micro-canary): 0.1% traffic, run contract unit checks and survivability smoke for 30 minutes.
  - Stage 2 (regional canary): 2% traffic for 2 hours, run degradation chaos tests in parallel.
  - Stage 3 (ramped): 10% for 24 hours, monitor quality delta and SLOs.
- Automatic rollback triggers:
  - p95 latency > 1.5x baseline AND p99 > 2.0x baseline for 5 consecutive minutes.
  - Any client-visible schema error for requests in the canary cohort.

Ownership and runbooks
- Test harness owners: Eng QA (primary), Eng Serving Runtime (secondary).
- On-call escalation: If a gating test fails during a release, pager to runtime-oncall team with tag 'survivability-block'.
- Runbook pointers:
  - /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/eviction-and-recoveries
  - /confluence/eng-infra/gpu-fleet-and-capacity/gpu-node-autoscaling-eviction-playbook-2026

Appendix: example evaluation config (YAML snippet)
- prompts_file: 'canary_prompts_v2.txt'
- metrics:
  - name: p95_latency_ms
    threshold: 1500
  - name: quality_delta_pct
    threshold: 5
- failure_modes: ['quantize_fallback','kv_evict','network_jitter']
- run_duration_minutes: 30

Change history and review notes
- 2025-11-06: initial draft authored by Priya Natarajan.
- 2025-12-10: added automated gating rules and CI job examples (review by Carlos Mendez).
- 2026-02-14: expanded observability fields and added rollback triggers (approved by Asha Rao).

References and related guidance
- See: request-fanout-attenuation-and-resilience-guardrails-2026 (performance standards).
- See: model-slicing-and-fallback-routing-guidelines-2026 (model-serving standards).
- See: sequence-length-aware-kernel-selection-guidelines-2026 (runtime architecture).

Contact
- For questions or runbook updates, contact: priya.natarajan@redwood.ai or the eng-qa Slack channel (#eng-qa).

[Mini-bundle PRD: Unified inference surface for chat, completion, embeddings, and rerank with launch surge plan]
description:
High-level PRD to deliver a compact, production-ready 'mini-bundle' that exposes a consistent API surface for chat, completion, embeddings, and rerank use cases. The intent is to offer a single onboarding flow, one billing SKU with per-route knobs, and an operational surge/rollback plan for launch day. This ticket scopes the product requirements, acceptance criteria, risks, and a tactical launch checklist for a targeted GA to early enterprise customers.

background:
We have multiple Large PRDs covering the full hosted API family. This effort is a deliberately constrained bundle (MVP) to speed time-to-value for teams that need a single integration covering the most common patterns: single-turn generation, chat turn sequences, vector embedding generation, and rerank scoring pipelines. Key differences from larger PRDs: tighter acceptance gates, explicit surge controls, and a built-in sampling quality monitor tied to rollout gates.

goals:
Deliver a single, documented API path that supports chat, completion, embeddings, and rerank with consistent authentication and billing
Provide per-route configuration: max_tokens, temperature, top_p, embedding_model, rerank_model and deterministic fallback mapping
Define launch operational plan that prevents capacity overload via adaptive throttles and a tiered fallback to smaller models/regions
Ship a monitoring plan that samples 0.5% of responses for quality evaluation and flags regression against a baseline prompt set

non_goals:
Full multi-modal support (images/audio) in this mini-bundle
Advanced model orchestration policies (A/B weighted routing across unlimited variants) beyond simple canary and fallback
Enterprise-only Dedicated capacity contracts — this targets hosted tier first

requirements:
API: Single endpoint group /v1/inference with mode param: {mode: "chat|completion|embedding|rerank"}
SDKs: Expose identical surface in SDKs (python/js) with clear defaults and per-route overrides
Billing: One SKU 'mini_bundle' with per-token generation and per-embedding unit rates; explicit metering for rerank scoring calls
Routing: Support region preference and a fallback route list; fallback must preserve response semantics within 95% of acceptance tests
Rate limits & quotas: Configurable per-tenant soft-limit + hard-limit; a surge policy that reduces batch size and routes to fallback models under sustained queue growth
Observability: Token-level cost, per-request latency, sample payloads (0.5%), and a regression alert if sampled quality score drops by >= 6% vs baseline
Security/compliance: All requests logged with request_id and redaction rules; ensure KMS integration for customer-managed keys is documented for Private later

acceptance_criteria:
API contract: OpenAPI entry and SDK surfaces pass contract linting and automated smoke tests
Functional tests: Chat single-turn and multi-turn (3 turns) acceptance suite passes with stability >= 99% over 24h soak
Embedding parity: Embedding model produces vectors within 2% cosine similarity of reference embedding for canonical dataset
Rerank correctness: Top-1 rerank precision on benchmark set >= 88% and latency P95 <= 220ms in hosted region
Billing validation: Billing meter events emitted for every request type and aggregated values match simulated invoice within 0.5%
Safety & redaction: Automated PII redaction hooks exercised and verified in 1000 sample requests
Surge behavior: Under load test (2x expected QPS sustained for 30m) the system enforces surge throttle and fallback route within 60s, with successful degradation behavior (no unhandled 5xx spikes >0.5%)
Canary and rollback: Canary cohort (5% traffic) does not regress metrics for 4 consecutive hours, otherwise automatic rollback to previous model happens
Docs & quickstart: Console quickstart, API docs, and example notebooks present and validated by Solutions Engineering

out_of_scope:
Dedicated capacity provisioning flows for this mini-bundle (handled by Dedicated roadmap)
Customer-managed on-prem installation in GA (Private flagged for later cycle)
Complex retraining/inference pipelines or multi-stage retrieval chains — only single call rerank is supported

dependencies:
ENG-22111 (runtime: per-request sampling and trace IDs)
ENG-23780 (billing: embed per-unit meter events)
ENG-24451 (routing: fallback policy primitives)
DES-1987 (docs: quickstart and SDK examples)
PM-582300 (safety: redaction and PII policy)

risks:
Surge underestimation: underestimated launch demand could exhaust GPU pools; mitigated by conservative initial quota and manual surge escalation playbook
Quality regressions due to fallback: cheaper fallback models may produce unacceptable outputs — sampled quality monitor and rollback gates required
Billing mismatch: complexity in metering different call types could produce unexpected invoices for customers; bill validation harness required
Docs/UX confusion: single endpoint with mode param may be confusing; provide strong examples and per-mode templates in SDKs

metrics:
Adoption: number of unique tenants calling mini_bundle endpoint in first 30 days
Latency: P95 latency for each mode (chat/completion/embedding/rerank)
Quality: sampled quality score delta vs baseline prompt set (daily)
Cost: average cost-per-1k-token and per-embedding unit by workload
Reliability: % requests successful (2xx) and 5xx rate under load
Billing accuracy: variance between simulated invoice and production invoices

rollout_plan:
Phase 0 (internal): SDK + API + docs internal preview with Redwood teams only
Phase 1 (alpha): Invite 5 strategic customers, conservative quotas, 1-week canary; active SRE monitoring and daily review
Phase 2 (beta): Open to self-serve signups with default quotas lowered and surge protections enabled; monitor for two weeks
Phase 3 (GA): Full listing in Console, marketing announcement, quotas increased per usage tiers with sustained SLOs

launch_checklist:
Create OpenAPI spec and publish to docs site
SDK releases (python/js) with example notebooks and unit tests
Billing hooks validated end-to-end with sandbox tenants
SRE runbook: surge playbook, escalation matrix, rollback steps
Monitoring dashboards: latency/cost/quality panels configured and alerted
Canary configuration: 5% routing rule and automated rollback triggers
Legal/safety signoff: PII redaction validated and incident response contact added
Support training: playbook and FAQ created for Support and Solutions Engineering
Runload tests: 2x expected QPS sustained 30m without >0.5% 5xx spikes
Smoke tests: end-to-end quickstart validated by two different engineers

engineering_notes:
Runtime changes required: per-request sampling hook, fallback routing semantics, and surge throttle metrics. Engineering should run an extended 24h soak test on staging with realistic prompt distributions supplied by Solutions Engineering. Coordinate with billing team to ensure meter event shapes are stable before SDK GA.

qa_plan:
Automated acceptance suites for each mode, plus 24h soak and the surge scenario test. QA to validate sampled quality pipeline and alerting. Manual regression checklist for SDK examples and docs. Use a reserved test tenant for billing validation.

[Reranker: precision regression harness for FP8/INT8 quant profiles]
description:
Goal: build a repeatable regression harness to validate FP8 and INT8 quantization profiles for the reranker model family and ensure ranking quality (NDCG/MRR) stays within the allowed regression budget. This ticket covers dataset partitioning, calibration procedure automation, deterministic seeding, post-quant noise profiling, and the first pass of acceptance thresholds.

Scope:
- Implement calibration workflow standardization (per-layer scale saving, calibration seeds, minibatch jitter).
- Add a stratified holdout query set for stability checks: head/long-tail/rare intents.
- Add post-quant diagnostics: per-query delta logs, KL divergence of logits, and per-layer activation drift.
- Run baseline fp32 vs INT8 vs FP8 across three calibration strategies: static (min-max), KL-based, and dynamic per-batch scaling.
- Publish results to the eval dashboard and produce an artifacts bundle with calibration mats for reproducibility.

Non-goals: Retraining or weight clipping strategies (will be separate spike).

Why this is necessary: Recent customer reports show occasional top-1 mismatches after the INT8 rollout on small but critical enterprise corpora. We need an automated, auditable process that surfaces regressions early and ties them to calibration profile decisions so Platform/SEs can pick safe defaults for Dedicated/Private deployments.

acceptance_criteria:
A reproducible harness (run script) that accepts model artifact, quant profile, and calibration recipe and emits NDCG@3,NDCG@10,MRR@1,MRR@5 with CI
Regression budget defined: max -0.5% absolute NDCG@10 or -1.0% relative MRR@1 compared to fp32 baseline (unless approved by PM)
Stored calibration metadata for each run (per-layer scales, calibration seed, minibatch order) saved to artifacts bucket and referenced in dashboard
Diagnostic pages added to internal dashboard: per-query delta sample, per-layer activation drift heatmap, and top-10 changed queries with diffs
Automation integrated with CI: any PR that changes quantization pipeline triggers the harness on a sampled commit and posts results to PR as a comment

test_plan:
Create stratified eval splits from prod-query-v2 (head/medium/tail) and synthetic perturbation set for robustness checks.
Run fp32 baseline (deterministic seed 20260310) across all folds to compute baseline metrics.
Quantize with INT8 and FP8 using three calibration recipes; capture per-layer scales and store calibration vectors.
Compute NDCG@3, NDCG@10, MRR@1, MRR@5 and per-query delta; aggregate CI with bootstrapping (1000 resamples).
Run post-quant noise profiling: measure KL(logits_fp32 || logits_quant) and activation drift per-layer for failure analysis.

initial_results:
Baseline fp32 (prod-query-v2): NDCG@10=0.6421, NDCG@3=0.6045, MRR@1=0.482, MRR@5=0.611
INT8 (KL-calib): NDCG@10=0.6398 (-0.0023 abs), NDCG@3=0.6012, MRR@1=0.480 (-0.002)
FP8 (dynamic per-batch): NDCG@10=0.6312 (-0.0109 abs), NDCG@3=0.593, MRR@1=0.473 (-0.009)
Notes: FP8 run shows regression beyond budget on tail queries; per-layer activation drift concentrated on layers 8-11.

risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: Calibration nondeterminism across GPUs leading to flakiness. Mitigation: enforce deterministic seeding, pin cuDNN flags, and capture minibatch order in artifacts.
Risk: Small head queries mask tail regressions. Mitigation: require stratified reporting and separate pass for tail-focused thresholds.
Risk: CI cost explosion if full harness runs on every PR. Mitigation: sample commits for nightly full-run and fast path (smoke) on PRs using representative shard.

[Hosted API: Multi-lane rollout PRD + Acceptance & Launch Checklist (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank)]
description:
Purpose: Define the product requirements, acceptance criteria, testing harness and step-by-step launch checklist for shipping a converged hosted inference surface covering chat, completions, embeddings and rerank. This ticket focuses on a multi-lane rollout model (latency-sensitive, cost-optimized, and fallback lanes) plus a synthetic acceptance harness to detect regressions by workload slice prior to progressive traffic shaping.

problem_statement:
Customers need predictable behavioral and performance guarantees when migrating to the unified hosted surface. Historically, quality regressions and hidden latency/cost spikes occur only after broad launch. We must provide a deterministic acceptance path so that model, runtime, and shaping changes can be validated per-lane before ramping to production traffic.

goals:
Define contract and behavioral surface for chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank endpoints (stable request/response fields).
Create lane definitions: low-latency (SLO 150ms P95 gen token), balanced, and cost-optimized (quantized) lanes with clear mapping rules.
Deliver an automated acceptance harness that runs golden prompts + stratified synthetic load across lanes.
Ship a launch checklist for staged rollout with canary %, rollback criteria and telemetry dashboards.

non_goals:
Not covering non-hosted/private deployments (Private/VPC).
Not standardizing internal model weight compatibility—model adapters handled by research onboarding doc.

api_contract_summary:
Unified endpoint family: /v1/inference/{mode} where mode in {chat, completion, embedding, rerank}. Requests include client_metadata, prompt/pair inputs, lane_hint optional header. Responses include output.tokens, structured.metadata.{latency, model_variant, quantization}, and quality_score when available. Backwards-compatible: v1 clients continue to function; new structured.metadata fields are additive.

lane_definitions:
low-latency: pinned high-priority queue, higher cost model families, target P95 token time <= 150ms for typical 256-token sequences.
balanced: default lane for general traffic, target P95 <= 300ms for 256-token sequences, optimized batching enabled.
cost-optimized: quantized models and heavy batching allowed, target throughput for embeddings 10k/sec per GPU and best-effort latency.

acceptance_criteria:
Functional: All endpoints respond with expected schema under smoke tests (chat/completion/embedding/rerank) and structured.metadata fields present.
Behavioral: Golden-prompt intent parity — top-1 intent match >= 98% vs baseline for chat; embedding cosine similarity mean >= 0.995 vs baseline embedding model on seeded corpus.
Performance: Per-lane latency SLOs met in synthetic profiles for 95th and 99th percentiles (thresholds documented in lane_definitions).
Cost: Cost-per-token for cost-optimized lane not exceed 0.8x current baseline when using suggested quantization profiles.
Stability: No increase in 5xx rate > 0.05% above baseline during a 30-minute full-suite acceptance run.
Safety: Safety filter throughput verified; no safety-rules false-positive increase > 1% on curated safety testset.
Operational: Telemetry emits per-request lane routing tag, model_variant, kernel_profile_id, and kv_cache_hit boolean; console dashboard populated and validated.
Security: SSO/Role-based access enforced for launch ops; audit logs present for production cutover events.

testing_plan:
Acceptance harness: nightly synthetic suite combining golden-prompts, adversarial prompts, and regionally-distributed traffic emulation.
Load profiles: small (10rps), medium (200rps), canary (1% gradual increase to 10%), and soak (8 hours at expected peak) across lanes.
Quality regression detection: automated diff report (semantic and token-level) vs baseline with alerts on >1% regression signals.
Integration tests: End-to-end with SDKs (python/js), streaming and function-call paths verified.
Chaos tests: network partition, node preemption and kernel-fallback scenarios executed in a staging ring.

rollout_plan:
Pre-launch: complete acceptance harness run in staging, sign-off from Eng, SRE, and Trust teams.
Phase 0 (Canary): 0.1% of production traffic for 1 hour -> verify 5xx, latency, quality metrics.
Phase 1: 1% traffic for 3 hours -> validate per-lane distributions and cost metrics.
Phase 2: 10% traffic for 12 hours -> monitor edge cases and multi-region failover.
Phase 3: 50% traffic for 24 hours -> readiness gate for GA.
GA: 100% rollout with ongoing monitoring and auto-rollback triggers enabled.

rollback_triggers:
Any 5xx spike > 1.0% sustained for 5 minutes.
P95 latency > lane threshold for 10 minutes with underlying kernel-level errors.
Quality regression alerts: top-1 intent mismatch > 2% over a 1-hour window for chat endpoints.
Customer-facing errors (SEV2/SEV1) reported by support during canary window.

observability_requirements:
Per-route dashboards: token-latency histograms, KV cache hit rate, batching efficiency, and model_variant breakdown.
Alerting: SLO burn rate alerts for each lane; anomaly detection for sudden quality metric drift.
Tracing: distributed traces must carry lane_hint and kernel_profile_id for root-cause analysis.
Retention: 30-day retention for request-level telemetry in staging; 90-day for production aggregated metrics.

risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: Hidden quality regressions when switching model_variant in cost-optimized lane. Mitigation: pairing quantized candidate with golden-prompt regression gates and canary only on background traffic first.
Risk: Increased tail latency under batching heuristics. Mitigation: introduce adaptive micro-batching cap and experiment toggle in runtime that can be switched off per-lane.
Risk: Telemetry gaps at high throughput. Mitigation: sampled request tracing plus synthetic probes and end-to-end e2e checks.

acceptance_checklist:
Acceptance harness green for all lanes (smoke + golden prompts + load).
End-to-end SDK smoke tests merged and passing (python/js).
Telemetry dashboards created and validated with synthetic probes.
Security review completed and RBAC enforced for launch ops.
Release notes drafted and customer migration guide written.
Support runbook and rollback playbook published in Confluence.
GA launch cutover window scheduled and stakeholders notified.

Eng: finish adaptive micro-batching toggle by 2026-03-20 (owner: Priya Rao).
SRE: run 8-hour regional soak in staging with acceptance harness by 2026-03-25 (owner: Jordan Kim).
PM: finalize migration guide and announce beta to pilot customers by 2026-03-28.

post_launch_checks:
24h post-GA: verify SLOs and burn rates across all regions.
72h post-GA: run manual spot-checks on golden prompt set and customer-reported examples.
30d post-GA: collect cost metrics vs projected and publish retrospective.

[Unified Inference API PRD: Chat/Completions/Embeddings/Rerank + Launch Readiness Playbook]
Summary:
This PRD defines a single, unified Inference API surface that consolidates chat, completions, embeddings, and reranking into a coherent developer experience for the hosted product. The goal is to launch an opinionated, backwards-compatible API that enables low-friction migration from existing endpoints and supports robust production characteristics: predictable latency, cost controls, versioning, and observability.

Goals (what success looks like):
- Self-serve onboarding for common use cases (chat, single-turn completion, bulk embeddings, rerank pipelines) with <200ms p50 generation for short messages on verified models.
- Clear migration path from older endpoints with minimal client change (compat shims where needed).
- Launch checklist completed: SDKs, docs, console routing, SLOs, rollout gating, and security review.
- No high-severity production regressions in the first 30 days post-launch.

Scope:
In-scope:
- API surface: /v1/infer/chat, /v1/infer/completions, /v1/infer/embeddings, /v1/infer/rerank. Unified auth and usage metering.
- Streaming support for chat/completions.
- Batch endpoints for embeddings (bulk mode) and rerank (candidate list input).
- Structured output options (format enforcement + schema validation hooks).
- Model pinning and version field in request.
- Default fallback routing policies (model family fallback + graceful degradation).
- Console onboarding flow, token-level cost breakdown, and per-route dashboards.
Out-of-scope for initial launch:
- Dedicated/Dedicated-only features (reserved capacity UI flows).
- On-prem installer packaging.
- Advanced auto-quantization recommendations in Optimize (will be part of later cycle).

Requirements (high-level):
1) API Design and Backwards Compatibility- Single auth token; same rate limit counters as existing hosted API but configurable by billing tier.
- Query parameters: model, version, temperature, top_p, max_tokens, stream=true/false, response_schema, deterministic_hint.
- Error semantics compatible with existing OpenAPI-based encoding with addition of clear retryable vs non-retryable codes for fallback routing.

2) Chat/Completions Behavior- Chat supports role-delimited messages with optional function-calling spec.
- System messages allowed and preserved by default; early warning if system messages exceed token budget.
- Streaming must emit deltas consistent with token boundaries, include metadata frames for model_version and kv_cache_hit (when provided by runtime).

3) Embeddings- Bulk embedding endpoint supports up to 4096 inputs per request; response order must match input order.
- Metadata: model name, dimension, latency_ms and cost_estimate fields in meta.
- Provide distance metric param: cosine | dot | l2 for returned vectors (default cosine).

4) Rerank- Accepts list of candidates and query; returns ordered candidate ids with score and optional logit_breakdown.
- Support two operational modes: score-only and score+rescore (returns regenerated short passage if requested).

5) Performance and Operational- Runtime should support prefix/KV caching with transparent hints from client for repeated context.
- Autoscaling policies for hosted capacity to keep P90 latency within target under expected traffic shape.

6) Observability & Rollout- Per-route SLOs, token-level cost metrics, anomaly alerts for quality regressions (integrates with evals harness).

Trade-offs and decisions so far:
- We will not attempt 1:1 API parity with external vendors; we provide a compatibility layer for the most common OpenAI-compatible fields and map the rest to Redwood primitives. This reduces launch complexity.
- Streaming frames will carry minimal metadata to avoid bloating the stream; additional diagnostics available via console trace logs.
- We will enable the structured-output enforcement opt-in instead of opt-out to reduce risk of breaking existing clients.

Acceptance criteria (must be satisfied before "In Review" -> "Planned" gating to dev):
AC-1: Spec published and reviewed in RFC with SDK teams and infra -- sign-off from SDK lead and Runtime lead.
AC-2: End-to-end happy path for each surface (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank) covered by integration tests against staging models and passes in nightly CI.
AC-3: SDKs (Node/Python/Go) implement the new endpoints, with examples and migration guide included in docs.
AC-4: Console pages for per-route latency/cost and rollout control exist and linked from PRD.
AC-5: SLOs defined and alerting configured; runbooks created for common incidents (rate limiting, model OOM, fallback faults).
AC-6: Security review passed and KMS integration validated for logs containing sensitive prompt data (masking + retention policy).
AC-7: Load test demonstrates required throughput and keeps error rates below 0.5% at expected peak load for each route.

API Contract Summary (developer-facing snippet):
- POST /v1/infer/chat
  body: {"model": "string", "version": "string", "messages": [{"role":"system|user|assistant","content":"string"}], "max_tokens":int, "stream":bool, "response_schema":object?} -> stream|json response with {choices:[{message, finish_reason}], meta:{model_version, latency_ms}}
- POST /v1/infer/completions
  body: {prompt(s), model, params...} -> streaming json chunking or batched completions array
- POST /v1/infer/embeddings
  body: {inputs:[string], model, metric:"cosine"} -> {data:[{embedding:[], input_index}], meta:{dimension, latency_ms}}
- POST /v1/infer/rerank
  body: {query, candidates:[{id, text}], mode:"score|rescore"} -> {ranked:[{id,score,explanation?}], meta:{latency_ms}}

Rollout and Launch Plan:
- Canary rollout (Week 0): 5% traffic to unified API via routing rules; smoke tests and integration checks run every 5 minutes.
- Gradual ramp (Week 1): 5% -> 25% -> 50%, each step gated by success criteria (P50/P90 latency, error rates, and quality evals on sampled prompts).
- Full switch (Week 2): remaining traffic migrated with immediate fallback rules to previous endpoints for >2x latency or >1% error rate.
- Post-launch monitoring (30 days): daily quality checks vs baseline eval set; automated alerts on quality regressions.

Launch Checklist (owner initials in parentheses):
- API spec finalized and published (EP)
- SDKs released with migration guide (OC)
- Console routes & dashboards created and linked (PM)
- Billing mapping and quota config validated (Finance/BI)
- E2E tests and load tests passing in staging (ENG)
- Security review + KMS verification complete (Sec)
- Runbooks and on-call rotations updated (SRE)
- Docs: quickstarts, migration guide, changelog (DX)
- Advertising/announce plan and support playbook (GTM)

Dependencies:
- Runtime: prefix/KV cache telemetry extension (ENG-3777)
- SDK: streaming protocol support for Go (SDK-219)
- Observability: tokenized cost pipeline instrumentation (OBS-112)

Risks & Mitigations:
- Risk: Regression in output quality when using fallback model variants. Mitigation: automated evals against critical prompt set and pessimistic fallback ordering; roll back quickly if regression > 5% in precision metrics.
- Risk: Increased cost from unbounded embeddings bulk jobs. Mitigation: per-request quotas, rate limiting, and warning headers for heavy jobs.
- Risk: Streaming edge cases across proxies. Mitigation: add non-streamed fallback path and streaming health checks in the console.

Open Questions (to resolve before full rollout):
- Should the reranker accept raw HTML in candidate texts or do we require sanitized plain text?
- What is the deprecation window for legacy endpoints after full switch? Proposed: 90 days with migration metrics.

- Staging runbook: https://drive.redwood.ai/f/staging-unified-infer
- SDK tickets: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues?q=unified-infer

Next steps:
- Finish API review with SDK + Runtime leads by 2026-03-21 (owner: EP).
- Schedule security review completion by 2026-03-28 (owner: Sec).
- Start canary rollout dry-run in staging 2026-03-30 (owner: SRE).

[Consolidated eval-driven acceptance and launch checklist for unified generation & retrieval endpoints]
description:
Purpose: Produce a single PRD-grade acceptance and launch playbook that verifies behavioral fidelity, latency/cost SLOs, and operational readiness for chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank endpoints. Focus is on evaluation-driven acceptance using curated prompt sets, automated quality gating, canary thresholds and rollout heuristics. This ticket collects requirements, defines pass/fail criteria, and lists the launch checklist items required for go/no-go. Non-goal: this ticket does not implement model-level tuning or replace model onboarding flow; it defines the acceptance gates for the hosted API surface only.

scope:
Include: chat (chat-completions semantics), completions (stateless prompt->text), embeddings, rerank (scoring/rerank API). Deliverables: PRD acceptance criteria, curated prompt/benchmark sets, automated smoke-tests and CI job, canary rollout thresholds, operator runbook and rollback steps, dashboard panels. Exclude: private/Dedicated-specific infra changes, billing contract adjustments, OSS SDK changes (those are separate tickets).

non_goals:
1) No model retraining or dataset creation. 2) No changes to customer-facing SDK semantics. 3) No on-prem deployment packaging in this ticket.

requirements:
Behavioral acceptance harness: shareable prompt sets covering 500+ edge cases per surface (generation hallucination checks, instruction-following, safety prompts, paraphrase resilience).
Quality metrics: define pass threshold for semantic similarity (embeddings), top-1 rerank NDCG@10 baseline, generation exact match + acceptability ratios. Each threshold must be tied to a baseline model version.
Performance SLOs: p95 latency targets per endpoint for default config (chat: 200ms token latency, completions: 120ms token latency, embeddings: 50ms per vector, rerank: 150ms per request).
Cost guardrails: median token unit cost must be within 15% of current production profile for model families on the hosted lane.
Telemetry: structured event schema for request/response, prompt fingerprint, model-family tag, KV-cache hit metric, batching size distribution.
Operational: alert thresholds for error-rate, tail-latency, model-degraded-quality regressions (as measured by eval harness).
Rollout policy: scripted canary with 3-stage rollout (internal <5%, partner beta 5-20%, global >=60%) with automatic pause on metric breach.
Backfill: migration notes and SDK compatibility checks for customers using legacy endpoints; deprecation windows documented.

acceptance_criteria:
PRD acceptance harness committed to repo: /repos/internal/pm/acceptance-harness with readme and usage instructions.
Quality: For each endpoint run the curated prompt set and meet thresholds vs baseline model (see links). Failure modes documented and triaged before go/no-go.
SLOs: p50/p95 latency tests executed across regions and recorded in dashboard. No more than 1 region may exceed p95 target by 20% during canary for go decision.
Reliability: system error-rate <0.5% for successful canary traffic over 24 hours. Any burst errors automatically rollback policy triggers.
Regression alarms: automated daily eval comparing new model/version to baseline; if quality delta >5% for critical prompts, block rollout.
Security & compliance: security review completed and KMS integration validated for request logs; audit log test vectors executed.
Observability: dashboard panels (cost/latency/error/quality) visible in Console and linked in playbook; alert runbook steps present.
Operator runbook: manual rollback steps + reheating cache instructions + escalation contacts present and validated in a tabletop run.

per_endpoint_acceptance:
Chat: sample-conversations suite (1200 cases) executed; expected instruction-following rate >= 95% and hallucination flag rate <= baseline + 2%. Must pass streaming sanity tests (chunk continuity, token ordering).
Completions: completion-length distribution checks and stop-sequence reliability tests. Determinism sampling smoke (seeded runs) must remain within acceptable variance.
Embeddings: embedding cosine baseline stability test (anchor-centroid variance < 0.02) and retrieval recall sweep using 10k test items; average recall@100 must not drop more than 3% vs baseline.
Rerank: NDCG@10 measured on standard query set (2k queries) and synthetic adversarial queries; must exceed baseline by tolerance or show no more than 2% degradation on critical queries.

rollout_plan:
Stage 0: Internal canary (incubate) - 1% internal traffic for 24h: smoke tests and ops drills. Metrics tracked in real-time dashboard.
Stage 1: Partner beta - 5-20% traffic with selected partners for 72h, include end-to-end billing and contract checks.
Stage 2: Regional ramp - sequentially open regions (US-East -> US-West -> EU) with 6h observation windows between steps.
Stage 3: Global ramp with automated progressive traffic increase up to 100% over 48h with final stability window of 7 days.
Auto-pause: if any of the following triggers occur during ramp - error-rate spike >1% delta, p95 latency >200% of target, quality regression >5% on critical prompts - then pause and rollback to previous stable variant.

[Ambidextrous billing sketches]
Topline idea:

Play with a 2-axis billing system that mixes a per-seat (or per-app) SLO premium + a variable per-token/interaction charge. Goal: give predictable committed revenue for enterprise while preserving a low-friction PAYG experience for devs.

Rationale / tradeoffs (quick):
- Per-seat or committed capacity gives us stable base revenue and justifies Dedicated/Private margins.
- Variable usage aligns cost with heavy consumers and avoids overcharging light users.
- SLO/throughput premium (small monthly fee) buys reserved throughput, lower p99 latency, and better batching/caching priority.
- Need simple mental model for customers: "base fee = guaranteed capacity + SLO; variable = actual token usage".

Concrete primitives to experiment with:
1) Base commitment tiers (monthly):
   - Micro: $100/mo -> 5k guaranteed tokens / priority queue share 0.5
   - Team: $1,000/mo -> 100k guaranteed tokens / pqueue 1.0
   - Pro: $10,000/mo -> 1.5M guaranteed tokens / pqueue 2.0
   Notes: these numbers are placeholders — main point is exponential step to capture commitment.

2) Variable usage price (per 1K tokens)
   - Standard model: $0.40 / 1k tokens for hosted baseline model (e.g., open-Llama q4)
   - Discounted on-top of committed buckets: usage that falls within committed bucket effectively costs $0.00 (prepaid), overage billed at 50% of list ($0.20 / 1k) up to 2x, then list price after that.

3) SLO/SLA premium add-on (optional):
   - Low-latency add-on: +$X/mo per seat or +% of base commit -> reduces p99 by ~30–40ms via higher priority routing; also enables KV cache pinning
   - Failover premium: +monthly fee for cross-region fallback (useful for enterprise)

Unit econ back-of-envelope (hosted):
- Assumptions (round numbers):
  * GPU amortized + infra per 1M tokens = $8 (after efficient batching/kv caching; optimistic)
  * Storage/network/caching incremental = $2 / 1M tokens
  * SRE & support overhead amortized = $3 / 1M tokens
  * Total cost ~ $13 / 1M tokens => $0.013 / 1k tokens cost base

- Price band example: list $0.40 / 1k -> gross margin ~ 0.387 / 1k ~ 97% (sounds great, but beware encoder/decoder mix & long context blowups)
- For enterprise private deployments we expect $0.10–0.20 / 1k effective margin after licensing and on-prem costs.

Sample customer scenarios (quick):
A) Small app (developer)
 - Base: free tier w/ 10k tokens / mo
 - Payg: $0.50 / 1k tokens beyond free
 - If they use 100k tokens -> bill = 90k * 0.5/1k = $45 -> low friction, easy conversion

B) Growing SaaS team (Team tier)
 - Commit: $1k/mo -> 100k tokens included
 - Actual use = 600k tokens -> overage = 500k tokens billed at $0.20/1k -> $100 -> total $1,100/mo
 - Unit econ: revenue per 1M tokens = 1100 / 0.6 = ~$1833 per 1M -> far above hosted costs. But key is the SLO premium and predictability.

C) Enterprise (Dedicated)
 - Commit: $10k/mo for reserved capacity and enterprise support (1.5M tokens included)
 - Actual 10M tokens / mo -> overage pricing tiered and negotiated; effective blended price maybe $0.08/1k -> revenue ~ $800 / 1M tokens -> lower margin but recurring contract + enterprise SLA.

Pricing levers we can test quickly:
- Lower base price and raise SLO premium vs opposite. Which converts better?
- Make overage discount generous for committed customers (encourage predictable commit).
- Introduce session bundles (N sessions / mo) rather than tokens for certain conversational products.

Experimental metric plan (MVP A/B):
- Metric: committed-conversion rate (trial->commit), ARPU at 30/60/90 days, churn post-commit, % of customers hitting >3x committed usage (danger signal).
- Secondary: avg tokens per session, avg session length, burst vs steady state usage.

Operational constraints / thoughts:
- Need enforcement: counting window, token definitions (input vs output; function calls); unify counting across hosted/dedicated/private.
- Billing cadence: monthly in arrears vs prepay buckets. Pref prepay for cashflow on commitments.
- UI: show customers projected overage by end of month, recommend upgrade if trending >80% commit.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- What is a defensible base commit entry price for SMB without losing PLG growth? ($100/mo? smaller?)
- How do we present SLO premium in product terms without being too technical? Need product wording.
- Should we support automatic surge protection that bills to a credit card at a premium rate if commit exhausted? (good UX but revenue-ops risk)
- How granular should seat vs app vs org commit be? Per-seat supports per-user SLO; per-app easier for server-to-server.
- Need simulation of token distributions across top 200 accounts to set caps & detect anomalies.

Actionable next steps (quick):
1) Run 2-week pricing experiment on internal sandbox customers: small commit ($50/mo) vs pure PAYG; monitor conversions.
2) Generate synthetic usage traces (burst-heavy vs steady) and compute P50/P95 cost per 1M tokens under current runtime batching assumptions.
3) Draft simple product microcopy for SLO premium and show to UX for feedback.
4) Hook billing team to validate implementation constraints (prepay buckets, rollover rules, overage caps).

Random heuristics/shortcuts for future calculations:
- If avg response length per call > 1k tokens, treat as "long context" and surface recommended quantization and caching.
- Consider "session multiplier": bill sessions < 5 exchanges at 50% token weight to encourage short interactive flows. (controversial)

Final note: focus experiments on making the first commit decision frictionless — small committed dollar values with clear upgrade path and visible usage health will likely yield best early revenue signal.

-- E.P.

[Four-tier quant profiling cheatsheet and sample calcs]
Purpose and quick summary:
This is a compact working sheet + reference for profiling models across four quant tiers we use in experiments: 32-bit baseline, FP8-ish (8-bit float or block-fp8), INT8 (symmetric/asymmetric per-channel), and 4-bit (GPTQ / AWQ style). Goal: fast heuristics to convert a latency+cost SLO into a recommended quant tier and light pre-deployment checklist.

Intended audience:
- ML infra / product engineers running pre-serve perf runs
- Solutions engineers advising customers on cost-latency tradeoffs
- Product PMs who need a one-pager for canary config suggestions

High-level decision flow (one-line each):
1) Capture SLO: p95 latency budget per request, plus monthly token budget (tokens/month).
2) Measure baseline 32-bit QPS and p95 for representative prompt distribution.
3) Measure each candidate quant tier on same hardware (same batch sizes / prompt length distribution).
4) Compute cost-per-token for each tier = (instance hourly $ / tokens served per hour) adjusted for GPU utilization.
5) Score tiers by multi-objective metric (latency penalty + quality delta + cost saving). Pick tier with acceptable quality delta under threshold.

Key knobs and shorthand definitions (for the sheet columns):
- model_name: e.g., gpt-small-v1
- hw: e.g., A100-80GB, H100-80GB, L4-40GB
- quant_tier: baseline_fp32, fp8, int8, 4bit
- p95_ms: measured p95 in milliseconds at target real-world concurrency
- tokens_per_sec: sustained throughput under typical batching strategy
- inst_hr_cost: instance hourly cost (cloud list price or committed rate)
- tokens_per_hr = tokens_per_sec * 3600
- $/token = inst_hr_cost / tokens_per_hr (adjust for multi-tenancy overhead as needed)
- quality_metric_delta: e.g., delta in eval accuracy/ROUGE/LLM-eval score relative to baseline (positive means worse)
- accept_quality_thresh: default 1.5% relative delta or +/- 0.02 absolute (tunable per customer)

Concrete sample rows (toy numbers) - copy into sheet to start: 
- Baseline fp32 on A100-80GB: p95_ms=210, tokens_per_sec=5200, inst_hr_cost=$9.6 -> tokens_per_hr=18,720,000 -> $/token=5.12e-7
- FP8 on A100: p95_ms=185, tokens_per_sec=5600, inst_hr_cost=$9.6 -> tokens_per_hr=20,160,000 -> $/token=4.76e-7, quality_delta=+0.6%
- INT8 on A100: p95_ms=160, tokens_per_sec=6000, inst_hr_cost=$9.6 -> tokens_per_hr=21,600,000 -> $/token=4.44e-7, quality_delta=+1.1%
- 4-bit on A100: p95_ms=145, tokens_per_sec=6500, inst_hr_cost=$9.6 -> tokens_per_hr=23,400,000 -> $/token=4.10e-7, quality_delta=+2.9%

Recommendation scoring formula (quick heuristic used in sheet):
score = normalized_cost_saving * 0.5 + normalized_latency_gain * 0.3 - normalized_quality_penalty * 0.8
Where normalized_* are scaled to [0,1] across the candidate tiers for the run. We weight quality penalty more heavily by default. Tune weights per-customer SLOs.

SLO-aware decision rules (practical shortcuts):
- If p95_measured <= 0.8 * p95_budget then prefer lower-bit tier with +quality monitoring; use canary split 5-10% traffic.
- If p95_measured > p95_budget -> avoid further quant steps that give <5% latency improvement; prefer model sharding or smaller sequence-length heuristics first.
- If tokens/month cost saving < 1% -> skip quant rollout (operational overhead not worth it).

Quality validation checklist (pre-canary):
- Run 3 prompt suites: safety-ish, business critical prompts, long-context prompts. Collect token-level logprobs and failure modes.
- Collect regression alerts: exact match, BLEU/ROUGE, hallucination rate proxies, and a small human review of 200 samples for the chosen tier.
- Add fallback policy: if model output score (LLM-eval aggregated) drops > accept_quality_thresh on live traffic, route to baseline until triage.

Batching and cache notes (how they shift numbers):
- Effective tokens/sec scales with batch size until memory-bound; each quant tier changes memory footprint -> allows larger batch -> non-linear throughput gains for INT8/4-bit.
- KV cache size is smaller for int8/4-bit, lowering memory pressure and improving concurrent QPS. Include cache hit-rate assumptions in tokens_per_sec col.

Edge-case heuristics we use in experiments: 
- For short prompts (<64 tokens) latency wins; give heavier weight to p95 differences and prefer INT8 over 4-bit because quant noise matters more for short-span completions.
- For long generation tasks (>512 tokens), throughput and memory footprint dominate; 4-bit usually gives best $/token but watch for drift in score.
- Mixed workloads: split by percentile of prompt length and compute weighted score per quant tier.

Notes on hardware interaction (practical):
- H100: FP8 execution paths are often more optimized than INT8; FP8 p95 delta vs fp32 may be smaller. Always measure fp8 separately.
- A100: INT8 commonly has large kernel speedups; AWQ/LLM.int4 variants depend on fused-kernel support.
- Cloud GPUs have different pricing models (spot / sustained use discounts) — attach the committed rate in inst_hr_cost when estimating production.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Add column for retry/backoff cost (percent extra tokens due to retries) — we sometimes see 1.5x effective tokens for noisy LLM interactions.
- Automate trimming of eval prompt set to be representative of customer's tail latencies.
- Add small Monte Carlo sim to estimate probability of quality regression exceeding threshold under data drift.

Rollout play for recommended tier (example):
1) Internal staging run with 10k prompts from production shadow for 24hrs. Confirm quality delta <= 1x accept threshold.
2) Canary 5% traffic, 2x monitoring frequency (per-minute evaluation for first 6 hrs).
3) If stable, increase to 25% after 24hrs, then 100% after 72hrs.
4) If any quality alert triggers, automatic rollback to baseline variant and create incident.

Appendix: quick calc snippets to paste into a spreadsheet (text formulas)
- tokens_per_hr = tokens_per_sec * 3600
- $per_token = inst_hr_cost / tokens_per_hr
- monthly_cost = $per_token * monthly_tokens_expected
- relative_cost_saving = (baseline_monthly_cost - tier_monthly_cost) / baseline_monthly_cost

Rough example customer scenario (for marketing/sales):
- 50M tokens / month, p95_budget = 300 ms on H100 cluster. Baseline fp32 monthly = $X. INT8 gives 18% cost reduction and p95=240ms -> recommended: INT8 canary, monitor for quality delta; projected $ saved = $Y/month.

Contact and provenance:
- Author: Aisha Kumar (product-optimize)
- Experiments and sample numbers pulled from internal perf runs Feb 2025 with H100 and A100 dev clusters.
- Reach out to Mateo (bench infra) for raw perf traces and Priya for eval suite details.

Notes-to-self / scratch: 
- Might fold this into the interactive cost-model worksheet that calculates expected monthly savings given arbitrary concurrency mix and retention TTL for KV caches.
- Keep a library of canonical prompt sets for short/medium/long to speed A/B analysis.

End of cheatsheet (working).

[Pricing talk tracks, tiers & discounting — metric framing]
summary:
Working draft of messaging & operational guidance for token-based pricing, recommended tier structure, and discount guardrails. Focused on buyer-facing talk tracks for finance/engineering/procurement, negotiator playbook, and short competitive notes.

body:
Purpose / audience:\n- This is a working GTM brief for Sales Enablement, Pricing PM, and ARR-facing AEs.\n- Goals: 1) Give concise 'why token pricing' talk tracks for different buyer personas; 2) propose a simple tier structure that maps to engineering value drivers; 3) give discounting rules + negotiation scripts.\n\nBackground context (quick):\n- We sell inference across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. Customers consume a mix of generation, embeddings, and reranking.\n- Historically buyers compare per-request pricing (bad for us) or per-1000-tokens (confusing without examples). Need unified framing that connects to buyer KPIs.\n\nMetric framing — core thesis:\n- Metric = tokens processed (input + output) normalized to a unit everyone can reason about.\n- Why tokens?\n  * Token is model-agnostic (works for text-gen, chat, embeddings) — single unit avoids stove-piped pricing.\n  * Engineers can optimize tokens w/out changing app semantics (prompt engineering, caching, truncation).\n  * Finance likes a determinable variable cost that scales with usage and is auditable.\n  * Sales can convert product usage forecasts to expected spend easily.\n- Counter: buyers ask \"but tokens are opaque\" → response: we provide token calculators, typical case studies, and per-route token visibility in Console (token-level cost breakdown).\n\nBuyer personas & quick talk tracks:\n1) Engineer / Platform team (technical)\n- Lead with measurable levers: batching, KV caching, quantized models, and sequence len distribution. Tokens let you measure and tune.\n- Talk points: \"You can lower per-response cost by X% by caching prefixes and batching — the token metric directly reflects those gains.\"\n- Example: \"A 25% reduction in average output tokens from 256 -> 192 reduces cost by ~25% and latency variance is lower.\"\n\n2) Finance / Procurement (commercial)\n- Lead with predictability and auditability. Tokens map to spend forecasts and usage alerts.\n- Talk points: \"We give per-route usage caps, per-token rates, and monthly invoices with detailed breakdowns. Commit discounts are yieldable for predictable budgets.\"\n- Example: produce 12-month model projection vs fixed-seat software subscription, show expected $/MAU.\n\n3) Product / Growth (outcome-oriented)\n- Talk to experiments and tradeoffs: tokens = variable cost tied to feature experiment usage.\n- Emphasize: ability to run AB tests with cost ceilings and rollback routing policies to cheaper model when cost spikes.\n\nTier structure (recommended):\n- Guiding principles: few tiers, clear scale triggers, map to support/SLAs, tie discounts to committed usage not subjective criteria. Keep names simple.\n- Proposed tiers (names + short descriptions):\n  1) Starter — self-serve, low friction, pay-as-you-go pricing, limited retention/console features\n  2) Growth — predictable throughput, moderate discounting, standard support, multi-model routing\n  3) Scale — annual commit, significant unit discounts, priority support, basic SLA\n  4) Dedicated/Enterprise — reserved capacity, SLA-backed latency/uptime, private control plane, negotiated pricing (but follow discount guardrails)\n- Unit discount curve (example guidance):\n  * Starter: baseline unit price\n  * Growth: ~10-20% off baseline after commit threshold (e.g., >$5k/mo committed tokens)\n  * Scale: 20-40% off baseline at higher commit tiers and 12-month terms\n  * Dedicated: custom, but avoid >50% list unless there is real strategic value (co-sell, anchor customer, marketplace listing)\n\nDiscounting rules & negotiation guardrails:\n- Principles: transparent, formulaic, time-limited, tied to commitment type.\n- Acceptable levers: commit volume (tokens/month), term length (6/12/24 months), prepayment (upfront = +5–8% incremental discount), channel/partner co-sell credits.\n- Forbidden/rare: ad-hoc headcount discounts, discounts below floor without Exec approval, per-deal exceptions for support-only asks.\n- Quick formulas (examples to use in negotiation):\n  * Volume discount bands: 0–$5k/mo = 0% | $5k–$25k/mo = 10% | $25k–$100k/mo = 25% | >$100k/mo = 35%\n  * Term uplift: 12mo = +5% off list; 24mo = +8% off list (stack with volume up to cap)\n  * Prepay uplift: prepay 12mo = additional 3–5% (cap combined discounts at ~45%)\n  * Professional services (SOW) should be contracted separately — do not discount token rates to buy PS time.\n- Discount approval process: AE to propose -> SalesOps pricing calculator -> AM/VP of Sales signoff for deals with >30% combined discount or >$1.5M ARR reduction vs list.\n\nCompetitive positioning notes (short):\n- Cloud AI incumbents: tend to price per 1k tokens or per-request with opaque compute multipliers; they emphasize model access but lack production controls.\n  * Positioning: Redwood = predictable economics + observability + serving controls (batching/caching) that reduce effective $/output.\n- Self-hosted runtimes / infra vendors: offer low unit cost but shift ops burden.\n  * Positioning: Redwood provides managed operational primitives (rollouts, fallbacks, capacity) — you pay for reduced operational TCO and faster time-to-value.\n- Other LLM APIs (consumer-first vendors): price aggressively but lack enterprise SLAs and dedicated capacity tiers.\n  * Positioning: Redwood is for teams that need predictable latency and cost as features scale to production.\n\nPricing page microcopy (short snippets — use as building blocks):\n- Headline: \"Pay for what you use — tokens that map to your product metrics.\"\n- Subline: \"One unit across chat, generation, and embeddings with transparent per-route usage and committed discounts for predictable scale.\"\n- Starter card: \"Self-serve. No commitment. Pay-as-you-go token pricing + developer tools.\"\n- Growth card: \"Save more as you scale — commit and get predictable unit pricing, standard SLA, and priority support.\"\n- Enterprise card: \"Dedicated capacity, private control plane, and enterprise SLAs. Custom pricing based on reserved throughput.\"\n\nAE talk tracks / objection responses (short bullets):\n- Objection: \"Why not price per API call?\" → Response: \"Calls vary wildly in cost (model size, token length). Tokens let you compare apples-to-apples and optimize without changing app semantics.\"\n- Objection: \"Tokens are hard to estimate for legal/procurement.\" → Response: \"We provide a token calculator and can model 12-month usage in the SOW for approval — plus per-route caps and alerts.\"\n- Objection: \"Competitor is cheaper per-call.\" → Response: \"Show sample invoices + latency/uptime differences; highlight caching/batching optimizations that lower effective cost and avoid surprise overage charges.\"\n\nExamples / worked scenarios (short):\n- Example A: SaaS product with 100k monthly active users, average 50 tokens/request, 200k requests/month → monthly tokens = 10M. At Growth band price $0.00002/token = $200/mo vs Starter @ $0.000025/token = $250/mo. Show how caching 20% reduces spend by $40/mo.\n- Example B: Search product using embeddings for 10M queries/month — cost calculus shifts to embedding-specific unit and dedicated throughput might be warranted. Show when to recommend Dedicated tier.\n\nNegotiation script (AE -> Buyer):\n- \"We recommend committing to Growth for 12 months at [X tokens/mo] which gets you a predictable $/token and priority routing. If usage is lower, unused tokens can be rolled into a 3-month carry-forward window (optional). For strategic pilot customers, we support a time-limited evaluation credit and reduced PS scope to accelerate integration.\"\n\nOpen questions / items for pricing committee:\n- Should we offer a standard 3-month pilot rate/credit for enterprise deals? Pros: lowers friction. Cons: sets expectation.\n- Carry-forward policy for unused committed tokens — how long and how much?\n- Floor discount in Marketplace listings vs direct sales — alignment needed with Partnerships.\n\nNext steps (operational):\n- Pricing PM to build volume-discount calculator in SalesOps (deadline: 2026-04-15).\n- Draft website pricing cards from microcopy above (Design + Web Ops).\n- Sales enablement one-pager + cheat sheet for AEs with example math + objections (owner: GTM enablement).\n\nNotes to self / TODOs (rough):\n- Add 3 real customer invoice examples (anonymized) that show token breakdown.\n- Work with Console PM to include token estimation tool in signup flow.\n- Validate discount caps with Finance (impact on gross margin).\n\n---\nThis doc is intentionally rough — use it as the source for a polished pricing playbook. Capture feedback in the linked Confluence page and iterate.\n

[PAYG-tier-thresholds-scratchpad]
Quick back-of-envelope notes for pricing tiers / unit econ — mostly for my head and to share with Dan/Ivy. Rough, lots of TODOs and questions.

Context / goals:
- Need simple starter + pro + enterprise anchors for hosted API that map to unit economics and encourage growth into Dedicated.
- Show 3 price levers: per-token PAYG, committed monthly bundles, reserved capacity commitments for enterprise.
- Keep free tier meaningful but not abusive.

ASSUMPTIONS (very rough; will refine with infra):
- GPU amortized cost (incl infra, ops, cooling, license): $2.50 / GPU-hour (conservative cheap infra region).
- Typical model profile we expect to push on hosted: 4-bit quantized 13B variant. Effective throughput: ~150 tokens/sec per GPU at steady-state for short requests (avg seq 64).
- Utilization target for hosted pool baseline: 60% (bursty demand + slack for spikes).
- Storage / network / infra overhead per token: ~20% on top of compute cost (caching, routing, SLO buffers).

BASIC MATH: compute tokens/hr per GPU = 150 tps * 3600 = 540,000 tokens/hr.
Effective tokens/hr @ 60% util = 324,000 tokens/hr.
Compute cost per effective token = $2.50 / 324,000 = $0.000007716 / token -> $0.007716 per 1k tokens.
Add 20% infra/mgmt overhead -> $0.00926 per 1k tokens (round to $0.0093).
Add margin + SG&A + support + amortized acquisition (~3x) -> target price per 1k tokens PAYG ~ $0.028-$0.035.

Sanity checks:
- If we price PAYG at $0.03 / 1k tokens, gross margin vs compute-only ~ 3.2x (0.03 / 0.0093). Reasonable to cover ops and growth.
- Embeddings: different profile – lower inference ops but more memory. Assume embeddings cost ~0.5x token compute cost per 1k tokens because batchable and shorter sequences -> base cost per 1k embedding-tokens ~$0.0045; price at $0.015 per 1k embedding-tokens.

Tier sketches (starter ideas):
- Free: 200k tokens / month + 50 embedding-requests free (small dev/test). Hard cap to prevent heavy users.
- Starter (pay monthly): $29 / month includes 3M tokens + 50k embedding units. Overage PAYG at $0.025 / 1k.
- Growth: $199 / month includes 20M tokens + 200k embedding units. Overage at $0.02 / 1k.
- Pro: $999 / month includes 150M tokens + 1M embedding units. Overage at $0.012 / 1k.
- Enterprise / Dedicated: custom, pricing anchored to reserved capacity (committed GPU-hours) with effective tokens-per-month guarantees; typical discounts 40–70% vs PAYG depending on commitment and SLA.

Rationale for numbers:
- Starter price: $29 covers fixed costs and yields low usage CAC funnel. If a starter user uses entire 3M tokens, implied unit price = $29 / 3M = $0.00967 / 1k tokens (below PAYG) -> encourages plan conversion but still above compute cost.
- Growth / Pro step-downs are compression from volume. We need to ensure pro still > compute+ops at target utilization to avoid negative margin. At 150M tokens included in Pro, implied unit price = $0.00666 / 1k tokens — that would be below earlier compute+overhead -> so Pro needs to be primarily for higher ARR customers who we expect to convert to Dedicated (or we ensure higher renewal economics via add-ons).

Committed capacity thought experiment (enterprise):
- Enterprise wants 30k rps sustained (example) -> translates to N GPUs. Need mapping of rps->tokens/sec based on avg request size.
- Offer reserved pool price: baseline $1.80 / GPU-hr (private large commitment) -> if enterprise commits 24/7 then effective tokens cost drops hugely.

Sensitivity table (quick):
- If throughput is 100 tps instead of 150: compute cost per 1k tokens -> $2.50 / (100*3600*0.6) *1000 = $0.013 = $0.013 per 1k -> after infra 20% = $0.0156 -> need PAYG ~ $0.05+ / 1k. So throughput is the single biggest driver.
- If util is 40% instead of 60%: compute cost per 1k increases proportionally.

Billing mechanics / UX notes:
- Show "included tokens" prominently; bill fractional tokens per request (not round up).
- Overage in 1k-token increments on PAYG buckets.
- Provide an "effective unit price" meter in Console so customers can see their realized $/1k aggregated (tokens consumed, cache hit rates, batching savings).

Promotion hooks / marketing angles:
- Starter bundles with predictable cost are attractive for product teams testing features (avoids surprise PAYG bills).
- Show a chart: "If you hit X monthly tokens, plan Y gives you N% savings vs PAYG."

Open questions / TODOs:
- Need exact infra cost breakdown from Infra/Finance: cooling, KMS, egress, redis/KV cache, tracing retention overhead -> ask infra for a per-GPU-hour cost table by region. (@Daniel)
- Need to measure real-world throughput numbers for the three model families (7B, 13B quant, 70B q4f16) under our serving runtime for representative seq lengths. Run load tests with sample prompt mix. (@Ivy)
- Decide on embedding unit definition (1 embedding request = average 256 tokens input? or per call?). Standardize across docs.
- How to price function-calling / tools costs where backend ops (tooling webhooks executor) add additional infra? Consider add-on billing for tool-exec minutes.
- Legal/tax implications for credits / free-tier promos in EU/APAC (VAT differences) -> loop in finance.

Next steps (practical):
- Pull infra numbers and run a small notebook to generate a matrix of prices vs utilization vs throughput (sweep). Link to notebook in linked_artifacts.
- Propose initial public-facing numbers for internal review (draft PRD).
- Build Console UX mock for included tokens meter and top-of-bill alert when monthly runrate > 3x plan.

Quick notes to self:
- Keep PAYG headline simple: $0.03 / 1k tokens (text gen) and $0.015 / 1k embedding-tokens as a public anchor while we validate numbers.

[Strip compat-proxy and unify persisted flag schemas]
description:
Summary: A legacy compatibility proxy and an ad-hoc legacy-flag-mapper were introduced in early rollout phases to accept old client configs and route traffic to fallback handlers. Over time these have become maintenance burden: duplicated telemetry, increased tail latency variance, and brittle conditional logic that blocks safe schema evolution. This ticket removes the compat-proxy and migrates persisted flag keys/configs to a single canonical config-schema v2. The work includes safe migration tooling, operator controls, and a staged rollout with clear observability.

acceptance_criteria:
Legacy compat-proxy binary and all HTTP/gRPC routes removed from the runtime and service mesh
Config-schema v2 is the sole accepted on-disk format; v1 reader deprecated and gated behind operator toggle
Migration scripts can perform idempotent dry-runs and produce a migration report listing changed keys
No customer-facing errors attributable to missing legacy keys during a 72h full-ramp window
Telemetry shows no net increase in P99 latency or error-rate > 0.5% vs baseline after full rollout

migration_steps:
