[unify-ci-actions-introduce-release-automation-and-cleanup-dev-deps]
description:
Motivation: our GitHub Actions setup had grown organic cruft: duplicated workflow YAML, inconsistent caching, and ad-hoc release steps across repos. This PR consolidates reusable workflows, standardizes caches and test matrix behavior, and enables deterministic release automation using release-please. The change set is focused on developer-experience and repo hygiene (no product logic changes).

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds .github/workflows/reusable-ci.yml and reusable-lint.yml to centralize build/test/lint behavior.
- Replaces three repo-specific workflows (ci-python.yml, ci-node.yml, ci-go.yml) with small entrypoint workflows that invoke the reusable workflows.
- Introduces a common action cache policy (key includes os, runner, node-version/python-version, and lockfile hash) to reduce cold-cache flakiness.
- Adds a test sharding strategy using matrix.include shards for the python test suite and parallelization hints for pytest-xdist when applicable.
- Migrates dependency automation from dependabot to a unified renovate configuration with onboarding for major monorepo rules (lockfile maintenance, group upgrades for devDeps).
- Bumps key CI dev deps: actions/checkout@v4, actions/cache@v4, pnpm/setup-pnpm@v2, actions/setup-node@v4 and setup-python@v4.
- Adds a release-please config and a GitHub workflow (release-please.yml) to create draft releases and CHANGELOG entries using conventional commits. This will replace manual release steps and the previous ad-hoc scripts in scripts/release/*.
- Removes legacy shell-based lint/test wrappers in scripts/ci/ in favor of reusable composite actions under .github/actions/ci-helpers/.
- Small refactors to tests to make them hermetic: pinning ephemeral network calls in two integration tests and reducing reliance on system time via freezegun in python tests.

Checklist (manual steps validated):
- [x] Cross-repo reusable workflow shape validated locally with act and against a staging branch in a sandbox repo.
- [x] Cache keys stress-tested (cold/warm) across linux/macos runners.
- [x] release-please created draft release during a dry-run using --dry-run.
- [x] Dependabot->Renovate migration: tested PR creation on a small sample group repository.
- [x] Flaky tests observed in previous builds were stabilized (see review comments).

How to review: the core is the reusable workflows and the release config; I recommend reviewing the YAML files first (.github/workflows and .github/actions), then the scripts/ci removal. Test-specific changes are intentionally small and annotated inline.

Rollout plan: merge to main will flip on the reusable workflows by renaming the old workflows to .disabled (kept for a week for quick rollback). After two successful main runs we will delete the .disabled files and mark this PR as fully applied. Release automation will be enabled in day-1 but set to create draft releases only (no auto-publish) until we validate changelog generation for 2 release cycles.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: subtle differences in runner env captured by old per-repo workflows. Mitigation: included explicit runner labels and expanded matrix combinations in reusable workflow; staged dry runs were executed.
- Risk: renovate onboarding churn. Mitigation: initial schedule is weekly and grouping policy limits PR noise for devDeps.

Related work items: ENG-4021, ENG-4278, OPS-189.

Notes: this PR intentionally keeps functional changes out of scope; any follow-up feature changes should be in separate PRs.

[Debounce presubmit triggers and introduce incremental linter cache]
description:
Motivation: presubmit pipelines have become noisy and slow due to immediate CI triggers on rapid developer pushes and many dependency-chore PRs. This PR implements a debounce layer for push/branch events so rapid successive commits within a short window are coalesced into a single presubmit run, and adds an incremental linter cache keyed by tool version + file globs to avoid re-linting unmodified packages. We also add a small dependency-whitelist mechanism so authorized chore PRs (approved dep bumps from our depbot pipeline) can take a lightweight validation path rather than the full heavy presubmit. The changeset is intentionally incremental: 1) an event debounce service that runs as a lightweight GitHub Actions composite step and a small Go shim to translate webhooks into coalesced workflow_dispatch events 2) a disk-backed incremental linter cache used by existing golangci-lint and eslint invocations with fallthrough to fresh lint runs when cache versioning mismatches 3) a dep-whitelist JSON manifest and workflow guard to route chore PRs to a lightweight pipeline 4) small release-hook adjustment to avoid firing release workflows for chore-only merges. Checklist: - [x] add debounce composite action + shim - [x] implement incremental lint cache and integrate with existing lint jobs - [x] add dep-whitelist manifest + lightweight workflow - [x] updates to docs and contributing guide - [x] smoke run on staging repository Rollout plan: deploy debounce action to canary org for 48h, monitor presubmit queue and merge latency, then flip org-level flag for full rollout. If regressions observed rollback by removing webhook-forwarding secret and revert action inputs. Related: ENG-2145 tracks presubmit cost reduction, ENG-2210 tracks dep-routing. Notes: debouncing window defaults to 90s (configurable per-repo) to balance feedback latency and unnecessary runs. The linter cache is safe by versioning linter tool versions and cache schema; any mismatch triggers a cold lint. This PR focuses on developer experience and CI cost; it does not change production runtime or model-serving behavior.

[Introduce prefill-conductor heuristic mapper and tenant defaults estimator]
description:
Adds a prefill-conductor heuristic mapper service and a tenant defaults estimator that synthesizes batching, cache, and quantization profiles from telemetry signatures. Motivation: many tenants have predictable temporal/size distributions but currently require manual tuning to achieve cost targets; this feature automates initial defaults and provides a safe canary rollout path. What this PR does: 1) a new heuristic_mapper component (Python) that ingests tenant signatures (request size histogram, cold/hot percentiles, token distribution) and produces ranked candidate profiles for batch_size, kv_cache_policy, and quant_profile with estimated unit-econ deltas; 2) a lightweight estimator endpoint in the optimize API that returns recommended defaults and confidence scores; 3) telemetry collectors (Go) to compactly record prefill and warm-start traces used by the mapper; 4) a simulation harness and smoke CLI for dry-runs against tenant traces; 5) integration with rollout policies so recommendations can be applied as canary updates for Dedicated and Private deployments; 6) docs and operator runbook describing safe thresholds and rollback actions. Safety and limitations: mapper is conservative by default (prefers smaller batches if confidence is low), records all decisions for auditing, and exposes "cost_sensitivity" and "latency_slo" knobs for tenant overrides. Testing: unit tests for mapper heuristics, integration test of estimator endpoint against synthetic traces, and a perf smoke that measures latency/regression at 95th percentile before merging. Migration: no breaking API changes, opt-in flag enable_prefill_mapper=false in config for existing installs. Checklist: [x] design doc linked (ENG-8274), [x] unit tests added, [x] integration smoke passing, [x] docs updated, [x] telemetry schema version bumped. Backwards impact: none expected. Rollout: staged canary to 5 tenants, monitor unit-econ and latency for 72h before full deploy.

[Introduce defaults-suggester: heuristic profiles for batching, cache TTLs and quantization presets]
description:
Context: Teams repeatedly ask for sensible defaults for batching, cache TTLs and quantization when onboarding models to Redwood. Currently defaults live in multiple places and require manual tuning with evals and internal heuristics. Goal: ship a small, auditable suggestion system that observes recent workload signals and proposes conservative default profiles for batching.window_ms, batch_size caps, prefix/KV cache TTLs, and quantization presets. The suggester is opt-in by default and produces human-readable suggestions surfaced in the Console and via a new API endpoint.

What this PR does: 1) Adds a lightweight offline heuristic engine (defaults-suggester) that consumes short-term aggregated telemetry (per-route QPS, median latency, 50/95/99 latency quantiles, token length distribution) and maps to a ranked set of suggested profiles. 2) Introduces a new API: POST /optimize/v1/suggestions which returns JSON suggestions with confidence scores and an explanation string. 3) Wire up Console: a Suggestions panel on per-route settings with an Apply & Preview flow that shows estimated unit-cost delta and latency impact. 4) Add a gated runtime flag so the runtime can accept a profile payload for immediate application (useful for Dedicated/Private workflows). 5) Provide a small set of canonical profiles (conservative, balanced, aggressive) for batching and quantization, plus TTL presets for prefix/KV caches. 6) Add end-to-end test coverage and benchmark harness runs comparing before/after for representative traffic shapes.

Design notes and trade-offs: - The engine intentionally errs conservative: suggestions will never increase batch window beyond a route-level safety cap derived from SLA settings. - Quantization suggestions prefer per-model family presets (e.g., OPT/GPT-like) and include fallbacks; we do not auto-apply quantization in-host, suggestions only. - Telemetry ingestion is opt-in; customers can disable telemetry for suggestions in account settings. For Private installs the suggester can be run locally against their telemetry export. - Suggestions include an estimated unit-cost delta computed from our unit-econ model; we expose the formula in the Console and include the prompt/eval link so teams can validate quality impact.

Files touched: runtime/batching/suggester.go, optimize/suggester/service.go, api/handlers/suggestions.go, console/src/routes/RouteSuggestionsPanel.tsx, console/src/api/suggestionsClient.ts, docs/operations/defaults-suggester.md, config/profiles/default-profiles.yaml, tests/e2e/suggestions_flow.test.ts, bench/harness/suggester_traffic_shapes.yaml, telemetry/migrations/add_suggester_event.sql, scripts/ci/bench-suggester.sh

Testing: - Unit tests for mapping heuristics and profile ranking. - E2E test simulating three traffic shapes (short chat, assistant longform, embeddings micro-bursts). - Benchmarks: microbenchmark harness run on a c6g-xlarge-equivalent cluster with representative models showed median latency change within +3% for conservative profiles and unit-cost reduction up to 24% for balanced profiles on nuclear workloads. Results attached to the CI artifact and linked in the console patch notes.

Rollout plan: feature gated. Step 1: merge behind feature flag and enable suggestions only for internal org and canary customers. Step 2: collect feedback for 2 weeks. Step 3: enable Console UI for self-serve with telemetry opt-in prompt on first usage. Step 4: document caveats and add guided eval for teams that accept aggressive quantization suggestions.

Open questions / TODOs: - Add an explicit opt-out banner in Console per compliance request (tracked in ENG-7922). - Provide an exportable CSV of suggestion history for audit. - Consider a future ML-backed suggestion engine once we have more signal.

References: Linear items ENG-7842, ENG-7901. Internal benchmark dashboards: /dash/bench/suggester/33219.

[introduce profile-curator service and autoconfig economizer for workload defaults]
description:
Motivation: Many customers and our own Dedicated clusters have operational drift between deployed inference defaults and the actual workload shapes. Engineers repeatedly tune batching, prefill TTLs, and quantization profiles per-model which leads to inconsistent unit economics and frequent regressions. This PR introduces a new Profile Curator service and an AutoConfig Economizer that can simulate workload slices, score candidate default profiles by unit-economic impact, and propose safe rollout plans.

What this change does: Adds a lightweight curator microservice (HTTP + internal gRPC proxy) that discovers model variants and recent telemetry, runs a candidate generation pipeline that emits batching/caching/quant profiles, simulates token-level cost/latency with a small stochastic workload sampler, and computes unit-econ deltas (cost per successful completion, tail latency impact). The output is: (1) a ranked set of profile candidates with expected savings and risk score, (2) a canary rollout plan that includes traffic split, fallthrough thresholds, and automatic rollback hooks.

Key features: 1) Profile generator: rule + ML hybrid that recommends batch_size, max_latency_target, kv_cache_ttl, quant_profile (int4/int8/config) per model family. 2) Unit-econ simulator: lightweight token-cost model using our serving runtime metrics to estimate GPU token cost, memory pressure, and expected tail-latency changes. 3) Safety and rollout: canary evaluator that monitors real-time observability hooks (error rate, P95, token drop) and enforces fallback to pinned profiles if thresholds are exceeded. 4) CLI and operator docs: curator apply/dry-run/score, and operator guide in docs/operations/cost-automation.md.

Backward compatibility and rollout strategy: The curator only creates suggested profiles and a rollout plan; it does not change runtime defaults until an operator approves and applies the plan (dry-run by default). We ship an optional operator mode to allow automatic application when a minimum expected savings threshold is exceeded and the canary passes. All generated profiles include an explicit safety tier and a default-to-pinned fallback.

Testing: Unit tests for the economizer engine and profile generator, integration tests that run a short simulated traffic replay against a local runtime stub, and a small perf harness to validate cold-start and KV-cache interactions. One flaky integration test (tests/integration/profile_curator_test.go) failed once on CI due to timing; it was retried and passed.

Related work: follows patterns from the optimizer workstream (ENG-7102) and complements the cost dashboards by producing actionable defaults instead of manual recommendations.

Notes for reviewers: focus on the economizer scoring math (internal/curator/autoconfig/economizer.go) and the safety evaluator thresholds in controller/rollout/curator_integration.go. The quantization selector is intentionally conservative (prefers int8 fallback profiles when int4 risk score > 0.15).

description:
Summary: Adds a small, auditable decision-tree based suggester service that consumes recent tenant telemetry and workload shapes to recommend safe defaults for batching, prefix/KV cache window, and quantization profile tiers. Motivation: customers frequently ask for one-click recommendations that reduce token cost without regressing latency or quality. The heuristic presets in Optimize are useful but brittle for mixed workloads; this PR introduces an explainable decision tree that maps telemetry signatures (median seq length, 95th latency, KV hit rate, model family, CPU/GPU footprint) to conservative default profiles. Key design goals: 1) deterministic and auditable recommendations, 2) low-cost inference (rules only reference aggregated telemetry, no raw prompts), 3) safe fallbacks and explicit human-readable rationale, 4) incremental rollout and A/B telemetry. What changed (high level): new service under /services/econ-suggester, a small rules engine with exported rationale strings, a CLI dry-run mode for operators, and a set of unit tests and integration harness scenarios. The decision tree is intentionally shallow (max depth 4) and implemented as data (yaml nodes) to allow future non-destructive updates via config. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked - [x] unit tests for tree evaluation - [x] integration test that runs the suggester against replayed tenant traces - [x] telemetry metrics (suggester.recommendations, suggester.rationale_hash) - [x] CLI dry-run and export to JSON - [x] e2e smoke run on staging - [ ] docs: user-facing guidance and Console integration (follow-up PR) Related: Linear ENG-13023, ENG-13590, infra/ops runbook entry https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-13023 Decision rationale export (example): "tenant: acme-corp, model: rw-1-mt, median_seq: 128 -> recommend: small-batch(8, 32ms-prefill), cache_window: 16kb, quant: q4_0; rationale: 'median_seq between 64-256 and KV hit < 5% suggests short-context batchable calls; choose conservative quant with no red-team to avoid quality regressions'" Commits (summary): - add [econ-suggester] lightweight decision tree evaluator and config loader - add CLI dry-run + replay adapter for trace-based evaluation - export suggester metrics and rationale hash for telemetry - add unit + integration tests - add initial YAML configuration (shallow trees) - add ci matrix job for suggester tests Changed files (high level): - services/econ-suggester/{main.go, tree_evaluator.go, config.yaml} - pkg/telemetry/suggester_metrics.go - tools/suggester-cli/{main.go, README.md} - tests/integration/econ-suggester/{replay_fixtures, smoke_test.go} - deployment/staging/suggester.yaml - Makefile: add suggester test target Review summary: The approach intentionally avoids ML-in-the-loop for the first iteration and focuses on explainability and safe defaults. description:
Summary: Adds a new service called 'Cost Pathfinder' — an advisor that recommends end-to-end inference defaults (batch sizes, prefix/KV cache policies, and quantization profile hints) for a given workload and SLO/cost target. The advisor runs both as an offline analyzer (sample-based profile) and as a light-weight runtime agent (shadow-eval + telemetry) that suggests conservative presets back to Redwood Optimize. Motivation: teams today manually tune batching and quantization leading to brittle rollouts and unpredictable unit economics. Pathfinder codifies a utility-aware scoring function that balances latency SLO, per-token cost delta, and quality risk (via shadow-eval electron).

Changes included: checklist: [x] design doc (linked LIGHT-ENG-1734), [x] advisor core + scoring, [x] scheduler integration shim for runtime suggestions, [x] CLI tool `rw-pathfinder` for offline profile generation and simulated load runs, [x] E2E integration tests in perf-canary harness, [x] observability dashboards + metrics, [x] safety budget guard and automatic rollback hooks.

- 5f6d7e8: add CLI and load-sim harness, --simulate-load flag
- 9a0b1c2: runtime shim to publish suggestions to Optimize API (shadow mode only by default)
- 3d4e5f6: add unit tests and perf-canary integration tests

Files changed (high level):
- pkg/advisor/pathfinder.go — core scorer + profile generator (new)
- cmd/rw-pathfinder/main.go — CLI and simulation driver (new)
- internal/optimize/shim.go — runtime suggestion shim (small integration)
- configs/pathfinder/default-profiles.yaml — curated conservative defaults (new)
- tests/perf/cases/pathfinder_integration_test.go — perf harness test (new)

Code highlights (illustrative, small snippets):
- scorer: Score = latency_slo_penalty * w1 + unit_cost_increase * w2 + quality_risk * w3
- safe fallback: if suggested_unit_cost_increase > budget_guard then mark profile as "conservative" and set prefill=on

Design notes / rationale: Pathfinder does not attempt to pick a single "optimal" config. Instead it returns a ranked set of profiles (fast, balanced, cheap) with an explicit expected token-econ delta and estimated p95 impact. The runtime shim supports a shadow-eval mode that runs quantized variants on a sample stream and records quality deltas to inform the quality_risk signal. To reduce blast radius, suggestions emitted to Redwood Optimize default to "suggestion:shadow-only" requiring an explicit operator confirmation before auto-apply.

Testing & benchmarks: Added a perf-canary workload that simulates mixed-length requests (10%, 50%, 40% token length buckets) and asserts: 1) recommended batch sizes reduce token-cost by >=9% vs baseline while keeping p95 below configured SLO+15ms, 2) shadow-eval quality delta <= 0.8% (for conservative profiles). Benchmarks run in CI are synthetic and flagged as flaky on older GPU types — we gate the stronger assertions behind `--ci` flag on the runner.

Observability: New metrics: pathfinder.recommendation.count, pathfinder.evaluate.latency_ms, pathfinder.quality.delta_pct, pathfinder.safety.rollback.count. Dashboards included in dashboard/01-pathfinder-overview.yaml and linked from Redwood Optimize navigation.

- Priya Rao: "Please ensure we don’t auto-apply suggestions for Dedicated customers by default. Also add a telemetry tag for tenant.plan."
- Asha: "Updated shim to mark suggestions as 'operator-confirm' for Dedicated in 9a0b1c2 and added tenant.plan tag to all emitted metrics." (commit 9a0b1c2)
- Ethan Cho: "Minor: can we tighten the unit test mocks to avoid depending on full Optimize backend?"
- Asha: "Added a lightweight local mock for optimize_client and moved heavier integration tests behind perf-canary harness."

CI history: initial CI run failed: py-sdk lint error in sdk/py/redwood/optimize_client.py (missing docstring) and one flaky perf assertion; fixes pushed in 7g8h9i0 and tests re-run. Second run: all checks passed (unit, lint, integration smoke). CI matrix included: go-1.21, py-3.11, linux-amd64, gpu-rt-stable.

Backward compatibility and safety: There are no breaking API changes. The only public API surface addition is a small helper in the Python SDK (optimize_client.suggest_profile()) marked experimental. By default, emitted suggestions are shadow-only and require explicit operator confirmation to become active. We added a safety budget guard that will refuse suggestions that exceed a tenant-specified % cost uplift without operator approval.

Rollout plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag `feature.pathfinder` (done); 2) deploy pathfinder in shadow mode for 2 weeks to top-tier tenants and run continuous quality checks; 3) open dashboard and ops runbook; 4) enable manual apply for select customers; 5) consider limited auto-apply with safe fallback after 8 weeks.

Follow-ups captured: ENG-1751 (expose optimizer constraints via API), ENG-1758 (auto-apply policy evaluation), ENG-1769 (improve shadow-eval sampling strategy).

Notes for reviewers of future changes: keep the safety budget guard front-and-center; prefer small incremental profile changes over large quant jumps; keep shadow-eval always enabled for new quant profiles.

[Staggered canary burst: pin inconsistency causes subset of requests to reroute to legacy variant]
description:
Issue summary:
During a staggered canary rollout for rw-instruct-7b-v3 in us-east-1, NimbleApps reported ~12% of their requests being served by an older model variant despite an explicit tenant-level model pin. The behavior lasted for ~45 minutes and coincided with an autoscaler prewarm burst triggered by a traffic spike.

Impact:
- Customer reported mixed outputs and downstream feature regressions for active users (measured anomalous quality score increase and user complaints).
- Approximately 11k requests affected for the customer across the incident window.

Environment:
- Production, us-east-1, Dedicated pool for NimbleApps (reserved capacity pool id: ded-342)

comments:
2025-11-02 Priya Singh (Support): Customer opened chat reporting that a portion of requests are returning legacy responses after we started the canary. They provided request IDs and timestamps. Asked to triage asap.
2025-11-02 Liam Chen (SRE): Acknowledged; collecting edge logs and routing snapshots. Initial hypothesis: pin commit race between orchestrator commit and edge cookie rotation during prewarm handoff.
2025-11-03 SRE-team (Liam Chen): Found routing mesh epochs where cohort snapshot contained mixed variant entries for tenant nimbleapps-17. Edge logs show affinity cookie TTL renewal at the same second as prewarm probe success; some flows lost pin before orchestrator snapshot completed.
2025-11-04 Support (Priya Singh) -> Customer: Confirmed we are rolling a targeted hotfix that changes prewarm handshake ordering to commit pins before edge cookie rotation. Asked customer for traffic window to cutover safely.
2025-11-05 NimbleApps (Customer): Verified behaviour has ceased after cutover; provided sampling confirming no legacy outputs in a 1h window post-fix. Thanked on call for quick turnaround.

investigation_notes:
What we observed:
- Autoscaler prewarm created N new prewarm nodes at t0+12s in response to surge.
- Prewarm handshake had a non-atomic ordering: node marked healthy -> edge cookie rotation -> orchestrator snapshot commit.
- In ~9% of sampled requests, edge rotated tenant affinity cookie just before orchestrator committed the new pin mapping, causing requests to land on edge shards that still resolved the tenant to the legacy variant.
- Orchestrator snapshots showed an overlapping epoch where two different routing tables were readable by different edge shards for ~18s.
- No GPU OOMs or serving runtime crashes found. Latency remained within SLO except for slight tail increase during the handoff window.

Hypotheses considered and eliminated:
- Tokenization mismatch in the model: rejected after verifying request payloads and embeddings.
- Customer-side pinned version misconfiguration: rejected; tenant manifest showed explicit pin to rw-instruct-7b-v3 prior to rollout.

Contributing factors:
- Prewarm handshake ordering (health -> rotate cookie -> commit) is non-atomic across control-plane and edge.
- Edge cookie rotation TTL is short and coincided with the commit window during a burst.
- Canary scheduling used staggered slice times (0s, +10s, +20s) which increased overlap surface for commit windows across shards.

resolution_notes:
Immediate mitigations applied:
1) Rolled a hotfix to orchestrator to change prewarm handshake ordering: commit pin mapping before issuing edge cookie rotation. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/3184. Deployed to us-east-1 dedicated pools at 2025-11-04T04:00Z.
2) Increased health-probe smoothing for prewarm nodes to reduce transient epoch changes during bursts.
3) Added a guard in edge-proxy to prefer orchestrator pin mapping when epoch differences detected within a 30s window.

Rollout notes:
- Hotfix applied via canary (5% -> 25% -> 100%) over a 3-hour window for dedicated pools; monitored cohort pins and customer telemetry.
- Post-deployment checks (logs + sampling from NimbleApps) showed 0% legacy-routed requests in the 1h stable window.

Follow-ups and action items:
- Engineering to add an orchestrator unit test that asserts prewarm handshake atomicity across control-plane and edge (owner: Liam Chen, target: 2025-11-12).
- Create a capacity-surge playbook to avoid staggered slice overlap during autoscaler prewarm (owner: Product, target: 2025-11-20).
- Postmortem scheduled and linked: https://confluence.redwood.ai/postmortems/SUP-209876-postmortem

Customer communication:
- Notified NimbleApps via support and scheduled an incident review call. Customer confirmed remediation and accepted workaround as final resolution.

[Tenant sticky-handoff leads to transient model rebinding during preemptive autoscaler eviction]
description:
Issue summary:\nDuring a scheduled capacity contraction triggered by the dedicated autoscaler (preemptive eviction window), several tenants experienced transient rebinding of model pins mid-session. Affected requests were routed to an older model variant for a subset of in-flight streaming sessions, causing partial/duplicate tokens and degraded output coherence for ~30 minutes.\n\nImpact:\n- Customer: BrightHealth AI (dedicated pool) reported increased token hallucinations and truncated streaming responses in prod us-east.\n- Scope: ~120 streaming sessions across 3 application endpoints, estimated 0.5% of total tenant requests in the window.\n- User-visible: incomplete structured JSON outputs, repeated token prefixes and occasional 502 from the edge when the session reconnect attempted to resume.\n\nEnvironment:\n- Dedicated GPU pool: dpool-us-east-3 (mixed reserved + spot).\n- Autoscaler policy: preemptive_scale_down enabled; spot eviction threshold 15m.\n- Rollout config: canary weight=10%, staged drain=false for ongoing promote. Some tenants had explicit model pins applied via the API.\n\nSteps to reproduce (customer provided):\n1. Tenant pins model redwood-open-13b-v1 via tenant config.\n2. Start multiple long-lived streaming sessions that keep KV cache hot (chat-like usage).\n3. Trigger autoscaler preemptive eviction simulation in staging (scale down spot nodes).\n4. Observe some streams switch mid-session to redwood-quant-13b-v1 (legacy variant) for a few tokens before failing back.\n\nObserved logs / metrics (snippets):\n- edge-proxy: \"session=abc123 lease=stale handoff=initiated target_variant=redwood-quant-13b-v1\"\n- orchestrator: \"pin-handoff request queued for tenant=brighthealth; source_node=pool-node-17; dest_node=pool-node-4; status=partial_commit\"\n- serving-runtime: \"kvcache-miss session=abc123 migration_in_progress=true tokens_streamed=6\"\n- dashboard spike: per-token latency spike from 40ms -> 220ms and increase in model mismatch error tags.\n\nInitial hypothesis:\n- Preemptive eviction caused asynchronous pin handoff: orchestrator sent a rebind to route the tenant, but the edge session lease renewal and KV cache migration did not complete atomically. As a result, in-flight streams saw the routing layer accept the connection to the fallback variant while the destination node had a cold KV cache, producing partial/duplicated tokens.\n- Staged drain=false (ongoing cutover) made the window shorter and increased race probability.\n\nInvestigation notes:\n- Correlated autoscaler eviction timestamps (2026-03-10T02:15Z) with session anomalies.\n- Retrieved orchestrator traces showing several \"partial_commit\" states where the handoff state machine did not progress to \"committed\" before the edge replayed the session on the destination.\n- Found edge-proxy code path did not check the handoff commit flag when resuming streaming sessions — it relied on a lease token that was refreshed but not tied to the pin commit.\n- Confirmed that the fallback variant (quantized model) was compatible but had different tokenization boundaries; combined with KV cache cold-start it produced duplicated prefixes.\n\nImmediate mitigations applied (2026-03-10 02:30Z):\n- Support set the autoscaler preemptive eviction window to conservative mode for BrightHealth's pool (bypass preemptive for 1 hour).\n- Enabled staged drain=true for rolling deploys for customer pool to force synchronous draining of sessions.\n- Applied an edge-proxy temporary guard: reject session resumes for a tenant until orchestrator commit_flag==true (hotfix).\n\nRoot cause and long-term fix:\n- Root cause: race between orchestrator pin-commit state and edge session resume path during preemptive node eviction; design assumption that lease refresh implied commit was false.\n- Fix implemented: orchestrator PR-1128 introduces an explicit pin-commit handshake; edge-proxy updated in PR-879 to validate commit token before resuming streaming connections. Patch ensures KV cache warmup is requested and confirmed as part of the commit handshake.\n- Rollout plan: staged rollout to us-east with canary weight=0 -> 25% -> 100% behind a feature flag; add observability metrics for \"handoff_commit_latency\" and a dashboard alarm.\n\nResolution notes:\n- Hotfix and guard prevented further occurrences; full patch released to prod us-east on 2026-03-11 04:00Z.\n- BrightHealth AI confirmed behavior returned to normal and provided sample session transcripts that are now consistent.\n- Follow-up: postmortem written and scheduled runbook update to require drain=true for any autoscaler preemptive policy by default for dedicated pools with active pins.\n\nReferences and crosslinks:\n- Slack: #support (thread tX1f2lK) \n- Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/serving/handoff-views\n- PRs: github.com/redwood-inference/orga/PR-1128, github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/PR-879\n

comments:
Priya Nair (2026-03-10): Customer reported repeated token prefixes and truncated JSON outputs during streaming. Attached sample transcripts and timestamps.
Liam Ortega (2026-03-10): Investigating. Pulled autoscaler logs and orchestrator traces; see partial_commit events. Temporarily adjusted autoscaler config for the customer's pool.
SRE - Mei Chen (2026-03-10): Applied edge guard to reject resume until commit flag set. Observed immediate drop in new incidents. Need full fix to avoid manual guard.
Eng - Rafael Torres (2026-03-11): PR-1128 and PR-879 merged to main; starting canary rollout in us-east behind feature flag. Metrics added for handoff_commit_latency.
CS - Hannah Li (2026-03-11): Customer validated fix with BVT traffic. Confirmed no regressions. Closing after monitoring window.
Postmortem (2026-03-12): Follow-up actions: runbook update, add integration test for in-flight streaming handoff under node eviction, change default autoscaler to avoid preemptive evict for pinned tenants.

[Unexpected model-pin transfer after prewarm expiry causes silent fallback and duplicate billing]
description:
Issue summary: Customer ClipperAI reports that during yesterday's staggered canary rollout their tenant traffic silently diverted to a degraded variant shortly after a prewarm step expired. Impact: multiple production requests returned the degraded model (gptx-3.0-quantized) for ~16 minutes and the customer observed a billing delta for both primary and degraded variant usage. Environment: Dedicated pool in us-east-1, tenant-specific routing with model pin grace-period configured to 30s, prewarm window configured to 5m.

Observed behavior: At 2026-03-09T22:14:05Z the canary prewarm job finished and the tenant had an active pin to redwood-v2-medium. At 2026-03-09T22:19:12Z the pin lease expired but instead of keeping the tenant on the primary variant until explicit commit, control-plane initiated a silent transfer that left some edge nodes routing to gptx-3.0-quantized. This created mixed responses and duplicate tallying in usage metrics.

Expected behavior: Pin grace-period expiry should not trigger an automatic model transfer during a staggered prewarm unless orchestration confirms cohort commit. Tenant should either remain on primary variant or be explicitly failed over with audit log and customer-visible event.

Steps to reproduce: 1) Create staged canary with staggered prewarm (prewarm 5m, pin grace 30s). 2) Finish prewarm then intentionally delay canary commit by ~2 minutes. 3) Observe edge routing and billing metrics for cross-variant request counts and check control-plane commit logs.

Business impact: Customer reported degraded quality for conversation flows and unexpected billing spike across both variants; they are asking for a remediation timeline and potential credits.

steps_to_reproduce:
Create dedicated tenant with staged canary and prewarm=5m, pin_grace=30s
Deploy redwood-v2-medium as primary and gptx-3.0-quantized as canary degraded variant
Allow prewarm to complete then delay commit signal for >60s
Generate steady traffic from tenant and observe routing traces and usage counters

2026-03-09T22:15:20Z edge-node-7: pin_lease_refresh tenant=clipper-123 lease_id=lease-789 status=ok

investigation_notes:
Support triage: replicated customer traffic pattern in staging with identical prewarm/pin settings; observed local-edge cache divergence after lease expiry
Hypothesis 1: edge local routing cache fell back to last-seen prewarm mirror state when lease expired instead of honoring central locked pin until commit
Hypothesis 2: orchestrator's pin handoff path contains a race where a failed prewarm/commit leaves metadata in "transfer_pending" state; edge reconciler treats transfer_pending as a valid variant
Observed: some edges reported decision_source=local-cache while control-plane recorded lease_expired and then later abort commit
Billing team: usage records show near-equal token counts for both variants during 22:19–22:35 window; indicates synchronous duplicate accounting rather than sampling noise

comments:
2026-03-10T09:02Z - Luis Alvarez (Assignee): Thanks for the report, Maya. I've started a scoped repro in staging and linked the orchestrator PR that adjusted transfer semantics last month. Initial results show edge cache TTL interplay. (see related PR)
2026-03-10T10:18Z - Maya Chen (Support): Customer provided additional request ids and the Redbox traces. They want to know if traffic was doubled-charged or if it was misattributed across variants.
2026-03-10T13:45Z - Billing (Ana Rodriguez): Billing confirms two distinct usage records were emitted for the same client request batch. We're flagging those records for credit review; will coordinate once root cause is confirmed.
2026-03-11T08:30Z - SRE (Kai Patel): Found a code path where local-edge reconciliation treats transfer_pending as commit=true when lease expires mid-sync. Pushing a hotfix branch to gate the behavior behind a safety check.
2026-03-12T14:05Z - Luis Alvarez: Hotfix PR created and testing underway: https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/4121. Mitigation for customers: extend pin_grace to 2m and disable staggered auto-commit until patch lands.


workaround:
Recommended mitigation applied for ClipperAI: extended tenant pin_grace to 120s and temporarily disabled staggered auto-commit in the dedicated pool. These changes prevented further mixed-routing during the next prewarm window.

root_cause:
Under investigation — initial SRE findings point to a race in the orchestrator's pin handoff logic where 'transfer_pending' metadata allowed edge reconcilers to consider the canary as active when central commit later aborted. Edge local-cache TTLs exacerbated the window of mixed routing.

resolution:
In progress — hotfix PR to change transfer_pending semantics and add explicit 'force-hold-until-commit' flag for pin leases. Once validated, we'll coordinate a staged rollout and notify the customer. Billing has started credit assessment for the duplicated usage records.

postmortem_plan:
If hotfix validates in staging, schedule emergency minor release to orchestrator, update runbook to recommend pin_grace >= prewarm window by default, add telemetry to detect duplicate-variant-usage spikes, and prepare customer-facing postmortem within 72 hours.

notes_for_engineering:
Add a guard in edge reconciler to ignore transfer_pending until explicit commit or explicit failover
Ensure billing deduplication keys include commit id or lease id to avoid double-charge on transient mixed-routing
Instrument metric: duplicate_variant_usage_ratio per-tenant to surface future regressions

[Split model pin handshake during prewarm + autoscale spike causes mixed-variant responses]
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (FastRetailer Inc.) reported intermittent mixed outputs from what should be a pinned variant during a canary rollout. Traffic was pinned at the route level to the new q3b build; however, ~1.5% of requests returned legacy-variant responses for a 6-hour window during a peak prewarm + autoscaler activity in us-east.

Impact:
- Customers observed inconsistent inference results for live personalization features (false positives in product recs).
- Estimated 1.5% of total requests for the tenant returned legacy model outputs between 2026-03-10T02:18Z and 2026-03-10T08:30Z.
- No data leakage reported; outputs were model-specific but functionally incorrect for pinned cohort.

Environment:
- Redwood Hosted dedicated capacity (customer dedicated pool) in us-east.
- Route: /v1/generate (tenant-specific route with explicit version pin to redwood/gpt-6b-q3b).
- Autoscaler policy: aggressive burst scaling (min 2, max 24 GPUs), prewarm enabled with shadow prewarm on new variant.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Deploy canary weight 10% -> orchestration triggers prewarm of new variant in dedicated pool.
2) Sudden client traffic spike (simulated by customer load test) causes autoscaler to spawn additional nodes and drain/populate caches.
3) Prewarm handshake to edge included an async cohort write to the routing-store while orchestrator was still reconciling a shard split.
4) A subset of edge proxies read an older cohort token from a local cache and returned legacy variant responses while control-plane showed pinned state.

Observed logs & artifacts:
- Edge proxy logs (excerpt):
  "2026-03-10T02:22:33Z EDGE[edge-12] route=tenant-17 cohort_read=cache_hit variant=legacy token_ttl=3s"
- Orchestrator event stream shows a prewarm commit and a concurrent shard-reshard event: "commit_prewarm:variant=q3b; shard-merge:start"
- Routing-store trace (debug): interleaved writes: write(v2_cohort) -> write(v1_cohort) with overlapping epochs.
- No 5xx spike; latency increased ~12% for pinned cohort during window.

Additional notes:
- Customer provided request IDs for samples. We verified mocked offline replay reproduces mixed-variant selection when prewarm and shard-merge overlap on a single orchestrator leader.
- Edge cookie TTL was configured aggressively (3s) and appeared to be a factor for fast-turnover cohorts.

Expected behavior:
- When a tenant pins a route to a variant, all requests for the pinned session should resolve to the pinned variant until an explicit unpin or rollout shift is performed. Prewarm should not allow legacy-variant responses for pinned sessions.


steps_to_reproduce:
Deploy canary with prewarm enabled and pin route to new variant
Generate sudden traffic spike concurrent with orchestrator shard-reshard
Observe routing-store epoch writes and edge cache reads for cohort tokens
Replay provided request IDs against test cluster with similar scaling profile

2026-03-10 03:10 - Aisha Patel (Support): Received customer report and sample request IDs. Notified SRE and assigned to oncall orchestrator owner.
2026-03-10 03:25 - SRE Triage (Riley Thompson): Observed shard-reshard events overlapping prewarm commits in logs. Marking as P1 and Sev1, engaging runtime team.
2026-03-10 08:45 - Liang Chen (Runtime Eng): Reproduced mixed-variant selection in internal repro harness. Hypothesis: non-atomic cohort write + edge cache TTL allowed transient reads of legacy cohort during reconciliation.
2026-03-11 11:05 - Marcelo Gonzalez (Orchestrator Eng): Confirmed orchestrator wrote two cohort records with same epoch when a leader transition happened during commit. Adding safeguard: write-idempotency + compare-and-swap on cohort epoch.

Customer's dedicated pool exposed the timing window because of their autoscaler profile and bursty traffic pattern.

[Cohort split and intermittent legacy-model routing during atomic rollout handshake]
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reported mixed outputs and occasional routing to an older model variant for a single tenant during a scheduled canary rollout. The tenant is explicitly pinned to a new model via the tenant-level pin API, but ~2-3% of requests observed over a 30-minute window were served by the legacy model.

Impact:
- Affects a production tenant (Acme Health) on enterprise plan.
- Incorrect model responses cause downstream QA failures and a temporary halt to a clinical inference workflow.
- Customer reported latency spikes coincident with misrouted responses.

Timeline (high level):
- 2024-05-11 09:00 UTC: Canary rollout initiated for redwood/open-13B-v2 -> new revision r2024-05-11.
- 2024-05-11 09:07 UTC: Control plane writes rollout snapshot; orchestrator starts slice-prewarm.
- 2024-05-11 09:12 UTC: Edge prewarm completed; tenant pin applied via pin API (confirmed by pin service).
- 2024-05-11 09:20-09:50 UTC: Customer observed intermittent legacy-model responses and raised this ticket.

Initial hypothesis:
- An ordering race between the atomic rollout handshake and edge session token rotation caused a cohort split: some edge nodes accepted the new snapshot but retained an older affinity mapping, causing requests from the same tenant to be routed to different variants.

Steps to reproduce (attempted):
1) Create a test tenant and explicitly pin to a new model revision.
2) Initiate a phased canary rollout with shadow prewarm and 5% traffic slice.
3) Trigger rapid edge reconnects by cycling a subset of edge proxies (simulated network blips).
4) Observe request routing and session affinity over 10k requests.

Observed logs and metrics:

[Consumption Telemetry Provenance and Crediting Specification]
Summary:
This design spec defines a single-source-of-truth for consumption telemetry provenance and the rules for crediting usage against customer contracts. The goal is to ensure that downstream billing, SLO-to-cost mapping, fidelity gating, and customer-facing dashboards all rely on consistent, auditable telemetry with deterministic crediting rules.

Audience:
- Product managers (pricing, packaging)
- Billing & finance engineers
- Observability and telemetry engineers
- Serving/runtime engineers
- Solutions and customer success teams owning onboarding

Goals:
1) Unambiguous provenance: every consumption event must include fields that allow any system to determine which contract, route, and fidelity setting should be charged.
2) Deterministic crediting: define the precedence rules and transformations used to map raw events to billable units and credits.
3) Minimal invasive instrumentation: reuse existing runtime events where possible and add clear enrichment layers rather than new event types.
4) Reconciliation readiness: include fields to support offline reconciliation and dispute investigations.

Scope and non-goals:
- In scope: hosted API, Dedicated reservation routing, and Private (control plane mediated) consumption events.
- Out of scope: raw on-prem kernel metrics, internal infra chargebacks, and ad-hoc manual credit issuance (these will be handled by separate playbooks).

Definitions (short):
- Consumption event: a single inference call or embedding request emitted by a runtime/edge proxy.
- Crediting: mapping consumption events to billable units or consumption credits.
- Provenance: metadata that identifies the origin, routing, policy decisions, and fidelity applied to the call.
- Fidelity: negotiated quality tier (e.g., high/standard/low), model variant, or quantization fallback applied at runtime.

Telemetry model (required fields):
Each consumption event emitted to the ingestion pipeline MUST contain the following canonical fields (human-readable table below):

| Field name | Type | Example | Purpose |
|------------|------|---------|---------|
| event_id | string | ev_01F8... | Unique event identifier for tracing and reconciliation |
| timestamp_utc | string (ISO8601) | 2029-11-30T13:22:05Z | Event creation time |
| customer_id | string | cus_2345 | Canonical tenant id used for billing lookup |
| route_id | string | r_prod_chat_v2 | API route or integration identifier |
| model_variant | string | gptx-7b-fp8 | Model variant used for generation |
| fidelity_tier | string | standard | Negotiated fidelity tier |
| tokens_input | integer | 72 | Input tokens measured by tokenizer |
| tokens_output | integer | 120 | Output tokens counted at finalization |
| latency_ms | integer | 134 | End-to-end latency observed at runtime |
| provenance_chain | string[] | ["ingress-proxy:edge-12","router:cost-aware-1","fallback:quantize-v2"] | Ordered list of routing/enrichment decisions (see semantics below) |
| credit_basis | string | tokens | Unit used for crediting (tokens, embed-vecs, requests) |
| credit_multiplier | number | 1.0 | Multiplier applied from pricing rules (e.g., fidelity multiplier) |
| billed_contract_id | string | con_99a | Contract used for billing; may be empty for pre-enrichment |
| ingestion_version | string | v2 | Version of telemetry schema/enrichment pipeline |

Note: provenance_chain is an array but stored as a flattened string in the event envelope (comma-separated) to maintain compatibility with current ES ingestion. In later versions we will support structured arrays in the pipeline.

Provenance semantics and normalization:
- The provenance_chain is defined as an ordered list of nodes that mutated or decided policy for the request. Each node uses pattern <component>:<id|reason>. Example: "router:latency-tiered-1" or "fallback:quantize-v2".
- Normalization rules: components should be stable identifiers (no ephemeral instance ids). Use standardized node ids maintained in the Runtime Component Registry.
- Enrichment layer (Enricher service): runtime emits a minimal event; the Enricher resolves customer->contract mapping, fidelity multipliers, and fills billed_contract_id. If enricher cannot map a contract, it sets billed_contract_id=null and flags the event with enrichment_status=partial.

Crediting rules (high level):
1) Determine credit basis: use credit_basis to map to pricing table (tokens, embeddings, requests).
2) Apply fidelity multiplier: multiply raw billable units by credit_multiplier before rounding.
3) Route-level overrides: If route has explicit override (route_override_multiplier), it takes precedence over fidelity multiplier.
4) Contract-level caps: If the resolved contract has caps or prepaid buckets, consumption should first decrement prepaid credits (FIFO by bucket age) and then create billed line items.
5) Rounding policy: round to nearest 0.01 credit unit. For token counts, convert using per-token granularity then apply multiplier.

Examples (policy application):
- Example 1: API call with tokens_input=100, tokens_output=200, credit_basis=tokens, credit_multiplier=1.25 => billable_tokens = 300 * 1.25 = 375 tokens => billed units = 375 
- Example 2: Embedding request credit_basis=embed-vecs, credit_multiplier=0.5, route_override_multiplier=1.0 => use route override => billed units computed with multiplier 1.0

Audit and reconciliation fields (recommended):
- raw_event_blob: base64-encoded original event payload (retained for 90 days)
- reconciliation_tag: string used to group events in offline runs (e.g., reconciliation_run_2029-11)
- dispute_flag: boolean | string reason (set by finance or CS)

Retention and privacy constraints:
- Retain full raw_event_blob for 90 days by default, purge thereafter unless flagged for dispute or compliance.
- Derived billing records (line items) kept for 7 years per finance retention policy.
- Customer-identifying fields must obey data residency rules; if a customer opts into ephemeral telemetry, customer_id must be hashed and a mapping table stored in a restricted store.

Backwards compatibility and versioning:
- ingestion_version is required. Consumers MUST support v1 and v2 semantics. v3 introduces structured arrays for provenance_chain and may change field names; migrations must be gated by ingestion_version checks.

Enrichment pipeline (implementation notes):
1) Ingress collects minimal event: event_id, timestamp, customer_id (or hashed id), route_id, tokens_* counts, model_variant, latency.
2) Enricher resolves billed_contract_id by querying Contract Resolver service and attaches contract metadata (tier, multipliers, caps).
3) Policy engine computes credit_multiplier and route overrides.
4) Output record written to the billing topic and to observability topic with reconciliation keys.

Schema migration plan (90-day rollout):
1) Week 0-4: Deploy Enricher in shadow mode; write enriched outputs to a new topic (billing-enriched-v2) but do not use for billing.
2) Week 5-8: Run daily reconciliation comparing existing billing topic vs enriched outputs; surface discrepancies to owners.
3) Week 9-12: Enable enrichment for non-critical routes (internal customers); continue monitoring.
4) Week 13-14: Enable for all routes and switch billing processors to enriched topic; deprecate v1 after 30 days.

Operational dashboards and alerts (recommended):
- Metric: enrichment_failure_rate > 0.1% over 1h => P1 to telemetry team.
- Metric: unassigned_contract_events_count > 1000/day => P1 to finance & solutions.
- Metric: crediting_delta_rate (enriched vs legacy) > 0.5% daily => review runbook.

Runbook excerpt: handling missing billed_contract_id
1) If enrichment_status==partial, route event to "missing-contract-queue" for manual or automated resolution.
2) On detection of spikes (>500 events/hour), pause auto-billing for affected customer_ids and open a finance ticket.
3) Notify CS owner and create a postmortem if >24 hours unresolved.

Sample event (ingested) payload (for implementers):
```
{
  "event_id": "ev_01F8XYZ",
  "timestamp_utc": "2029-11-30T13:22:05Z",
  "customer_id": "cus_2345",
  "route_id": "r_prod_chat_v2",
  "model_variant": "gptx-7b-fp8",
  "fidelity_tier": "standard",
  "tokens_input": 72,
  "tokens_output": 120,
  "latency_ms": 134,
  "provenance_chain": "ingress-proxy:edge-12,router:cost-aware-1",
  "credit_basis": "tokens",
  "ingestion_version": "v2"
}
```

Pricing & packaging implications (brief):
- This spec enables predictable mapping of negotiated fidelity multipliers and route overrides to billing. Product must publish a canonical mapping table (PR for PRD).
- Sales playbooks should reference crediting examples during contract negotiations.

Ownership and rollout stakeholders:
- Product (owner): Maya Thompson 
- Infra/Enricher implementation: Liang Chen
- Billing & Finance: Priya Kapoor
- Observability: Ethan Park
- CS: Sofia Martinez

Compatibility notes with Private deployments:
- Private deployment control plane must run a local Enricher or forward minimal events to Redwood control plane with explicit consent. Policy: if customer rejects remote enrichment, a restricted mapping artifact (signed contract token) must be provided during onboarding.

Open questions / decisions required:
1) Do we allow route-level multipliers to exceed contract multipliers? (security & finance implications)
2) Exact rounding granularity for fractional token multipliers (0.01 vs 0.001).
3) Should provenance_chain store component versions for stronger auditability?

References and related artifacts:
- Contract Resolver API spec (link internal)
- Billing processor playbook (link internal)
- Observability dashboard templates (link internal)

Appendix: Example reconciliation SQL (simplified)
```
SELECT e.event_id, e.customer_id, e.billed_contract_id, l.contract_id AS legacy_contract,
       (e.billable_units - l.billable_units) AS delta_units
FROM billing_enriched_v2 e
LEFT JOIN legacy_billing_lines l ON e.event_id = l.event_id
WHERE e.timestamp_utc >= '2029-11-01'::date;
```
End of spec.


[Audit events for Dedicated rollout actions (staged rollouts)]
## Overview
This document defines the audit logging requirements and event schema for **Dedicated staged rollouts for reserved pools**. It covers:
- Event types and semantics for actions: **create/update/promote/abort/hold/force overrides**
- Required fields for compliance, forensic review, and customer change management
- RBAC requirements (who can do what, and what must be logged)
- Retention and export (internal UI + customer export + SIEM)
- Example event payloads

This spec applies to all deployment modes of Dedicated pools (single-region and multi-region), and to all rollout targets (model version, runtime build, routing policy, config changes).

## Goals
1. **Deterministic & auditable change history**: A human reviewer can reconstruct what changed, who initiated it, when it took effect, what gates were evaluated, and why the system promoted/aborted.
2. **Tamper-evident audit trail** suitable for regulated customers’ change-management expectations.
3. **Low risk of sensitive data leakage** (no prompts, user content, or secrets).
4. **Consistent eventing across entry points** (Console, API, automated policy engine actions).

## Non-goals
- Provide a general-purpose eventing framework for all Redwood features.
- Store raw metrics time series in audit logs (we link to evidence queries and dashboards instead).

## Definitions
- **Dedicated pool**: Reserved GPU capacity pool associated with a customer account.
- **Rollout plan**: A staged plan applied to a Dedicated pool.
- **Stage**: A defined traffic/replica partition in the rollout.
- **Gate**: A set of criteria that must pass to promote a stage.
- **Actor**: The entity that initiated the action (human user, service principal, or system automation).

## Eventing principles
### 1) Where events are emitted
Events MUST be emitted server-side by the system of record for the action:
- Control plane service: **dedicated-pool-rollouts-service**
  - Creates/updates rollout plans
  - Processes promote/abort/hold/override requests
  - Emits canonical audit events
- Policy engine (if it triggers automated transitions)
  - MUST call control plane transition APIs; the control plane emits the audit event with actor_type=system and actor_service=policy-engine
- Console
  - MUST NOT emit audit events directly; it calls control plane APIs with end-user identity and request context

### 2) Idempotency and deduplication
- All mutating endpoints MUST support an **Idempotency-Key** (header) and return the same result for a retry.
- Audit events MUST include:
  - `request_id` (unique per request attempt)
  - `idempotency_key` (dedupe across retries)
  - `event_id` (globally unique)
- The audit pipeline MUST de-duplicate on `(event_id)`; consumers should use `(event_id)` as primary key.

### 3) Schema versioning
All events include:
- `schema_name`: `redwood.audit.dedicated_rollouts`
- `schema_version`: `1.0`

Backward-compatible changes (additive fields) keep the same version. Breaking changes require a version bump and coordinated export updates.

### 4) Privacy and data minimization
Audit events MUST NOT include:
- Prompts, completions, embeddings, customer payloads
- Secrets (API keys, tokens), KMS material
- Raw request/response bodies

Allowable data includes:
- Resource identifiers, stage indices, stage configs at a high level
- Threshold configuration (numbers/percentages) and summarized observed values
- Links to internal dashboards / evidence queries

### 5) Time
All timestamps MUST be RFC3339 UTC (e.g., `2025-03-12T21:14:33Z`).

## Event taxonomy
All event types share a prefix and use dotted naming:
- `dedicated.rollout_plan.created`
- `dedicated.rollout_plan.updated`
- `dedicated.rollout_plan.promotion_requested`
- `dedicated.rollout_plan.promoted`
- `dedicated.rollout_plan.aborted`
- `dedicated.rollout_plan.held`
- `dedicated.rollout_plan.resumed`
- `dedicated.rollout_plan.force_promoted`
- `dedicated.rollout_plan.force_aborted`
- `dedicated.rollout_plan.gate_evaluation_recorded`

Notes:
- We separate `promotion_requested` from `promoted` to capture async workflows.
- `gate_evaluation_recorded` is emitted when the system evaluates gates and persists a result that affected promotion/abort/hold decisions.

## Common event envelope (required fields)
Each event MUST contain the following fields (names are stable; values vary by event type):

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---|
| event_id | string | yes | UUIDv7 recommended |
| event_type | string | yes | One of taxonomy values |
| occurred_at | string | yes | RFC3339 UTC |
| schema_name | string | yes | `redwood.audit.dedicated_rollouts` |
| schema_version | string | yes | `1.0` |
| environment | string | yes | `prod`, `staging`, etc. |
| region | string | yes | Control plane region emitting the event |
| actor_type | string | yes | `human` \| `service` \| `system` |
| actor_id | string | yes | User ID or service principal ID |
| actor_email | string | no | For humans when available |
| actor_service | string | no | e.g., `console-backend`, `policy-engine` |
| actor_ip | string | no | If sourced from user action |
| authn_method | string | no | e.g., `sso`, `api_key`, `service_token` |
| request_id | string | yes | Trace/request correlation ID |
| idempotency_key | string | no | If supplied |
| account_id | string | yes | Customer account ID owning the pool |
| org_id | string | no | Internal org mapping if applicable |
| dedicated_pool_id | string | yes | The Dedicated pool |
| rollout_plan_id | string | yes | Stable rollout plan identifier |
| rollout_plan_version | string | yes | Optimistic concurrency version (integer serialized as string) |
| console_session_id | string | no | If triggered via Console |
| change_reason | string | no | Required for overrides; recommended otherwise |
| ticket_ref | string | no | e.g., `INC-...`, `SUP-...`, `JIRA-...`, `LINEAR-...` |
| severity | string | no | `info` \| `warning` \| `critical` (for override/abort) |
| outcome | string | yes | `success` \| `failure` |
| error_code | string | no | If failure |
| error_message | string | no | Sanitized; no secrets |

### Resource identity conventions
- `account_id`, `dedicated_pool_id`, `rollout_plan_id` MUST be globally unique identifiers.
- For multi-region pools, the event should still reference the single pool; region-specific details belong in the per-event payload (see below).

## Event-specific payload requirements
Event-specific fields MUST be included in the same JSON object as the envelope (no nested objects required by this spec), but nested structures are allowed in storage/export. When constrained to flat export (e.g., some SIEM sinks), use `payload_json` as a string.

For internal storage (Audit Log Store), nested JSON is allowed; for this Confluence spec, examples show nested JSON for readability.

### dedicated.rollout_plan.created
Emitted when a rollout plan is created.

Required additional fields:
- `rollout_target_type`: `model_version` \| `runtime_build` \| `routing_policy` \| `config_bundle`
- `rollout_target_ref`: stable reference (e.g., model id + version)
- `stages_count`
- `stage_spec_summary`: short string summary (e.g., `1%/10%/50%/100%` or `replicas: 1/2/5/all`)
- `initial_state`: expected `draft` or `running`

### dedicated.rollout_plan.updated
Emitted when the plan definition is modified (before running) or when allowed editable fields are changed.

Required additional fields:
- `updated_fields`: list of field paths (stringified)
- `before_hash`, `after_hash`: stable hashes of canonicalized plan spec for tamper-evidence and quick diffing
- `edit_policy`: `allowed` \| `restricted` (indicates whether edit was permitted during running state)

### dedicated.rollout_plan.promotion_requested
Emitted when a promotion is requested (human or system). This is important even if later denied.

Required additional fields:
- `from_stage_id`
- `to_stage_id`
- `requested_by`: `human` \| `system`

### dedicated.rollout_plan.promoted
Emitted when promotion completes and routing/pool partitioning is updated.

Required additional fields:
- `from_stage_id`
- `to_stage_id`
- `promotion_mode`: `standard` \| `force`
- `gate_summary`: `passed` \| `skipped` \| `failed` \| `unknown`
- `routing_commit_id`: identifier of the routing config snapshot applied
- `effective_at`: RFC3339 timestamp when the new stage became effective

### dedicated.rollout_plan.aborted
Emitted when the rollout is aborted.

Required additional fields:
- `abort_reason`: `gate_failure` \| `operator_action` \| `system_safety` \| `capacity_safety` \| `telemetry_missing` \| `other`
- `rollback_to_stage_id`: typically previous stable stage, often `0` (baseline)
- `in_flight_policy`: `pinned` \| `drain_then_reroute` (per streaming semantics)

### dedicated.rollout_plan.held / resumed
Emitted when the rollout enters/exits hold state.

Required additional fields:
- `hold_reason` (for held)
- `hold_timeout_seconds` (if applicable)

### dedicated.rollout_plan.force_promoted / force_aborted
Emitted when an admin override is used.

Required additional fields:
- `override_type`: `force_promote` \| `force_abort`
- `override_scope`: `single_stage` \| `entire_rollout`
- `override_approver_id` (if dual-approval is enabled; optional in v1)
- `override_guardrails`: string summary of guardrails presented to actor (e.g., “requires dedicated_rollouts.admin; reason required; customer-visible”) 

Policy:
- `change_reason` MUST be provided.
- `severity` MUST be `warning` or `critical`.

### dedicated.rollout_plan.gate_evaluation_recorded
Emitted when gate evaluation is computed and persisted (including missing-data outcomes).

Required additional fields:
- `stage_id`
- `evaluation_window_seconds`
- `evaluation_start_at`, `evaluation_end_at`
- `gate_outcome`: `passed` \| `failed` \| `unknown`
- `missing_data_policy`: `fail_closed` \| `fail_open` \| `manual`
- `gate_evidence_uri`: link to Console evidence view (stable, permission-checked)
- `gate_evidence_summary`: short human-readable string

Recommended additional fields (when safe and not too high-cardinality):
- `observed_error_rate`, `threshold_error_rate`
- `observed_p95_ms`, `threshold_p95_ms`
- `observed_saturation`, `threshold_saturation`
- `observed_oom_rate`, `threshold_oom_rate`

## RBAC requirements (actions and who can perform them)
### Roles
This spec assumes the following RBAC concepts (names are representative; implementation may map to Redwood’s authz system):
- `dedicated_rollouts.viewer`: read-only access to rollout plans and audit trail
- `dedicated_rollouts.operator`: can create plans, request promotion/abort/hold for eligible pools
- `dedicated_rollouts.admin`: can force overrides; can operate across accounts where allowed
- `customer_admin`: customer-side admin (Dedicated customer) with limited rollout controls if enabled

### RBAC enforcement MUST be auditable
For any request that results in an audit event:
- The server MUST enforce RBAC.
- If RBAC denies, emit an audit event with:
  - `event_type`: same action family (e.g., `dedicated.rollout_plan.promotion_requested`)
  - `outcome`: `failure`
  - `error_code`: `forbidden`
  - `actor_id`, `account_id`, `dedicated_pool_id` populated

This creates a record of attempted access (important for regulated environments).

### Actions matrix (v1)
- Create plan: operator/admin (and optionally customer_admin on allowlisted accounts)
- Update plan:
  - In `draft`: operator/admin
  - In `running`: restricted to admin-only fields (e.g., gate thresholds if allowed) — emit `edit_policy=restricted`
- Promote stage:
  - Standard: operator/admin
  - Force: admin only (always requires `change_reason`)
- Abort rollout:
  - Standard: operator/admin
  - Force abort: admin only
- Hold/resume:
  - Operator/admin; holds over N hours may require admin (configurable)

## Retention, storage, and export
### Retention policy
- Audit Log Store (internal): **400 days** hot retention.
- Cold archive (compliance): **7 years** for events associated with accounts flagged as regulated (e.g., financial services) and for all `force_*` override events.
- Customer-facing export availability:
  - Default: **180 days**
  - Enterprise add-on: up to **400 days** (matches hot retention)

### Storage and access
- Primary store: `auditlog-prod` (write-once append semantics).
- Access:
  - Security & Compliance: read for all accounts
  - SRE/Platform oncall: read for operational troubleshooting
  - Customer Admins: read limited to their `account_id` and filtered fields

### SIEM export
- Export pipeline MUST include all events in this schema to the SIEM sink with the same `event_id`.
- Latency objective: events available in SIEM within **5 minutes** p95.
- If export fails, events remain in primary store; export retries must not create duplicates.

### Field redaction rules
Before exporting to customer or SIEM:
- Remove internal-only fields as needed (e.g., some `actor_ip` values may be internal proxy IPs; keep end-user IP when present).
- Do not include internal hostnames, node IDs, or GPU serials in customer export.
- `error_message` must be sanitized to avoid including secrets.

## Required audit coverage (what MUST produce events)
The following API endpoints / operations MUST generate audit events:
- POST `/v1/dedicated-pools/{pool_id}/rollout-plans` -> `dedicated.rollout_plan.created`
- PATCH `/v1/dedicated-rollout-plans/{plan_id}` -> `dedicated.rollout_plan.updated`
- POST `/v1/dedicated-rollout-plans/{plan_id}:promote` -> `promotion_requested` + `promoted` (if completed) or failure record
- POST `/v1/dedicated-rollout-plans/{plan_id}:abort` -> `aborted`
- POST `/v1/dedicated-rollout-plans/{plan_id}:hold` -> `held`
- POST `/v1/dedicated-rollout-plans/{plan_id}:resume` -> `resumed`
- POST `/v1/dedicated-rollout-plans/{plan_id}:force-promote` -> `force_promoted` (+ `promoted` with `promotion_mode=force` if separate)
- POST `/v1/dedicated-rollout-plans/{plan_id}:force-abort` -> `force_aborted` (+ `aborted` with `abort_reason=operator_action` if separate)
- Gate evaluator persistence (policy engine / telemetry pipeline) -> `gate_evaluation_recorded`

- Audit events must be queryable by:
  - `account_id`, `dedicated_pool_id`, `rollout_plan_id`
  - `event_type`, `actor_id`, time range
  - `ticket_ref`
- Console must provide an **Audit Trail** tab for rollout plans (separate design doc), backed by the audit store.
- Support must be able to export a CSV/JSON report for a given plan/pool/time window.

## Testing and validation
- Unit tests: verify each mutating endpoint emits exactly one event per successful state transition.
- Integration tests: retry the same promote request with the same idempotency key; confirm only one promotion event is recorded.
- Security tests: ensure `error_message` sanitization and no secrets.
- Export tests: ensure events arrive in SIEM and customer export with stable `event_id`.

## Open questions
1. Dual-approval for overrides: do we require `override_approver_id` in v1 for regulated accounts?
2. Customer visibility: do we show `actor_email` for Redwood staff in customer exports, or map to a role-based label (e.g., “Redwood Operator”)?
3. Cold archive scope: should all Dedicated rollout events be 7-year archived or only regulated/override-related?
