[Traffic escrow and rehearse proxy for staged promotes]
body:
Motivation:
We frequently observe that promotes that look good on telemetry during a short canary window still cause edge-case regressions once given full traffic. This PR introduces two complementary primitives: (1) a traffic_escrow service that holds routing decisions and only releases commits once a rehearse pass and smoke policy succeed, and (2) a rehearse_proxy that can inject synthetic canary traffic and replay recorded request traces into candidate serving revisions without affecting production state.

Goals:
- Allow operators to stage promotes with a commit escrow lease that requires an endorsement from rehearse results before full cutover.
- Provide a reproducible, auditable rehearse run that exercises session affinity, header routing, and KV cache warmup without serving user writes to production.
- Reduce time-to-revert via an escrow ledger that records the include/exclude criteria, lease owner, and rehearse outcomes per promote.

What this PR contains (single-string description):
Implemented a TrafficEscrow controller, a RehearseProxy sidecar + router middleware, a small replay harness for synthetic canaries (replay driver + sampler), and related observability (metrics, traces, and a prometheus scrape target). Included an admin API to grant/revoke escrow leases and an operator CLI hook to trigger a rehearse run. The rehearsals are configurable with smoke policies and timeout/rollback thresholds.

Checklist:
- [x] TrafficEscrow controller + database-backed ledger (sqlite for dev, Postgres migration script included)
- [x] RehearseProxy middleware for routing and replay isolation
- [x] Replay driver and synthetic canary harness with pluggable samplers
- [x] Feature flag gating (rollout.traffic_escrow) and integration tests
- [x] Prometheus metrics + tracing spans for rehearse runs
- [x] Operator CLI commands and docs stub

High-level commits:
- commit 1: controller: add TrafficEscrow CRD and schema, controller reconciliation loop with lease lifecycle
- commit 2: middleware: rehearse proxy router and headers + session-affinity passthrough
- commit 3: replay: synthetic canary driver and reservoir sampler, smoke policy evaluator
- commit 4: telemetry: metrics, traces, and prometheus target
- commit 5: migrations: add escrow ledger table and migration script
- commit 6: tests: e2e rehearse integration tests + unit tests for policy evaluator

Changed files (high level):
- services/traffic-escrow/controller.go (new)
- services/traffic-escrow/ledger/migrations/0001_create_escrow_table.sql (new)
- services/traffic-escrow/api/escrow.proto (new)
- runtime/middleware/rehearse_proxy.go (new)
- runtime/replay/driver.go (new)
- runtime/replay/sampler.go (new)
- deploy/helm/templates/escrow-deployment.yaml (mod)
- observability/metrics/escrow_metrics.go (new)
- cli/ops/escrow_cli.go (new)
- docs/ops/traffic-escrow.md (new)
- tests/e2e/rehearse_integration_test.go (new)

Small illustrative snippet (rehearse proxy header handling):

func (rp *RehearseProxy) ServeHTTP(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    if rp.isRehearseRun(r) {
        // tag and route to candidate revision; keep responses sandboxed
        r.Header.Set("X-Rehearse-Run", rp.currentLeaseID)
        rp.routeToCandidate(w, r)
        return
    }
    rp.routeNormal(w, r)
}

(Full diffs are intentionally small here; implementation files are focused and mostly additive.)

Operational notes:
- Default behavior is a no-op until rollout.traffic_escrow is enabled.
- The escrow ledger keeps soft TTLs for leases; expired leases auto-fail after the configured grace period.
- Rehearse runs can be run in parallel for non-overlapping cohorts; controller rejects overlapping leases by default to avoid double-warmup.

Review thread summary (single string):
See reviewers list for full thread. Key points from review: Liam asked for stronger invariants around overlapping leases; addressed by adding overlap detection in the controller and a unit test. Maya requested clearer observability for rehearse runs; added metrics and traces and a prometheus scrape target with labels rehearse_run and cohort_id. Diego recommended a Postgres migration rather than sqlite for staging; added migration and a readme about storage backends. CI flakes on the first run due to a timing issue in the replay sampler; fixed by adding deterministic seeding in tests.

Selected review comments and replies:
- Liam O'Connor (2026-02-16): "Controller needs deterministic behavior when two promotes touch the same cohort. How does reclamation work?"
  - Author reply (Priya): "Added overlap checks and a ReclaimLease method; controller now serializes conflicting lease requests and exposes a metric escrow_conflicts_total."

- Maya Li (2026-02-18): "Can we get a top-level metric that shows rehearse run pass/fail ratio over the last 24h?"
  - Author reply: "Added rehearse_run_result_total{outcome=\"pass\"|\"fail\"} and example dashboard panels in docs/ops."

- Diego Alvarez (2026-02-19): "DB choice: use Postgres in staging. Please include migration and docs."
  - Author reply: "Included migration script and a small switch in config to pick sqlite for dev, postgres for staging/prod."

CI and test summary:
- CI pipeline: unit (go test), linters (golangci-lint), integration (docker-compose rehearse harness), e2e (k8s kind).
- Run 1: unit/lint passed, integration timed out (race in replay sampler), rerun tests after deterministic seeding.
- Run 2: all checks passed.

Post-merge actions:
- Enable rollout.traffic_escrow behind a canary flag for SRE on a single cluster for two weeks (ENG-2401).
- Run a handful of rehearses using recorded traces to validate session-affinity and cache warmups.
- Add a small playbook to run a fast revert if rehearse failures exceed threshold.

Why this is different from existing rollout features:
This PR focuses on the concept of escrowed commits plus a rehearse proxy that allows routing and replay isolation so that candidate revisions can be exercised end-to-end without touching production state. Existing staged promote primitives at Redwood emphasize traffic phasing and shadowing; traffic escrow gives an operator-level commit gating primitive with a ledger and rehearsals that are auditable and replayable.

Risk assessment:
- Low to medium risk: mostly additive components behind feature flags. The largest surface is the rehearse proxy which touches routing; we've guarded it with feature flag gating and unit tests.

Notes for on-call and SRE:
- Metric to watch: escrow_conflicts_total, rehearse_run_result_total, rehearse_run_duration_seconds_bucket, rehearsal_sandbox_errors_total.
- CLI: redwood ops escrow grant --lease-id=<id> --cohort=<name> --owner=<user>

If any follow-ups are requested, they will be tracked in ENG-1024 and ENG-2401.

release_notes:
Adds a traffic escrow component and a rehearse-proxy to allow dry-run rehearsals of staged promotes. No API changes for external customers; operational feature behind feature flag. Improves safety for deferred promotes and reduces blast radius of bad promotes by enabling synthetic canary replays and commit-escrow leases.

Diego Alvarez: Use Postgres in staging; add migration and docs for storage backends.
SRE: Flag gating and rollout plan required before enabling in prod; recommended a canary cluster run.

[Introduce Rehearsal Lanes: dry-run cohorts and rollback advisor]
description:
Summary:
This PR adds a new rollout primitive — Rehearsal Lanes — that allow teams to run deterministic dry-run cohorts (rehearsals) before promoting models into live canaries or A/B lanes. Motivation: many incidents stem from behavioral regressions that only appear under production traffic mixes; rehearsals provide a lightweight, observable rehearsal path that exercises routing, KV caching, and downstream integrations with synthetic smoke datasets and sampled real sessions.

What changed (single string):
- Core runtime: new RehearsalScheduler and RehearsalController (planner) that coordinate dry-run cohorts tied to existing rollout objects. Rehearsals are replay-driven: they can replay recent production sessions (session sampling) or run synthetic smoke vectors. Rehearsal lanes are traffic-free: they never return responses to end users but exercise the full inference path, caches, and feature hooks.
- Rollout API: added new optional fields to the rollout spec: "rehearsal": {"enabled":"bool","sample_rate":"float","mode":"synthetic|replay","smoke_set_id":"string"} (note: schema additions are backward compatible; new fields are optional). Added endpoints to schedule immediate rehearsals and to list rehearsal runs with telemetry snapshots.
- Console/UI: Rehearsal run timeline, replay logs, per-run smoke metrics, and a one-click "promote after rehearsal" button. UI surfaces rehearsal failures and links to the rollback advisor.
- Telemetry: rehearsal-specific telemetry labels (rehearsal.run_id, rehearsal.mode, smoke_set) and a new rehearsal-pass/fail signal feeding the rollout gate engine. Telemetry snapshots are retained for 30 days for faster bisect.
- Rollout safety: integrated Rehearsal -> Gate link: rehearsal failures can be wired to block canary promotion automatically, or generate an advisory ticket. Added a small rollback-advisor module that analyzes recent rehearsal run diffs, top-line SLO regressions, and suggests one of: revert, pause-and-investigate, or proceed-with-canary. Advisor outputs a human-readable rationale and confidence score.
- Test infra: end-to-end rehearsal test harness, synthetic smoke generator (100+ vectors), and integration tests that verify session affinity and KV cache warmup behavior.
- Docs: new docs page (operational runbook) and quickstart tutorial for creating rehearsal lanes and interpreting advisor recommendations.

Commits summary:
- c1a9f6b: initial RehearsalController + scheduler implementation (planner + basic API)
- 34b2d11: add rehearsal telemetry labels and storage snapshotting
- 7d4f2c0: console components and rehearsal timeline UI
- 9f3a8aa: rollback advisor heuristics and scoring engine
- a6e2b98: synthetic smoke generator + test vectors
- b51c4d7: e2e rehearsal test harness and CI job
- f8c3d21: docs and runbook + tutorial updates

Files touched (high-level):
- src/runtime/rehearsal/controller.rs
- src/runtime/rehearsal/scheduler.rs
- src/api/rollouts/schema_v2.rs
- src/api/rollouts/handlers/rehearsal.rs
- web/console/src/components/RehearsalTimeline.tsx
- web/console/src/hooks/useRehearsalRuns.ts
- infra/telemetry/rehearsal_labels.yaml
- tests/e2e/rehearsal_harness.py
- tools/smokegen/README.md

Motivation and design notes (concise):
- Rehearsals must be non-intrusive: they must not consume live quota for user-facing endpoints or change downstream state. This PR enforces a replay-only mode by default and provides opt-in hooks for safe downstream simulation.
- Emphasis on early detection: rehearsals run the same code paths as production (runtime kernels, batching, kv-cache) and surface performance and quality regressions earlier than shadow-to-canary transitions.
- Advisor is intentionally conservative: it recommends revert or investigate in high-confidence regressions and only recommends proceed-with-canary when signal is weak and performance is stable.

Backward compatibility and migration notes:
- Rollout specs without rehearsal fields behave unchanged. The schema change is additive. Existing rollout controllers ignore rehearsal fields if absent.
- Console feature flag gated at rollout.preview.rehearsal until next minor release (to allow staged enablement for production tenants).

Testing and CI:
- Added nightly CI job: ci/rehearsal-e2e that runs the harness with 3 smoke sets and asserts no unexpected downstream writes.
- Unit tests cover scheduling logic, gating interactions, and advisor scoring thresholds.

Operational considerations:
- Resource accounting: rehearsals run on low-priority pool by default and carry a configurable quota. We added a quota-meter and billing tag to ensure rehearsal runs are tracked but not billed to production token budgets.
- Data retention: rehearsal session snapshots are scrubbed of PII and retained per privacy policy.

Release notes: "Add Rehearsal Lanes (dry-run cohorts) to rollout API; include console support, telemetry, and a rollback advisor to help detect regressions before canary promotions."

What's next (future work):
- Add automated rehearsal scheduling based on anomaly detection windows (follow-up PR).
- Native integration with Dedicated to run rehearsals against pinned GPU pools for performance-sensitive models.

Ravi Patel (approve): Tests look good; minor nits on log verbosity fixed.

[orchestrated-rewind-adjudicator-with-synthetic-smoke]
description:
Motivation: Rollouts that rely solely on passive telemetry and long-running A/B experiments often detect regressions too late for low-latency LLM inference workloads. This change introduces the Rewind Adjudicator, an operator-side component that orchestrates short-lived staged shadow rehearsals using a synthetic smoke runner to accelerate regression signal and provide an actionable rollback suggestion. Design summary: The adjudicator is a stateful controller that can be enabled per rollout via helm values or the rollout spec. It coordinates three phases: 1) Dry rehearsal where a bounded subset of traffic is shadowed and replayed deterministically against a candidate revision; 2) Synthetic smoke where generated prompts (user-provided or default prompt bank) exercise known SLO-sensitive slices and produce a compact metrics digest; 3) Decision adjudication where telemetry anchors (latency P95, token-cost delta, accuracy proxy via eval hooks) are compared against configured fidelity gates and historical baselines to compute a risk score and suggested action. Key behaviors: - Non-blocking: when the adjudicator is experimental it only attaches suggestions to the rollout decision; when promoted it can block promotion until gates pass. - Deterministic replay seeding ensures reproducible smoke runs for postmortem. - Graceful fallback: if the adjudicator or replay runner fails the orchestrator continues with existing staged rollout policy and records the failure as an event for triage. API and surface changes: - rollout.spec.adjudicator.{enabled,mode,probeSet} new fields to opt-in and configure synthetic smoke parameters. - rdctl adjudicator subcommand: rdctl rollout adjudicator status|replay|force-rollback. - Console panel to visualize adjudicator decisions and replay traces. Testing and rollout plan: Unit coverage for the decision logic and telemetry extraction. E2E suite triggers a short staged shadow rehearsal and asserts the adjudicator suggests rollback under injected regression signals. Feature gated behind helm.values.rollouts.adjudicator.enabled=false by default. Observability: added Prometheus rules and tracing annotations for adjudicator-run.{start,success,fail} and a compact decision event schema emitted to the event bus for easier SLO backfills. Security and compliance: replayed inputs are masked by default using existing PII redaction hooks; customers can opt into raw replays via Private deployments and KMS-wrapped storage. Backwards compatibility: no changes to the public runtime API. Migration: operators can enable the adjudicator per-rollout incrementally and tune probe sets with the new rdctl CLI. Impact: expected to reduce mean time to detect latent regressions in canary/promote flows by surfacing actionable signals within minutes rather than hours. Related work: builds on ENG-7201 (staged-shadow plumbing) and complements ENG-7920 (telemetry anchors). Linear: ENG-8421 and ENG-8479. CI matrix: flaky test adjusted and stabilized in e2e harness. Merge notes: squad validated on dedicated staging cluster for three days with controlled traffic and synthetic regressions applied.

release_notes:
Adds a Rewind Adjudicator that coordinates staged shadow rehearsals and automatic rollback suggestions based on synthetic smoke results and user-configured fidelity gates. No breaking API changes.

Asha Patel (author): Default behavior now applies redactPipeline to all replay inputs. Added docs in cmd/rdctl/rollback_adjudicator.md and a helm toggle to opt into raw replays for Private installs.

If adjudicator causes unexpected blocking, disable by setting rollouts.adjudicator.enabled=false and trigger rdctl rollout adjudicator force-rollback to revert suggestions.

[Lane Attestor: traffic gating with resume-safe rollback and payload-sanitized shadowing]
description:
Context: As we scale multi-stage rollouts (shadow -> canary -> promote) we observed rare but user-visible regressions caused by payload-sensitive model behavior and partial session handoffs. This PR implements a 'Lane Attestor' that augments our rollout pipeline with: 1) real-time attestation signals (smoke test pass, schema conformance, hallucination proxy score) used as gates; 2) sanitized shadowing for A/B analysis to avoid leaking broken inputs to downstream services; 3) resume-safe rollback anchors that preserve session affinity and allow immediate traffic rewinds without dropping in-flight sessions. What changed (high level): - New attestor core and policy engine (serving/orchestrator/attestor) that evaluates per-cohort signals and emits gate decisions. - Shadow proxy: sanitizes and tags shadow payloads, forwards them to variant replicas and to the replay buffer. - Rollback anchors: checkpointed session leases and lightweight snapshotting so a rollback can rehydrate session state and resume with the previous model variant. - Operator surface: Helm values, console flags, and a runbook for manual intervention. - Tests: unit, integration, and an e2e canary-sim harness. Rollout plan: staged rollout through Dedicated -> Hosted: 0.1 -> 0.25 -> 0.5 -> 1.0 with 30-minute holdpoints. Automatic rollback triggers: (a) latency P95 increase > 35% for 10 minutes; (b) hallucination-proxy rate > 3% absolute increase vs baseline for 10 minutes; (c) HTTP error rate > 0.5% absolute increase for 5 minutes. Manual operator steps documented in docs/runbooks/lane-attestor-playbook.md. Checklist: - [x] Core attestor runtime implemented - [x] Shadow sanitization + replay buffer integration - [x] Rollback anchors + session checkpoint tests - [x] Helm chart values and kube manifests - [x] Console feature flag + dashboards - [x] E2E canary simulation harness - [x] Docs/playbook and Linear tickets linked Testing notes: unit and integration tests added; canary-sim replicates production traffic distribution and validates rollback anchor behavior. Metrics to watch: token-level cost, P95 latency, hallucination-proxy rate, end-to-end success rate, replay buffer lag. Related: ENG-1942 (attestor design doc), ENG-2067 (session checkpointing), SUP-342 (customer incident that motivated safe rollbacks).

release_notes:
Introduces the Lane Attestor component: a lightweight attestation layer that gates canary and shadow traffic based on fast semantic smoke checks, payload sanitization, and session-safe rollback anchors. Adds operator playbook and Helm values for Private deployments.

notes_for_release:
Feature gated behind 'attestor' console flag and helm value. Default off for existing orgs; opt-in recommended for new clusters. Operators should follow docs/runbooks/lane-attestor-playbook.md for manual rollback playbook. Monitor metrics: attestor.gate_denials, replay_buffer.lag_ms, session.anchor_restore_failures.

[Rate-window oscillation during scheduled batched ingest causing intermittent 429s after auth refresh]
description:
Customer reports intermittent 429 responses during their nightly batched ingest run after they enabled short-lived credential rotation. Symptoms appear as small bursts of successful uploads followed by repeated 429s for 30-90s, then normal traffic resumes. The pattern repeats roughly every 5-8 minutes during the job window.

impact:
Multiple failed batch chunks in nightly ETL job; downstream indexer saw partial data and required manual retries. Estimated 15% of batches failed during the 2-hour window. Customer requests guidance and a mitigation path to prevent data loss and reduce retries.

steps_to_reproduce:
1) Set up a dedicated pool account with short-lived signed API keys (TTL ~ 5 minutes).
2) Run concurrent uploader workers that reauthenticate on TTL expiry and immediately restart chunk uploads without jitter.
3) Observe client-side logs showing simultaneous signed-key refresh and then a flood of requests to /v1/embeddings endpoint.
4) Check server responses: initial small window of OKs then a wave of 429s; repeating every few minutes as refill windows interact with auth refreshes.

logs:
Gateway logs: token_accounting: window_refill=1610ms drift=+420ms; per-route-burst_used=1523; tenant_credit_left=480
Rate limiter trace (2026-03-10T02:14:23Z): owner=streamlytics-route-19 refill_epoch=1641 sawtooth_delta=+1.2s counts=[ok=312, throttled=47]
Auth service: issued short-lived key id=sk_tmp_4a2 exp=2026-03-10T02:19:00Z; multiple near-simultaneous refreshes from 10 workers
Customer uploader logs: 429 count spikes at 02:14:26Z, 02:21:35Z, 02:28:42Z (interval ~7m)

investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: simultaneous short-lived key rotation across uploader workers creates a burst that aligns with the rate-limiter refill epoch causing a sawtooth/oscillation effect.
Confirmed via trace correlation: gateway token window refills occur on a fixed epoch and the client's reauth fanout often fell within the same refill window after TTL expiry.
Observed additional contributing factor: dedicated-pool per-route burst pool was configured conservatively; tenant-level smoothing parameter (smoothing_factor) set to low value causing coarse refill granularity.
Reproduced in staging by simulating 12 workers reauthing at TTL expiry without jitter and running concurrent chunk uploads; saw identical repeating 429 pattern.
Temporary mitigation trial: staggered reauth in staging with +/- 60s jitter eliminated the oscillation. Increasing per-route burst pool size to 8x reduced visible throttles but did not fully remove sawtooth under worst-case fanout.
Found a gateway accounting edge-case: when a short-lived key is reused across HTTP/2 multiplexed connections the token-window bookkeeping occasionally double-counts the preflight for each stream; created issue INT-3392.
Logged related gateway PR that addressed double-counting: github.com/redwood-inference/gateway/pull/612 (fixes preflight-accounting on multiplexed streams).

Streamlytics 2026-03-11: Implemented jitter and saw immediate reduction in 429s during next run. Asked for permanent config recommendation and whether Redwood can adjust burst pool for their dedicated tenant.

Scoped a controlled config change to the customer's dedicated pool to increase per-route burst allocation from 2->16 for nightly ingest windows; change scheduled 2026-03-13 03:00 UTC with rollback plan. Gateway double-counting bug fix merged and staged (PR #612). Customer reported immediate improvement after jitter; final verification pending post-maintenance run.

[Periodic tenant-wide 429 waves when signed-url refreshes coincide with telemetry flush sweeps]
description:
Issue summary:
BrightCart reported recurring 429 throttles that affect a large proportion of their tenant traffic in short waves (~45–90s) during today’s rolling warmup window. Pattern appears correlated with two independent scheduled operations: (A) client-side signed-url refresh processes (many short-lived clients renewing credentials in tight windows) and (B) BrightCart’s nightly telemetry flush (lots of background POSTs to ingestion endpoints).

Impact:
- ~30% of requests from BrightCart receive 429s for short bursts, causing degraded UX for interactive flows (timeouts on chat widgets).
- Incident is customer-visible in prod-us-west and affects both text-generation and embedding routes.

Environment:
- Customer tenant: brightcart-prod (enterprise)
- Deployment: Redwood hosted (dedicated capacity pool for tenant)
- Region: us-west
- Observed during scheduled warmup window: 03:00–03:30 UTC daily

Requested outcome:
- Understand why these short bursts are being counted as tenant-wide quota exhaustion rather than being isolated to background sweep traffic.
- Recommend short-term mitigation and long-term config changes to prevent overlap-induced 429 waves.

steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer runs scheduled telemetry flush job that posts ~2000 small payloads concurrently to /v1/ingest with signed-url auth (occurs at 03:05 UTC).
2) Simultaneously, a fleet of client workers perform signed-url refresh and immediately open short-lived streaming sessions to check status (~500 concurrent sessions).
3) Within 10–30s of overlap, platform rate limiter begins returning 429 to interactive and ingest routes for the tenant.
4) Wave persists ~45–90s then subsides as refill window progresses and background sweep finishes.

logs:
2026-03-10T03:05:12Z edge-proxy[ingress] INFO tenant=brightcart req_id=abc123 status=200 path=/v1/ingest size=512
2026-03-10T03:05:14Z rate-limiter WARN tenant=brightcart token_window=short refill_remaining=0 rejected=120
2026-03-10T03:05:16Z edge-proxy[ingress] ERROR tenant=brightcart req_id=def456 status=429 path=/v1/generate reason=rate_limit_exceeded
2026-03-10T03:06:40Z scheduler INFO job=telemetry-flush completed payloads=1978 duration=95s

comments:
Maya Patel (Support) - 2026-03-10: Customer opened ticket with console screenshots and a timeline showing 429 peaks matching their telemetry flush. Asked for immediate mitigation during nightly window.
Jeremy Cho (SRE) - 2026-03-10: Acknowledged. Requested sample request IDs, edge-proxy access logs, and tenant quota accounting snapshot for 03:00–03:10 UTC.
BrightCart Ops (customer) - 2026-03-11: Provided signed-url refresh cadence (every 60s across 500 workers, default jitter disabled) and telemetry flush job manifest. They can reschedule within 2 hours if needed.
Omar Velasquez (Rate-limiter eng) - 2026-03-11: Noted that refill windows are aligned to epoch boundaries and short-window burst accounting can cause transient tenant-wide depletion when two windows of different traffic classes align. Investigating whether background flushes are being charged to interactive priority lane.
Jeremy Cho (SRE) - 2026-03-12: Implemented temporary rate isolation rule for brightcart-prod to segregate telemetry endpoint into background pool; monitoring for 24h.
BrightCart Ops - 2026-03-12: Confirmed immediate drop in user-facing 429s during nightly run after temporary isolation applied. Observed small number of failed telemetry items retried successfully.

investigation_notes:
Hypothesis A: Signed-url refreshes create many short-lived sessions which touch the same per-tenant token bucket accounting as interactive calls because signed-url callbacks include the same route tag — causing simultaneous drains.
Hypothesis B: Telemetry flush uses chunked POSTs that the ingest path tags as 'interactive' due to legacy header; should be counted against background/bulk pool.
Telemetry from console shows refill_remaining reached zero at 03:05:14Z and rejected spikes coincide with scheduler completion times. Token accounting dump shows large debit entries labeled 'ingest' but with weight equivalent to interactive tokens.
Edge-proxy analysis: keepalive count surged due to zero jitter refresh; connection churn also increased NAT mapping reuse, possibly causing multiple token attributions per logical job run.
Related config: Customer uses dedicated pool with default burst pool sharing; no explicit route-based isolation configured prior to mitigation.

root_cause:
Background telemetry flushes and high-frequency signed-url refreshes were both being debited against the tenant's shared burst token window and, because both traffic classes aligned with the same refill epoch, the short-window refill was exhausted causing tenant-wide 429s.

resolution:
Applied a two-part mitigation and follow-ups:
- Short-term: created a temporary split in rate pools for brightcart-prod: /v1/ingest routed to background-burst pool with separate refill cadence; interactive routes kept on interactive-pool. This reduced user-facing 429s immediately.
- Medium-term: recommended customer enable jitter for signed-url refresh (randomized 30–90s) and move telemetry flush to staggered batches or to a dedicated background route.
- Long-term: engineering to deploy a console UI control for per-route burst isolation and a safeguard that refuses to tag large scheduled jobs as interactive.

Customer impact after mitigation: user-facing 429 rate dropped from ~30% to <1% during next scheduled run. Telemetry retries increased transiently but completed.

follow_up_tasks:
ENG-12590: Add route-level burst pool UI and API (owner: rate-limiter team)
OPS-4491: Create KB entry for customers on 'Signed-url refresh jitter and telemetry batching' (owner: Solutions Engineering)
SRE-3322: Schedule a config rollout to make background ingestion auto-isolate on dedicated pools for enterprise tenants (owner: SRE)
CS-210: Reach out to BrightCart in 48 hours to confirm stability and discuss best-practices adoption (owner: Customer Success)
Customer action: BrightCart to enable jitter for signed-url refresh and adjust telemetry flush to 10 parallel batches spread across 10 minutes.

notes:
This ticket highlights a common failure mode when scheduled background traffic and frequent credential refreshes are not isolated by route or priority. Recommend updating onboarding docs for enterprise tenants to include default isolation recipes.

[Client-side request coalescer causing concentrated bursts and unexpected 429s]
description:
Issue summary:\nCustomer enabled a client-side request coalescing library (v2.4.0) across multiple stateless uploader workers. Instead of reducing traffic, the coalescer is producing aligned flushes that arrive as concentrated micro-bursts to the API gateway. Those bursts correlate with periodic 429s across other tenants in the same dedicated pool window.\n\nImpact:\n- Several of the customer's high-priority streaming endpoints experience 429s ~every 30-90s during large ingest runs.\n- Downstream service metrics show elevated token-bucket exhaustion on the gateway for the customer's tenant during those bursts.\n- Other tenants on the same Dedicated pool reported transient increases in 429s (customer provided support logs).\n\nEnvironment:\n- Customer: DataStream Labs (dedicated pool, committed capacity)\n- Region: us-east\n- API: /v1/generate (streaming and non-streaming) and /v1/embeddings/batch\n- Client: internal nodejs uploader using coalescer v2.4.0 (open-source library) behind a proxy pool of ephemeral connections\n\nSteps to reproduce (as provided by customer):\n1) Spin up 64 short-lived uploader workers, each using coalescer with 200ms coalesce window and 5s flush fallback.\n2) Begin batching 1k small requests (50–200 tokens) across workers.\n3) Observe gateway graphs and client retries; 429s appear at burst boundaries when many coalesced flushes align.\n\nObservations / Logs:\n- Gateway token-bucket refill metric shows refill window alignment spikes concurrent with coalescer flushes.\n- Throttle headers from responses show X-RateLimit-Limit and X-RateLimit-Remaining suddenly drop to 0 for a short interval.\n- Customer attached pcap-level timings showing many identical small requests being sent in <10ms windows after coalescer flush.\n- No model-side OOMs or 5xx errors observed. Serving runtime reports normal latency otherwise.\n\nInitial hypothesis:\n- Client-side coalescer aligns I/O across many workers, producing microbursts that exhaust per-tenant token windows (burst+refill) despite average rate being under quota. The dedicated pool's per-tenant short-window accounting (e.g., 1s micro-window) is sensitive to instantaneous bursts.\n- Additional factor: the customer's proxy pool reuses a small number of outbound IPs causing health-checks and coalesced flushes to collide into the same token accounting shards.\n\nCustomer asks:\n1) Can Redwood recommend configuration changes (on client or tenant side) to avoid these 429s while keeping coalescing benefits?\n2) Is there a server-side guard or a dedicated-pool setting to smooth short-window bursts for mixed realtime+bulk workloads?\n\nRequested attachments from customer (provided):\n- client-traffic-trace-2026-03-12.pcap (sensitive redacted)\n- gateway-tenant-throttle-2026-03-12.csv\n- sample client config (coalescer settings and worker pool sizes)\n\nProposed next steps:\n- SRE/Rate-limiter to confirm per-tenant short-window accounting thresholds and whether they can be relaxed for this dedicated pool.\n- Ask customer to try increasing coalescer jitter/randomized flush (200ms -> 20–50ms random jitter) and reduce global worker concurrency to see if the bursts attenuate.\n- Evaluate adding a tenant-level burst-smoothing policy (soft queueing) as a short-term mitigation.\n- If necessary, schedule a joint debug session to reproduce with our internal coalescer harness.\n

[Timezone-rollover worker burst triggering tenant 429s and console quota mismatch]
description:
Issue summary: Multiple customers experienced persistent 429 throttles starting ~2026-03-12T04:00:00Z. Root cause appears tied to an orchestrated worker refresh that executed en masse at tenant-local-midnight after a DST/timezone roll event. Impact: Several dedicated tenants (including SlideStream Media) saw short bursts of hundreds of concurrent warmup/keepalive requests that depleted tenant token windows and caused streaming and bulk endpoints to return 429s. Console quota readouts reported 'tokens remaining' that did not match live throttle behavior (console showed ~30% remaining).

impact:
Customer-facing errors (429) for streaming and batch ingestion. SlideStream reported 12-minute service degradation impacting live captioning flows. Estimated affected customers: 4 dedicated tenants in us-east; transient soft throttles observed for ~10 other self-serve tenants. Revenue impact under review; multiple escalation calls occurred.

steps_to_reproduce:
Simulate timezone/DST rollover by advancing tenant-local clock to midnight while cron workers scheduled without jitter start a refresh cycle.
Trigger orchestrated worker restart across a tenant's ingestion pool (simulate multiple workers starting within <30s window).
Send multiplexed streaming warmup + several small batch embed jobs concurrently from same API key.
Observe token-window depletion and 429 responses from /v1/streams and /v1/embeddings endpoints within 5-15s.
Compare console quota readout to real-time /rate-limit headers on responses to see mismatch.

observed_behavior:
Rapid surge of requests from orchestrated workers (peaks measured at ~85k requests/min across the tenant's pool). Rate-limiter consumed tenant burst credits in under 12s. Responses returned HTTP 429 with X-RateLimit details showing window exhausted. Console displayed quota ~30% remaining due to cached snapshot refresh lag and lack of immediate reconciliation with in-memory token counters.

expected_behavior:
Tenant-local scheduled jobs should include jitter and stagger to avoid synchronized bursts. Console quota metrics should reflect real-time token counters or flag stale data explicitly. Rate-limiter should handle short synchronized spikes without immediate hard-throttles by smoothing refill or using short grace credits where configured for dedicated tenants.

logs_and_metrics:
Edge gateway logs: spike in POST /v1/streams from 10 instances -> 85k r/min at 2026-03-12T04:01:02Z
Rate-limiter metric: tenant_window_tokens_remaining went from 420k -> 0 in 11s
Serving runtime: queue length jumped to 410, per-GPU mem pressure + 18% latency P95 increase
Console metric lag: quota-snapshot.last_refresh 2026-03-12T03:59:00Z while live counters showing exhaustion at 04:01:03Z
Customer logs (SlideStream): repeated 429s with ids: ssm-req-117234, ssm-req-117240

investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: misconfigured cron jitter resulted in synchronized warmups at tenant local midnight; confirmed via orchestration logs showing scheduled jobs with identical cron expressions without jitter for several customer clusters.
Observed refill logic uses UTC-midnight reference for credit refill but token-window consumption is calculated in tenant-local time slice for burst accounting -> mismatch during timezone roll events.
Console uses a cached snapshot persisted to Redis every minute; during burst the cache was stale and did not reflect in-memory token drain.
Confirmed correlated Slack thread: #support (thread t-512) with customer screenshots. See link: https://slack.redwood.io/archives/support/p16234
Telemetry shows pattern repeats for tenants with many short-lived ephemeral workers that rotate at local-midnight. Not common but present in ~0.4% of tenants.
Cross-reference: similar customer-impact pattern to SUP-762318 (tail 429s after dedicated pool scale-down warmup) but root cause here is time-sync + cron-jitter absence.

temporary_mitigation:
Applied emergency temporary bump of burst credits for affected dedicated tenants in us-east for 60 minutes (operator action: increase_burst_credit tenant_id: ss-004 -> +150k tokens).
Rolled out a per-tenant short-term smoothing policy on rate-limiter to allow 3s smoothing window for synchronized warmups (feature flag: rl_smoothing_short_burst = true) to reduce hard 429s while permanent fix is deployed.
Advised SlideStream to add client-side jitter to their local-midnight refresh cron as immediate mitigation.
Invalidate console quota cache on manual override to force immediate snapshot refresh when anomalies detected (temporary operational runbook step).

planned_fix_and_timeline:
Short term (48h): deploy patch to orchestration scheduler templates to inject random jitter into tenant-local scheduled jobs (rollout to dedicated clusters in us-east first).
Medium term (2 weeks): update token refill logic to normalize refill windows across UTC vs tenant-local transitions and add DST-aware reconciliation on boundary events.
Medium term (2 weeks): update console to mark quota snapshots stale if in-memory counters diverge >10% and show 'reconcile' button to force refresh.
Long term (Q2): implement adaptive smoothing in rate-limiter that detects synchronized warmup patterns across workers and applies per-tenant soft-grace credits automatically based on historical behavior.
Customer communication: draft status note to affected customers with incident summary and crediting plan (CS to own messaging).

resolution_notes:
Workarounds applied and smoothing flag reduced number of immediate 429 responses to near-zero within 6 minutes of mitigation.
Burst credit increase prevented further degradation; monitoring shows normalised request rates and token counters were replenished by 04:14Z.
Patch for scheduler jitter merged to main (PR #4491) and queued for staged deploy to production dedicated clusters starting 2026-03-14.
Follow-up: billing team to evaluate one-time credit for SlideStream covering 12 minutes of service disruption; CS owner: Priya Rao.
Postmortem scheduled: https://confluence.redwood.io/display/POST/2026-03-12+Timezone+Rollover+Burst+Incident

2026-03-12 04:10 - Liam O'Connor: Applied temporary burst credit for ss-004 and toggled rl_smoothing_short_burst flag for us-east. Monitoring shows 429s dropping off.

[Repeating 429s for tenant caused by delegated service-account refresh loop consuming burst credits]
description:
Issue summary:
Customer DataHarbor reports periodic waves of 429 throttles across multiple endpoints during daytime ingest windows. They see server-side rate-limit rejections for a sustained 30–90 minute window even though aggregate token usage reported in their console remains under their committed burst and sustained quotas.

Impact:
- Multiple background jobs and webhooks failing with 429s (non-idempotent retries cause downstream duplicates).
- Customer reports increased error rates in their SLA dashboards and two supportable customer incidents.
- Revenue-impacting: delayed batch commits and retry storms.

Environment:
- Dedicated tenant on prod-us-east, dedicated GPU pool.
- Jobs originate from a delegated service account (service-account-managed by DataHarbor) that rotates short-lived credentials every ~2 minutes.

Steps to reproduce (provided by customer):
1) Deploy connector that rotates delegated SA keys and launches 8 parallel upload workers.
2) Each worker uses temporary credentials to start streaming SSE connections + periodic background flush jobs.
3) Observe console & client errors: 429s appear within 3–5 minutes and persist in waves.

Observed behavior:
- 429 responses have X-RateLimit-Reason header: "burst_credit_exhausted" or sometimes missing header (opaque 429).
- Console token usage graphs show transient micro-spikes but not sustained over-billing matching the 429 duration.
- Logs show repeated token bucket refill attempts correlated with many short-lived sessions tied to the delegated SA refresh.

Expected behavior:
- Short-lived credential rotations should not cause tenant burst credits to be depleted repeatedly; system should amortize transient reconnects and keep background probes/healthchecks excluded where configured for dedicated tenants.

Initial diagnostics attached by customer:
- Sample logs (redacted) showing auth refresh timestamps and 429 timestamps.
- Wireshark snippet showing quick TCP teardown/connect cycles.
- Console screenshots of token bucket and per-route counters.

Immediate ask from customer:
1) Explanation for why burst credits are consumed faster than console suggests.
2) Temporary mitigation to stop ongoing 429s while we investigate root cause.
3) Permanent recommendation for their delegated-credential rotation pattern.

[Gateway bifurcation for graceful multi-region takeover with per-connection KV checkpointing]
description:
Problem: During regional disruptions we currently perform blunt traffic drains or full cutovers that can truncate long-lived streaming sessions and lose in-flight KV state. This causes visible client disconnects, token replays, and SLO violations for tail latency and availability.

Goal: Implement a gateway bifurcation pattern that enables graceful takeover between two active regions that share a coordinated per-connection KV checkpointing mechanism, short token-grace window, and circuit-decay policy. The mechanism should: preserve active streaming attachments where possible, reduce user-visible interruptions, maintain SLOs for p95/p99 latency, and allow progressive traffic rebalancing with automated load-shedding triggers and circuit breakers for overloaded endpoints.

acceptance_criteria:
New gateway bifurcation control plane can execute staged traffic split 100% -> 80/20 -> 50/50 -> 0% with per-connection checkpointing applied during each stage
Active streaming sessions can resume on target region with KV checkpoint replay within token-grace window for >= 95% of test sessions in canary
Circuit-decay policy triggers and drops low-priority background requests while preserving high-priority tokens; measured p99 latency remains within SLO (<= 800ms) during 70% simulated surge
Automated rollback when telemetry shows error-rate delta > 2% or SLA budget burn > 30% in 10m window
End-to-end observability: dashboards for per-connection handoff success rate, checkpoint latency, token-grace expirations, and circuit-breaker activations are available in Console
Runbook updated with step-by-step operator commands and emergency cutover procedure

design_notes:
Bifurcation model: introduce a light-weight control plane API that instructs edge gateways to enter a 'bifurcate' mode where connections are tracked and checkpoints emitted at defined safe boundaries (e.g., sentence boundaries or invocation end for non-streams)
KV checkpointing uses existing prefix cache format but augments with 'handoff-metadata' containing sequence id and minimal opaque resume token
Token-grace window: short TTL (default 45s) during which requests with valid resume token are allowed on destination region before full auth revalidation, configurable per-customer
Circuit-decay: instead of hard reject on threshold breach, reduce priority of non-interactive routes progressively using weighted drop and backoff so that interactive sessions retain headroom
We will avoid synchronous cross-region KV replication; instead use per-connection snapshot + opportunistic async pre-warm on destination to keep overhead low

technical_approach:
Edge changes: gateway will emit checkpoint artifacts to S3-backed artifact store (or internal blob cache) keyed by connection-id and region, with signed short-lived pointer visible to target region
Control plane: bifurcate controller service with APIs: /start-bifurcate, /advance-stage, /rollback, /finalize. Controller computes staged percentages and pushes policies to gateways via gRPC config streams
Resume flow: destination gateway receives resume token, fetches checkpoint, rehydrates KV cache and replay last few tokens to restore deterministic decoder state; if checkpoint unavailable or stale, fallback to canonical stateless retry path
Load-shedding triggers: telemetry-driven rules based on queue depth, GPU headroom, and p99 latency; rules feed into controller which adjusts split and activates circuit-decay rules
Safety nets: global circuit-breaker per-customer that can instant-fail new sessions to protect cluster and prevent cascading failures
Backwards compatibility: non-streaming and stateless flows unaffected; default behavior for customers not opted-in remains original cutover path

rollout_plan:
Phase 0 - Internal Canary: deploy bifurcate controller and edge code to test cluster; run synthetic suite with deterministic streams (2/10 - 2/24)
Phase 1 - Limited Canary: enable feature for internal services only, monitor handoff success and token-grace expirations, iterate on checkpoint size and pre-warm thresholds (3/1 - 3/8)
Phase 2 - Customer Canary: opt-in 3 low-risk customers with long-lived streams; run staged splits with progressive % increases (3/9 - 3/16)
Phase 3 - Ramp: enable auto-split for broad traffic with conservative defaults and telemetry thresholds; maintain human-in-loop for first 48 hours (3/17 - 3/24)
Rollback: emergency commands in runbook to abort and redirect all bifurcate traffic back to original region and invalidate resume tokens

telemetry:
Per-connection metrics: checkpoint_size_bytes, checkpoint_emit_latency_ms, resume_fetch_latency_ms, resume_success_bool
Handoff metrics: handoff_attempts_total, handoff_success_rate, handoff_fallback_rate
SLOs: p95/p99 latency pre/post-handshake, availability per-region, error-rate by route
Circuit metrics: circuit_open_count, average_decay_rate, dropped_requests_by_priority
Alerting: conservative alerts for handoff_success_rate < 90% in 5m and p99 latency regression > 20% vs baseline

test_plan:
Automated unit tests for checkpoint serialization/deserialization and token signing
Integration tests with simulated cross-region resume using local artifact store
Chaos tests: introduce network partitions and verify controller rolling advance/rollback semantics
Load tests: synthetic streams plus background embedding/ingest traffic to evaluate circuit-decay efficacy
Canary dashboards and SLIs tracked during each stage; automatic gates for phase transition

risks:
Resume token leakage: mitigated by short TTLs and signature verification; requires security review
Large checkpoints may add storage/IO pressure during mass handoffs; mitigation: cap checkpoint size and prefer incremental diffs
Checkpoint replay may diverge for non-deterministic model serving paths (e.g., sampling); mitigation: restrict replay to deterministic sampling or force deterministic mode during handoff windows
Increased control plane complexity and blast radius if controller miscomputes split — mitigations: rate limits, circuit-breakers, and manual abort
SLO trade-off: during surge the system may favor availability of interactive sessions by dropping background work; this needs clear product communication

[Resilient disconnect recovery and compact cleanup for partial streaming generations]
description:
Problem: Clients frequently disconnect mid-generation (network blips, mobile backgrounding, browser tab close). Currently we either hold resources for long TTLs or aggressively GC partial outputs and KV cache, both causing either wasted GPU time or poor resume UX and lost partial results. This ticket implements a middle-ground: a lease+grace recovery system with compact cleanup for partial generations that preserves resumability for a bounded window while enabling predictable memory/GPU reclaiming.

design_summary:
We introduce a small state machine for each in-flight generation: Active -> Detached (client disconnected but generation may continue) -> Quarantined (no client & low-likelihood resume) -> Tombstoned (final GC). Key components: 1) Short-lived resume leases (resume token with epoch, ttl, checksum) that clients can present to reattach; 2) Ephemeral prefix/KV snapshotting to allow resuming mid-KV-cache with continuity; 3) Adaptive grace period heuristics derived from request size, model latency, and user tier; 4) Compact cleanup job that coalesces partial outputs into a minimal tombstone record for auditing and metric computation and frees GPU memory. This is compatible with function/tool calling and structured outputs: tool call semantic boundaries are atomically checkpointed (can't leave a dangling function call half-applied), and structured outputs are stored as incremental deltas so resumed sessions reconstruct a deterministic final payload.

acceptance_criteria:
Resumable sessions: clients presenting a valid resume token within the adaptive grace period can continue generation and get identical final structured output as if never disconnected
Resource reclaim: ephemeral KV cache and generation memory reclaimed within configured SLA (default 60s for P0, 180s for P1 customers) after tombstone transition
No tool-call leakage: function/tool calls invoked before disconnect are either completed, rolled back, or placed into a safe retry queue, with no duplicated external side-effects in typical resume flow
Observability: new metrics (resume_attempts, resume_success_rate, average_grace_duration, tombstone_count) emitted and visible in Console dashboards
Compatibility: feature gated for older SDKs—fallback behavior matches existing semantics when resume token is not supported

[Ephemeral-output sweep and client-resume protocol for disconnected streaming sessions]
description:
Goal:
Roll out a conservative, observable mechanism to reclaim ephemeral generation state when clients disconnect or time out, while enabling safe resume for clients that reconnect shortly after a network blip. This ticket implements: a sweep/tombstone lifecycle for in-progress generations, a short-lived resume token scheme, and an integration layer that reconciles KV-cache ownership and billing attribution when a session is reclaimed.

Background & motivation:
We see two common failure modes in streaming: (1) noisy mobile clients that disconnect and immediately reconnect, causing duplicated work and KV cache fragmentation, and (2) lost clients that never resume, leaving warm generation state occupying memory and blocking autoscaled GPUs. Current heuristics aggressively keep generation state for long time windows, which increases memory pressure and cost. We need a middle ground that recovers resources promptly for abandoned sessions while preserving a near-instant resume path for legitimate reconnects.

Scope & non-goals:
- Implement server-side ephemeral-sweep policy, resume token format, and reconciliation hooks for KV cache entries.
- Add metrics + tracing for lifecycle transitions (ACTIVE -> SUSPENDED -> TOMBSTONED).
- Provide a console dashboard slice for suspended sessions older than X.
- Non-goal: UX changes to SDK retry/backoff logic (that's for SDK team; we will document recommended client behavior).

Design overview:
1) Session leases: when a streaming generation is created we issue a short lease (default 60s) that auto-renews on heartbeats or tokenized ACKs from the client.
2) SUSPENDED state: if heartbeat or progress ACKs stop, mark the generation SUSPENDED and start a grace timer (default 5min). Suspended state preserves memory references but marks the session as reclaimable.
3) Resume token: when a client reconnects within the grace window it can present a signed resume token (issued at start) to reattach to the same generation; token usage increments an attach counter in the audit log.
4) TOMBSTONE sweep: after grace window expires, we tombstone generation artifacts (release outgoing buffers, decrement cache ownership, mark KV entries as orphanable). Tombstoned sessions are soft-deleted for 24h before hard GC to assist forensic/debugging.
5) Ownership reconciliation: a background reconciler scans orphanable KV keys and attempts to merge small fragments or reassign them to a warm-backup pool; this avoids fragmentation spikes on heavy reconnect churn.

Trade-offs considered:
- Short leases reduce wasted memory but increase sensitivity to transient packet loss. We mitigate by using client ACKs and conservative defaults (60s / 5min) and providing explicit guidance to SDKs to send lightweight pings.
- Resume tokens introduce complexity and potential privacy considerations; tokens are short-lived, HMAC-signed, and do not contain user payloads.

Acceptance criteria:
- Server correctly transitions sessions through ACTIVE -> SUSPENDED -> TOMBSTONED states in test harness.
- Reconnect with valid resume token reattaches to in-progress generation without duplicating tokens in the KV cache.
- Tombstoned sessions free >90% of previously held memory within 2 minutes of sweep run in scale tests.
- Metrics emitted: suspended_count, resumed_count, tombstone_count, kv_orphans_reassigned, tombstone_gc_latency.
- End-to-end integration tests covering: immediate reconnect, delayed reconnect (within grace), reconnect after tombstone (should not resume), and forced client abort.

Implementation plan:
- Phase 1 (this ticket): implement lease/heartbeat, suspended state, resume token verification, tombstone marker, basic reconciler and metrics. Add unit tests + integration harness.
- Phase 2: refine KV merge heuristics, expose console view, add canary rollout to small subset of hosted customers.
- Phase 3: add autoscaler signal integration so reclaimed resources can be used by additional workloads quicker.

Risks & mitigation:
- Risk: resume tokens abused for replay -> mitigated by one-time attach counters and short TTLs.
- Risk: tombstone sweeps causing burst memory churn -> mitigated by rate-limited reclaim and gradual release strategy.
- Risk: latency regressions for active sessions -> all added checks are off the hot path; heartbeats are handled by lightweight path with fast-path bypass.

- PR (initial): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8421
- Load test results (prototype): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/streams/ephemeral-sweep-proto

Operational notes for rollout:

- Canary: enable for 5% of new hosted sessions, observe suspended_count/resume_rate for 48h.
- Rollback plan: revert flag; artifacts are tombstoned but soft-delete window retains diagnostics for 24h.

Resume token reattach path tested end-to-end with KV-cache consistency checks
Tombstone sweep reclaims >90% memory in scale test

[Unbalanced egress surge: asymmetric circuit-breaker trips & coordinated multi-region shed remediation]
description:
Summary:
On 2026-02-17 22:12 UTC a sudden client egress surge originating from a small APAC customer cohort caused asymmetric queue pressure across two active regions (us-west-2, ap-southeast-1). Local circuit breakers tripped in ap-southeast-1 due to bursty long-sequence requests while us-west-2 remained underutilized. Traffic affinity and sticky routing amplified failover to the congested region, triggering a cascading load-shedding policy that exceeded our 99th-percentile SLO for the Chat API for 27 minutes.

Detection and impact:
- Detection: alerting on 99p latency and circuit-breaker open-rate triggered at 22:14 UTC. Synthetic user probes and customer support reports confirmed degraded client experience by 22:18 UTC.
- Impact: ~6% of production requests experienced latency > 99th percentile and 0.9% experienced 5xx errors due to token-budget exceeded and early-degraded responses. Two paying customers reported increased error rates affecting critical flows.

Root cause analysis (concise):
1) Egress surge source: an external batch job from a single customer sending high-token requests without rate-limits at 22:12 UTC.
2) Affinity routing behavior: request affinity and sticky-region routing directed retries and follow-up requests preferentially to the same region, causing uneven distribution despite global capacity.
3) Circuit breaker configuration: CB threshold logic used per-region absolute concurrency and did not account for request token-cost variance (long sequences tripped CBs faster).
4) Load-shedding policy coupling: the shedding controller prioritized preserving P50 latency metric by shedding long requests first; this unintentionally increased tail latency for short, latency-sensitive requests due to priority inversion inside local priority queues.
5) KV-cache warmup lag: failover to hot region caused many cold KV cache misses increasing per-request runtime and worsening CB trips.

What worked:
- Automated fallback to secondary model variants prevented a full outage for most traffic.
- Circuit-breaker telemetry and sampling allowed us to quickly identify token-cost distribution skew.
- Rollback-safe canary (in place) limited blast radius during mitigation work.

What failed / partial mitigations:
- Global router did not detect and smooth cross-region imbalance quickly enough.
- Shedding heuristics lacked token-awareness and priority fairness; initial mitigation caused a spike in short request latency.

Immediate mitigations applied during the incident (timeline):
- 22:20 UTC: throttled the offending customer IP at the edge (temporary ACL) to stop the source burst.
- 22:24 UTC: relaxed sticky-routing heuristics to prefer capacity-aware routing across regions.
- 22:32 UTC: temporarily lowered long-request priority in local queues to reduce priority inversion.
- 22:39 UTC: warmed KV cache via targeted synthetic prefetch for hot-model prefixes; CB open-rate dropped by 45% in 5 minutes.
- 22:45 UTC: full recovery declared at 22:39–22:45 UTC window once 99p latency returned under SLO and error rate stabilized.

Longer-term root-cause mitigations and design changes proposed:
- Token-aware circuit-breakers: extend CB logic to weight concurrency by estimated token-cost and dynamic sequence-length histograms.
- Cross-region smoothing: implement proactive rebalancing in the global router using sliding-window capacity signals to avoid affinity amplification.
- Priority fairness algorithm: implement a fairness layer that prevents priority inversion when long requests are shed.
- Synthetic warmers and graceful KV migration: pre-warm KV entries on failover and add adaptive warmup budgets.
- Customer rate-limiting: enforce fine-grained per-api-key rate quotas with burst tokens to prevent similar unfettered bursts.

Related artifacts:
- Incident timeline (Chronicle): https://confluence.redwood.ai/chronicles/INC-2026-0217-egress-surge
- Spike analysis doc: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/spike-egress-surge-analysis-933212
- Production graphs (Datadog): https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors?query=ENG-933212
- GitHub PR for temporary ACL and router change: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/8124

Recommendation for severity and SLO adjustments:
We recommend a temporary reduction in long-request SLO weight while we roll out token-aware CBs and fairness scheduling. This avoids masking regressions while we build robust admission control.

[Graceful epochal switchover with circuit quarantining for active-active gateway]
description:
Problem: In active-active hosted API rollouts we see two classes of instability during region failovers: (1) abrupt traffic shifts cause transient p99 spikes and KV cache misses that break streaming session continuity; (2) noisy-region error bursts cascade into global retries and saturate healthy regions. Goal: Implement an epochal switchover protocol that (a) performs observable, time-boxed traffic attenuation per region, (b) fences/quotarines regions that trigger circuit thresholds to limit blast radius, and (c) preserves streaming session continuity wherever possible via session fencing tokens and KV cache pre-warm handshakes. Success metrics: reduce cross-region p99 latency spikes during failover by >=45%, limit error amplification events to <1/month, and preserve >=95% of active streaming sessions without manual intervention during planned and unplanned region handovers.

acceptance_criteria:
Controlled attenuation: weighted routing can perform a 10-step linearly decreasing traffic shift over 5 minutes with telemetry at each step
Circuit quarantine: a region exceeding 5% 5m error-rate while p99 latency>2s triggers automated quarantine that prevents >10% additional traffic routing to that region
Session continuity: streaming sessions using session-fence token can resume in target region within 8s end-to-end without client reauthentication for >=95% of sessions
Observability: dashboard shows per-epoch metrics (step latency, queue depth, KV miss rate) and can correlate to rollback/onwards decisions
Chaos-tested: end-to-end integration test simulating KV-store lag, partial instance loss, and ingress partition demonstrates graceful attenuation with no more than 5% increased token cost vs baseline

design_decisions:
Use epoch numbers attached to session tokens: each switch operation increments an epoch; requests carry epoch to allow thin gate logic at edge to determine if session needs handoff
Progressive attenuation vs instant cutover: selected linear multi-step attenuation (default 10 steps over configurable window) to give KV and cache layers time to warm in target region
Circuit quarantining: adopt a two-tier breaker — soft breaker for automated weighted reduction (backoff) and hard quarantine which removes routing weight until auto-heal or manual unblock
Telemetry signals: primary signals are p99 latency, 1m error-rate, request backlog depth, and KV miss-rate; combined into a small hazard score to avoid noisy single-signal triggers
Streaming handoff: implement a short-lived resume token (epoch + session id + checksum) that allows receiver-side rehydration of stream state from a synchronized KV snapshot; we accept a trade-off of additional KV replication traffic for continuity

implementation_notes:
Edge changes: implement epoch header parsing and soft/hard breaker logic in gateway routing layer; add per-connection drain hooks for streaming sockets
KV sync: extend existing KV checkpoint API to support quick delta snapshot for session resumes; optimistic RPO acceptable for 5s window
Control plane: add 'epoch' concept to rollout controller and expose step control in Console Rollouts UI with manual override
Autoscaler interaction: ensure attenuation does not trigger aggressive scale-to-zero; expose expected qps per-step to Dedicated autoscaler
Testing: unit tests for epoch collision, integration tests for resume token flow, and staged canary in us-west-2 to validate metrics and dashboards
