[Mini snapshot stitching — personal idea pad]
Context / quick brain-dump:

Goal (one-liner): explore a lightweight, relevance-driven micro-snapshot system that stitches short summaries of recent user activity to keep long conversations useful without storing/serving full token histories.

Problem statement:
- Customers are hitting token budget + latency limits when we naive-append entire sessions for long-lived conversations (support agents, coding assistants, docs browsing).
- Full KV caches + long prompts blow up memory or cost on hosted endpoints and dedicated pools.
- Existing eviction heuristics (LRU by token age) lose semantically important context.

Why a "mini-snapshot" approach?
- Create tiny, time-indexed summaries (50-200 tokens) of contiguous interaction windows that capture intent, facts, and anchors.
- Stitch snapshots into a compact context bundle that can be re-expanded or used directly by the model depending on quality/latency needs.

High-level design options (brainstorm):
A) Server-side incremental summarizer (preferred for hosted):
   - After each turn or every N turns, run a low-cost summarization model (small LLM) to produce a micro-snapshot.
   - Store snapshots as indexed objects (time, relevance vectors, pointers to source tokens if needed).
   - At request time: select top-K snapshots by relevance to prompt + include recent full turns up to short window.
   - Optionally expand selected snapshots back into natural-language paragraphs before sending to main model or send as compact items with meta tags.

B) Client-side (edge) sketch:
   - Device/browser builds snapshots and sends them as compact payloads. Good for privacy-sensitive flows.
   - Less control over model selection / cost.

C) Hybrid: cheap server summarizer + on-demand deep rehydrate using longer summarizer/embedding lookups.

Selection & ranking signals:
- Recency weight (decay function)
- Embedding cosine similarity between incoming query and snapshot embedding
- Explicit user flags (pin / important)
- Domain heuristics (e.g., code diffs, system messages higher weight)

Storage model options:
- Flat list of snapshots per session (append-only), small metadata index for fast k-NN via embedding store.
- Tiered retention: hot (last 10 snapshots), warm (30), cold (archive or delete).

User stories (rough):
- As a customer support agent, I want the assistant to remember key customer intent from earlier in the day without re-sending entire logs so that reply latency stays low.
- As a developer using Redwood dedicated, I want snapshots to be reversible (point to original tokens) so I can debug hallucinations.
- As a compliance admin, I want to set retention policy (7/30/90 days) for snapshots independent of full transcripts.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- System produces micro-snapshots that reduce average tokens sent per request by >=30% for long sessions (>2000 tokens) without lowering measured helpfulness by >5% (human-eval).
- Snapshot selection latency adds <=25ms median overhead to routing path for hosted API.
- Admins can configure per-org retention policy in Console.

Metrics to track:
- tokens_sent_per_request (median / p95) before vs after
- mean_reply_time (ms)
- helpfulness_score (human eval / automatic scoring) delta
- snapshot_hit_rate (fraction of convo requests that used at least one snapshot)
- recall_failures (cases where user complains session forgot something pinned in past)

Open implementation questions / risks:
- Summarizer quality vs cost: cheap summarizers might omit critical facts -> need fallback to original turns or explicit verification step.
- Drift: snapshots might become stale; need automatic refresh or TTL.
- Privacy: storing even tiny summaries can be sensitive; must map to org retention/KMS rules.
- Debuggability: when a model uses a snapshot and hallucinates, engineers need a trace back to original tokens. Keep pointers or store provenance hashes.

Experiment plan (3-week spike):
Week 0: narrow scope, pick two verticals (support chat, code assistant).
Week 1: implement server-side summarizer pipeline (simple microservice) + store snapshots as JSON objects, create embeddings index. Quick A/B harness.
Week 2: run live A/B on internal traffic for both verticals, collect token counts, latency, and quick human eval (20 examples / vertical).
Week 3: analyze, triage failure cases, refine snapshot size and ranking heuristics.

Rollout considerations / progressive modes:
- Off by default; opt-in per org via Console feature flag.
- Start with read-only snapshots (no rehydration) then enable re-expansion later.
- Canary on hosted only; Dedicated customers can opt in to running summarizer in their VPC.

UX / API surface ideas:
- New request parameter: session_mode: [full, compact, smart] where smart toggles snapshot stitching.
- Developer endpoint to pin/unpin snapshots and to request provenance for a given response id.
- Console UI: session timeline with micro-snapshots shown, ability to edit or pin snapshots.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Talk to SRE about storage cost estimates (snapshot object size * retention).
- Check with Security on whether snapshot text counts as retained PII (likely yes).
- Prototype summarizer: try 1) instruct-tuned 7B quant, 2) distilled LLM, 3) heuristic template-based summarizer (cheap baseline).
- Wire up an offline eval harness: pairwise comparisons (full-history vs compact-with-snapshots).

Edge cases / small thoughts:
- Multi-user threads: snapshots should include participant role tokens; may need per-party snapshots.
- System messages / tool outputs: prefer to always include these as anchored snapshots.
- For code assistants: snapshots should preserve code snippets as attachments rather than flattened prose to avoid losing grammar.

Unresolved questions to bring to sync w/ Kai & Maya:
- Snapshot canonical format: NL paragraph vs key-value bucket? Which is easier for downstream models to use reliably?
- Optimal snapshot size (start with 100 tokens-ish?)
- How often to re-run summarizer for long idle sessions?

References / quick links:

[Cobalt sprint: compact-session-orchestrator mini-PRD fragments]
Context / one-line
Cobalt = experimental compact-session orchestrator that runs as a light sidecar (hosted and private) to reduce per-session token costs and enable cheap long-horizon conversations + offline inference reuse. This doc is a collection of fragments for the sprint PRD — rough user stories, hypotheses, acceptance criteria, quick architecture notes and experiment plan.

Why this exists (problem summary)
- Teams building long-lived assistants see token costs explode for long sessions.
- Current approaches (full transcript replay, naive truncation) either lose important context or cost too much.
- We need a pragmatic, low-risk component that sits between request routing and model runtime to compress/transform session state in a manner that keeps useful signals for generation while cutting tokens by ~4-10x for older history.

Primary goals / success metrics (working)
- Reduce average tokens sent to LLM for sessions > 2k tokens by 60%+ without >5% drop in human-rated task success (or degrade gracefully by defined profile).
- Decrease hosted API token bill for targeted cohort by 40% in A/B test (6 week window).
- Latency overhead: <= 50ms p95 extra on request path for cache-hit flows; spinner flows may be longer but < 200ms additional p95.
- Rollout safety: can disable per-customer or per-route; autoswitch to raw transcript mode on quality regressions.

Constraints / non-goals
- Not a replacement for full eval/QA. This is an inference-time optimization, not a fine-tuning or retraining approach.
- Not handling multimodal or large file attachments in first iteration.
- Sidecar must be light-weight, CPU-first prefer; optional optional GPU for heavy embedding ops but baseline should not require GPUs.

Key features (MVP list)
1) Age-based compaction: older segments (beyond N tokens or N turns threshold) get summarized into compact JSON "stubs" that preserve: user intent, important entities, reply history gist, and pointer to canonical embeddings.
2) Semantic deduplication: detect repeated factual statements/boilerplate and collapse them into single compact references.
3) Prefix preservation hook: allow pinned prompts, system messages and last M turns to be sent verbatim (configurable per-route).
4) Fallback & safeties: keep original full transcript in server-side storage for immediate rehydration if user asks to revisit or QA detects hallucination signal.
5) Async offline refresh: a background worker can regenerate compactions when new signals arrive (no blocking on request path).
6) Observability: per-session compression ratio, schema of removed tokens, quick diff preview, quality regressions flagged to console.

User stories (rough)
- As a PM for a conversational product, I want my long-running sessions to cost less so I can scale active users without price changes.
- As an SRE, I want the compactor to be toggleable per-customer and have circuit-breakers for quality rollback.
- As an engineer, I want a simple API to request 'rehydrate(session_id, until_turn=42)' to restore full context for debug paths.
- As a UX researcher, I want a small tool to show what was removed and why (token budget justification) so we can analyze regressions.

Acceptance criteria (MVP)
- End-to-end flow implemented: on incoming request, sidecar returns a compacted context + header describing compression ratio and indicators.
- Default compaction policy (configurable): keep last 6 turns verbatim, compress earlier turns beyond 2k tokens.
- Integration tests proving rehydration returns original transcript and generation responses can be reproduced with rehydrated context.
- Console dashboard tile: per-route avg compression ratio, p95 extra latency, and weekly quality alert counts.
- Feature flag exists for per-customer opt-out; rollout pipeline in console demonstrates toggling.

Open questions / decisions to make
- Compaction format: free-text summary vs structured stubs (entities + intent + condensed messages). Hybrid likely best, but need a canonical schema. Quick thought: one JSON stub per compressed block with fields [summary_text, entities[], salient_user_goals[], embedding_id].
- Where to store rehydration data: ephemeral in sidecar cache (fast) vs durable store (S3) — cost/latency trade-offs. Candidate: keep last 24h in sidecar local cache, archive older to object storage and fetch on-demand.
- Which model to use for summarization/compaction? Use a smaller in-house model (xsmall) for cost; evaluate quality vs using hosted medium model. Also possibility: deterministic heuristics first iteration (rule-based extraction) to minimize model calls.
- How to detect quality regressions automatically? Option: track divergence from baseline via small eval set of prompts per-customer + human-rated sample. Could use perplexity / model confidence heuristics as a cheap proxy.

Mini architecture sketch (notes)
- Request flow (fast path): client -> API Router -> Compact Sidecar (policy apply) -> Serving Runtime. Sidecar returns: compact_context (text + metadata) + compression header.
- Background worker: pulls session deltas, regenerates stubs, computes embeddings, writes to embeddings-store and object storage.
- Cache layers: local LRU memcache per sidecar instance for hot sessions; shared redis for cross-instance pointers; S3 for archival.
- Security: ensure private deployments keep compaction/rehydration data on-customer storage or under KMS. Avoid sending full archive to hosted models unless explicitly allowed.

Experiment plan (first 6 weeks)
Week 0-1: build rule-based compaction prototype (deterministic heuristics) and a tiny dashboard. Run internal load tests.
Week 2-3: implement summarization plug (xsmall model) and sidecar API. Start internal A/B on 10% of internal traffic.
Week 4-6: expand to opt-in beta customers (2-3 teams). Collect qualitative feedback and small human evals. Iterate policy thresholds.

Quick A/B metrics to collect
- Compression ratio distribution (median, p75, p95).
- Per-session token delta (tokens_before - tokens_after).
- Generation quality delta on sampled prompts (human rating change).
- Request path latency delta (p50, p95).
- Billing delta (hosted token spend) for cohort.

Risks and mitigations
- Risk: compression removes critical context causing hallucinations. Mitigation: conservative default policy; immediate rehydration on flagged outputs; human-in-loop for first customer rollouts.
- Risk: throughput bottleneck if compaction is synchronous. Mitigation: async compaction + short-circuit heuristics (no compaction for high-priority low-latency routes).
- Risk: storage bloat/complexity. Mitigation: TTL policies, aggregated archiving, customer-configurable retention.

Tasks / next steps (practical)

- [ ] Small console dashboard tile with compression metrics (Evan).

- Consider cheap semantic hashing for de-dup (use local simhash + threshold).
- For private deployments, provide a local-only compaction model binary so data never leaves customer boundary.

[Ephemeral context eviction strategy (scratchpad)]
Purpose:
- quick notes + exploratory designs for ephemeral per-session context eviction for local/edge sessions (users/ folder brain dump).
- goal: keep tail latency low while bounding memory usage for many concurrent sessions on a single worker.

Constraints / assumptions:
- sessions have variable token budgets (some long-lived chat, some bursty QA).
- model runtime holds KV cache in GPU memory where possible; falling back to compressed CPU store or disk.
- some prefixes are high-value (system prompts, recent user conversation), others are cheap to recompute or rehydrate.
- we must avoid catastrophic quality regressions when evicting (i.e., don't evict the system prompt unless explicit).

Goals / metrics:
- mem_per_worker <= configured cap (e.g., 48GB GPU / worker).
- P99 latency increase due to eviction < 5% for typical chat workload.
- cache_miss_rehydrate_time < 200ms for hot rehydrates (prefetched).
- track quality_delta_by_evict (small prompt sets to detect degeneration).

Eviction policy palette (brainstorm):
1) TTL + token-count caps (simple)
   - each session gets token_budget (configurable by tier), TTL since last active.
   - evict sessions idle > TTL or when total_tokens > cluster_budget.
   - pro: simple. con: not adaptive to importance.

2) Weighted LRU (LRU with weights by importance)
   - weight(session) = base + recent_activity*alpha + pinned_flag*inf + recency_boost
   - eviction sorts by weight ascending.
   - need a cheap estimate: store last_n_token_count, last_active_ts, pinned boolean.

3) Prefix-preserving partial eviction (shrink from tail)
   - keep first K tokens (system prompt + recent N tokens), evict middle older chunks but preserve prefix.
   - idea: store context as circular segments: [prefix | core | tail]. Evict core segments first.
   - useful to prevent losing system prompt and immediate recency.

4) Semantic compaction / summarization
   - when session goes cold, run lightweight summarizer (or call hosted summarize endpoint) to compress history into a short synthetic summary chunk. Keep summary in cache instead of full tokens.
   - tradeoff: compute cost and possible hallucination; good for long chats.

5) Hot-cold tiering + background rehydrate queue
   - hot sessions remain in GPU; cold sessions moved to compressed CPU store or paged to disk. On access, background rehydrate attempts to prefetch top-K sessions predicted to be accessed next.
   - prediction model could be simple heuristic (recent activity, user tier) or ML-based.

6) Token-coalescing and shared common prefixes
   - if multiple sessions share identical system prompts or identical initial prefixes, store a shared read-only prefix cache and reference it, minimizing duplication.

API / config sketch (rough):
- SessionManager config (yaml-like):
  eviction_policy: "weighted-lru"  # options: ttl, weighted-lru, prefix-preserve, semantic-compact, tiered
  total_token_budget_per_worker: 1200000
  default_session_token_budget: 8192
  min_prefix_keep_tokens: 128
  cold_store: {type: "compressed-heap", path: "/mnt/cache"}
  rehydrate_prefetch: {enabled: true, lookahead: 16, background_worker_count: 2}
  summarizer: {enabled: true, model: "small-summarizer-v1", max_tokens: 128}
  eviction_hook: "/internal/session/evict-hook"

- Minimal endpoints (sketch):
  POST /session/create -> {session_id, token_budget?}  // note: create can accept pin/prefetch hint
  POST /session/pin -> {session_id, reason}  // disables eviction for pinned items
  POST /session/peek -> {session_id, window=256} -> streaming small chunk without full rehydrate
  POST /session/evict -> {session_id, force=true|false}  // exposed for admin / debug
  POST /session/summarize -> async request to generate compressed summary

ASCII diagram (rough):

  client ---> session-manager ---> runtime (GPU KV cache)
                 |                       |
                 |                       --> cold-store (compressed CPU / disk)
                 |
                 --> rehydrate-queue (background) --> runtime

Notes on storage model:
- store per-session KV in segments: metadata (head pointers), prefix_segment (immutable), active_segment (mutable, GPU hot), archive_segments (compressed).
- each segment has token_count, compressed_size, checksum.
- implement quick heuristics to estimate rehydrate cost = compressed_size / io_bandwidth + decompress_time + copy_to_gpu. Use as eviction cost estimate.

Rehydration flow (sketch):
- on first token request for a cold session -> respond with ephemeral placeholder if model supports streaming? otherwise block until rehydrate.
- better: return partial continuity by streaming from a summary + then rehydrate full context in background and patch KV cache once ready. Caller may get a signal (event) when full context is available.

Observability signals to add:
- gauge: sessions_in_gpu, sessions_in_cold, sessions_pinned
- histogram: rehydrate_latency, evicted_tokens, eviction_trigger_reason (manual/ttl/memory)
- alert: sustained_rehydrate_rate > threshold -> indicates under-provisioned memory or bad policy

Quality guardrails:
- never evict segments marked mandatory (system prompt, safety info).
- add per-session tests: generate reference replies for a small eval prompt set before/after eviction policy to detect drift. Store eval score changes in a time-series.

Open questions / TODOs:
- how to represent "importance" cheaply across millions of sessions? propose: 8-bit importance score updated on activity, decayed exponentially.
- should summarization be local (edge) or call hosted summarizer? latency vs quality tradeoff.
- exact serialization format for compressed segments (zstd + vector-quantized embeddings?).
- eviction interactions with model kv cache format (some models require absolute contiguous KV vs chunkable frames). Need runtime API to allow chunked imports.
- policy for multi-tenant workers: per-customer quotas vs global worker quotas.

Immediate next steps:
- spike: implement weighted-lru skeleton + TTL fallback in dev branch. Measure memory vs P95 latency on small cluster with mixed chat/qa workload. (owner: me)
- prototype prefix-preserve: implement segment-trimming API and a test harness to assert system prompt persistence. (owner: Liam)
- draft a minimal session-manager config proposal for product to review (owners: me + Priya).

Quick todo list:
- [ ] write integration test harness for rehydrate_latency
- [ ] add metric events for eviction_reason
- [ ] benchmark summarizer cost vs compression ratio
- [ ] add a small CLI tool to inspect session segments on a worker (for debugging)

Random notes / heuristics (brain dump):
- keep ~128 tokens of prefix by default; recent 512 tokens are cheap to keep for responsiveness; older content can be compressed aggressively.
- for conversational agents with tool use, prefer to keep tool-call history intact (can't lose it) — treat it as pinned.
- offer customer-level knobs: aggressive (best-effort), conservative (preserve quality), premium (larger hot budget).

End of scratchpad.

Notes to self: when I revisit, add concrete benchmark numbers from the 2025-inference-bench run and link GH PRs.

[Practical A/B Framework: Adaptive Sample Sizing, Exposure Throttles, and Auto-Revert Playbook]
description:
Design and deliver a production-ready A/B testing framework for model versions that combines adaptive sample-size calculation, exposure throttles (time- and traffic-based), automated statistical checks, and deterministic auto-rollback behavior. The goal is to enable product and platform teams to run principled model comparisons with clear safety gates and low operational overhead.

background:
Current rollout tooling supports ad-hoc canaries and manual A/B splits but lacks: (1) a standardized experiment spec that encodes hypothesis + primary metric, (2) automated sample-size adaption when variance or event rates differ, (3) traffic throttles that respect latency SLOs and capacity budgets, and (4) a deterministic auto-revert mechanism tied to statistical checks. Multiple incidents showed slow detection of regressions when traffic rates were low or metrics were noisy.

goals:
Provide an experiment spec template (hypothesis, primary/secondary metrics, min detectable effect, alpha, power)
Implement adaptive sample-size estimation and runtime re-calibration based on observed variance
Add exposure controls: percent-of-traffic ramps, time-window caps, and request-rate ceilings per cohort
Automate statistical checks (frequentist + optional bayesian) and define deterministic auto-rollback conditions
Expose experiment status and per-metric confidence in Console; ship alerts for early-warning signals

non_goals:
Building a full statistical modeling studio — we provide guardrails and defaults, not a custom analytics engine
Support arbitrary offline metric pipelines in v1 — rely on Console metrics and dataplane counters
Replacing canary-based kernel/serving rollout logic — integrations only

success_metrics:
Time-to-detection for a 5% degradation on primary metric reduced from median 48h to <8h
Number of manual aborts during rollouts reduced by 60% within two sprints of launch
>70% of internal model experiments created with the new spec within quarter after launch

rollout_plan:
Phase 1: Specification and offline simulator + PRD (2 weeks). Phase 2: Implement sample-size engine and exposure throttles in control plane (4 weeks). Phase 3: Integrate statistical check runner and auto-rollback extension (3 weeks). Phase 4: Pilot with two internal product teams (2 weeks). Phase 5: Cross-team rollout and console UX polish (2 weeks).

statistical_tests:
Defaults: two-sided t-test for continuous primary metrics, chi-squared for binary metrics, with alpha=0.05 and power=0.8. Implement sequential testing safe-guards (alpha spending / group sequential boundaries) to allow interim looks. Offer a bayesian posterior-check option for teams that prefer probability-of-being-better thresholds. All tests produce effect size, p-value, confidence interval, and required sample remaining when underpowered.

exposure_controls:
Traffic split primitives (absolute percentage, cohort-based targeting), adaptive ramp scheduler (initial holdout -> 1% -> geometric ramp with max slope), rate ceilings (requests/min per variant), time-window caps (max exposure minutes per hour), and capacity-aware throttling (integrates with Dedicated capacity telemetry). Defaults prioritize safety: no automatic ramp above 10% until min sample is observed.

safety_gates:
Hard Abort: primary metric drops by X sigma within a single analysis window
Soft Hold: variance > threshold or underpowered — pause traffic ramp until metric stability is observed
Circuit Breaker: latency P95 exceeds SLO for variant more than twice baseline for 5 consecutive minutes
Budget Guard: stop further exposure if cumulative token cost for experiment exceeds allocated budget

telemetry_and_alerting:
Emit experiment-state events (started, ramp, hold, abort, complete) and per-metric analysis summaries to Console. Create alert rules: critical (auto-rollback triggered), warning (soft hold), and info (near-threshold). Instrumentation includes cohort-level counts, conversions, sample variance, estimated power, and latency distributions. Dashboards prebuilt for experiment owners.

tasks:
Finalize experiment spec schema and JSON schema for API
Implement sample-size calculator service with APIs for runtime re-eval
Add exposure scheduler in control plane; integrate rate ceilings with serving runtime
Implement statistical runner + sequential test library; wire to auto-revert hooks
Console: experiment creation UI, status timeline, and metric panels
Documentation and runbook: experiment design checklist and troubleshooting
Pilot run with Search team and Embed product; gather feedback

notes_and_decisions:
Decision: use frequentist defaults + optional bayesian path — gives broad familiarity for PMs and DSs
Decision: enforce min-sample before ramps >10% to avoid premature conclusions
Trade-off: sequential testing increases detection speed but complicates error-rate accounting; solution is alpha spending with conservative boundaries
Implementation note: sample-size re-estimation runs every 30 minutes during an experiment

risk_and_mitigation:
Risk: noisy metrics lead to false aborts — Mitigation: require consistency across multiple windows and use hold state before abort
Risk: teams misconfigure hypotheses — Mitigation: provide templates and required fields in spec with validation
Risk: interaction with Dedicated autoscaling — Mitigation: integrate capacity signals into exposure scheduler to avoid cost spikes

open_questions:
Q: Should we support cohort-level stratified randomization in v1? (trade-off: complexity vs. statistical fidelity)
Q: What are default min-detectable-effect values per metric type? Need DS guidance
Q: How do we surface post-rollback investigation artifacts automatically?

[cohort-scheduler slot fragmentation causing priority degradation (postmortem & actions)]
description:
Summary: During a weekday peak window we observed repeated tail-latency spikes and throughput reduction for hosted text-generation routes using the continuous batcher. The symptom set looked like: batch formation stalling for specific request cohorts, disproportionate growth of high-priority queue wait times, and persistent slot fragmentation on several GPU workers. This ticket captures the incident timeline, analysis, mitigations applied during the event, and a consolidated action plan to prevent recurrence.

timeline:
2026-03-09 09:03 UTC: First alert triggered on route /v1/generate 99.9th latency > 1.5s.
2026-03-09 09:05 UTC: Multiple downstream SLO alerts; oncall rotated.
2026-03-09 09:08 UTC: Grafana shows sustained increase in per-worker small-batch ratio and KV-cache miss amplification for user cohort A.
2026-03-09 09:12 UTC: Investigated recent scheduler change rolled in 2026-03-08 (commit 7d3a2f): "cohort_slot_sharing=enabled".
2026-03-09 09:22 UTC: Hotfix deployed (rollback of cohort_slot_sharing flag) to reduce slot fragmentation.
2026-03-09 09:30 UTC: Latency begins to recover; 99.9th drops back toward baseline over next 20 minutes.
2026-03-09 10:00 UTC: Incident declared mitigated; follow-up analysis assigned to continuous-batching team.

root_cause:
A scheduler change intended to improve packing across logical cohorts introduced an allocation path that allowed small, high-priority requests to reserve fractional execution slots without accounting for adjacent pending requests. This produced slot fragmentation on a subset of workers under skewed arrival patterns (mixed short + long sequence workloads). The fragmentation prevented the continuous-batcher from coalescing compatible requests efficiently, causing starved larger batches and backpressure amplification for priority queues. Two contributing factors: insufficient telemetry around per-cohort fragmentation and an interaction with recent KV-cache eviction tuning that increased miss variance.

immediate_mitigations:
1) Rolled back the cohort slot-sharing flag (2026-03-09 09:22 UTC). 2) Temporarily tightened priority admission thresholds to reduce fractional slot claims. 3) Increased aggressive KV-cache grace window to reduce miss amplification for affected cohorts. 4) Added a short-running job to rebalance worker slot assignments across AZs.

long_term_actions:
Implement a deterministic slot allocator that prevents fractional reservations (owner: @miguel, estimate: 8 pts, cadence: runtime-1.20)
Add per-cohort fragmentation metrics to Grafana (metrics: cohort_fragmentation_ratio, cohort_small_batch_ratio) and alert when fragmentation>0.35 for 3m (owner: @shreya, estimate: 3 pts)
Create a chaos test that mixes short/long sequence traffic to validate batching heuristics under skew (owner: @devops, estimate: 5 pts)
Instrument KV-cache hit/miss variance per cohort and correlate with batch sizes; surface anomalies in console (owner: @april, estimate: 5 pts)
Design and roll out a conservative default for cohort_slot_sharing with feature flags that enable gradual ramp and canary (owner: @aisha, estimate: 3 pts)
Add runbook entry for slot-fragmentation incidents with rapid rollback steps and dashboard save (owner: SRE, estimate: 2 pts)
Schedule post-deploy canary load for scheduler changes that exercise mixed-workload patterns (owner: release-eng, estimate: 2 pts)
Evaluate alternative packing heuristics that prioritize filling execution windows before honoring micro-priority claims (owner: research, estimate: 8 pts)

testing_plan:
Nightly synthetic workload that simulates three cohorts: short-chat (<=64 tokens), long-completion (>=1024 tokens), and mixed-burst traffic. Validation gates: end-to-end 99.9th latency within 10% of baseline and batch coalescence ratio within expected range. Introduce controlled KV-cache miss spikes to measure sensitivity.

deployment_plan:
Phase 1: Land deterministic allocator behind feature flag and run in canary lane for 48h across 5% of traffic. Phase 2: If stable, widen to 25% and enable additional telemetry. Phase 3: Full rollout in runtime-1.20 with post-rollout validation and automated rollback trigger. All changes require a documented canary checklist and owner sign-off.

[Specify prompt-set sampling matrix and A/B criteria for Optimize]
description:
Create a clear, operational spec for how Optimize evaluates model changes: define a prompt-set sampling matrix, per-metric regression thresholds, A/B success criteria, and automated rollback triggers. This ticket will produce acceptance criteria, measurement queries, and a lightweight playbook to hand to SRE/QA for implementation and to Growth for A/B coordination.

context:
Recent customer incidents and internal experiments show a gap between our evaluation artifacts (dense prompt sets) and production traffic distribution. Engineering needs deterministic pass/fail rules to automate canary-to-rollout transitions and to trigger rollbacks without manual triage. This work complements prior PRDs on eval gating but focuses on sampling strategy and explicit A/B thresholds appropriate for Optimize workloads (generation quality + unit cost).

scope_inclusions:
- Sampling matrix mapping production traffic slices (intent buckets, token length, top-k/top-p settings) to prompt-set subsets.
- Per-metric baseline definitions and regression thresholds (BLEU/ROUGE variants where applicable, embedding-similarity, hallucination rate, safety flags, latency, cost per 1k tokens).
- A/B test success criteria (primary and secondary metrics, minimum sample size, minimum detectable effect).
- Automated rollback triggers for severe regressions and escalation paths.
- Acceptance criteria and monitoring queries for Console dashboards and alerts.

scope_exclusions:
- Building the full A/B experimentation framework (this ticket defines the spec and measurement queries; implementation will be a follow-up).
- Long-form human eval instrumentation (we only define when/where human evals are required and the sampling for them).

requirements:
1) Sampling matrix: map at least 6 production slices -> prompt-set partitions; include weighting and randomization strategy.
2) Metrics: list final metric names, computation windows, and baseline values (30-day rolling).
3) Regression thresholds: specify soft and hard thresholds per metric, with examples.
4) A/B criteria: define primary metric, MDE, min duration, and risk-adjusted success rule.
5) Rollback triggers: enumerate conditions that cause automatic rollback vs. immediate page.
6) Measurement artifacts: SQL/ClickHouse queries or PromQL snippets for each metric and a dashboard wireframe.
7) Acceptance tests: synthetic runbook that SRE/QA can follow to verify gating works in staging.

acceptance_criteria:
- Sampling matrix defined and approved by ML Research and Growth; includes mapping for intent, token-length buckets, and feature flags.
- For each metric, a baseline and two thresholds documented: soft (warning) and hard (rollback).
- A/B test spec includes: primary metric (embedding-similarity for reranking; quality score composite for generation), MDE (5% relative for primary metric unless justified), min sample size calculation, and min runtime (48 hours or 100k impressions, whichever is larger).
- Automated rollback rules documented: hard threshold breach for primary metric over a 1-hour rolling window triggers rollback; any safety-flag spike above 0.5% triggers immediate halt and paging.
- Measurement queries validated against a 14-day historical window and produce expected baselines.
- PRD + playbook reviewed and approved in stakeholder review with signoffs from ML Research, SRE, Growth, and Legal (if safety thresholds touch policy).

metrics_and_thresholds:
- Quality composite (weighted: 0.6 human-like scoring proxy, 0.3 factuality/QA, 0.1 safety): baseline=0.87; soft threshold = -2% relative; hard threshold = -5% relative.
- Embedding-similarity (cosine) on rerank: baseline=0.79; soft=-3%; hard=-7%.
- Hallucination rate (auto-detected): baseline=0.9% absolute; soft=+0.5pp; hard=+2.0pp.
- Safety flags (policy classifier): baseline=0.12%; soft=+0.3pp; hard=+0.5pp (page on hard).
- Median P95 latency: baseline=210ms; soft=+50ms; hard=+120ms.
- Cost per 1k tokens: baseline=$1.08; soft=+10% relative; hard=+25% relative.

sampling_matrix_summary:
- Slice A: High-frequency intents (search/qa) -> 40% of test set (stratified by prompt templates).
- Slice B: Long-form generation (>512 tokens) -> 15%.
- Slice C: Short completions (<50 tokens) -> 15%.
- Slice D: Low-frequency/edge intents (support workflows) -> 10%.
- Slice E: Safety-sensitive content (policy heuristics) -> 10% (oversampled 3x for human eval triggers).
- Slice F: Canary flag / experimental features -> 10% (route to separate cohort).
Weighting and randomization: deterministic hashing on user-id + timestamp with daily re-seeding in staging; sample allocation is configurable via Optimize Console.

a_b_spec_summary:
Primary metric: quality composite for generation; Secondary: latency and cost.
MDE: 5% relative on primary metric (unless traffic slice justification provided).
Min runtime: 48 hours OR 100k impressions per cohort.
Success rule: primary metric improvement > MDE AND no hard-threshold breaches on safety/latency/cost for both cohorts.
If primary effect is within [MDE, 2*MDE], apply manual review before rollout.

rollback_triggers:
1) Hard threshold breach on primary metric sustained for >1 hour -> auto-rollback to previous model variant.
2) Safety flags exceed hard threshold in any 60-minute window -> immediate halt + page SOC and Product.
3) Latency P95 > hard threshold for >30 minutes affecting >=50% of requests -> rollback.
4) Cost per 1k tokens exceeds hard threshold AND traffic impact >10% -> pause rollout and notify Engineering.
5) Composite alert: two or more soft-thresholds breached simultaneously for >3 hours -> send warning and require go/no-go from PM + ML Research.

decision_log:
- 2026-02-27: Agreed on composite primary metric to capture quality tradeoffs across generation tasks.
- 2026-03-03: Set MDE default to 5% relative; exceptions require documented justification.
- 2026-03-08: Adopted automated rollback on 1-hour hard breaches for primary metric.
- 2026-03-11: Finalized sampling matrix weights after ML Research and Growth signoff.

open_questions:
- Should human-in-the-loop evaluation be required for all safety-sensitive slices before rollout? (proposal: yes for hard-threshold-adjacent changes).
- Do we want separate MDEs per traffic slice by default? (proposal: default MDE, but allow slice-specific overrides).
- Who owns operationalizing the SQL/PromQL snippets into alerting rules? (SRE recommended; PM to coordinate).

next_steps:
1) Circulate draft PRD + measurement queries to SRE and ML Research for final validation (owner: Ethan).
2) Capture dashboard wireframes and create two alerting rules in staging (owner: SRE).
3) Prepare a short runbook for on-call & product to follow during canary (owner: PM).
4) Schedule stakeholder sign-off meeting for 2026-03-18.
5) Handoff to implementation ticket(s): ENG-12088 (sampling infra), ENG-12089 (A/B instrumentation), ENG-12090 (dashboard & alerts).

[Sequential Bayesian early-stop controller for multi-metric A/B model experiments]
description:
Problem statement: As teams run progressive model upgrades we need a lifecycle controller that can safely decide when to stop, expand, or rollback an experiment without relying on fixed-duration buckets. Current canary/AB tooling in Redwood requires manual monitoring and conservative time windows, which slows rollouts and increases operational burden. This ticket proposes a sequential decision engine that applies Bayesian posterior checks and multi-metric safety budgets to provide automated early-stop and auto-rollback actions, while exposing control knobs to product and platform teams.

background_and_motivation:
Why Bayesian sequential checks: sequential experiments produce repeated looks at the data; frequentist tests must be adjusted (alpha-spend) and are brittle with variable traffic. A Bayesian posterior approach with pre-specified decision thresholds simplifies continuous monitoring, naturally handles stopping rules, and integrates well with multi-metric utility functions. We want a controller that: 1) supports primary/guardrail metrics, 2) handles unequal sample sizes across cohorts, 3) integrates with shadow traffic for preflight analysis, and 4) emits explainable reasons for rollbacks for audit logs.

acceptance_criteria:
API: ability to create an experiment manifest with primary metric, list of guardrail metrics, safety budgets, and decision rules (posterior thresholds and minimum sample sizes).
Controller: evaluation loop that computes posterior distributions for metric deltas in near-real time and emits decisions: CONTINUE, EXPAND, HALT, AUTO-ROLLBACK.
Console: UI shows live posterior probability curves, sample counts, and the controller's recommended action with rationale and last trigger reason.
Rollout automation: when auto-rollback trigger fires, system performs a reversible rollback and writes a structured audit entry with metric snapshots, posterior values, and links to relevant PRs/dashboards.
Safety budgets: per-customer and per-cohort budgets prevent runaway exposure; controller enforces budget caps and sends alerts when budgets are low.
Testing: integrated simulation harness that runs historical traffic replays and synthetic degradations to validate Type I/II behavior and average time-to-detect for degradation scenarios.
Telemetry: instrumentation for posterior traces, decision timestamps, and per-variant metric streams fed to Cost/Latency/Quality dashboards.
Documentation: PRD and runbook describing configuration knobs, recommended thresholds for typical metrics (e.g., latency, error-rate, quality delta), and post-mortem checklist after an auto-rollback.

metrics_and_stat_checks:
Primary metric: chosen by experiment manifest; controller computes posterior on delta = variant - control.
Posterior model: beta-binomial for binary metrics, Gaussian with hierarchical variance for continuous metrics; default weakly-informative priors provided.
Decision rule examples: if P(delta < -eps_primary | data) > 0.95 AND n_samples >= min_n_primary -> AUTO-ROLLBACK; if P(delta > eps_primary | data) > 0.975 -> EXPAND.
Guardrails: evaluate guardrail metrics with asymmetric thresholds (e.g., latency: eps=+50ms, error-rate: eps=+0.5%); a single guardrail breach with P(breach) > 0.9 for sustained window triggers HALT and shadow only.
Sequential controls: minimum look interval (e.g., 5 minutes), minimum n for primary and for guardrails, and exponential backoff on decision cadence when traffic low.
False alarm control: support configurable equivalent of alpha-spend expressed as posterior probability thresholds and minimum exposure before allowing expansion.
Drift detection: KS-test or CUSUM on input feature distributions triggers a shadow analysis job that evaluates model-sample mismatch before any decision to expand.

implementation_notes:
Controller will be implemented as a separate service (rollout-controller) that subscribes to per-variant metric streams from metrics-pipeline and KV cache of sample counts.
Leverage existing eval infra (ENG-3178) to run offline posterior checks and simulation harness; expose a lightweight online inference module for low-latency posterior updates.
APIs: POST /experiments (manifest), GET /experiments/:id/status, PATCH /experiments/:id/controls, POST /experiments/:id/rollback to allow manual override.
State machine: EXPERIMENT_STATE {DRAFT, RUNNING, PAUSED, HALTED, ROLLED_BACK, COMPLETED}. Controller transitions must be idempotent and persisted in the control-plane DB.
Audit logging: every auto-decision writes a structured entry to audit-log with decision_reason, posterior_snapshot, and links to related dashboards/PRs.
Scaling: online posterior updates should be batched and use approximate updating (e.g., moment-matching) to avoid per-request heavy compute. Heavy re-computation can be scheduled off the critical path.

ui_changes:
Experiment detail page: add 'Posterior view' with probability curves and decision boundary lines; include timeline of decisions and exposures.
Quick action buttons: Pause, Force-rollback, Escalate to SRE with pre-filled context (metric snapshots + links).
Safety budget panel: shows remaining exposure by cohort and estimated days until budget exhaustion at current ramp rate.
Simulation tab: allow product teams to run hypothetical degradations against historical data to preview controller behavior.

api_changes:
New resource ExperimentManifest with fields: name, description, primary_metric, guardrails[], min_samples, posterior_thresholds{}, safety_budget{}, shadow_policy{}.
New endpoints for controller control and status streaming (server-sent events) for live posterior traces.
Webhook contract for auto-rollback and alerts to integrators (Slack, PagerDuty, Ops runbook link).

tests_and_eval_harness:
Replay harness will replay 6 months of production traffic to validate Type I error (target < 5%) and mean time to detect various degradation magnitudes (±5%, ±20%).
Synthetic stress tests: create adversarial input distributions and latency spikes to ensure guardrail triggers work and shadow-only mode prevents user exposure.
A/B simulation grid: run experiments across sample rates (0.1% to 30%) and cohort skews to surface behavior under low-traffic scenarios.
Automated regression suite tied to PRs that runs a short simulation and checks controller's front-line decisions against golden rules.

rollout_plan:
Phase 0 (internal): implementation in staging using synthetic traffic, run 2-week smoke to validate infra and telemetry.
Phase 1 (beta): enable controller for internal product teams only, default conservative thresholds; gather feedback for 4 weeks.
Phase 2 (opt-in): expose to selected customers with design/solutions help; provide training and runbooks.
Phase 3 (ga): enable in console as an available option with recommended presets; provide migration guide for existing canary strategies.
Rollback semantics: auto-rollback will trigger a reversible operation that preserves old variant pinning for 24h; manual review required for permanent decommissions.

risk_and_mitigation:
Risk: noisy posterior estimates at low volumes could lead to false rollbacks. Mitigation: enforce minimum sample thresholds and a low-traffic backoff policy.
Risk: controller complexity increases surface area for bugs that could auto-rollback broadly. Mitigation: default disable auto-rollback for externally visible customers; require opt-in and use safety budgets.
Risk: operational cost for continuous posterior updates. Mitigation: use approximate incremental updates and compute heavy recomputations asynchronously.
Risk: lack of explainability for stakeholders. Mitigation: produce human-readable decision reasons and snapshot attachments in audit logs.

[Variant safeguard: sequential statistical tests, exposure ramps, and shadow launch controls]
description:
Build a first-class A/B and canary experimentation framework for model versions focused on safe rollouts. This ticket covers experiment setup UX, exposure and ramp controls (time-based and event-based), sequential statistical checks (alpha spending, stopping rules), shadow traffic plumbing, and automatic rollback triggers for safety regressions. The goal is to enable product and platform engineers to run short-lived canaries, multi-armed experiments, and continuous shadow tests with strong guardrails that prevent customer-facing regressions.

acceptance_criteria:
Console UI: experiment creation flow that supports canary and A/B modes, exposure schedules (linear, exponential, manual), and optional shadow-only routing
Exposure engine: server-side percent bucketing and time-based ramp policy that can be paused/modified without redeploy
Stats engine: sequential testing library integrated into the runtime that supports user-configurable alpha spending functions and minimum sample thresholds
Observability: per-variant dashboards with sample counts, latency P50/P90/P99, token-cost per request, and custom quality metrics from user-provided evals
Auto-rollback: configurable safety rules (e.g., delta_latency > 2x, increase in error rate > 0.5%, quality metric drop > 3%) that trigger automatic traffic rollback and create an incident ticket
Shadow traffic: ability to mirror X% of production traffic to a variant without affecting responses, with sampled diffs and KL/divergence style signals captured
APIs and SDKs: endpoints for creating/stopping experiments programmatically and fetching real-time exposure allocations
Audit and compliance: experiment audit trail capturing creator, changes, and exposures stored for 1 year (configurable)

implementation_todo:
ENG: build exposure service endpoints and percent-bucketing (ENG-43210)
ENG: integrate sequential-statistics library (psi-seq) into runtime and expose audit logs (ENG-43650)
ENG: shadow proxy component and sampled diff collector (ENG-43890)
ENG: console UI screens for experiment creation, live status, and an interactive ramp editor (ENG-44012)
ENG: auto-rollback orchestration that invokes routing change and incident creation (ENG-44101)
PM: write runbook and standard experiment templates for canary, multi-arm A/B, and shadow-launch tests
DX: sample prompts and eval sets for common regressions (summaries, completions, embeddings)

rollout_plan:
Phase 0 (A/A calibration): run 48h A/A on production with stats engine to tune false positive thresholds
Phase 1 (shadow launch): mirror 5% of traffic for 7 days, collect diffs and quality signals
Phase 2 (canary): linear ramp 0.5% -> 1% -> 5% with 12h holds, sequential checks at each hold
Phase 3 (scale): 10% -> 25% -> 50% after stability gates, then full promotion
Abort policy: if any safety rule triggers, rollback to previous allocation and open incident; require manual approval to restart the experiment

monitoring_signals:
Correctness: user-defined quality evals (per-prompt scoring) with baseline delta and confidence intervals
Latency: p50/p90/p99 with baseline ratio and absolute ms thresholds
Errors: model runtime errors, HTTP 5xx, tokenization failures
Cost: avg token cost and tokens per request delta
Upstream regressions: KL divergence and response distribution drift in shadow diffs

rollback_rules:
Immediate rollback if error rate increases by >0.5% absolute and sustained for 30 minutes
Rollback if latency p99 > baseline_p99 * 2 for 1 hour
Rollback if user-defined quality metric drops by >3% with p < 0.05 in sequential test
Soft-stop (pause ramp) if sample size for variant < configured minimum after scheduled hold

notes:
Design trade-off: prefer conservative default alpha spending (O'Brien-Fleming style) to minimize false positives on small canaries; allow advanced users to choose Pocock or continuous monitoring modes
We will implement sequential checks server-side to centralize decisioning and prevent client drift. This increases coupling but simplifies rollout rollbacks and audit logs.
Shadow traffic is implemented as asynchronous mirroring to avoid tail latency impact. Mirrored requests are sampled for token-level cost analysis and stored in a compressed trace store.
To reduce cost, prefix/KV cache warmup for canaries will reuse existing warm caches where possible; however, this can bias latency metrics — we will annotate warm-cache experiments explicitly.
Safety escalation: auto-rollback creates a standardized incident with stack traces and an optional revert flag for model variants in Dedicated and Private deployments

comments:
Sofia Martinez (Design): Request to surface warm-cache annotation in the metric timeline — otherwise teams will misinterpret improved latencies.
Ethan Zhou (Research): Recommend defaulting to two-stage rollouts: 1% -> 10% with a 24h hold to capture rare regressions before larger exposure.
Priya Raman (SRE): Auto-rollback should integrate with existing alerting (PagerDuty) and include a dry-run mode for safety-rule evaluation without changing traffic.
Liam O'Connor (Assignee): Planning to prototype the sequential checks with live A/A runs first to calibrate false positive rates. Will share early telemetry in two weeks.

[manifest rollup + attestation gating: canonical index and CI enforcement]
description:
Motivation: Private-installer releases need a single canonical manifest index that the CI can attest and gate on before publishing to customers. This PR implements a manifest rollup transformer that ingests per-arch/per-release artifact metadata, computes a deterministic canonical index (content-addressed ordering + delta graph), emits an attestable bundle, and wires an optional CI gating check that rejects a release if attestations are missing or provenance fails verification.

This is intended to reduce the number of manual steps in private-installer release runs, make rollbacks deterministic (by publishing a signed index snapshot), and give SREs/Customers cryptographic proof of the exact artifacts applied by an upgrade. Related Linear: ENG-4379 (manifest rollup) and ENG-4391 (attestation policy).

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds manifest-rollup binary and library used in the release pipeline to compose a single canonical manifest index from per-artifact metadata.
- Produces a deterministic index file (index.json.sha256) plus an attestable bundle (index.tar.gz.sig + provenance.json) suitable for cosign/canonical verification.
- Integrates a new CI gating job (release-index-verify) in .github/workflows/release.yml that verifies signatures, provenance chains, and KMS references before allowing the release job to proceed.
- Adds a backfill migration script to regenerate canonical indexes for a small subset of historical releases (used in the migration smoke tests).
- Documents the attestation policy and failure modes in docs/installer/release-attest.md.

Checklist: [x] unit + integration tests for rollup logic, [x] end-to-end CI check wired, [x] docs updated, [x] security review acknowledged.

Notes: The design favors deterministic ordering over human-readable diffs (index is content-addressed). The attestation policy is configurable per-env (see installer/release-attest.md). If the KMS path is unavailable the gate fails closed; we ship a temporary bypass keyed to a Linear ticket for emergency rollouts but it is disabled by default.

review_comments:
Ethan Park: Can we please avoid depending on a single KMS path? Suggested adding a fallback verify-only mode — responded that verify-only exists but the gate fails closed by default.
Sofia Martinez: Tests look good; request small refactor to separate signing from upload side-effects — author split attest.go into attest_sign.go and attest_upload.go in a follow-up commit.
Daniel Kim: Question about index size and memory use for very large releases; added streaming writer + chunked processing to indexer and added integration test that simulates 10k artifact entries.

merge_details:
Merged by squash on 2025-02-02 after CI green and two approvals. Merge commit message lists ENG-4379 and SUP-1284 and includes a short migration plan. Post-merge: CI kickstarted a backfill job for 5 historical release candidates against a staging bucket; no regressions observed. Documented emergency bypass procedure in ATTENTION.md.

release_notes:
Private-installer: canonical release index and attestation gating added; release CI now rejects un-attested indexes by default.
Operators: new migration script to backfill canonical indexes for selected historic releases.
Security: index bundles are signed (cosign) and provenance.json is published alongside the index for downstream verification.

[Batched release signing, compact provenance index and rollback checkpoint snapshots]
description:
Context: Private deployments that rely on airgapped installers and TUF-style release manifests are increasingly constrained by provenance index size and KMS signing rate limits during large coordinated rollouts. This PR introduces three coordinated changes: (1) batched signing with a pooled offline signer to reduce per-artifact KMS operations during release windows, (2) a compact, chunked provenance index format that permits streamable verification and reduced disk footprint on airgapped hosts, and (3) lightweight rollback checkpoint snapshots that enable fast, atomic rollbacks without replaying the full artifact graph.

What changed (high level):
- CI pipeline: new pipeline job ci/pipelines/offline-release.yaml that orchestrates batched signing, uploads chunked index pieces, and emits checkpoint metadata. The job supports both online (cosign/KMS) and offline (HSM/dedicated signer host) modes.
- Indexer: tools/indexer/compact_indexer.py implements chunking heuristics (by artifact-batch and time-window), gzip + snappy backends, and generation of per-chunk provenance attestations.
- Signer: ci/release/batched_sign_and_index.go adds a signer pooling mode that groups artifacts into signing batches (configurable), minimizes KMS API calls, and emits a batch manifest with cosign signatures and key identifiers.
- Rollbacks: scripts/mk-checkpoint.sh and release/checkpoints/README.md document creation and validation of rollback checkpoints. Checkpoints are small JSON manifests that reference chunk IDs and signature digests to allow atomic switch-over at deploy time.
- Helm & Terraform: helm/charts/private-installer/templates/release-index.yaml updated to reference chunked indexes and support staged preflight checks; terraform/modules/release-manifests/main.tf exposes variables for checkpoint retention and chunk lookup.
- Docs & tests: docs/private-installer/compact-index.md describes offline validation steps; added unit/integration tests to ci/integration/ that validate integrity across signing modes.

Testing & validation:
- Unit tests: index chunking, signature bundling, and checkpoint generation covered with parameterized tests.
- Integration: end-to-end CI job runs in sandbox using a local signer image + ephemeral KMS emulator; artifacts uploaded to staging registry and validated with the modified installer.
- Performance: compact indexing reduced on-disk index size by ~58% on our benchmark dataset (50k artifacts); batched signing reduced KMS request counts by ~83% for a typical release window (measured in ci/perf/signed_batch_bench).

Migration and rollout notes:
- Backwards compatibility: the installer supports both legacy index.json and the new chunked index via a compatibility shim; new installs will prefer chunked indexes when available.
- Rollout plan: gated behind a feature flag (release_index_chunking) for three weeks on staging, then progressively enabled for production releases. The CI pipeline preserves both index types for 30 days and creates checkpoints after each major release to support rollback.
- On-prem operator action: for airgapped upgrades, operators must copy chunk files and the corresponding checkpoint manifest to the airgap media; docs include a checklist.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: signer pooling increases blast radius if a batch is compromised. Mitigation: each artifact still has per-artifact signature entries in the batch manifest; key rotation and per-batch attestation UIDs are enforced.
- Risk: index chunk loss could prevent partial verification. Mitigation: each chunk has redundancy metadata and the installer will fall back to full index verification if chunk integrity fails.

Follow-ups: add delta-only chunk generation (ENG-2309) and long-term retention pruning policy (ENG-2310).

Maya: Added --batch-size flag and set default to 25 (see batched_sign_and_index.go).

Samir: The compatibility shim looks good, but add an integration test that intentionally drops a chunk to ensure fallback succeeds.
Maya: Added test_compact_index.sh which simulates missing chunk and validates fallback path.
Priya (approval): LGTM after tests green and pipeline vetted.
Diego (approval): Approved — signed batch schema looks sane.

release_notes:
- Add support for chunked/compact provenance indexes for private installer releases to reduce on-disk footprint and enable streamable verification.
- Introduce batched release signing mode to reduce KMS call volume during large rollouts.
- Add lightweight rollback checkpoints for fast, atomic rollback capability.
Operators: follow docs/private-installer/compact-index.md for airgap checklist.

[aggregate artifact origins into release index for private-installer]
release_notes:
Add cross-repo artifact origin aggregation to release index used by private-installer; includes pipeline changes, index schema extension, signature/verification cross-checks, and docs for operator consumption.

description:
Context and motivation: Private-installer releases consume artifacts produced by multiple build pipelines (core runtime, helm charts, terraform modules, third-party vendor artifacts). Existing release index entries pointed to single build blobs but lost origin metadata (repo/build-job/container image digest). This PR extends the release index generation to aggregate origin provenance across repos/pipelines so operators can inspect where each artifact came from and verify chain-of-custody at install time.\n\nWhat this PR does: - Adds an `origins` aggregate block to the release index JSON that lists source repository, pipeline job id, build commit, and optional SBOM/cosign references per artifact. - Modifies the private-installer indexer job to query multiple artifact registries and cross-reference artifact digests to upstream build metadata (via the new origin-mapper service). - Adds origin-mapper microservice (lightweight Go lambda) that merges build metadata across internal buildkite/jenkins/job-run APIs and returns a normalized origin statement for an artifact digest. - Updates CI/CD pipelines: new step in release pipeline to call origin-mapper and attach signed origin blobs to TUF/manifest staging area. - Enhances verification: indexer validates cosign signatures on origin blobs (if present) and records signature verification result in the index. - Adds operator docs and an index API example in private-installer docs for auditors to query artifact origins during upgrades/rollbacks.\n\nChecklist (implemented): - [x] Extend release index schema (index-schema/v2) with `origins` field and verification metadata - [x] Origin-mapper service implementation and unit tests - [x] Release pipeline changes (buildkite/jenkins) to emit origin blobs - [x] Indexer changes in private-installer repo to consume origin blobs - [x] Add integration test that replays multi-repo build metadata into staging index - [x] Docs: private-installer operator guide section on origin queries - [x] Security review: minimal privileges for origin-mapper to query job metadata APIs\n\nCommits (high-level): - feat(indexer): add origin mapping hooks and schema v2 metadata - feat(origin-mapper): initial service with buildkite and jenkins adapters - ci(release): add origin-stage and sign-origin steps, upload to staging TUF area - docs(installer): add operator guide and example queries - test(integration): multi-repo origin aggregation smoke test - fix(ci): tolerate missing SBOM references for third-party mirrored artifacts\n\nFiles/areas changed (high-level): - private-installer/cmd/indexer: indexer changed to call origin-mapper and persist origins into index JSON - private-installer/internal/index/schema_v2.go: new schema and JSON marshaling changes - tools/origin-mapper/: new Go service and adapters for buildkite/jenkins - infra/ci/pipelines/release.yml: added origin-stage, sign-origin and upload steps - docs/private-installer/origins.md: operator documentation and API examples - charts/private-installer/values.yaml: small annotation for chart provenance - scripts/dev/replay-origins.sh: local dev helper to simulate upstream metadata\n\nReview conversation (summary): - Lina: "Nice; can we guarantee origin-mapper rate limits won't blow up during a large release?" Author: "Origin-mapper queues queries and caches job metadata for 24h; added circuit-breaker and bulk query path. See origin-mapper/README for eviction rules." - Ethan: "Add tests for mirrored artifacts where upstream job metadata is absent." Author: "Added integration test that marks missing upstream metadata and attaches best-effort origin assertion with source:mirror and mirror-ref." - Zoe: "Signature verification path looks good, but require operator flag to enforce failed verification as hard-fail for critical releases." Author: "Added CLI flag `--enforce-origin-verification` to indexer and documented recommended usage in docs." - Security review (internal): "Ensure origin-mapper tokens scoped read-only and short lived." Author: "Confirmed; CI injects ephemeral tokens, and service uses read-only tokens with minimal TTL. Details in infra/ci/README-security.md."\n\nCI summary: - Initial run: integration tests failed due to missing adapter for legacy Jenkins job API (fixed in second commit). - Second run: unit + integration + lint passed. - E2E staging run: origin blobs uploaded and cosign verification passed for signed artifacts; unsigned third-party artifacts recorded with `verified:false`. [intake-orchestrator: sign & index release assets for private installer]
release_notes:
- Add intake orchestrator job to build, attest, and index private-installer release artifacts. - Ensures signed attestations per-asset and a compact ingestion manifest for air-gapped installs. - Backwards-compatible index format with a migration shim for older installers.

description:
Motivation: Private installs need a robust intake pipeline that separates artifact build from signing and indexing so edge air-gapped clusters can pull a compact, verifiable release manifest. Current pipeline bundles all steps which makes offline mirroring brittle and hard to audit. This PR introduces an 'intake-orchestrator' actor that produces per-asset attestations and a sharded compact index consumed by the private-installer. What changed: 1) New CI job ci/pipelines/intake-orchestrator.yaml that orchestrates build->push->attest->index phases. 2) tools/release/attestor: per-asset attestor that uses cosign to produce detached attestations and stores provenance metadata in JSON-LD. 3) tools/release/index-writer: writes a compact release intake manifest with shard metadata, artifact fingerprints, and attestation links. 4) charts/private-installer: adds index-configmap and values toggles to control index version and fallback behavior. 5) terraform module for index hosting and signed index rotation. 6) docs and integration test to validate end-to-end intake to installer flow. Implementation notes: the attestor produces an attestation envelope that includes artifact.mediaType, digest, build_id, builder_id and an incremental raft-like 'artifact_raft_id' used to order shards. Index-writer shards entries by prefix hash to keep shards < 10MB and emits a top-level index.json that references shard manifests. The orchestrator retries transient push/sign failures and exposes per-artifact status to the CI job. Security: signing is performed with cosign using a rotated key per-release. cosign-rotate.sh automates rotation into the release KMS and updates the index metadata to point to the current key id. To avoid exposing private keys in CI logs, signing is executed in an isolated ephemeral runner with KMS-backed key handles; we also added audit log hooks. Backwards compatibility: index-writer emits an index.version field. When the private-installer reads an index with version >1 it uses the new shard fetcher; we added a migration shim in charts that supports older versions by doing a single-file fetch if the installer is on older releases. Tests & CI: added test/integration/intake-end-to-end.test which runs a mini registry, performs a build, pushes artifacts, signs them, writes index shards, and validates the installer's fetch+verify path. CI pipeline includes unit tests for attestor and index-writer and an integration stage that runs on a gated runner. Performance: shard sizing heuristics chosen after benchmarks in benchmark-lab show optimal shard target ~6-8MB for our typical release mix. Observability: index-writer emits Prometheus metrics (index_shards_written, attestation_failures, signing_latency) and traces that are captured by the release pipeline. Rollout plan: feature gated behind values.privateInstaller.indexing.enabled=false by default. Rollout steps: enable in canary release pipelines for next two releases, smoke verify downloads from an air-gapped mirror, then flip default to true. Migration: added migration docs in docs/release/private-intake.md with step-by-step for operators to migrate older installers. Review notes: Marco asked to ensure attestation format is stable and recommended adding a deterministic canonicalization step for the JSON-LD; implemented canonicalizeAttestation() and added tests. Hannah requested stronger CI assertions for key rotation; added an explicit rotation test and a preflight that validates cosign key presence before writing index. Ravi suggested reducing memory footprint of index-writer; refactored streaming encoder to reduce peak memory during large releases. Conversation log highlights: Marco Alvarez (reviewer): "Please ensure attestations are deterministic and signed against a canonicalized payload. Also add a compatibility version in the index." Priya (author): "Added JSON-LD canonicalization and index.version. PTAL." Hannah Cho (reviewer): "CI should fail if cosign key missing or KMS access denied to avoid unsigned indexes being published." Priya: "Added preflight check and unit test, CI now blocks on key presence." Ravi Patel (reviewer): "Index-writer memory was high in my run; consider streaming encoder." Priya: "Refactored to streaming encoder, peak memory dropped from ~180MB to ~28MB in tests." Approvals: Marco approved on 2025-11-17. Hannah approved on 2025-11-18 after CI rerun. Merge: squashed and merged into main on 2025-11-18 via squash merge. CI: all checks passed at merge time. Files changed (high-level): added orchestration pipeline YAML, attestor and index-writer Go packages, chart updates to mount index config, terraform module changes to host index shards behind signed CDN, cosign rotation helper script, integration test and docs. Related work: ties to ENG-4122 (release automation rework) and ENG-4219 (attestation format consolidation). Rollback: index-writer writes a lockfile with the previous index root so consumer can roll back to prior manifest; terraform module includes an invalidate endpoint that can be used to roll forward to last-good index. Notes for on-call: if index ingestion fails in production, disable values.privateInstaller.indexing.enabled in values and re-deploy; the installer will fall back to legacy single-file index retrieval. This PR is intentionally conservative in surface area and gated; further follow-ups will convert other pipelines to use the intake-orchestrator and add more attestation fields for SBOM integration.

[Introduce delta artifact signing + rollback-plan generator for private-installer releases]
description:
Motivation: Private deployments need predictable, auditable updates and safe rollback paths for clusters that cannot reach our hosted control plane. This PR adds a compact delta artifact signing flow and an automated rollback-plan generator that: 1) produces per-release delta bundles (tar.gz deltas + provenance metadata), 2) signs delta manifests with our KMS-backed signing key, 3) generates a machine-readable rollback plan (instructions + required artifacts) for every release bundle, and 4) exposes Terraform-friendly outputs so on-prem upgrade orchestrators can fetch verified deltas and apply rollbacks without live API access. This is intended to reduce bandwidth for upgrades, accelerate patch creation, and give operators clear, auditable rollback instructions.

5 commits: (1) build: add delta bundler and provenance schema; (2) security: integrate KMS signing helper and rotation hooks; (3) tooling: rollback-plan generator and YAML schema; (4) terraform: exports to module outputs + example usage; (5) tests: add CI validations and e2e smoke for apply/rollback flow.
