[Policy & Process Almanac: Company-wide Standards and Templates]
Overview:

This document is the single-source reference for company-wide policies and process templates across Access & Permissions, Change Management, Data Management, Procurement & Expenses, Vendor Management, Travel, and Internal Templates. Intended audience: people-ops, finance, engineering, product, security, and managers who must follow or approve cross-functional requests.

Goals:
- Provide clear, actionable procedures for common requests and approvals.
- Reduce turnaround time by standardizing thresholds, owners, and templates.
- Ensure security and compliance controls are applied consistently.

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to all Redwood Inference employees, contractors, and people with accounts on Redwood-managed systems.
- Exceptions require documented approval via the Exceptions process (see Escalation & Exceptions).

Quick policy matrix (summary):
| Domain | Primary owner | Typical SLA / Threshold | Key artifacts |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Access & Permissions | people-ops / security | Standard requests: 3 business days; Emergency elevated access: 2 hours | Access request template, RBAC group list |
| Change Management | eng-platform | Normal changes: 5 business days pre-notice; Major infra changes require CAB approval | Change request template, rollback playbook |
| Data Management | security / finance-legal | Data deletion requests: 10 business days; Retention: defined per classification | Data classification matrix, retention schedule |
| Procurement & Expenses | finance-legal | Purchases <$5k: 3 business days; >$50k: exec approval + 20 business days | PO template, vendor evaluation checklist |
| Vendor Management | finance-legal / security | New vendor onboarding: 15 business days | Vendor questionnaire, contract template |
| Travel | people-ops / finance-legal | Pre-approval: 5 business days; Expense submission: within 15 days of return | Travel request & expense templates |

1) Access & Permissions
Principles:
- Principle of least privilege by default.
- Temporary elevation preferred over long-lived high privileges.
- All privileged access requires an owner and an audit TTL.

Role definitions (examples):
- Reader: read-only to resources; auto-approver via manager.
- Contributor: ability to create resources; manager + tech lead approval.
- Admin: elevated privileges; security review + VP approval for permanent access.

Standard request flow (self-service for most):
1. Employee opens Access Request using the access_request template (link in Templates section).
2. Manager verifies business justification and approves in the system.
3. Technical owner approves (for contributor/admin).
4. Provisioning occurs via IaC or identity provider (IdP) automation.
5. Access is auto-expired after TTL unless renewed via a documented review.

Access thresholds requiring extra review:
- Any request granting "Admin" or "Privileged" role on production systems requires security review.
- Cross-tenant/VPC access requires network security sign-off and on-call notification.

Example CLI request (for advanced teams using the RBAC API):
```
curl -X POST https://identity.redwood.example/api/v1/access-requests \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"user":"alice@redwood.com","role":"prod-db-contributor","expiry":"2026-04-15","justification":"incident debug"}'
```
RBAC groups (current canonical list):
- redwood-readonly
- redwood-devs
- redwood-prod-ops
- redwood-admins
(Updates to the canonical list must be proposed via the Change Management process and documented in the RBAC registry.)

2) Change Management
Change types and required approvals:
- Minor (non-production config changes, docs): owner approval.
- Standard (code deploy, infra config): owner + release manager approval.
- Major (schema migrations, network changes, infra rollouts): CAB approval (weekly CAB meeting).
- Emergency (P1/P0 incidents): follow the Incident Commander's emergency change flow; retrospective required.

Change lifecycle checklist (before scheduling):
- Define impact window and rollback plan.
- Confirm pre-deployment validation tests.
- Notify stakeholders via the release calendar (email + Slack channel).
- Schedule change outside blackout windows unless emergency.

Pre-approval windows and SLAs:
- Standard changes: submit 5 business days before planned date.
- Major changes: submit 10 business days before planned date.
- The CAB meets every Tuesday at 09:00 PT; decisions recorded in the change tracker.

Rollback policy:
- Every change must include a tested rollback procedure that can be completed within the rollback window (target: 60 minutes for infra rollbacks).
- If rollback cannot be completed automatically, include manual runbook steps with required on-call contacts.

Change request template (brief):
- Title, owner, scope, start/end window, rollback steps, validation plan, stakeholder list, risk level.

3) Data Management
Classification levels:
- PUBLIC: safe to share externally. Retention: 3 years unless specified.
- INTERNAL: company-internal; retention as required by business.
- CONFIDENTIAL: PII, financials, customer data; retention per legal & contract.
- RESTRICTED: regulated data (HIPAA, PCI, etc.) — special handling and encryption at rest + in transit.

Retention & deletion:
- See the Data Retention Schedule table below for defaults. Deletions must be recorded in the Data Deletion Log.

Data retention schedule (examples):
| Data class | Default retention | Owner |
|---|---:|---|
| Public assets (marketing) | 3 years | Marketing lead |
| Internal analytics | 2 years | Data Platform team |
| Customer logs (non-PII) | 1 year | Customer Success |
| Customer PII | as contracted; minimum 7 years | Legal 

Encryption & key management:
- All CONFIDENTIAL and RESTRICTED data must be encrypted with customer-managed keys where contractually required.
- KMS usage: AWS KMS + HSM integration for private deployments; key rotation every 365 days recommended.

Data transfer checklist (example YAML template for cross-region movement):
```
transfer_request:
  owner: eng-data-platform
  source: us-west-2-pipeline
  destination: eu-central-1-lake
  data_class: INTERNAL
  approval: [security, legal]
  date_required: 2026-04-01
```

4) Procurement & Expenses
Procurement tiers & approval matrix:
| Tier | Value | Approver(s) |
|---|---:|---|
| Tier 1 | <$5,000 | Requester manager |
| Tier 2 | $5,000 - $50,000 | Manager + Finance (budget owner) |
| Tier 3 | >$50,000 | Director + Finance + Legal review (if third party) |

Purchase order (PO) process:
1. Raise a PO request in the procurement tool with supplier info and SOW.
2. Finance verifies budget and issues PO.
3. Contracts team reviews if third-party software/service.
4. Supplier receipt must match PO; invoices routed to AP for three-way match.

Expense policy (travel and non-travel):
- Employees must submit expenses within 15 calendar days of transaction.
- Meals and incidental per diem capped per location (see Travel section).
- Unapproved or late submissions may be delayed or denied.

Allowed payment methods:
- Company card: primary for travel and approved subscriptions.
- Personal reimbursements: supported with receipts and manager approval.

5) Vendor Management
Onboarding checklist (new vendor):
1. Vendor Profile: legal name, tax ID, region.
2. Security Questionnaire: SOC 2/ISO attestation or complete CAIQ.
3. Contract review: legal and procurement.
4. Risk assessment: data access, SSO, encryption requirements.
5. PO / payment terms setup.

Vendor risk levels and controls:
- Low: consultants without access to customer data — standard contract.
- Medium: vendors with limited system access — SSO + scoped permissions + annual review.
- High: vendors with customer data or production access — security controls, quarterly audits, and encryption requirements in contract.

Renewal & offboarding:
- Notify stakeholders 60 days before contract end for renewals.
- Offboarding checklist includes termination of all credentials, return/destruction of data, and deletion from asset registry.

6) Travel Policies
Booking & approvals:
- Use the corporate travel tool for all business travel.
- Domestic trips <48 hours require manager pre-approval. International travel requires security & people-ops notification.

Per diem & reimbursements:
- Per diem rates follow the government locality table adopted by Redwood; see travel-per-diem template.
- Economy class for flights under 6 hours; premium economy or business requires director approval.

Expense submission steps:
1. Submit expense within 15 days of return with itemized receipts.
2. Manager approves in expense system.
3. Finance processes payment on the next payroll cycle.

Safety & emergency contact:
- Before international travel, register trip with people-ops and provide emergency contact information.

7) Internal Templates & Quick Links
Included templates (copy/paste into the request tools):
- Access request template: (fields) requester, manager, role, expiry, justification, technical owner.
- Change request template: (fields) title, owner, windows, rollback steps, validation steps.
- Vendor onboarding checklist (as described above).

Sample Access Request (one-line):
Title: Temporary PROD DB Contributor
Requester: alice@redwood.com
Manager: bob@redwood.com
Role: prod-db-contributor
Expiry: 2026-04-12
Justification: customer incident debug

8) Roles & Ownership (contact pointers)
- people-ops: people-ops@redwood.example (policy questions, travel, benefits)
- finance-legal: procure@redwood.example (POs, vendor contracts)
- security: sec-eng@redwood.example (access reviews, data policy)
- eng-platform: infra@redwood.example (change board, release calendar)

9) Escalations & Exceptions
Exception request process:
1. Submit an Exceptions Request document with justification and compensating controls.
2. Owner team reviews within 5 business days.
3. If risk > medium, route to the Cross-Functional Exceptions Panel (CFEP) for final decision.

Emergency escalation flow (P0/P1):
- Page on-call via PagerDuty -> Incident Commander -> Notify CTO and Head of Security -> Temporary emergency change allowed with post-incident CAB review.

Appendix: Useful links and artifacts
- Access request template: /confluence/templates/access-request
- Change request tracker: /confluence/tools/change-tracker
- Data retention schedule: /confluence/policies-and-process/data-retention-2025
- PO template: /confluence/templates/purchase-order
- Vendor questionnaire (CAIQ): /confluence/security-and-compliance/vendor-caiaq

Revision history:
- 2026-01-12: Created by Priya Menon; initial policy draft.
- 2026-02-20: Added procurement tiers and vendor renewal timings (reviewers Marco Alvarez, Sofia Patel).
- 2026-03-05: Finalized RBAC group canonical list and CLI example; published.

End of document.


[comp-and-bands-review-playbook-and-merit-process-2026]
Summary
This playbook describes Redwood Inference’s annual compensation band review and merit cycle, plus the operational steps managers and people-ops must follow for offer approvals, pay adjustments, and pay-equity checks. It combines timeline, approval matrix, calibration guidance, communication templates, and escalation paths. Purpose: ensure fair, defensible, and timely compensation decisions that align with performance, market data, and budget constraints.

Scope
Applies to all full-time and permanent part-time employees in North America and Europe for Redwood-hosted payroll. Contractors and third-party temps follow separate vendor-pay guidelines (see vendor-finance). Covers base salary, spot bonuses, title changes tied to band movement, and merit increases. Does not cover equity refreshes or promotion bonus programs (handled by Total Rewards special programs).

Principles
- Market-driven: use up-to-date benchmark data (Mercer/Levels.fyi/internal comp bands).
- Pay-equity first: ensure adjustments reduce documented gaps by role, gender, and region before discretionary over-target increases.
- Manager accountability: managers own calibration preparation and written justification for out-of-band decisions.
- Transparency: employees receive clear rationale and timing for changes; non-confidential summaries published for org-level trends.

Definitions
- Band: pay band range for a role/level (e.g., ENG-3: $140k–$200k USD).
- Target midpoint: market-aligned midpoint used for benchmarking.
- Merit pool: team-level budget allocated for salary increases (percentage of payroll).
- Out-of-band increase: raise that would move base outside the role band or above the established band cap. Requires escalated approvals.

Compensation Bands (example table)
Role/Level | Region | Band Min | Band Midpoint | Band Max
ENG-2 | US (CR) | $110,000 | $135,000 | $160,000
ENG-3 | US (CR) | $140,000 | $170,000 | $200,000
SWE-Staff | US (CR) | $200,000 | $235,000 | $280,000
Product-PM-2 | US (CR) | $120,000 | $150,000 | $185,000
Note: Bands vary by region currency and cost-of-labor adjustments. Always reference the latest band CSV in People-ops -> Compensation -> current-bands.csv.

Annual Merit Cycle Overview (timeline)
1) Planning (Q4 prior fiscal year): People-ops publishes budget guidance and merit pool % targets to Heads of Org. Example: company target merit pool = 6% of base payroll for FY26; teams may be allocated between 3%–9% depending on performance and hiring posture.
2) Calibration & Manager Prep (Jan): Managers prepare draft increases, linking to performance reviews and calibration docs. People-ops schedules calibration windows by department.
3) Executive Calibration (Feb): Cross-org calibration meetings with Director+ to review above-target requests and out-of-band moves.
4) Final Approvals (early Mar): Finance and People-ops finalize budgets and sign off.
5) Payroll Cutover (mid Mar): HR inputs finalized changes to payroll provider; effective date is first full pay period in April.
6) Employee Communications (same week as cutover): Managers deliver 1:1 messages with pay letters and FAQs.

Manager Checklist (before submitting increases)
- Confirm employee's band and current comp vs midpoint and market comp.
- Attach performance summary: top 3 accomplishments, evidence of impact, and rating.
- Show proposed increase, new base, and % of merit pool used.
- For out-of-band requests, include business rationale, retention risk analysis, and suggested alternate mitigations (bonus, promotion timeline).
- Check for potential pay-equity regressions in your team (people-ops will run automated checks but managers should flag anomalies).

Calibration & Decision Rules
- Standard increases: up to 6% for most employees (guided by band position and performance rating).
- High-performer increases: 6%–12% with documented impact and peer calibration support.
- Promotions with role/level change: typically include base increase of 10%–20% depending on band movement; must be accompanied by new role description and promotion packet.
- Out-of-band (above band max): CTO or People Ops VP approval required + Director-level justification.
- If requested increase exceeds available merit pool, managers must prioritize based on retention risk and business criticality and provide rebalancing plan.

Approval Matrix (who signs what)
- Manager (team level): sign-off on proposed increases and file documentation.
- Director: approves standard increases and promotions within team budget.
- People-ops Lead: approves calibration exceptions up to $X total additional spend per month (internal threshold).
- VP People Ops + Finance: signs off on out-of-band moves, comp compression resolutions > 10% gap, and region-level policy changes.

Offer & Hiring Exceptions (fast-track rules)
- Standard offers: within band and sign-on threshold require Manager + Recruiter approval.
- Above-band offers <= 10% above band max: Director + People-ops approval (expedites available for time-sensitive hires).
- Critical hires or counteroffers that exceed 10% above band max: require VP People Ops + Finance and an approved business case.
- Emergency retention increases: documented retention risk, attempted interventions (bonus, non-monetary), and a 6-month follow-up plan.

Pay Transparency Guidance (manager-facing)
- Public information: high-level band ranges and compensation philosophy are published internally.
- Private information: individual salary numbers are confidential and should not be disclosed by managers except to payroll, finance, or people-ops staff with legitimate business need.
- Manager talking points for 1:1s: focus on performance impact, development plan, and timing. If asked directly about peer salaries, defer to People-ops and offer to explain band structure instead.

Template: Manager 1:1 Pay Conversation
1) Affirm contribution and context: "I appreciate your work on X; because of the impact on Y, we've recommended..."
2) Explain change succinctly: "Your new base will be $XXX, effective April 1. This reflects performance/market/promotions."
3) Next steps: "We'll update payroll and you’ll see the increase on your next paycheck; here's the development plan that supports continued growth."
4) If asked about colleagues: use band-level and philosophy language; do not disclose numbers.

Escalations and Appeals
- Employee questions escalate to manager -> People-ops rep -> HRBP -> VP People-ops. People-ops maintains an appeals log.
- Appeals must be submitted within 30 days of communication and should include the employee’s rationale and supporting evidence.
- People-ops will respond with a timeline for review (typical response: 10 business days).

Operational Runbook: Submitting a Request
1) Manager completes the Compensation Worksheet (People-ops -> Templates -> comp-worksheet.xlsx).
2) Attach performance summary and promotion packet (if relevant).
3) Submit via People-ops compensation portal by the calibration deadline.
4) People-ops runs automated equity and compression checks and returns an exception flag report.
5) If exception flagged, manager addresses or escalates with added justification.

Data & Reporting Requirements
- Every increase must be recorded in the compensation ledger with: employee ID, current/base salary, new salary, effective date, approver names, and justification.
- People-ops publishes anonymized quarterly compensation health dashboards (labels: median-to-midpoint ratio, gender pay gap by level, out-of-band %).

Common Scenarios & Guidance
- Compression (junior > senior): file a compression mitigation plan; prioritize critical cases for immediate adjustment.
- Cross-region adjustments: use regional cost-of-labor multiplier table; consult People-ops for exchange-rate locked effective dates.
- Promotion denied after performance rating improved: provide written developmental plan and reassessment timeline (usually next 6 months).

FAQs
Q: When will I see my increase?
A: Effective date aligns with payroll cutover (first full pay period in April).
Q: Can managers give raises outside the merit cycle?
A: Spot increases are rare — limited to retention or market-correction situations and require documented exception.

Appendix: Useful Links
- Compensation band CSV: People-ops -> current-bands.csv
- Compensation worksheet template: People-ops -> Templates -> comp-worksheet.xlsx
- Appeals form: People-ops -> Compensation Appeals -> submit-a-claim
- Payroll provider integration docs and cutover checklist: Finance -> Payroll -> payroll-cutover.md

Ownership & Contacts
- Document owner: Aisha Patel (People Ops Manager)
- Operational contact: Marcus Chen (Total Rewards Sr. Analyst)
- Policy steward: VP People Ops (for policy changes and executive approvals)

Revision history
- 2025-04-15: Created (initial framework and band examples).
- 2026-02-12: Updated merit pool guidance and approval thresholds; added remote-region multiplier note.

This playbook is the authoritative guidance for compensation and merit processes at Redwood Inference. For exceptions or region-specific questions, contact the operational contact listed above.

[Region Surge Prediction and Operator-Guided Failover Playbook]
Summary:

This runbook describes operator-guided failover for region-level capacity surges predicted by our ensemble signal. The playbook combines an automated prediction signal (SurgeScore) with human validation steps to reduce false positives and avoid unnecessary cross-region traffic shifts. Target audience: oncall platform engineers and SRE run leads.

Scope and goals:

- Scope: Redwood Inference hosted and dedicated control-plane traffic routing to edge/data-plane regions (cloud regions and peered POPs).
- Goals:
  - Detect high-confidence regional client demand surges before SLOs degrade.
  - Provide step-by-step operator guidance for controlled, reversible failover to secondary regions or burst capacity pools.
  - Preserve token-cost and latency SLOs while minimizing user-visible errors.

Key metrics and SLOs referenced:

- API foreground p50/p95 latency SLOs: p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 400ms.
- Token error-rate SLO: < 0.1% request-level errors.
- Region capacity headroom target: >= 15% free GPU slots per shard.

Signals and thresholds (inputs to decision):

- SurgeScore (model-based): probability [0-1].
  - Low: < 0.3 — informational only.
  - Medium: 0.3–0.6 — require human review.
  - High: > 0.6 — trigger oncall paging.
- Region-p95-latency-ratio: p95_region / p95_global > 1.4
- Queue depth growth: 5min growth rate > 30% and sustained 3 measurements
- Scheduler evictions: >= 5 evictions/min over 2 consecutive mins
- Token error spike: 3x baseline in rolling 5m

Dashboards and alerts to consult:

- Dashboards:
  - "Region Health Overview" (Dash ID: PLT-REGION-001) — high-level latency, error-rate, queue depth by region.
  - "Surge Prediction Heatmap" (PLT-PRED-003) — shows SurgeScore across regions and tenants.
  - "Burst Pool Utilization" (PLT-BURST-002) — current burst capacity usage.
  - "Scheduler Evictions and GPU Interference" (PLT-GPU-007).
- Alerts (examples):
  - alert: RegionHighSurgeScore
    expr: surge_score{job="surge-pred"} > 0.6
    runbook: this doc (section: Emergency failover)
  - alert: RegionP95Spike
    expr: increase(region_p95_ratio[5m]) > 0.4
  - alert: QueueDepthGrowthHigh
    expr: rate(api_queue_depth[1m]) > 0.3

Who should be paged:

- Primary: platform-oncall (rotation)
- Secondary: runtime-systems team lead (if infrastructure-level action likely)
- Optional: customer-success for high-profile customers with region affinity (runbook owner to decide)

Preliminary triage (0–10 minutes):

1. Confirm the SurgeScore alert in the prediction dashboard. Note the affected region, tenants, and expected surge duration (model provides 15/60/240m buckets).
2. Validate telemetry: check Region Health Overview for p95/p50, errors, queue depth and evictions.
3. Check scheduled maintenance and deployment slate (Platform Calendar) to rule out planned work.
4. If SurgeScore is Medium (0.3–0.6): run synthetic validation (section: Synthetic validation). If no corroborating signals, monitor and re-evaluate in 10 minutes.

Synthetic validation (commands and queries):

- PromQL sample to validate queue depth vs baseline:
  avg_over_time(api_queue_depth{region="eu-west-1"}[10m]) / avg_over_time(api_queue_depth{region="eu-west-1"}[6h])
- Synthetic request script (kube job):
  kubectl run synth-validate --image=redwood/synth-check:stable --restart=Never -- \
    --target-region eu-west-1 --profile low-latency --qps 5 --duration 60s
- Expected result: < 5% of synthetic requests exceed p95 threshold. If > 20% fail, escalate immediately.

Decision matrix: when to enact operator-guided failover

- Conditions to proceed (need 2/3):
  1) SurgeScore >= 0.6 OR SurgeScore >= 0.45 with sustained p95_ratio > 1.4
  2) Queue growth sustained and scheduler eviction rate high
  3) Synthetic checks confirm > 10% degradation or token error spike
- If 2/3 conditions met, proceed to controlled failover. Otherwise continue monitoring and mitigations (cache warming, prefix caching).

Operator-guided failover steps (controlled):

Estimated duration: 8–25 minutes depending on propagation.

1. Announce on #platform-ops and set incident channel. Post summary: region, SurgeScore, metrics, tentative action.
2. Scale burst pools (noninvasive):
   - CLI: rwoodctl capacity burst-scale --region eu-west-1 --factor 1.5 --reason "Surge validation"
   - Verify burst pool nodes come online in bursts dashboard.
3. If burst scaling insufficient after 3m, prepare traffic shift playbook:
   a. Select target region(s) with capacity headroom (prefer same continent).
   b. Put routing into "guided-failover" mode (no automatic spread):
      - API: curl -X POST $CONTROL_PLANE/api/v1/routing/mode -d '{"mode":"guided","from":"eu-west-1","to":["eu-central-1"]}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
   c. Apply weighted steering: start at 5% traffic shift to target region for top 5 tenants by traffic, monitor for 2 minutes.
   d. Increase in 10% increments every 2 minutes while monitoring p95 and token errors.
4. If target region p95 degrades > 20% over baseline, immediately rollback last increment and reduce weight by 50%.
5. Once 80–90% of non-affinitized traffic is shifted and SLOs are stable, enable routing automation back to normal but keep a conservative rate limit for 30 minutes.

Emergency failover (when SLOs failing and rapid action required):

- Trigger criteria: sustained token error-rate > 0.5% or p95 > 2x baseline for > 3 minutes.
- Steps:
  1) Page leaders and set incident severity to SEV3+.
  2) Execute immediate traffic redirect to fallbacks:
     rwoodctl routing redirect --from eu-west-1 --to eu-central-1 --force --percent 50
  3) Throttle low-priority tenants via soft-quota:
     rwoodctl quota set --tenant <tenant-id> --region eu-west-1 --qps 5
  4) If cross-region redirect causes cost explosion, enable cost-guard: rwoodctl cost-guard --enable --threshold 1.5x
  5) Declare incident and follow incident runbook for customer comms.

Rollback criteria and procedure:

- Rollback if: target region p95 worsens by > 20% or token error-rate increases after shift, or if core infra events are detected in target region.
- Procedure: decrement traffic weights to last known-good state in 2 steps, scale down burst pools if overprovisioned, and restore routing mode to "conservative".

Post-action checklist (within 60m):

- Confirm all tenants have stable latencies and errors.
- Collect the timeline: SurgeScore, synthetic results, routing weight changes, and operator actions. Attach to incident channel.
- Open a short incident report (IR) and tag for retrospective.

Runbook commands and examples (cheat sheet):

- Check SurgeScore (CLI):
  rwoodctl metrics get --name surge_score --region eu-west-1 --window 5m
- Burst-scale example: rwoodctl capacity burst-scale --region eu-west-1 --factor 1.5
- Guided routing mode: curl -X POST $CONTROL_PLANE/api/v1/routing/mode...
- Immediate redirect: rwoodctl routing redirect --from $REG --to $TO --percent 50 --force

Game day and simulation exercises (recommended cadence):

- Quarterly simulation: run a synthetic surge for 120m against a sandbox region. Validate detection, operator playbook timing, and rollback.
- Bi-annual full game day: include customer-success and sales for comms practice.

Known risks and mitigations:

- Cross-region latency penalty: mitigate by preferring same-continent targets and by warming caches in the target region prior to shifting significant traffic.
- Cost runaway: enable cost-guard and monitor burst-pool billing metrics. Pre-authorize spend thresholds with finance for emergency scaling.
- Tenant affinity violations: mark high-affinity tenants in the routing config to avoid shifting critical traffic.

Ownership and escalation contacts:

- Runbook owner: Dana Chen (platform-ops lead) — dana@redwood.ai
- Pager: platform-oncall rotation (Slack alias @platform-oncall)
- Exec escalation: Marco Ruiz (runtime-systems)

Postmortem and continuous improvement:

- For every guided failover, capture a short retrospective within 72 hours with:
  - Root cause hypothesis
  - Which signals were correct/incorrect
  - Time-to-decision metrics and blind spots
  - Action items with owners and due dates

Change history:

- 2025-11-12: Created by Dana Chen.
- 2026-01-09: Updated decision matrix and added SurgeScore thresholds after Q4 simulations.

Appendix: telemetry queries and recommended dashboard panels

- PromQL: surge_score by region -> avg_over_time(surge_score[1m])
- PromQL: region p95 ratio -> histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le,region)) / scalar(global_p95_baseline)

Tables (quick references):

| Action | CLI / API | Expected time | Safety check |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Burst-scale | rwoodctl capacity burst-scale --factor X | 1–3m | node ready count > 0 |
| Start 5% shift | routing API POST | 1–2m | target p95 within 10% |
| Increment +10% | routing API POST | 2m | monitor token error-rate |
| Emergency redirect 50% | rwoodctl routing redirect --force | <1m | oncall confirm SEV3 |


[Workspace promotion and fast rollback for multi-region GPU IaC]
Overview:

This runbook defines the canonical process for promoting Terraform changes across multiple regions that host GPU pools, and for performing an expedited rollback if a promotion causes capacity or network regressions. It focuses on safety, recovery speed, and minimal customer impact for Redwood Inference's multi-region GPU infra.

Intended audience:
- Infra engineers on-call for gpu-fleet, cloud-accounts, and terraform modules
- Release engineers operating the IaC pipelines
- SRE and capacity planners who verify post-promotion health checks

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to Terraform-managed resources that affect GPU capacity, networking (VPCs, route tables, NATs), and core IAM/billing boundaries for tenant pools in all production regions.
- Backend: S3 remote state with object versioning + DynamoDB state lock (AWS).
- CI: Buildkite or equivalent pipeline that runs plan/apply per workspace and region.
- Snapshots: We maintain automated state snapshots in s3://redwood-terraform-snapshots/ and retain at least 30 days.

Goals:
1) Promote changes with clear canary and verification gates per region.
2) Make it possible to fully rollback in under 20 minutes for common failure modes (failed applies, capacity regressions, route/NAT misconfig).
3) Preserve audit trail and avoid state corruption during forced operations.

Terminology:
- workspace: Terraform workspace used to represent environment/region (e.g., prod-us-west-2, prod-eu-central-1).
- promotion: moving a module change from staging->canary->prod across regions.
- snapshot: a point-in-time export of the terraform state file (terraform state pull).

Prerequisites and safety checks before promotion:
- Confirm workspace naming: lower-case, region suffix, semantic release tag in commit message (e.g., terraform/aws/gpu: v1.23.0).
- CI pipeline green for unit tests, fmt, and terraform validate on the branch.
- Remote-state is unlocked: aws dynamodb get-item --table-name tf-locks --key '{"LockID":{"S":"<workspace>"}}' should return empty or a stale owner older than 30m.
- Verify S3 object versioning enabled for the backend bucket and the latest snapshot exists.
- Capacity freeze window check: ensure no scheduled major migrations or QBR windows.

Promotion workflow (recommended):
1) author push -> PR with module changes and description of resource impact (estimated new GPUs, expected rolling reboots).
2) automated plan in CI produces plan artifacts per region workspace. Attach plan to PR.
3) Staging apply: run apply in a non-customer-facing staging workspace backing a canary tenant pool. Verify smoke tests.
4) Canary region: pick a single low-traffic production region (by traffic matrix). Apply with limited scope (use -target for initial canary if change is large).
5) Verification gates after canary (30–60 minutes):
   - GPU warm-pool size matches intended delta (infra metric: gpu.pool.warm_count).
   - No increase in 5xxs or throttled requests for downstream serving services (api.slo.token_latency > threshold).
   - Networking path checks succeed (internal curl to service endpoints, NAT rules validated).
6) If gates pass, schedule phased promotion across remaining regions with staggered windows (min 15–30m between regions).

Terraform commands and operational snippets:
- Select workspace:
  terraform workspace select prod-us-west-2 || terraform workspace new prod-us-west-2
- Create plan file (CI):
  terraform init -backend-config="bucket=redwood-tfstate" -reconfigure
  terraform plan -var-file=regions/us-west-2.tfvars -out=plan.prod-us-west-2
- Apply from plan with remote locking enforced in CI agent:
  terraform apply -input=false plan.prod-us-west-2
- Snapshot state (manual fast snapshot):
  terraform state pull > /tmp/prod-us-west-2-$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ).json
  aws s3 cp /tmp/... s3://redwood-terraform-snapshots/prod-us-west-2/ --acl bucket-owner-full-control
- Quick state restore (read-only verification):
  terraform state pull | jq '.modules[].resources[] | select(.type=="aws_instance")' > verify.json

Fast rollback procedures (common failure modes):
A. Failed apply or partial apply detected immediately after apply finishes:
1) Stop further promotions and add "rollback-in-progress" label in incident channel.
2) If apply failed and left resources partially created: run terraform apply again against the original plan if safe. If that is not safe, go to snapshot restore (see C).
3) For safely revertible changes (variable flips, scaling down new count): create a short revert commit that restores the previous module input and run plan+apply in that workspace.

B. Capacity regression (warm pool or allocations decreased / degraded):
1) Detect via alerts: gpu.pool.warm_count < expected by >10% for 10 minutes or gpu.alloc.fail_rate increased >1%.
2) If the change is a config variable (e.g., desired_warm_pool_size): revert the variable via a targeted apply. Use -target to limit scope.
3) If networking rule misconfiguration suspected, revert affected route tables / security groups via terraform apply with a revert commit. Simultaneously open routing validation job (curl tests) to confirm restore.

C. State corruption or irrecoverable dependency mismatch: snapshot restore path (slower, reliable).
1) Notify on-call SRE and create incident.
2) Acquire latest snapshot version from s3://redwood-terraform-snapshots/<workspace> using object version id.
3) Lock the workspace (DynamoDB): add manual lock owner and mark maintenance in PagerDuty incident.
4) Replace remote state object (example):
   aws s3 cp s3://redwood-terraform-snapshots/prod-us-west-2/<versioned-file> s3://redwood-tfstate/prod-us-west-2.tfstate --metadata-directive REPLACE
   (Ensure correct ACL and server-side encryption headers preserved.)
5) Run terraform plan -refresh-only and validate that drift is resolved.
6) Apply a no-op plan and then run standard smoke tests before unlocking.

Emergency fast-rollback checklist (<= 20 minutes target):
- Roles on-call: infra-oncall (primary), infra-release (secondary), platform-sre (pager).
- Step 0: Create incident channel and annotate affected regions + commit SHA.
- Step 1: If simple revert possible, merge revert commit and trigger CI apply in affected workspace with concurrency=1. (Estimated time 5–10m).
- Step 2: If snapshot needed, request snapshot restore (operator): aws s3 cp <snapshot> back to bucket (10–15m depending on region/object size).
- Step 3: Run smoke tests and confirm metrics.
- Step 4: Close incident and record actions in postmortem doc.

Observability and verification tests (automated):
- CI/Smoke jobs executed after apply per region:
  1) gpu-pool-health-check (returns 200 and expected pool sizes)
  2) internal-network-echo (connectivity over service mesh)
  3) token-latency probe (synthetic requests comparing pre/post latencies)
- Dashboards:
  - gpu-infra/Capacity Overview (gpu.pool.* metrics)
  - infra-network/Egress & NAT health (nat.errors, route.failures)
- Alerts:
  - gpu-pool-warm-count < threshold for 10m -> page infra-oncall
  - terraform-apply-error (CI) -> page infra-release slack + email

Automation and CI pipeline recommendations:
- Keep plan artifacts per region and attach to PR for review. Do not rely solely on plan logs.
- CI agents perform remote backend init with -reconfigure on each run to avoid stale state issues.
- Set pipeline concurrency to 1 per workspace to avoid accidental concurrent applies.
- Provide a manual "promote-to-region" step that requires two infra approvals for changes that touch network or IAM.
- Use the pipeline to automatically create state snapshots before each prod apply and tag snapshot with commit SHA.

Configuration table (core constraints):
- Terraform version: "1.5.x" in CI and local dev (must match exact patch for providers).
- AWS provider: pinned to a tested provider version (example: 5.17.0).
- Backend bucket: redwood-tfstate (versioning: enabled).
- Snapshot bucket: redwood-terraform-snapshots (lifecycle: 90d, encryption: SSE-KMS).
- Lock table: redwood-tf-locks (DynamoDB with TTL on lease metadata).

Roles and ownership:
- Promotion owner: infra-release team (runbook executor).
- On-call responder: infra-oncall (SRE).
- State restore approvals: require two infra-release members plus a platform-sre reviewer for region changes impacting networking.

Post-incident follow-up and metrics to record:
- Time to detect, time to rollback, time to full recovery (target: detect <10m, rollback <20m, recovery <60m).
- Root cause summary and a concrete remediation (e.g., adjust canary size to 5% of traffic).
- Update CI gating rules or module tests to prevent recurrence.

Appendix: Useful commands and examples
- List workspace versions and select:
  terraform workspace list
  terraform workspace select prod-eu-central-1
- Pull remote state snapshot locally:
  terraform state pull > snapshot.json
- Force unlock (use only with approval):
  terraform force-unlock -force <LOCK_ID>
- S3 copy for snapshot restore (example):
  aws s3 cp s3://redwood-terraform-snapshots/prod-us-west-2/20250206T150000Z.json s3://redwood-tfstate/prod-us-west-2.tfstate --metadata-directive REPLACE --sse aws:kms --acl bucket-owner-full-control

Related runbooks and docs:
- remote-state-segmentation-and-cross-account-locking-primer (for backend design)
- gpu-capacity-reconciliation-audit-and-credits-ledger (for cost reconciliation after incidents)
- ci-cd-gpu-image-promotion-canary-cd-playbook (for pipeline patterns used by promotion)

Revision history:
- 2024-09-12: Created by Sofia Ramirez (initial draft).
- 2024-11-05: Added fast rollback checklist and snapshot restore steps after on-call drill.
- 2025-02-06: Clarified approval matrix and tightened snapshot retention guidance.

Contact: infra-release@redwood.example.com for questions and exceptions.

[Onboarding Event Schema (v1) — Hosted API onboarding + checklist progress]
## Overview
This page defines the **standardized event schema (v1)** for onboarding and checklist progress tracking across Redwood Inference (Hosted API first; Dedicated/Private later). The goal is consistent instrumentation from:
- **Gateway / serving edge** (server-side events for request outcomes)
- **Control plane** (API key creation, quotas/budgets, model pinning, routing/fallback policy)
- **Console** (page views / actions that do not have a server-side equivalent)

This schema is used by:
- The **Checklist Progress Service** (step completion state)
- The **Onboarding KPI dashboards** (TTFS/TTFP, funnel, drop-offs)
- Support tooling (interpreting “what happened” without collecting sensitive payloads)

## Goals
1. Provide a single, validated envelope for onboarding events.
2. Ensure events are **PII-free** and do not include prompts/responses.
3. Support **idempotent** and **order-independent** processing (out-of-order delivery is expected).
4. Constrain high-cardinality dimensions to keep analytics datasets and dashboards stable.
5. Provide a clear **versioning strategy** for future expansion.

## Non-goals
- This spec does **not** define the UI checklist step taxonomy (see checklist template / PRD).
- This spec does **not** define storage/warehouse tables (owned by Telemetry/Data Eng).
- This spec does **not** authorize arbitrary custom events from customer apps.

---

## Data classification + privacy requirements
**Classification:** Internal product telemetry (non-customer-content).

**Must NOT include (hard prohibitions):**
- Prompt text, completion text, embeddings, images, tool arguments/results
- Customer-provided end-user identifiers (email, name, phone, IP address)
- Raw HTTP headers beyond the explicitly allowed fields below
- Free-form error messages that might contain customer data (use enumerations)

**Allowed (with constraints):**
- Redwood tenant identifiers (UUID)
- Redwood user identifiers (UUID) *only for Console / control plane actions*
- Redwood API key ID (UUID) — never the API key secret
- Request IDs / trace IDs generated by Redwood
- Enumerated error types and status codes

**PII note:** Some fields (e.g., `actor_id`) can still be considered personal data in certain jurisdictions. Treat this stream as covered by standard Redwood telemetry retention and access controls (see Security review page).

---

## Event envelope (required for all onboarding events)
All events MUST conform to the following envelope.

### Required fields
| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `event_name` | string | Canonical name. See Event Catalog below. |
| `schema_version` | string | Schema major version. For this document: `"1"`. |
| `event_id` | string (UUID) | Unique ID for this event. Used for dedupe. |
| `occurred_at` | string (RFC3339) | When the action happened (source time). |
| `received_at` | string (RFC3339) | When telemetry ingested it (ingest time). |
| `source` | string | One of: `"gateway"`, `"control_plane"`, `"console"`, `"sdk"` (limited), `"batch_backfill"`. |
| `tenant_id` | string (UUID) | Redwood tenant/org identifier. |
| `environment` | string | `"prod"`, `"staging"`, `"dev"` (Redwood internal environments only). |

### Common optional fields (allowed if applicable)
| Field | Type | Constraints / Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `actor_id` | string (UUID) | Redwood Console user ID. Required for Console events; optional elsewhere. |
| `api_key_id` | string (UUID) | Allowed for gateway/control plane events. Never include the key secret. |
| `request_id` | string | Redwood-generated request ID; max 64 chars. |
| `trace_id` | string | Trace ID; max 64 chars. |
| `region` | string | Enumerated cloud region set (see Cardinality constraints). |
| `deployment_mode` | string | `"hosted"` (v1). `"dedicated"`/`"private"` reserved for later. |
| `sdk_language` | string | `"python"`, `"typescript"`, `"go"`, `"java"`, `"ruby"`, `"unknown"`.
| `sdk_version` | string | Max 32 chars; must match `^v?[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+.*$` when known. |
| `client_platform` | string | `"server"`, `"browser"`, `"cli"`, `"unknown"`.
| `user_agent_family` | string | Normalized UA family (e.g., `"redwood-sdk"`, `"openai-compat"`, `"curl"`); max 32 chars. |
| `checklist_step_id` | string | Only for step-related events; enumerated list owned by DevEx/Console (no free-form). |
| `result` | string | `"success"`, `"failure"`, `"partial"`.
| `http_status_code` | string | String form to avoid numeric parsing issues; must be 3 digits when present (e.g., `"200"`, `"401"`). |
| `error_type` | string | Enumerated (see Error types). Do not include raw error messages by default. |
| `idempotency_key` | string | Max 80 chars; stable per logical action. Strongly recommended for control plane / console actions. |

### Error types (enumeration)
Use `error_type` only when `result != "success"`.
- `"auth_invalid_api_key"`
- `"auth_missing_api_key"`
- `"auth_insufficient_permissions"`
- `"rate_limited"`
- `"quota_exceeded"`
- `"billing_inactive"`
- `"invalid_request"`
- `"model_not_found"`
- `"model_not_available"`
- `"timeout"`
- `"upstream_error"`
- `"internal_error"`
- `"unknown"`

---

## Cardinality constraints (hard rules)
To keep the analytics dataset stable, the following rules apply:

1. **No free-form “labels” or “tags” fields**.
2. `event_name` is a strict enumeration (see catalog). New names require Telemetry approval.
3. `region` must be one of:
   - `"us-east-1"`, `"us-west-2"`, `"eu-west-1"`, `"eu-central-1"`, `"ap-southeast-1"`
   - `"unknown"` (only if source cannot determine)
4. `sdk_language` must be one of the allowed set listed above.
5. `user_agent_family` must be chosen from a maintained allowlist; fall back to `"unknown"`.
6. `checklist_step_id` must be an approved step identifier (kebab-case, max 48 chars). No dynamic content.
7. Avoid adding fields that would explode cardinality (examples: `model_name` free-form, customer endpoint URLs, arbitrary exception strings).

---

## Event catalog (v1)
The events below are the v1 set used for onboarding funnel + checklist progress.

### Control plane events
| event_name | When emitted | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `"onboarding.api_key.created"` | API key created in Console or API | Include `api_key_id`, `actor_id` when available. |
| `"onboarding.api_key.deleted"` | API key deleted | Rarely used for funnel; helps Support triage. |
| `"onboarding.quota.viewed"` | Quota page viewed (Console) | Console source only. |
| `"onboarding.quota.updated"` | Quota changed | Include `result`, `error_type` if failure. |
| `"onboarding.budget.created"` | Budget alert created | Include `idempotency_key`. |
| `"onboarding.model_pinning.updated"` | Model version pin set/changed | Do not include free-form model names; use `model_id` only if it is from a controlled catalog ID set. |
| `"onboarding.fallback_policy.updated"` | Fallback policy set/changed | Include policy type enumeration only (e.g., `"region_failover"`, `"model_variant"`). |

### Gateway events (server-side request lifecycle)
| event_name | When emitted | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `"onboarding.request.first_2xx"` | First successful (2xx) inference response for tenant | Primary signal for **TTFS**. Include `http_status_code`, `request_id`, `region`, `sdk_language` when known. |
| `"onboarding.request.first_stream_established"` | First time a streaming response successfully starts | Do not log tokens/content. “Established” means first server event was sent. |
| `"onboarding.request.first_401"` | First auth failure due to missing/invalid API key | Include `error_type` (`auth_missing_api_key` or `auth_invalid_api_key`). |
| `"onboarding.request.first_403"` | First forbidden / permissions issue | Use `auth_insufficient_permissions`. |
| `"onboarding.request.first_429"` | First rate limit response | Use `rate_limited`; include `http_status_code` = `"429"`. |
| `"onboarding.request.first_5xx"` | First server error for tenant during onboarding window | Use `upstream_error` or `internal_error` (no raw message). |

### Console events (navigation + non-server actions)
| event_name | When emitted | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `"onboarding.console.checklist_viewed"` | Checklist UI rendered | Required for measuring exposure vs completion. |
| `"onboarding.console.step_opened"` | User opens a specific step detail | Include `checklist_step_id`. |
| `"onboarding.console.deep_link_clicked"` | Click from step to target page/docs | Include `checklist_step_id` and `target` as an enum (`"docs"`, `"console_page"`, `"quickstart"`). |

### Checklist step events (normalized)
Some systems will emit explicit step completion events when there is no reliable server-side derived signal.

| event_name | When emitted | Requirements |
|---|---|---|
| `"onboarding.checklist.step_completed"` | A step transitions to complete | MUST include `checklist_step_id` and a stable `idempotency_key`. |
| `"onboarding.checklist.step_reset"` | Admin/support resets a step | MUST include `checklist_step_id`, `actor_id`, and `reason_code` enum (see below). |

**Checklist admin reset reason codes (enum, optional field `reason_code`):**
- `"support_troubleshooting"`
- `"customer_request"`
- `"bug_workaround"`
- `"data_correction"`

---

---

## Emission guidance (source-specific)
### Gateway
- Emit events **server-side** at the gateway after auth and routing decisions.
- For “first_*” events, the gateway should rely on a **durable per-tenant latch** (or emit all occurrences and let the progress service compute the first; see ADR).
- Do not attempt to infer checklist steps that require Console configuration (e.g., budgets) purely from request traffic.

### Control plane
- Emit on successful write transactions (create/update) and include `result="failure"` + `error_type` for validation errors.
- Always include `idempotency_key` for create actions to prevent duplicate “created” events from retries.

### Console
- Console events are allowed only for:
  - checklist exposure/interaction
  - page views where the server cannot reliably infer intent
  - explicit step completion when no derived signal exists
- Console MUST NOT send any customer content. If a UI form accepts free text, do not emit it.

### SDK (limited)
SDK-originated onboarding events are **not** a general channel. Allowed only for “client hint” enrichment when the gateway cannot determine values (e.g., `sdk_language`, `sdk_version`). SDKs should prefer encoding hints via user-agent tags rather than a separate event stream.

---

## Versioning and change management
### Schema version field
- `schema_version` is a **major version** string.
- This document defines version `"1"`.

### Backwards-compatible changes (stay on v1)
Allowed without bumping `schema_version`:
- Adding a new optional field with clear constraints
- Adding new `event_name` values (requires review + update to this page)
- Adding new enum values to fields *only if they are low-cardinality and documented*

### Breaking changes (require v2)
- Renaming fields
- Changing meaning of an existing field
- Removing fields or changing required/optional status
- Relaxing privacy constraints (e.g., allowing customer content)

### Deprecation policy
- Deprecate `event_name` values only with **30 days notice** and a parallel emission period.
- Maintain mapping logic in the progress service if needed to support older clients during rollout.

---

## Validation + data quality requirements
Telemetry ingestion MUST enforce:
1. Envelope presence and required fields.
2. `schema_version == "1"` for v1 pipeline.
3. Enum validation for `source`, `deployment_mode`, `sdk_language`, `region`, `error_type`.
4. Max length validation for IDs/strings as specified.
5. Dropping/rejecting payloads containing prohibited fields (prompt/content indicators).

Recommended automated monitors:
- Event freshness SLO: p95 `received_at - occurred_at` < 5 minutes (prod)
- Sudden spikes in `onboarding.request.first_401` and `onboarding.request.first_429`
- Missing `tenant_id` or malformed UUIDs > 0.1% (should be near-zero)

---

- Dedicated/Private deployment modes: expected additional fields (cluster_id, vpc_region) and privacy review.

[One-Stop Ops Ecosystem Guide: Access, Change, Data, Procurement, Vendors, Travel, Templates]
Overview

This playbook consolidates company-wide operational policies and end-to-end processes that touch access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel policy, and reusable internal templates. The goal is to reduce cross-team ambiguity, shorten approval cycles, and enforce minimum compliance & security standards while preserving developer velocity.

Scope

- Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and vendor representatives who interact with production or sensitive systems.
- Covers cloud & on-prem resources, vendor-supplied services, and any expense or procurement action initiated on behalf of Redwood.

Primary service references (examples)

- Identity & Access: Okta (SSO), AWS IAM, GCP IAM, internal RBAC service (redwood-auth).
- Secrets & Keys: HashiCorp Vault, AWS KMS (customer keys where required), HSM-backed key stores for Restricted data.
- Procurement & Expenses: ProcureFlow (internal procurement portal), Concur (travel & expense), Stripe/Adyen for payments.
- Change & Ticketing: Jira (change requests), PagerDuty (oncall routing), Confluence (document storage).

Roles & Responsibilities

- Requester: Initiates requests (access, change, purchase, travel). Responsible for accurate justification and cost coding.
- Approver: Assigned manager or budget owner; must validate business need and security posture.
- Security Reviewer: Reviews high-risk access, vendor security questionnaires, and data handling clauses.
- Procurements Team (Finance): Runs vendor onboarding, issues POs, validates contracts.
- Platform/Infra Owner: Executes changes or grants system-level access; responsible for operational testing and rollback procedures.

Access & Permissions

Principles:
- Least privilege by default; grant only the permissions necessary for the task.
- Time-bound access for most high-privilege grants; default max of 72 hours unless business case provided.
- Separation of duties: staff who approve changes should not be the only ones making them in production for critical systems.

Request process (standard flow):
1) Requester fills the Access Request template in ProcureFlow/Confluence (use the template at end of this doc).
2) Request is routed to Requester’s Manager for approval (SLA: 48 business hours).
3) If resource is flagged "Sensitive" or "Restricted" (see Data Classification) Security Reviewer is cc'd and must approve (SLA: 24 business hours).
4) Platform Owner implements the grant and records evidence (timestamp, approver id, change id).

Expedited/Emergency access:
- For urgent incidents, request via PagerDuty incident channel with an Emergency Access ticket in Jira. Emergency grants are logged and must be reviewed in the next 72-hour post-incident review.

RBAC matrix (simplified)

| Role | Typical permissions | Access duration | Approval path |
|------|---------------------|-----------------|----------------|
| Viewer | Read-only dashboards, logs | 6 months | Manager auto-approve |
| Developer | Deploy to non-prod, read prod metrics | 90 days | Manager approval |
| Oncall Engineer | Escalation, runbooks, limited prod run commands | 30 days (auto-rotate) | SRE lead approve |
| Admin / SRE | Create/destroy infra, token minting | 72 hours default, require MFA & hardware key | Manager + Security |

Helpful CLI example (internal):

redwood-ops-cli request-access --resource arn:aws:iam::123456789:role/prod-readonly --reason "Investigate latency spike" --duration 4h

(Outputs a Jira change request link and creates an audit entry in Vault audit log.)

Change Management

Classification:
- Minor: Non-user-facing, low-risk config changes (no approval required beyond owner).
- Standard: User-facing or infra changes that require manager approval and a scheduled window.
- Major: Releases, database schema changes, or anything touching PII or Restricted data. Requires change advisory board (CAB) review.
- Emergency: Incident-driven, followed by postmortem and retroactive CAB notification.

Change windows and SLOs:
- Standard change review SLA: 3 business days for routine approvals.
- Deployment rollback detection: monitor for 5-minute error spike > 3x baseline; automatic rollback policy triggers if threshold persists for 15 minutes.

Rollout patterns and minimum telemetry:
- Canary: 5–10% traffic for minimum 10 minutes, monitor latency (p95), error rate, and key business metrics.
- Gradual ramp: 25% → 50% → 100% with 15–30 minute guardrails at each step.
- Feature flags should be used for user-facing changes; use LaunchDarkly or internal flag service.

Emergency change workflow (short):
1) Create Emergency Change ticket in Jira with "EMERG" tag.
2) Notify oncall via PagerDuty.
3) Apply minimal change and validate.
4) Open post-incident review within 72 hours; CAB to record decision and any permanent changes.

Data Management

Classification tiers (company-wide):
- Public: Information intended for external publication.
- Internal: Company operational data; default for most internal documents.
- Sensitive: Customer-identifiable data, analytics derived from identifiable users. Requires encryption at rest & transit, access audits.
- Restricted: PII, PHI, regulated data. Requires HSM-backed keys, monthly access review, and two-person access approvals for exports.

Data retention & backup policy:
- Critical logs: 365 days online, 5 years in cold storage (S3 Glacier).
- Production DB snapshots: Daily snapshots retained for 30 days, weekly snapshots retained for 6 months, monthly for 3 years (if required by contract).
- Backups verification: Restore test quarterly for each critical service; Platform team owns verification and records it in the quarterly Ops report.

Encryption & key management:
- All Sensitive/Restricted data must be encrypted at rest using AES-256. Keys for Restricted must be KMS-backed and rotate at least every 365 days.
- Secrets stored only in HashiCorp Vault; secrets rotation policy: database credentials rotate every 30 days by default.

Data sharing & exports:
- Exports of Sensitive/Restricted data require documented business justification, Security sign-off, and a temporary export token with a max TTL of 2 hours.

Procurement & Expenses

Principles:
- Centralized vendor onboarding for any vendor with access to company systems or any expected spend > $5k.
- Purchase Order (PO) required for capitalized hardware or any contract > $10k annually.
- Card-level expenses for travel and small purchases follow Concur workflows with receipts.

Approval matrix (examples):
- <$1,000: Team lead approval.
- $1,000–$10,000: Department manager approval and budget code.
- >$10,000: Finance (Procurements Team) + Legal review for contract terms.

Vendor onboarding checklist (minimum):
1) Completed vendor security questionnaire (VSA).
2) Contract template signed (SLA, liability, data handling, termination).
3) PO issued (if applicable).
4) Technical contact listed and access provisioning plan documented.
5) Insurance & compliance evidence collected.

Common procurement steps (short form):
1) Create procurement request in ProcureFlow with justification and budget code.
2) Manager approves per matrix.
3) Finance verifies vendor standing and issues PO.
4) Legal signs contract if required.
5) Platform configures vendor access per onboarding plan.

Expense & travel specific rules:
- Nightly hotel rate cap (domestic): $300/night unless pre-approved.
- Meal per diem: $60/day domestic; actuals reimbursed with receipts up to policy limits for international travel.
- Mileage reimbursed at IRS / local statutory rate; file through Concur within 30 days.

Vendor Management

Ongoing oversight:
- Quarterly vendor risk reviews for vendors with production access or > $25k annual spend.
- Security posture checks: penetration test evidence, SOC2 report, ISO27001 where relevant.
- SLAs & remediation: Vendors must commit to incident notification within 4 hours for security incidents affecting Redwood.

Offboarding:
- Access revocation must be coordinated between Platform Owner and Vendor Management team.
- Verify data return/destruction clauses executed.
- Perform asset inventory reconciliation: credentials, SSH keys, API keys revoked, and confirmed in Vault audit logs.

Travel Policy (high level)

Booking & approvals:
- All travel must be booked via ProcureFlow/Concur with pre-approval for international travel.
- Managers approve travel based on business justification and budget.

Health, safety & security:
- For travel to high-risk regions, additional Security clearance and travel advisory review are required. Reach out to security@redwood.ai for approvals.

Templates & Attachments

This section contains short, copy-and-paste templates for common requests. Insert into ProcureFlow or Confluence forms as required.

1) Access Request (short form)

- Title: Access Request — [resource] — [team]
- Requester: [name] / [email]
- Resource: [ARN / service name / URL]
- Justification: [business reason]
- Duration requested: [hours / days]
- Approver: [manager name]
- Security impact: [None / Sensitive / Restricted]

2) Change Request (Jira summary)

- Summary: [Service] — [Change type] — [Planned UTC window]
- Description: Technical plan, rollout steps, monitoring queries, rollback steps, stakeholder list, impacted customers.
- Verification criteria: exact metrics (p95 latency < X ms, error rate < Y%) and smoke-test checklist.

3) Vendor Onboarding Checklist (to attach)

- Company legal name:
- Contract owner (Finance):
- Security questionnaire link:
- PO number:
- Prod access plan (yes/no): details

Example: Access Request CLI payload (JSON)

{
  "requester": "alice@redwood.ai",
  "resource": "arn:aws:iam::123456789:role/prod-readonly",
  "reason": "Investigate perf regression",
  "duration_hours": "4"
}

Audit & Reporting

- Monthly access review: managers receive an automated summary of active grants and must certify or revoke.
- Quarterly compliance report: Finance+Security produce a report summarizing vendor posture, high-risk access, and unresolved findings.

Appendix: Owners & Contacts

[Request Lifecycle and Controls Catalog — 2026]
Purpose
-------
This catalog defines the lifecycle for operational requests and the associated control gates across Access & Permissions, Change Management, Data Management, Procurement & Expenses, Vendor Management, and Travel. It provides standardized request forms, approval matrices, SLAs, and template artifacts to reduce tribal knowledge and speed consistent decisions.

Scope
-----
Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and vendor agents who submit or approve requests for: system access, configuration changes, data uses, purchases, vendor engagements, and company travel. Exceptions must be approved by the owning function and recorded in the exception registry.

Principles
----------
- Least privilege and just-in-time access.
- Separation of duties for financial and security-critical approvals.
- Automated enforcement where possible; manual review when risk exceeds automation thresholds.
- Clear SLAs and escalation paths for business continuity.

Roles and responsibilities
--------------------------
- Requester: initiates the request with required justification and attachments.
- Approver: designated role(s) who evaluate and approve/reject per the approval matrix.
- Owner/Maintainer: team that implements the request (SRE, infra, facilities, travel ops).
- Security Reviewer: performs data/privacy/security review when flagged.
- Finance Reviewer: approves expenditures above configured thresholds.
- Legal Reviewer: reviews contracts, vendor terms, and high-risk data-sharing agreements.
- Compliance & Audit: retains records and performs periodic reviews.

Access & Permissions (IAM)
-------------------------
Purpose: Standardize requests for cloud/console/API access and role grants.

Access request flow (standard)
1. Requester completes Access Request form in ProcureFlow/IAM Portal including justification, duration, resource scope, and owner.
2. Auto-validation run by IAM Service: checks policy templates and existing memberships.
3. If low-risk (pre-approved role & <30 days) automatic grant occurs; otherwise routed to Approver(s).
4. Security Reviewer is added if role includes sensitive scopes (PII, audit logs, production write).
5. Owner executes grant and documents ticket ID.

SLAs and thresholds
- Standard requests: 24 business hours.
- High-priority (production incident): 4 hours (phone + portal).
- Emergency after-hours: on-call approver phone escalation; retrospective approval within 24 hours.

Approval matrix (examples)
| Resource category | Typical approver(s) | Security review required | Auto-grant allowed? | Max duration |
|-------------------|---------------------|-------------------------:|--------------------:|------------:|
| Non-prod read-only| Team lead            | No                      | Yes                 | 90 days     |
| Non-prod write    | Team lead + SRE      | No                      | Conditional         | 30 days     |
| Prod read         | Product manager + SRE| Conditional              | No                  | 30 days     |
| Prod write        | Product manager + SRE + Security | Yes         | No                  | 7 days      |
| Audit logs access | Security + Compliance| Yes                     | No                  | 7 days      |

RBAC templates (recommended labels)
- role:data-scientist: read-only datasets + dev compute
- role:inference-operator: production inference write, model deploy APIs
- role:observability-reader: metrics/logs read-only (no PII)

CLI example (request automation)
```
# Request temporary role for debugging
rlctl access-request --user alice --role inference-operator --resource project:redwood-prod --duration 6h --reason "investigating latency spike"
```

Change Management
-----------------
Scope: configuration changes to infra, runtime, CI/CD pipelines, production model rollouts, and security controls.

Change categories
- Standard (low-risk, pre-authorized routine changes)
- Normal (planned changes requiring approval and scheduling)
- Emergency (out-of-band fixes for incidents)

Normal change process (numbered)
1. Create RFC in Change Registry (ticket template: ChangeRequest). Include scope, rollback plan, test plan, schedule, owners.
2. Technical review by SRE/Platform and dependency owners.
3. Security and compliance review if change touches data control plane or auth.
4. Scheduled maintenance window and stakeholder notification.
5. Execute change and mark lifecycle states: planned -> staging -> validation -> production -> closed.

Emergency change flow
- On-call SRE follows emergency authorizer list (Primary SRE on-call, then Engineering Manager, then CTO).
- Execute emergency fix and attach retrospective within 48 hours.
- Post-incident RFC must be submitted within 5 business days.

Change guardrails
- All production changes must have automated rollback steps and observability runbooks attached.
- No schema-changing data migrations in production without dry-run and 2 approvers.

Data Management
---------------
Data classification
- Restricted (PII, PHI, financial records): encryption at rest and in transit, access by exception only.
- Internal (product telemetry, internal notes): restricted to employees, aggregated exports require approval.
- Public (marketing materials): permitted for external distribution.

Retention and deletion
- Default retention: product telemetry 90 days (hot), 365 days (cold); logs 180 days.
- Restricted data retention must be approved by Data Governance and Legal.
- Data deletion requests follow standard ticketed workflow and are recorded in the Data Deletion Log.

Data use approvals
- Any project that trains models on customer data must complete a Data Use Assessment and obtain Legal + Security signoff.
- Example: dataset_redwood_customers_2025 requires DU-approved contract & KMS policy.

Encryption and key management
- All production encryption keys must be provisioned via KMS/HSM. Key rotation every 90 days for high-sensitivity keys.

Procurement & Expenses
----------------------
Procurement thresholds and approvals
| Amount band (USD) | Required approvals | Procurement channel |
|-------------------:|--------------------|-------------------|
| <$2,500            | Manager            | Card/ExpensesApp  |
| $2,500–$25,000     | Manager + Finance  | ProcureFlow (PO)  |
| $25,000–$250,000   | Manager + Finance + Procurement | ProcureFlow + Contracting |
| >$250,000          | Exec sponsor + Legal + Procurement | Strategic sourcing |

Preferred procurement flow
1. Create Purchase Request with justification, budget code, and vendor information.
2. Finance validates budget and is assigned approver.
3. Procurement reviews for preferred vendors and negotiates T&C if applicable.
4. PO is issued; vendor onboarding checklist triggered for new vendors.

Expense policy
- Employees should expense costs within 60 days. Card disputes must be filed within 90 days.
- Travel bookings: Economy or lowest reasonable fare; upgrade only with exec approval.

Vendor Management
-----------------
Vendor risk levels and onboarding checklist
- Risk levels: Low, Medium, High (based on data access, control plane integration, criticality).
- Onboarding steps for new vendor (checklist):
  1. Business justification and owner assignment.
  2. Security questionnaire (VendorRisk) completion.
  3. Contract with minimum security clauses (encryption, breach notification, subprocessor list).
  4. Procurement creates PO and payment terms.
  5. Technical integration review and test plan.
  6. Compliance records stored in Vendor Registry.

Contractual minimums (summary)
- Data processing agreement for any vendor handling customer data.
- Right to audit clause for high-risk vendors.
- Minimum 30-day termination notice and documented exit plan for critical services.

Vendor monitoring
- Quarterly review for medium/high vendors; monthly health checks for critical platform vendors.
- Maintain scorecard: uptime, incident response time, patch cadence, security findings.

Travel Policies
---------------
Pre-approval and booking
- All travel reimbursed must be pre-approved by the Requester’s manager in the TravelPortal.
- Book through TravelPortal or approved agency for company liability coverage.

Per diems and allowable expenses
- Domestic: meals up to $75/day; Lodging: reasonable single occupancy rate.
- International: per-region rates available in TravelPortal templates.
- Alcohol may be expensed only while entertaining clients with prior manager approval.

Safety and emergency
- Employees traveling to countries with Level 3 or higher travel advisories require Security team approval.
- Emergency contact: travel-support@redwood.com and on-call security phone.

Templates & quick artifacts
--------------------------
Included templates (stored in Templates folder in ProcureFlow)\- Access Request form (JSON/YAML example below)
- Purchase Request form

- Data Use Assessment template

Purchase Request example fields

Escalation and exceptions
-------------------------
- Escalation path for stalled requests: Requester -> Approver -> Owner team lead -> Function head -> People Ops / Finance escalation.
- Exceptions to policy must be documented with risk assessment and approved by the responsible function head and Risk Committee.

Auditability and retention
-------------------------
- All approvals and artifacts are recorded in ProcureFlow and retained for a minimum of 7 years for procurement; access logs retained per Data Retention schedule.
- Regular audits: Quarterly spot-checks for access grants and annual vendor compliance review.

Adoption and tooling notes
