[Historical dashboard panels show stale counts and lose trace links after retention compaction warmup]
description:
Issue summary: Several customers (notably LumenHealth) report that historical dashboard panels (time ranges > 30 days) intermittently show zeroed or stale metric counts and their trace links are missing. The problem is transient: panels become correct again after ~10-30 minutes without user action. Impact: dashboards with SLA and usage rollups show incorrect historical values; alerting based on those rollups can under- or over-fire. This affects customer trust in console analytics and can mask billing/usage anomalies. Environment: production us-east region. Affected customers reported on enterprise tier; observed across multiple orgs.

steps_to_reproduce:
1) Open Console -> Dashboards -> choose a dashboard with weekly/monthly rollups (time range > 30 days). 2) Observe counts for a low-cardinality metric (e.g., route_success_rate, total_tokens) and trace-link anchors. 3) Rapidly change time window back and forth (e.g., 90d -> 30d -> 90d) and refresh. 4) Some panels will render with zeroed or very old counts and trace-link buttons show 'No traces' instead of opening the trace view. 5) Wait 10-30 minutes; panels recover without manual cache clear. Repro is intermittent (~1 in 10 attempts during retention compaction windows).

observed_logs:
console-frontend: panel-render: query=rollup_v2 start=2025-12-01 end=2026-03-01 shard=warm-compact read_mode=primary; retention-indexer: compaction job id=cmp-2026-03-12-08 warmup=true; indexer-lag: lag=18m; kv-cache: miss-rate spike to 78%. Trace-hook service logs show O(200) missing anchors during query window. No 5xx in api-gateway. No token auth errors. Relevant links: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/retention/indexer-run-03-12, https://kibana.redwood.internal/app/discover#/logs?q=cmp-2026-03-12-08

investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: retention compaction warmup job is causing a temporary partition state where rollup queries hit compacted partitions that are in 'read-repair' mode; dashboard renderer treats empty result as zero and trace-hook anchor resolution returns empty. Confirmed with SRE that a compaction job ran with warmup=true and indexer lag spiked ~18 minutes. Queries during warmup hit a mix of old and compacted store replicas; read-repair and backfill to hot replicas happen asynchronously. Observed that the console frontend does not fallback to hot-replica read-path when primary returns empty for rollups, so panels show stale/zeroed values. Trace-links are resolved by joining rollup keys to trace-anchor index which is being reindexed during compaction; when anchor index is temporarily empty, UI shows 'No traces'. Repro correlates strongly with compaction windows and indexer backfill events.

impact_and_scope:
- Affects historical panels (>30d) across multiple enterprise orgs in us-east during retention compaction windows.
- Observed on ~4 orgs in last 72h, including LumenHealth and 2 other enterprise accounts.
- Alerts relying on those rollups may be suppressed or show incorrect counts for the duration of compaction warmup.
- No data loss: data is present after reindex/backfill; this is a read-path consistency/window problem.

workaround:
Short term: ask customer to (a) avoid rapidly toggling large time windows during the scheduled compaction window, or (b) use a narrower time range (<=30d) which reads from hot partitions. Support can also force a panel refresh via console 'Force reload' (admin button) which triggers a hot-replica read. We have provided LumenHealth with instructions for forced refresh and notified them of the scheduled compaction window.

root_cause_summary:
Race between retention compaction warmup and dashboard read-path: compaction marks partitions compacted while the indexer backfills the hot replica asynchronously. Dashboard queries hitting compacted-but-not-yet-backfilled partitions return empty rollups; UI treats empty as zero. Trace-anchor index reindex causes temporary absence of anchor joins. No write-side data loss.

proposed_fix:
1) Frontend: treat empty rollup responses as 'retry with hot-replica' instead of rendering zero. 2) API layer: add fallback read-path to hot replicas when compaction-warmup flag is set for the partition. 3) Indexer: reduce warmup aggressiveness and emit explicit 'warmup-in-progress' header that the API can use to select fallback. 4) Add an observability alert for 'rollup-empty-during-compaction' so SRE is alerted earlier. Implementation PR: https://github.com/redwood/reindexer/pull/1189 (adds warmup header); https://github.com/redwood/console/pull/4712 (frontend retry).

comments:
2026-03-12 Priya Sharma (Support): Customer LumenHealth reported dashboards showing 0 tokens and missing trace links for month view. They attached screenshots and time of occurrence (2026-03-12 08:17 UTC). No API 5xx from their account.
2026-03-12 Ethan Park (SRE): Confirmed compaction job cmp-2026-03-12-08 ran in us-east and indexer laged ~18m. Observed kv-cache miss spike. Investigating read-path behavior when warmup=true.
2026-03-12 LumenHealth - Mary O'Neill (Customer): We rely on monthly usage dashboards for billing reconciliations. Can you provide a short-term mitigation? We saw panels return to normal after ~25 minutes but need assurance this won't affect month-end reports.
2026-03-12 Priya Sharma (Support): Shared workaround: avoid wide time toggles and use Force reload. Scheduled notification to the customer for next compaction window. Escalated to engineering for fix prioritization.
2026-03-13 Ethan Park (SRE): Created hotfix PRs to add warmup header and frontend fallback. Deploying to staging for validation. Will schedule prod rollout during low-traffic window and notify customers.
2026-03-13 Support (Priya): Updated customer with ETA for fix and added LumenHealth to early verification list.

resolution:
In Progress: Hotfix PRs opened and staged. Short-term guidance provided to customer; monitoring for recurrence. Final resolution pending deployment of API fallback and frontend retry. Follow-up postmortem to be created after prod rollout.

follow_up_actions:
Deploy reindexer warmup-header to prod behind feature flag
Update console to retry rollup reads from hot-replica when empty
Add observability alert for rollup-empty-during-compaction
Postmortem documenting mitigation and scheduling change to compaction windows

[Console metrics disappeared for subset of org routes after tenant schema migration]
description:
Issue summary:
Customer OptimaDocs reports that after a scheduled tenant schema migration we performed on 2026-03-09, several dashboard widgets and the Console usage rollups for some of their org routes display zero or drastically lower metrics. Raw event ingestion appears intact (we can see individual request logs and traces), but aggregated counts and heatmaps are missing for specific route prefixes (org/optima/*).

Impact:
- Multiple dashboards for OptimaDocs show empty time series for the 2026-03-09 00:00 - 2026-03-10 12:00 window.
- Alerts tied to rollup thresholds did not fire correctly, causing a delayed detection of a throughput regression.
- Customer-facing analytics in Console are unreliable for the affected routes; this impacts billing visibility and product monitoring.

Environment:
- prod-us-east, tenant migration job run 2026-03-09 03:42 UTC.
- Affected tenant: org-id optima-2042.

Steps to reproduce (support verified):
1) Login to Console as customer (optima-2042) and open the traffic overview dashboard.
2) Filter by route prefix org/optima/documents.* between 2026-03-09 00:00 and 2026-03-10 12:00.
3) Observe that panel 'Requests per minute by route' shows a flat zero series; traces and raw logs for same times exist in trace explorer.

Observed behavior:
- Aggregation queries hitting the analytics-backend return empty result sets for the affected org_alias.
- Querying raw events by org_id returns matching records (sample log ids: req-20260309-9a1b, req-20260309-9a2c).
- Console rollup index name used in aggregation appears to be the pre-migration alias for some shards, resulting in a mismatch.

Expected behavior:
- Dashboard panels and rollups should reflect aggregated counts based on raw events regardless of background migration, or fall back gracefully with a clear notice if a migration is in-progress.

Temporary workaround provided to customer:
- We advised OptimaDocs to view raw events/trace explorer for immediate debugging.
- Support created an alias redirect on the query layer (internal workaround) to point aggregation queries at the correct post-migration index; this restores panel results for most widgets while a permanent fix is prepared.

Additional context and evidence:
- Sample raw event: {timestamp: "2026-03-09T03:45:12Z", org_id: "optima-2042", route: "org/optima/documents/upload", request_id: "req-20260309-9a1b"} (present in raw logs but missing from hourly rollups).
- Aggregation query (anonymized) returned HTTP 200 with empty buckets for the affected time range.
- Migration job log excerpt: "migration: tenant-mapping update applied for optima-2042, aliases rotated 03:42 UTC" (see Confluence runbook link).

investigation_notes:
2026-03-10 09:10 - Support: Confirmed raw events and traces exist for affected time window; aggregation returns empty buckets for specific org_alias.
2026-03-10 11:23 - SRE: Reproduced locally against a staging snapshot; observed that aggregation service queries an alias resolved to v23 indexes while the rollups were written to v24 during migration overlap.
2026-03-10 13:00 - DataEng hypothesis: race condition in alias-rotation script where some routing keys retained old alias; aggregation backend caches resolved alias for 6h by default and did not refresh after rotation.
2026-03-11 02:14 - Engineering: Cache invalidation path confirmed; aggregation client does not detect index alias change when a mapping version bump occurs, leading to zero results until cache TTL expires or manual invalidation occurs.
2026-03-12 18:40 - Patch created to add alias-change event hook to aggregation client and to proactively invalidate cache on migration completion (PR linked).

comments:
2026-03-10 - Maya Chen (Support): Acknowledged. Assigned to SRE for immediate triage and requested escalation due to billing impact.
2026-03-10 - Ravi Patel (SRE): Reproduced in staging. Placing temporary query alias redirect for optima-2042. Notifying DataEng for root cause. #support-optima
2026-03-11 - OptimaDocs (customer): Thank you — dashboards are returning data after your workaround. Can you confirm whether historical rollups will be repaired?
2026-03-12 - DataEng (Elena Morales): We will run a backfill to re-aggregate the missed windows to metrics-rollup-v24. Backfill ETA: 2026-03-14 04:00 UTC. Post-backfill we will run validation scripts and merge aliases cleanly.
2026-03-14 - Ravi Patel (SRE): Backfill started at 2026-03-14 04:12 UTC (job id backfill-867530). Monitoring progress; will update when complete.

resolution_summary:
(pending) Temporary alias redirect restored dashboard visibility; root cause is aggregation-client cache not invalidating after index alias rotation during tenant schema migration. Fix implemented in PR to add alias-change hooks and reduce cache TTL; backfill scheduled to regenerate missing hourly rollups for optima-2042. Final resolution will be updated after backfill completes and validation passes.

resolution_notes:
Change merged: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/1284 - add alias-change event hook to aggregation client and proactive cache invalidation
Backfill job initiated: backfill-867530 (started 2026-03-14 04:12 UTC).
Post-backfill validation steps: compare hourly rollup totals against raw event counts; run dashboard smoke tests for OptimaDocs org routes.
Follow-up: Add a migration-run checklist to the runbook to remove in-flight cache TTLs prior to alias rotation (Confluence updated).

followup_actions:

[cross-sdk cursor-adapter and token-swap reauth for streaming ergonomics]
description:
Summary:
Introduce a lightweight cross-language cursor adapter for streaming responses and a compact 'token-swap' reauthentication flow (soft backoff + immediate-swap fast-path) to make long-lived streams robust across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs. This PR focuses on ergonomics (sync/async iterators), parity of consumer-facing APIs, and a minimal surface for implementers to hook platform-specific auth logic.

Motivation and context:
- Customers reported fragility when long-lived streams encountered short-lived credentials or refresh failures; current SDKs either dropped the stream or required heavy client code to resume.
- The goal is to let SDKs automatically swap credentials mid-stream and continue receiving tokens while preserving ordering and backpressure semantics.
- We also want a single, small adapter pattern so language SDKs share the same behavioral contract without forcing identical internals.

What this change does:
- Adds a cursor-adapter abstraction implemented in each SDK: Python (StreamingCursor), TS (CursorAdapter), Go (cursoradapter.Cursor). The adapter exposes a unified contract: peek(), ack(), extendAuth(newToken), and close().
- Implements token-swap reauth which attempts a fast-path auth swap (synchronous in-process) and falls back to a jittered soft-backoff if the provider is unreachable for N attempts.
- Surfaces ergonomics: Python exposes an async generator plus a convenience sync iterator; TS exposes AsyncIterable and a small pull-based helper; Go exposes a channel-backed iterator with context cancellation and explicit Resume() helper.
- Adds tests and e2e harness scenarios simulating short-lived token rotation, intermittent network, and mid-stream model fallback.
- Bumps SDK versions: python 0.18.0, typescript 1.7.0, go v0.9.0.

Checklist (high-level):
- [x] Design doc link: internal doc ID ENG-2147 (attached in Linear)
- [x] Implementation in all three SDKs + unit tests
- [x] Integration tests against the streaming canary harness (perf-canary)
- [x] Docs: quickstart snippet and migration notes in SDK changelogs
- [x] Release notes drafted

Compatibility and migration notes:
- Consumer-facing change is additive; existing streaming code will continue to work. To opt into token-swap behavior consumers must either use the new adapter directly or enable auto-reauth in the client config (off by default).
- There is a small behavioral change for Go: Resume() is now recommended instead of re-creating the iterator for resuming after auth refresh, but old pattern still functions.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: mid-stream credential exchange could reorder messages if adapters are misused. Mitigation: adapter enforces single-writer semantics and sequence checks; tests simulate race conditions.
- Risk: aggressive retries could overwhelm auth service. Mitigation: backoff parameters are conservative by default and configurable via client options.

Follow-ups (engineer TODOs):
- Expose metrics: token_swap_attempts, token_swap_success, token_swap_backoff_count (ENG-2203).
- Add an examples repo snippet showing server-initiated rotate flow.

[tri-sdk: stream resume + preflight auth handshake + ergonomic streaming builders]
description:
Motivation: We continue to see customer reports and internal test flakes where long-running streaming calls fail mid-stream with a 401/403 when tokens rotate or when transient network blips occur. Existing SDK behavior either kills the stream or requires heavy user-side glue to resume. This PR implements a three-part change for parity across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs: 1) a lightweight preflight auth handshake on stream open so the client and server can agree on a token-refresh strategy and initial resume id; 2) an idempotent stream-resume token and server ack protocol (protocol described in pkg/api/stream/protocol.md) allowing clients to reconnect and request content after the last acked chunk; 3) ergonomic streaming builders / iterators so application code can resume the stream with minimal plumbing. The description below describes the non-obvious implementation details, test coverage, and upgrade notes.

protocol_summary:
The stream now begins with a preflight control frame: { type: "preflight", client_resume_id, token_version }. The server responds with { type: "preflight_ack", server_resume_id, accepted_token_version }. During normal streaming, server emits periodic ack markers: { type: "ack", server_resume_id, offset }. On reconnect clients present the last seen server_resume_id and offset. The server will replay from the safe offset or return a non-retryable error if the session window has expired.

python_changes:
Added AsyncStreamBuilder in sdk/python/redwood/streaming.py which wraps the websocket/http2 stream and exposes an async for interface. Default backoff shapes were adjusted to jittered-exponential with max 30s and default attempts=6. Token refresh hook integrated: if a 401 occurs mid-stream the builder attempts a non-blocking refresh and performs a resume handshake. Example usage in docs: async for chunk in client.stream.create_stream(request, resume_policy="auto"):
    handle(chunk)

typescript_changes:
Added ReadableStream wrapper and pipeTo helper in sdk/typescript/src/stream/index.ts. New StreamConfig exposes resumePolicy and authPreflight options. We export a node-friendly stream.Readable and browser ReadableStream interop. Tests added that run in node and headless chromium to validate reconnects and backpressure handling.

go_changes:
Added iterator-style StreamNext(ctx) in sdk/go/stream/client.go that returns (chunk, resumeToken, err). Token refresh is context-aware; client can inject a RefreshTokenFunc. Tests added to simulate mid-stream 401 and validate resume works without duplicate delivery.

tests_and_ci:
Added cross-language e2e tests under sdk/*/tests that run against the local stream canary. CI matrix added a 'stream-e2e' job. First pipeline run failed due to flaky timing in the Python reconnect test (timeout=0.5s too low); adjusted timing and retries, rerun succeeded. New tests cover: preflight failure modes, resume within session window, resume after server restart (session window expired), ack idempotency.

review_comments:
Diego Alvarez: Can we avoid exposing resume tokens in logs by default? Suggest redacting in SDK debug mode.
Maya Chen (author): Good catch — tokens are now redacted via a small change in logger.Serialize() and unit tests added.
Priya Nair: The TS ReadableStream interop is great. Please add a small example showing piping into fetch request body for server streaming use-cases.
Maya Chen: Added pipeTo example and updated docs/sdks/streaming.md
Liam O'Connor: Go API ergonomics look clean. Please ensure the zero-value client is still invalid (panic/clear error) to avoid silent misuse.
Maya Chen: Added a NewClient constructor and documented behaviour in docs.

notes_for_release:
SDKs: python 1.4.3, typescript 2.0.0, go 0.9.1. Highlights: preflight auth handshake for streaming, idempotent resume tokens, ergonomic async/iter interfaces. Migration: users on long-lived streams should migrate to resumePolicy="auto" to benefit from seamless reconnects. See docs/sdks/streaming.md for code samples and protocol details.

release_notes:
Added preflight handshake to reduce mid-stream auth failures
Clients can now resume streams without application-level buffering
New ergonomic builders: AsyncStreamBuilder (Python), ReadableStream wrapper (TS), iterator API (Go)
Backoff defaults tightened to reduce overload during mass reconnects
SDK version bumps: Python 1.4.3, TypeScript 2.0.0, Go 0.9.1

upgrade_instructions:
1) Update SDK packages to the new versions. 2) In long-running stream handlers, switch to the provided builders/iterators and set resumePolicy="auto". 3) If you log full stream metadata, update logging config to redact resume tokens. 4) For private deployments, ensure stream session window (config 'stream.session_window_seconds') is set compatibly with server retention (recommended >= 120s).

backwards_compatibility:
Clients that do not opt into preflight will continue to work: server accepts an absent preflight and falls back to previous behavior (no resume). The new resume protocol is additive; servers will only require it after a future major version bump.

[Compact reauth helpers and typed stream adapters to align ergonomics across Python/TypeScript/Go]
description:
Motivation: SDK users reported repeated friction when reauthorizing long-lived streaming sessions and when migrating examples across languages. This PR introduces a compact set of reauth helpers and small typed stream adapter layers for Python, TypeScript, and Go to achieve API ergonomics parity and reduce boilerplate. Goals: 1) Provide a minimal "credential refresher" helper that can be composed into existing stream connectors; 2) Add lightweight typed stream adapters that expose a consistent async-iterator/pull-stream surface across languages; 3) Reduce duplication in examples and make cross-language migration straightforward; 4) Bump TypeScript and Go SDK patch versions to include the adapter and helper packages. High level changes: - Py: package redwood_sdk.streaming.reauth with CredentialLease and refresh callback shim; new examples in examples/streaming/reauth_demo.py. - TS: introduce @redwood/sdk-helpers/reauth and stream-adapter async generator wrapper; update ts-sdk readme examples. - Go: add compact cred.Refresher interface and stream/adapter package with typed channel-backed iterator; small concurrency guard to avoid double-refresh. - Cross-lang: harmonize env var names and docs snippets (REDWOOD_TOKEN_TTL_HINT). Compatibility: default behavior is backward compatible; helpers are opt-in. We added a low-overhead heartbeat/lease check that will attempt reauth only when TTL drops below threshold. This PR intentionally avoids a global credential cache to keep surface area small and deterministic for Dedicated/Private deployments.

diff_summary:
Small to medium: add helper modules in each SDK, a couple of example files, docs page, and version bumps. No changes to runtime or server-side code. Tests: new unit tests for reauth logic (py/ts/go), integration smoke test updated to exercise a credential lease refresh path.

1) feat(ts): add reauth helper and typed stream adapter (ts/helpers/*) ; 2) feat(py): add CredentialLease shim and examples (py/redwood_sdk/streaming/reauth.py) ; 3) feat(go): introduce cred.Refresher and stream/adapter (go/sdk/cred, go/sdk/stream/adapter) ; 4) docs: cross-language examples and migration guide ; 5) chore: bump ts/sdk to 1.13.2, go/sdk to v0.9.7, py SDK to 2.8.4 ; 6) fix: race in go refresher backoff logic (follow-up commit)

testing_notes:
Added unit tests covering: credential TTL check edge cases, concurrent refresh dedupe, stream adapter order preservation, and graceful consumer cancellation. Ran full sdk test matrix on linux/amd64 and linux/arm64. Observed a transient timing flake in the TS generator under heavy load; added a small jitter to the retry timer to mitigate.

review_comments:
Diego: requested clarity on backoff config and a test for simultaneous refresh requests; Claire: asked for clearer example of how this behaves under Dedicated reserved capacity; Owen: pointed out a potential panic in go channel iterator when consumer cancels mid-refresh. Author addressed all requests: added backoff config struct with defaults, added Python and TS unit tests for concurrent refresh, fixed go panic by adding a non-blocking select and close-safety guard. Final approvals from Diego and Claire on 2026-03-04.

release_notes:
Added compact credential refresher helpers and typed stream adapters across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs. Opt-in helpers simplify reauth logic for long-lived streams; examples and migration guide included. Bumped Py SDK to 2.8.4, TS SDK to 1.13.2, Go SDK to v0.9.7.

notes_for_consumers:
How to adopt: - Minimal: import the helper and pass a small refresh callback that exchanges your rotated secret for a token; - Migration: replace your ad-hoc token refresh loops with CredentialLease / Refresher for predictable TTL checks; - Performance: the helper checks TTL every 10% of token lifetime by default and will only attempt refresh once per lease window. - Dedicated: no changes required to server config; helpers are client-side only.

maintainer_guidance:
This change is low-risk and intended to be backwards compatible. If downstream code uses an internal credential cache, recommend a staged rollout and verify behavior in Dedicated staging. Monitor token-refresh-related errors (tag: sdk.cred.refresh.fail) and streaming reconnects (tag: sdk.stream.reconnect) for first week after release. If needed, revert is simple by removing helper imports; behavior falls back to previous explicit refresh loops.

[Compact credential priming and fluent pullstream APIs across Python/TypeScript/Go]
description:
Motivation: SDK consumers repeatedly asked for smaller, deterministic integration points for auth warmup and easier streaming consumption patterns. Current SDKs have similar behaviors implemented ad-hoc per-language; this PR unifies the core primitives and surfaces ergonomic facades in each SDK so teams can opt-in to credential priming and a fluent pullstream API without large surface changes.

Summary: This change introduces a compact credential priming policy in the shared SDK surface and language-specific ergonomic wrappers: a small Python priming facade that starts background token warmup, a TypeScript fluent pullstream consumer that turns the async iterator into a chainable DSL, and a Go adapter that provides a low-alloc pullstream handle plus an opt-in priming hook. The PR also adds cross-sdk deterministic retry matrices documentation and a short migration guide.

What I changed (high level):
- Extracted priming logic into sdks/shared/credentials/priming_policy.go and exposed a minimal API used by each SDK.
- Python: sdks/python/redwood/session/priming.py — session.priming.start(prime_before=30s) and a background worker with bounded concurrency.
- TypeScript: sdks/typescript/src/pullstream/fluent.ts — fluent .map/.filter/.batch chainable helpers and a small adapter to convert existing async iterables.
- Go: sdks/go/pullstream/adapter.go — pullstream.Handle and an OptInPriming(ctx) helper to reduce allocations in high-throughput servers.
- Tests: integration and unit tests added for priming behavior and pullstream ergonomics.
- Docs: migration guide and examples for each SDK.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc reviewed with SDK leads (ENG-4952)
- [x] Shared priming policy implemented and covered by unit tests
- [x] Language wrappers implemented and smoke-tested against staging backends
- [x] Changelogs and migration notes added
- [x] CI pipeline green after rerun

Compatibility notes: The priming API is opt-in; no breaking changes to existing public SDK surface are made by default. The new fluent pullstream is additive — consumers can migrate gradually. The shared deterministic retry matrix is documentation-only for now; follow-up PRs will wire it into client-side presets.

Benchmark & safety: Microbenchmarks show <3% latency increase at cold start for priming enabled workloads but >15% tail reduction for sustained streaming scenarios where token refresh races previously occurred. Priming defaults are conservative (disabled) and limited to the session object to avoid unexpected network traffic.

Testing/CI: All language pipelines run; intermittent flaky test in TypeScript pullstream suite was addressed by adding a short jitter in test harness. The CI run associated with this PR passed on the second attempt (flaky e2e rerun).

Review summary: See review conversation below for requested changes and responses.

Merge: squashed and merged into main on 2026-02-26. Release notes appended to SDK CHANGELOGs.

Notes for maintainers: follow-up tasks include wiring deterministic retry presets into SDK constructors (ENG-4988) and adding telemetry for priming hits/misses to the Console observability surface.

[Long streaming chat hangs mid-response after proxy chunk reassembly failure]
description:
Issue summary:
Customer LexiDocs reports their long-form streaming chat sessions (SSE) frequently stop emitting further tokens ~30–90s into a multi-minute generation. Client remains connected; no explicit SSE close. This started after 2026-03-09 02:00 UTC deploy of an edge proxy rewrite rule.

Impact:
- Several customers on Dedicated experienced mid-generation stalls affecting production chat features.
- Writes as 'hang' (no new data) requiring user refresh; some users reported multiple attempts to re-request leading to duplicate assistant messages.
- Incident causes downstream timeouts in LexiDocs processing logic; revenue-impacting for high-concurrency workflows during business hours.

Environment:
- Redwood prod, us-east region (edge cluster east-1).
- Affected routes: /v1/chat/stream (SSE) and websocket multiplexing.
- Traffic passes through our new streaming-rewrite proxy that performs HTTP/2->HTTP/1.1 translation and header normalizations for tenant gateways.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided & internal):
1) Create a long prompt that triggers multi-minute generation (e.g., 6k token instruction + large completion target).
2) Start streaming SSE request via curl or browser client.
3) Observe initial token stream for ~20–90s then stream stops sending new data despite model still generating on worker (worker logs show active token production).
4) Client connection remains open; no "event: close" or final bracket is sent.
5) Replaying same request against a bypassed route (skipping streaming-rewrite proxy) completes normally.

Relevant logs / snippets:
- Edge proxy (haproxy-like) shows repeated small writes merged into a bigger TCP segment; upstream chunk boundary markers ("\n\n" SSE delimiter) missing after a particular rewrite path. Example tail: "data: {\"delta\":\"token\"}\r\ndata: {\"delta\":\"token\"}\r\n" then abrupt pause.
- Serving runtime worker logs (timestamps aligned) show generated token batches continuing for another 45s after client-side silence.
- tcpdump on edge indicates a mid-stream rewrite that collapses two chunked frames into one without re-inserting SSE event separators, causing client-side SSE parser to wait for delimiter.
- No 5xx seen; connection not closed by proxy.

Additional context:
- Change rolled out 2026-03-09 02:00 UTC to streaming-rewrite proxy intended to compress headers and reduce TLS handshakes.
- Not every long stream affected; appears correlated with sequences that produce many very small chunk writes (highly tokenized output).
- Customer attempted simple workaround: enable shorter max-token-per-chunk at client side; reduced frequency of stalls but not eliminated.

investigation_notes:
Hypothesis 1: Proxy byte coalescing removed SSE event delimiters (\n\n) causing client parsers to wait indefinitely for delimiter - supported by tcpdump traces.
Hypothesis 2: HTTP/2->HTTP/1 translation routine incorrectly translated 'Transfer-Encoding: chunked' boundaries when header compression triggered during rewrite - reproduced locally under high token emission rates.
Instrumented edge rewrite to log raw socket writes and SSE event emission times. Found write batching calls merging two separate event writes into one write without the middle delimiter when backlog > 16KB.
Serving runtime indicates no worker evictions or OOMs during affected sessions; KV cache and model workers continued producing tokens (rules out model-side stall).
Reproduced the failure in staging with same rewrite code and a scripted client that emits many tiny token writes; bypassing rewrite removes the failure.

resolution_notes:
Mitigation (short-term): Enabled tenant streaming bypass flag for LexiDocs and other impacted dedicated customers. This routes SSE directly to serving edge without rewrite layer. Customer confirmed immediate improvement.
Fix (long-term): PR merged (github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4211) which: a) disables write coalescing for SSE endpoints, b) enforces explicit SSE delimiter preservation during HTTP/2->HTTP/1 translation, c) adds unit tests simulating high-frequency tiny writes.
Deployment plan: Roll out to 5% of edge nodes on 2026-03-13 08:00 UTC, monitor streaming success rate and token delivery latency, then progressive rollout to 100% if metrics stable.
Follow-ups: Add synthetic end-to-end long-stream canary tests to CI (task INT-3882), update runbook with steps to toggle tenant bypass and identify proxy rewrite regressions, and notify customers via status page about 'streaming stability improvement' on 2026-03-14.
Postmortem action items: 1) Add precise SOCK_WRITE tracing for streaming-rewrite, 2) Add alerts for 'stream silence while worker active' pattern, 3) Backport fix to older edge clusters still running legacy rewrite.

description:
Issue summary:\nOn 2026-03-10 between 02:15-03:20 UTC PioneerBiotech reported intermittent truncated streaming responses and duplicated transcript fragments for long-running chat sessions on their private deployment. Customers also observed a billing spike for token counts that did not match recorded complete responses.\n\nImpact:\n- Multiple production customers of PioneerBiotech experienced missing chunks and partial transcripts in streamed completions for ~65 minutes.\n- Billing reported a temporary 18% delta for affected requests during the window.\n- User-facing errors included short, duplicated dedicated GPU pool, HSM-backed KMS for model key material.\n- Model: redwood-open-7b-v2 pinned in their canary routing policy.\n\nSteps to reproduce (high-level):\n1) Establish a long-running streaming chat with multi-turn history and patterns that exercise KV cache and prefix caching.\n2) Simulate sustained small parallel fanout (20 concurrent streams) with occasional large-generation turns (seq len > 1200).\n3) Rotate HSM keys for the control plane (customer-triggered maintenance) while streams are active.\n4) Observe dropped or reordered streaming chunks and duplicate transcript fragments in client logs.\n\nObserved logs/traces (highlights):\n- serving-runtime logs: repeated inflight-queue priority reassignments for connection IDs tied to PioneerBiotech (conn=pb-*) at 2026-03-10T02:16:05Z.\n- controlplane: health-check loop reported worker handoff during HSM ack at 02:16:00Z.\n- stream-assembler: \"fragment-seq-mismatch\" warnings and \"duplicate-chunk-id\" events between 02:16:06Z-02:20:45Z.\n- billing pipeline: token-accounting emitted partial-commit events for streams marked \"replay-required\".\n\nTemporary mitigation applied during the incident:\n- Support/Eng enabled conservative inflight-priority gating for PioneerBiotech's tenant at 02:31 UTC to stop priority inversion and allow reassembly backfill.\n- Rolled back a recent private-controlplane change that tightened worker handoff window (customer-approved).\n- Triggered a controlled KV-cache warming job to rebuild prefixes for active sessions.\n\nRoot cause summary (post-incident investigation):\n- During an HSM key rotation, the private control plane accelerated worker handoffs to avoid transient key-unavailability. That handoff logic had a bug: it prematurely demoted stream reassembly workers and requeued inflight requests without preserving per-connection priority metadata. The inflight-queue scheduler then performed a priority inversion: short retransmit tasks were preferred, starving long-running stream reassembly tasks and causing chunk reordering and duplicate deliveries.\n- The billing pipeline treated requeued fragments as new arrivals because a transient sequence flag was lost during requeue. This produced the observed billing overcount.\n\nResolution and rollout notes:\n- Patch deployed to private-controlplane (PR #432) that preserves per-connection priority metadata during worker handoffs and marks requeued fragments with \"replay-tag\" to avoid double-counting in billing. Deployed to PioneerBiotech control plane at 2026-03-11 05:20 UTC.\n- Billing team ran a reconciliation job to correct the overcounted tokens during the incident window; customer invoice was adjusted (credit issued on 2026-03-12).\n- Canary verified for 24 hours with synthetic long-stream load; no reassembly errors observed.\n\nPost-incident action items (owner in parentheses):\n- Add guardrail to HSM rotation flow to ensure worker handoff gating does not drop priority metadata (Diego).\n- Add e2e test that rotates keys during active streaming to validate reassembly behavior (QA / SRE).\n- Update billing pipeline to ignore fragments flagged \"replay-tag\" and ensure idempotent token accounting (Billing team).\n- Customer-facing postmortem and credit confirmation to PioneerBiotech (CS Liaison: Maya).\n\nBusiness/customer notes:\n- PioneerBiotech is on a private deployment with enterprise SLAs. [SSE stream abruptly closes and final tokens dropped for long assistant responses]
description:
Issue summary:
Customers report that SSE (text/event-stream) chat sessions serving long-form assistant responses are terminating before the final tokens are emitted. The client sees the stream close suddenly and the response is missing last paragraphs (usually >800 tokens). No explicit 5xx error returned to the client; connection terminates and client-side library reports EOF. Impact: multiple production customers on Dedicated capacity experienced truncated replies in the afternoon of 2026-03-10. This affects UX for long assistant outputs (summaries, long-form generation) and caused one customer to revert to polling for short-term mitigation.

Impact:
- BrightByte Health observed ~12% of long streaming responses truncated between 15:10–16:40 PDT on 2026-03-10.
- Increased support volume and PagerDuty alerts from Customer Success and SRE.

Environment/Context:
- Dedicated pool: d-pool-us-west-2-3
- API path: /v1/chat/stream (SSE) behind service-gateway (Envoy + NGINX ingress in front of gateway for legacy customers)
- Observed primarily with long context and responses that trigger continuous token emission for >14s. Short replies unaffected.

Expected behavior:
- SSE stream should remain open until server emits the final event and properly flushes trailing data.

Observed behavior:
- Stream abruptly closes mid-response; client receives truncated content and no clear server-side 5xx. Upstream logs show upstream connection closed with reset by peer in some cases.

Additional notes:
- Customers use standard Accept: text/event-stream; some are behind corporate proxies which show similar failures but at a lower rate.


steps_to_reproduce:
1) Create a chat session using /v1/chat/stream with an instruction that elicits a long response (>800 tokens).
2) Use curl or a JS EventSource client to consume the stream.
3) Observe that after a burst of token events, the connection may close before the final 'done' event is sent; reproduced more reliably under moderate concurrent load (30-50 rps) against the dedicated pool.
4) Repeat with same prompt against a shorter-response prompt to confirm no truncation.


logs:
- service-gateway (proxy) logs: several entries 'upstream prematurely closed connection' and 'connection termination: downstream reset' correlated with timestamps 2026-03-10 15:17:33–15:40:12 PDT.
- Serving-runtime logs (worker-7): 'flush interval exceeded, coalesced chunks sent' followed by 'write failed: connection reset by peer' with no additional error.
- Envoy stats: increases in 504-overriden timeouts and connection failures on listener 8443.
- No application-level 5xx returned to clients in many truncated cases; tcp-level FIN/RST is observed.


investigation_notes:
Hypotheses considered:
- Idle/proxy timeout in NGINX/Envoy/Corporate proxy cutting long-lived streaming connections when chunk sizes are small.
- Serving runtime flush behavior emits many small chunks; some intermediaries buffer and then decide to close based on perceived inactivity.
- Network path MTU or TLS renegotiation edge-case causing TCP reset under bursty token emission.

What we tested:
- Increased keepalive and proxy idle timeouts on a staging gateway and re-ran the prompt: truncation rate dropped significantly.
- Instrumented worker to coalesce token writes to larger chunks (flush every 128 tokens or 250ms whichever first) in a canary build: replication improved.
- Captured pcap on a test environment: confirmed RSTs originate from the gateway process when upstream read/write queue spikes.

Interim conclusion:
- Root cause is a combination of small-chunk flushing from the serving runtime and conservative timeouts/buffering behavior in the gateway (Envoy/NGINX combo) which, under moderate concurrency, leads to upstream connection resets and silent stream termination.


comments:
Aisha Ramey (customer): We're seeing truncated clinical summaries in production when we ask the model for long outputs. Happens ~1 in 8 requests. Impacting our demo tomorrow.
Riley Chen (support): Received logs and reproduction steps. Escalating to SRE; capturing traces. Please provide example request IDs if you can.
SRE (Luca Moretti): Reproduced in canary by driving 40 rps against d-pool-us-west-2-3. Saw gateway produce connection resets when write queue grew. Increasing proxy idle timeout and coalescing flushes reduces failures.
Customer Success (Maya Patel): Provided three example request IDs and confirmed business impact. Asked for ETA on fix or recommended mitigation.
Riley Chen: Rolled out gateway config change (increase idle_timeout to 90s and disable proxy_buffering for SSE routes) to affected Dedicated pools as an immediate mitigation. Also toggled canary runtime build to coalesce writes in staging for verification.

resolution:
Immediate mitigation: increased proxy idle_timeout to 90s for SSE endpoints and disabled response buffering on ingress NGINX for dedicated pools. Recommendation issued to customers experiencing truncation: re-open session or fallback to polling if intermittent.

Longer-term fix implemented: serving-runtime change to coalesce token writes (flush policy: max 128 tokens or 250ms) merged to main (github.com/redwood-inference/service-runtime/pull/822) and deployed to Dedicated pools during maintenance window on 2026-03-12. Gateway rollback protections and improved observability (per-token lag metrics) added.

Post-deploy validation: truncation rate for BrightByte Health fell from 12% to <0.5% in the 24h after the deploy. No related rollouts required for Hosted customers.

Follow-ups: Add a streaming SLO and synthetic that exercises long SSE responses across all dedicated pools; document HTTP proxy recommendations for customers that front Redwood with corporate proxies.

[WebSocket fragmented-frame handling leads to streaming chat stalls under moderate packet reordering]
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (NovaAssist) reports that WebSocket streaming chat sessions occasionally stall mid-message in eu-west production. The client receives an initial prefix of tokens, then the stream is silent for 20–90 seconds before the connection resets or the client reconnects and receives a truncated completion. This started on 2026-03-09 ~09:00 UTC and affects ~3% of sessions for the customer but is visible in general metrics as a small uptick in streaming timeouts in eu-west.

Impact:
- Customer-facing chat features freeze mid-response; user must reconnect or refresh.
- Affects enterprise-tier workloads using long responses (>1,200 tokens) and clients behind lossy corporate networks.
- Symptoms: no 5xx from API, no obvious rate-limit; visible as stuck websocket connection with inbound keepalive and no outbound messages.

Environment:
- prod | eu-west
- API endpoint: wss://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream
- Websocket proxy: internal ws-proxy fleet behind api-gateway
- Serving runtime: redwood-serving v1.12.0 (eu-west pool)
- Observed for models: redwood-rlhf-1b, gpt-4o-mini

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1) Establish websocket to /v1/chat/stream with streaming enabled and a long system+user prompt producing >1,000 tokens.
2) On client or middlebox, introduce moderate packet reordering and forced MTU fragmentation (tc qdisc netem shuffle 25% + mtu reduction).
3) Observe server emits tokens then stalls mid-output; connection remains open but zero bytes sent for 20–90s.

Observed behavior:
- Proxy logs show an open upstream socket with no writes for the stall period.
- Application-level logs in serving-runtime show no error; generator appears blocked waiting for socket write to complete.
- tcpdump shows fragmented frames and repeated TCP retransmits during stall window.

Expected behavior:
- Token stream continues steadily to EOF until generation completes or a clear error returned.

Initial logs / snippets:
- ws-proxy (eu-west-3) stderr: "[WARN] write timeout after partial-frame: fd=1023" repeated.
- kernel retransmits spike seen on host ip 10.4.12.23 between 09:14:02 and 09:14:46 UTC.
- serving-runtime trace id: trace-eu-20260310-771b shows normal generation loops but blocked on socket write syscall.

Temporary workaround provided to customer:
- Instructed to enable client-side immediate reconnect on stream stall after 10s; also reduced client-side keepalive interval. This mitigated UX but is not a server fix.

Investigation notes:
- Correlated increase in proxy write-timeout counters with kernel-level fragmented packets.
- Reproducer created by SRE (link in PR) using tc netem + websocat; reliably reproduced the stall locally against ws-proxy image.
- Hypothesis: ws-proxy (libws v2.2.x) mishandles fragmented websocket frames when the upstream write syscall returns EAGAIN or partial write; proxy marks frame as "incomplete" and later drops subsequent fragments instead of coalescing, causing the serving-runtime to block waiting for an ACK that never arrives.
- Confirmed by instrumenting ws-proxy: seen state machine stuck in "awaiting continuation" after partial write.

Root cause:
- A regression introduced in libws v2.2.1 -> v2.2.3 where fragmented-frame continuation handling failed to requeue partial frames on EAGAIN. Under packet reordering/fragmentation, this path was exercised and left the upstream socket in a state where writes would not progress, effectively stalling token emission.

Resolution and rollout:
- Patch applied: upgrade ws-proxy to libws v2.3.1 (fixes fragmented-frame requeue) and added defensive coalescing in proxy write path (PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/4581).
- Tuned proxy settings: proxy_read_timeout=300s, proxy_send_timeout=60s, disabled proxy_buffering for streaming routes.
- Hotfix deployed to eu-west via canary (10% -> 50% -> 100%) between 2026-03-11 03:20 UTC and 2026-03-11 05:10 UTC.
- Verification: internal synthetic tests with netem showed no stall on patched proxy; production error rate for websocket stalls in eu-west dropped from 2.9% -> 0.1% for long-stream sessions.

Follow-up actions:
- Add unit/integration test that simulates fragmented websocket frames and partial writes.
- Improve SLO alerting to detect increases in websocket write-timeouts earlier.
- Postmortem doc scheduled on Confluence and postmortem runbook link included below.

2026-03-10 11:12 UTC — Jordan Lee (SRE): Reproduced locally with tc netem + websocat. Observed proxy write-timeout loops. Raising priority to P1 and paging infra team. Linked INC-20260310-7.

Patch deployed to websocket-proxy (libws v2.3.1) and config tuning; hotfix rolled to eu-west and validated with synthetic tests and customer confirmation.

Regression in libws fragmented-frame handling caused proxy to drop continuation frames after partial writes (EAGAIN), leaving upstream writes blocked under packet reordering/fragmentation.

[Progressive stream freeze after runtime kernel swap causes SSE/WebSocket disconnects]
description:
Issue summary: Since 2026-03-09 22:00 UTC, Cloudscribe reports progressive freezes and eventual disconnects for long streaming chat responses using SSE and WebSocket. The stream appears to emit tokens normally for ~20–40s, then pauses for 5–30s and ultimately the connection resets with a 101/EOF. This correlates with a kernel swap event observed on the serving runtime nodes.

Impact: Multiple users on Cloudscribe's dedicated pool experience mid-response stalls. User-facing symptom is partial message delivery and abrupt stream termination. Estimated 40% of long-stream requests (context > 8k tokens) are affected in us-west during peak.

Environment: prod dedicated pool (Cloudscribe reserved), serving-runtime v2.8.1, api-gateway v1.6.4, kernel-manager v0.9.0, region us-west.

Steps to reproduce (observed with customer and internally):
1) Create chat stream request with model=gptx-13b-dlite, max_tokens=4096, streaming mode SSE or websocket.
2) Send prompt that triggers 800–1200 token generation over multiple batches (e.g., multi-section summarization).
3) Observe token emission for ~20–40s, then a long pause.
4) Connection either resumes after ~15s (rare) or closes with client error and partial content.

Observed behavior: Token stream halts mid-generation; client receives keepalive frames but no token payloads. HTTP connection logs show TCP FIN or 101/RESET after pause. Kernel swap events (worker replacement where the runtime swaps optimized kernels/kernelsets due to quantization fallback) co-occur in the host logs.

Expected behavior: Continuous token stream until generation completes or deterministic error is returned. Kernel reconfiguration should be transparent to in-flight streaming responses.

logs:
2026-03-09T22:13:27Z [serving-runtime] cid=cs-0f9a3a gen=start model=gptx-13b-dlite worker=wrkr-23
2026-03-09T22:13:52Z [kernel-manager] wrkr-23 kernel-swap:start reason=quant-fallback trace_id=tr-9b2
2026-03-09T22:13:52Z [serving-runtime] wrkr-23 cache:flush prefix-kv user=cs-0f9a3a
2026-03-09T22:14:10Z [serving-runtime] wrkr-23 stream:emit last_chunk=token_482
2026-03-09T22:14:25Z [network] conn=conn-7f4 keepalive:received but no payload
2026-03-09T22:14:40Z [serving-runtime] wrkr-23 stream:error code=E_STREAM_FREEZE msg="no progress after 15s"
2026-03-09T22:14:41Z [api-gateway] conn=conn-7f4 client-reset status=499
2026-03-09T22:14:41Z [kernel-manager] wrkr-23 kernel-swap:complete kernel_id=k-88d


investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: kernel-manager kernel swap path causes temporary lock/stop-the-world for KV cache or token emission loop on worker threads leading to stream stalls. Reproducer runs show stalls only when kernel-swap overlaps with in-flight continuous generation beyond a certain batch count.

What we've checked:
- Correlated stack traces from wrkr-23 show token emission thread waiting on kernel-loader mutex around the swap window.
- Traced network keepalives show active TCP connection during stall. No 5xx from model itself until stream:error.
- CPU and GPU utilization did not spike; rather worker thread entered blocked state.
- Canary deployments with kernel-manager v0.9.1 (patch) that defers cache flush show reduced occurrence in staging.

Open questions:
- Is kernel swap happening synchronously on the main token emission thread?
- Are there any fallback code paths that don't resume token emission after cache reclamation?

Next steps:
- Patch kernel-manager to perform non-blocking kernel hot-swap (v0.9.2 candidate) and run canary in Cloudscribe's dedicated pool.
- Add additional tracing around token emission mutexes and publish metrics for swap-duration.
- Notify customer of temporary mitigation to avoid rolling kernel updates during long-running streams.

steps_taken:
1) Reproduced with Cloudscribe test account — confirmed stalls when kernel-swap occurred.
2) Temporarily disabled automatic kernel-swap for Cloudscribe dedicated pool at 2026-03-10T03:00 UTC; customer reported immediate reduction in incidents.
3) Deployed kernel-manager v0.9.1 to staging with deferred cache flush behavior; internal runs show regressions down from ~40% to ~3% in stress tests.
4) Captured extended traces and added instrumentation for swap-duration metric (mm.kernel_swap.duration_ms).

workaround:
Temporarily pin serving-runtime kernel-manager to v0.9.0 without automatic live-swap on Cloudscribe's dedicated pool. Advise customers to avoid starting long (>30s) in-flight streams during rollout windows. Consider setting shorter max_tokens or incremental calls as a short-term mitigation.

resolution_notes:
In Progress — kernel-manager non-blocking hot-swap patch under review. Customer notified of temporary pin and observed reduction in incidents. Engineering estimates 48–72 hours to finish patching and run extended canary across dedicated pools. Linked to PR for patch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4123.

2026-03-10 08:15 PDT - Ava (Support): Cloudscribe confirms pin removed second day; incidents dropped from ~12/hr to ~1/hr during morning peak.
2026-03-11 10:24 PDT - Ravi (Eng): Preparing v0.9.2 candidate. Added additional metrics and guard to avoid swap when any active stream length > 6k tokens.
2026-03-12 09:01 PDT - Cloudscribe Support (customer): Thank you — pin helped. We need ETA for full fix so we can lift the pin and receive updates as patches land.

root_cause:
Preliminary: kernel-manager performed synchronous hot-swap that flushes/evicts KV cache on the token-emission thread. This could block emission while the kernel artifact is loaded and cache state reconciled, causing long pauses and connection resets in streaming clients.

customer_impact_summary:
Cloudscribe (dedicated) saw mid-generation freezes for long streaming chat responses in us-west. Estimated 40% of long streams affected at peak before mitigation; customer experienced degraded UX and increased error rates. Temporary pin reduced impact substantially.

follow_up_actions:
1) Roll v0.9.2 non-blocking kernel-manager to dedicated pools with staged canary.
2) Add alerts for mm.kernel_swap.duration_ms > 2000ms.
3) Update runbook to avoid live-swap during rolling updates for customers with high long-stream usage.
4) Postmortem to be created after fix deployment and stability window.

[Usage Insights beta: feature flag + account allowlist + admin enablement workflow]
## Summary
Implement targeted enablement for the Usage Insights beta (route+model breakdown + exports) using a feature flag and an account/workspace allowlist, with an internal admin toggle + a rollout checklist.

This ticket is specifically about gating and operational enablement (who sees the feature and how we turn it on safely), not the feature UI itself.

## Background / Why
We need a controlled beta rollout for Usage Insights:
- Ensure only selected workspaces/accounts can access the feature while we validate correctness vs billing and performance.
- Avoid accidental exposure of cost data to customers/workspaces that have cost views disabled.
- Provide a repeatable internal workflow for AEs/SEs/CSM to request enablement (INT tickets) and for Eng/SRE to rollout gradually.

Related artifacts:
- Beta candidate list (Drive): sources/google_drive/shared_drives/product/console-and-rollouts/usage-insights-beta-customer-list.json
- Release notes draft: sources/confluence/product-docs/release-notes/console-2026-03-usage-insights-beta.json
- API contract review thread: sources/slack/eng-platform/1737821108.json

## Requirements
### Gating layers
1) **Global flag** (env-scoped)
   - Name: `console.usage_insights.beta`
   - Default: OFF in production
   - Can be turned ON in staging/dev for ongoing QA

2) **Workspace allowlist** (production)
   - Only workspaces explicitly allowlisted can access Usage Insights routes in console + query API.
   - Allowlist keyed by `workspace_id` (not workspace slug/name), to avoid renames.
   - Allowlist changes should be auditable and revertible.

3) **RBAC/permissions check**
   - Even if allowlisted, users must pass cost-view permission checks (see ENG-3820).
   - If workspace setting is “Hide cost” (or equivalent), show the page shell but block cost amounts + exports with clear messaging.

### Admin enablement workflow
Provide an internal-only admin surface to:
- Add/remove a `workspace_id` from the allowlist
- View current allowlist entries + who/when added it
- See the current state of `console.usage_insights.beta` in the active environment

Constraints:
- Admin surface must be restricted to Redwood staff roles (internal admin), and changes must create an audit log event.
- Rate limit changes and require a short reason string (e.g., “Beta enablement: AcmeAI enterprise eval”).

### Rollout checklist (must be captured in this ticket)
- Confirm data freshness dashboard is green and reconciliation drift < tolerance for last 24h.
- Confirm SLO monitoring/alerts configured for query service.
- Confirm RBAC enforcement shipped (ENG-3820) and export audit logging shipped (ENG-3816 / related PR).
- Enable in staging for end-to-end verification.
- Add 1–3 low-risk workspaces first (non-Private deployments; normal time ranges) and monitor.
- Expand to remaining beta list.
- Document support/SE playbook for enablement requests.

## Implementation notes
### Where gating should be enforced
- **Console UI**: hide navigation entry and route access unless allowlisted + global flag enabled.
- **Backend** (authoritative): enforce in query endpoints and export job creation. UI gating alone is not sufficient.

### Proposed data model
- `feature_flags` (existing) for global flag.
- New table/collection: `console_feature_allowlist`
  - `feature_key` (e.g. `usage_insights_beta`)
  - `workspace_id`
  - `enabled` (soft-delete via boolean)
  - `created_by` (internal user id)
  - `created_at`
  - `updated_at`
  - `reason`

### Admin endpoints (internal)
- `POST /internal/admin/feature-allowlist/usage-insights` (add)
- `DELETE /internal/admin/feature-allowlist/usage-insights?workspace_id=...` (remove)
- `GET /internal/admin/feature-allowlist/usage-insights` (list)

### Audit logging
Emit audit events for:
- allowlist add/remove
- toggling global flag (if we support toggling via admin UI)

Event fields expectation (minimum):
- actor (internal user)
- action
- feature_key
- workspace_id
- reason
- request_id

(Align with Security request INT-9140 follow-ups where applicable.)

## Acceptance criteria
- In prod, feature is not visible/accessible unless both global flag ON and workspace allowlisted.
- Backend rejects requests from non-allowlisted workspaces with a consistent error code (`FEATURE_NOT_ENABLED`), logged with workspace_id.
- Admin can add/remove allowlist entries via internal admin tool; actions are audited.
- RBAC check is still enforced even when allowlisted.
- Rollout checklist exists and is used during beta enablement.

## Test plan
- Unit tests for allowlist enforcement middleware (console backend).
- Integration tests:
  - allowlisted workspace can access query endpoints
  - non-allowlisted workspace gets `FEATURE_NOT_ENABLED`
  - allowlisted + cost-hidden workspace cannot export
- Manual E2E in staging:
  - verify nav visibility and deep-link behavior
  - verify audit log entries

## Rollout checklist (operational)
1. Pre-flight
   - Data freshness within SLA; no active reconciliation drift alerts.
   - Query service p95 latency within beta budget.
   - SRE on-call aware of enablement window.
2. Staging
   - Enable global flag
   - Add test workspace_id
   - Validate console flows + export
3. Production
   - Enable global flag (prod)
   - Allowlist 1–3 workspaces from beta list
   - Monitor: error rate, timeouts, warehouse cost, reconciliation drift
   - Expand allowlist in batches (5–10)
4. Comms
   - Update #eng-releases thread with which workspaces enabled
   - Notify Support/SE for enablement confirmations

## Open questions
- Do we want account-level allowlist in addition to workspace-level? (Current recommendation: workspace-level only; customers often have multiple workspaces with different permissions.)
- Do we need region scoping for Private/VPC workspaces? (Likely no for beta, but confirm with Logan/Nadia if datasets differ.)

[Introduce compact form row layout and inline validation summary]
description:
Problem: Product teams are building dense configuration panels and admin UIs that require tighter vertical rhythm and clearer inline validation than our current form rows allow. Existing components are optimized for roomy product surfaces; squeezing them causes inconsistent spacing, duplicated helper text, and validation noise.

Goal: Add a compact form-row variant and an inline validation summary mode that: (1) reduces vertical spacing while preserving touch/click targets, (2) surfaces one-line inline errors and an optional summary banner, (3) reuses design tokens so theming and contrast requirements remain consistent, and (4) provides a clear migration path for existing usages.

Outcomes (acceptance criteria):
- New FormRow prop compressed=true that reduces vertical padding and collapses helper/error rows while keeping the label readable.
- Input primitives (TextField, Select, Toggle) accept compressed=true and have documented token mappings.
- Inline validation summary: small red single-line messages for per-field errors and an optional top-level summary with count + anchor links.
- Accessibility: label associations, live region announcements for error messages, 4.5:1 contrast for error text where required.
- Tokens: spacing scale tokens consumed via components (spacing.form.row-compact -> 8px top/bottom), and a new token for compact helper font-size.
- Migration guide and 1-2 example pages (Billing settings, Admin bulk edits) implemented in Storybook and verified by QA.

Design notes:
- Use token spacing.form.row-compact = 8 and spacing.form.row-default = 16.
- Helper text compression reduces from 12px -> 11px, with line-height preserved to avoid clipping.
- Error state uses color.semantic.error-600 and a subtle icon (12px) inline to the left of text in compact mode.

API proposal (component props):
- FormRow: compressed: boolean, validationMode: "inline" | "summary" | "none" (default: "inline")
- TextField/Select/Toggle: compressed: boolean, showHelperOnFocusOnly: boolean (optional)

Migration plan:
1) Design system exposes compressed prop and tokens.
2) Update internal storybook with examples (billing, admin).
3) Outreach: create a migration doc and notify product teams via #design-systems with sample PRs.
4) Engineering rollout: enable flag gated rollout (console feature flag) to flip component default in selected routes.

Testing and QA checklist:
- Storybook: compressed stories, all validation permutations.
- Keyboard: tab order, focus ring behavior in compact rows.
- Screen reader: NVDA/VoiceOver announces error text and summary update.
- Cross-browser: ensure no clipping on Safari iOS (small font issues).
- Visual regression: Percy/Chromatic snapshots for compact vs default.

Out-of-scope: redesign of floating labels or helper-affix behaviours (handled in separate tickets).

[Interactive Pathway Cards and Rollback Explorer for Tenant Connectivity]
description:
Design an interactive, scan-first surface in the Private Console that helps operators quickly understand tenant cluster connectivity and perform safe rollback actions for recent upgrade rollouts. The core idea is a compact set of 'Pathway Cards' that summarize connectivity, recent latency/egress trends, and a contextual rollback explorer that shows what will change if a rollback is initiated.

background:
Private clusters have complex inter-region networking and upgrade workflows. Operators told us they want a single-pane way to: (1) see which tenant requests flow through which hop, (2) understand cost/latency exposure per path, and (3) trigger safe rollbacks with clear impact previews. Existing designs are scattershot across the cluster and rollout pages.

goals:
(1) Reduce mean time to awareness for path-level failures; (2) Surface cost/latency trade-offs inline with connectivity; (3) Provide a friction-minimized rollback flow that shows simulated outcomes before commit.

proposed_screens:
1) Tenant Pathway List: compact cards per logical path (eg. tenant-gateway -> edge-proxy -> cluster-nodes -> external-egress). Each card shows status chip, 1-hr latency sparkline, 24h egress cost estimate, and an Expand action.
2) Expanded Card Modal: shows step-by-step hop visualizer with packet-loss %, median latency, last successful health check, and overlay toggles (Latency / Cost / Bandwidth).
3) Rollback Explorer: timeline scrubber of recent rollouts for the selected path, delta preview of routing and capacity changes, flagged dependent tenants, and a one-click safe-rollback with preflight checklist.
4) Simulation Mode: 'What-if' toggle that runs a dry-run against the routing policy engine and displays potential failover routes and cost delta.

mockups:
Figma frames include compact list, expanded details modal, rollback timeline, and simulation overlay. See frames: Pathway_List_v3, Pathway_Expanded_v2, Rollback_Explorer_v1.

prototype_links:
https://www.figma.com/file/ABCDEFG/tenant-pathway-cards-2025
https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1example-design-artifacts

acceptance_criteria:
Pathway List renders correctly for tenants with 1-10 routing hops
Expanded Card shows hop-level metrics and health check history
Rollback Explorer simulates the chosen rollback and surfaces at-risk tenants
Design tokens and spacing align with console style guide
Edge cases: offline clusters and missing metrics show graceful placeholders and clear next steps

review_feedback:
Security review: ensure rollback dry-run does not leak internal topology to non-admin roles. Ops requested an 'undo' snackbar after rollback with a 5-minute reversal window. Accessibility: keyboard focus order for expanded cards must be tested.

decisions:
1) Use card-first approach (list -> expand modal) instead of inline expansion to keep the list scannable. 2) Simulation Mode will be bounded to role=operator and requires audit-log entry. 3) Cost overlay will show estimated 24h delta, not real-time billing data (privacy and API limits).

risks:
Overloading the card UI with too many metrics could reduce scanability. Telemetry APIs may not provide consistent per-hop egress breakdown for all clusters — fallback will show aggregated regional costs. Rollback automation must be conservative; push confirmation and dependency warnings.

engineering_notes:
Backend contract: GET /internal/paths?tenant_id=... -> returns ordered hops, health, latency_samples, cost_estimate_24h. ENG-1842 tracks batching and caching for these calls. Rollback flow requires POST /rollouts/rollback-preview and POST /rollouts/rollback (with dry_run flag). Engineers have requested simulated payload examples in the spec folder.

[Console Waystation: Modular Sidebar Tiles & Route Prioritization]
description:
Redesign the Redwood Console left rail/navigation to support fast multi-workspace switching, dynamic route prioritization based on telemetry, and a modular tile system that surfaces per-workspace dashboards, rollouts, and cost lenses.

problem_statement:
Current sidebar is dense, non-adaptive across long-lived sessions, and forces workspace context switches that interrupt user tasks. Users in multi-tenant flows lose place when switching workspaces; cost lenses and rollout status are buried behind too many clicks. We need a navigation model that supports quick contextual switching, reduces cognitive load, and surfaces telemetry-driven prioritization for routes and alerts.

goals:
Reduce time-to-context when switching between workspaces to under 2s for primary flows
Surface rollouts and high-cost routes in the rail without leaving current view
Provide a predictable, testable IA for teams using Dedicated and Private deployments
Make the sidebar responsive to session telemetry (recent routes, error spikes, active rollouts)
Preserve keyboard-first navigation and accessibility standards

proposed_solution_summary:
Introduce a modular 'tile' sidebar where each tile represents a workspace or a cross-workspace surface (dashboards, rollouts, cost). Tiles can expand into micro-panels for fast interactions. The rail adapts to telemetry: it reorders tiles by recent activity and highlights tiles with active rollouts or cost anomalies. Implement a compact collapsed state and a pinned 'anchor' area for top-priority tiles. Provide admin controls for pinning/order and per-tenant personalization.

design_decisions:
Use modular tiles rather than nested trees to reduce click depth
Telemetry reordering will be conservative: only reorder after sustained activity (60s) to avoid jarring movements
Pinned anchors are immutable for a user session unless explicitly changed by the user
Micro-panels will lazy-load content to preserve startup performance
Keyboard focus order mirrors visual order for accessibility

tradeoffs:
Telemetry-driven reordering may confuse users if too aggressive; mitigated with conservative thresholds and a subtle animation
Micro-panels surface data but increase complexity of state management; requires careful perf budgets and caching
Pinned anchors add UI controls but increase learning cost for new users

prototype_links:
https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/console-waystation-sidebar-tiles?node-id=0%3A1
https://www.invisionapp.com/share/Waystation-Interactive-Prototype-2025

usability_findings:
Tree-testing with 8 power users found 43% slower task completion for workspace-aware flows in current IA
Prototype A (tile expansion on hover) caused accidental opens; users preferred click-to-expand for stability
Users asked for a visible cost badge on tiles; small red badge improved anomaly detection in tests
Keyboard users requested consistent shortcuts to pin/unpin tiles; mapping added to final spec

acceptance_criteria:
Design spec reviewed and signed off by PM and Eng (UX/Eng review complete)
Interactive prototype validated with at least 6 end users and measurable TPS improvement in task time
Figma tokens and component variants exist for tile states (collapsed, expanded, pinned, alert)
Engineering has a performance plan: micro-panel lazy-loading, caching strategy, and telemetry debounce thresholds
Console e2e test plan includes keyboard nav, screen-reader ARIA attributes, and workspace switch unit tests

next_steps:
Finalize responsive behavior for narrow viewports and mobile web
Hand off component spec, tokens, and motion guidelines to platform team (due 2025-03-07)
Coordinate with telemetry infra to expose recent-route and cost-anomaly signals (ticket ENG-3021)
Run A/B experiment on conservative vs aggressive telemetry reorder to measure user confusion metric
Prepare rollout changelog and admin settings page for tenant-level pin defaults
