[Mixed-priority cgroup and soft-quota playbook for multi-tenant inference]
Summary

This playbook defines a pragmatic, deployable policy and reference implementation pattern for enforcing mixed-priority resource controls on Redwood inference nodes. It combines OS-level cgroups, a soft-quota crediting algorithm, and scheduler-level hints to guarantee tenant fairness for bursty traffic while protecting latency-sensitive SLAs. The goal is predictable SLOs with controlled cost and graceful degradation under contention.

Scope

- Applies to dedicated GPU hosts and shared GPU slice deployments used for multi-tenant inference.
- Covers CPU, GPU memory residency, NVLink and PCIe bandwidth gating, and host-level network egress shaping where supported.
- Does NOT replace cloud provider-side hard quotas or hypervisor limits; this is an infra-layer policy implemented inside Redwood-managed nodes.

Definitions and terminology

- Soft-quota: a rate-style allocation enforced by token/credit accounting rather than hard kernel-level denial. Gives tenants temporary burst capacity until credits are exhausted.
- Cgroup profile: named resource envelope mapped to a tenant route or model variant (e.g., low-priority-batch, standard-realtime, realtime-guaranteed).
- Preemptible slot: runtime slot eligible for preemption when higher-priority work arrives. Clients may receive a retryable 429 with retry-after hints.
- Credit refill window: interval on which soft-quota credit balances are replenished.

Principles

1) Prioritize latency SLOs for realtime-guaranteed tenants; starvation-avoidance for all others.
2) Make policies observable and auditable: every decision must emit events and metrics.
3) Prefer non-destructive throttling before eviction.
4) Provide transparent billing signals: exhausted credits should generate usage traces and billing-affecting tags.

Service model and mapping

- Map inbound request classes to cgroup profiles at the edge ingress (edge-proxy or inference gateway) based on API token, route, or customer contract.
- Example profile names: realtime-guaranteed, standard, burstable, spot-preemptible.

Resource profile table (reference)

Profile | GPU share | CPU share | Burst credits per minute | Preemptible
---|---:|---:|---:|---:
realtime-guaranteed | 60% | 4 CPUs | 0 | false
standard | 25% | 2 CPUs | 100 credits | true
burstable | 10% | 1 CPU | 1000 credits | true
spot-preemptible | 5% | 0.5 CPU | 5000 credits | true

Operational invariants

- P95 latency for realtime-guaranteed must remain under 80 ms for 2kB prompt workloads under nominal load.
- P99 latency degradation must be limited to 3x baseline under accepted degraded mode.
- No tenant should consume >2x its configured long-term average without exhausting burst credits.

Soft-quota algorithm (summary)

1) Each profile has a token bucket: capacity (burst cap) and rate (sustained).
2) Requests consume tokens proportional to an estimate of per-request GPU time (token_cost = base_cost + size_factor).
3) When tokens are available, allow request and deduct tokens. When depleted, attempt polite throttling: apply queueing/backoff first (retry-after 150–500 ms depending on queue depth), then reject with 429 when queue > max_queue_len.
4) Credits are replenished on a 1s tick with leaky-bucket refill semantics; windows can be tuned per workload.

Cgroup & kernel-level controls (implementation notes)

- Use systemd.slice + unified cgroup v2 where available. For GPU residency/visibility we use Nvidia MIG or runtime-controlled CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES mapping. For non-MIG GPUs, rely on process-level CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES combined with per-process niceness and CPU bandwidth controls.
- Example cgroup layout (text description): root/rdw/guaranteed.slice, root/rdw/standard.slice, root/rdw/burstable.slice, root/rdw/spot.slice.
- CPU bandwidth values set with systemd CPUQuota= and MemoryMax= where applicable.

Example cgroup profile YAML (to be consumed by node agent)

profile_name: standard
labels: ["multi-tenant", "standard"]
cpu_quota_percent: "25%"
gpu_share_percent: "25%"
burst_capacity_tokens: "1000"
refill_rate_tokens_per_s: "16"

(node-agent will translate to systemd + token-bucket state on startup)

Preemption and eviction policy

- Soft preemption: first step is to stop accepting new requests for preemptible profiles and burn down queues. Provide clients with a Retry-After header. Emit PreemptionWarning event to tracing.
- Hard eviction: only when soft preemption fails for longer than 30s AND SLOs for realtime-guaranteed are violated by >10% over a rolling 1m window. Evicted sessions are checkpointed if runtime supports incremental KV-cache persistence; otherwise return structured error with model-invocation-id for audit.

Telemetry and SLI set (required metrics to emit)

- profile.request_rate (per-profile, r/s)
- profile.token_balance (gauge)
- profile.rejects_429 (counter)
- node.gpu_utilization (gauge)
- node.preemption_events (counter with reason label)
- request.latency_p50/p95/p99 (per-profile)

Alerting thresholds (recommended)

- SLO breach alert: realtime-guaranteed.p99 > 120 ms for 2 consecutive 1m windows -> page SRE oncall.
- Exhaustion alert: profile.token_balance < 1% of capacity for 5m -> create sustained-throttling ticket.
- Preemption storm: node.preemption_events > 10 in 1m -> create incident and auto-scale farm capacity.

Testing and validation

- Synthetic load: use the perf-harness tool with a mixed-profile manifest. Example CLI:
  rdw-perf start --manifest tests/manifests/mixed-bursty-50-30-20.yaml --duration 10m --trace=on
- Chaos test: inject CPU throttling (stress-ng) and GPU memory pressure (cuda-memtest) during a 30m soak; verify token balances and preemption events are emitted and SLOs respected.
- Contract tests: run end-to-end convergence tests in staging where billing tags, traces, and token accounting are validated.

Rollout plan (canary -> gradual -> global)

1) Implement node-agent feature flag behind runtime.flag.soft_quota_v2. Deploy to 2 canary nodes in staging.
2) Run mixed synthetic load for 24h and validate metrics/alerts.
3) Canary in production: enable on 5 nodes serving non-critical tenants for 48h with increased sampling.
4) Gradual rollout: 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% of nodes, with 6h observation between steps.
4a) If preemption storm or SLO regressions are observed, auto-rollback to previous flag state.

Operational runbook (summary)

- Detect: Alert for realtime-guaranteed.p99 and node.preemption_events.
- Mitigate: Increase node pool capacity (scale up dedicated nodes) or temporarily reduce burst refill rates via platform API: POST /admin/quota/adjust {"profile":"burstable","refill_rate":4}.
- Recover: If hard eviction triggered, restart affected runtime with persisted KV-cache, and run postmortem with request ids (attach trace ids to incident).

Ownership and change control

- Primary owner: infra-scheduling@redwood.com (team: eng-infra).
- Secondary owner: serving-runtime@redwood.com for runtime integration.
- Any config changes to default profiles must go through CHANGE-FEATURE ticket and be approved by owners; large profile changes require a 1-week staged rollout and telemetry gating.

Security and privacy considerations

- Token accounting and audit logs must not include PII. Traces related to billing or chargebacks should be stored in restricted retention with RBAC.
- Ensure GPU-side libraries are up-to-date to avoid kernel CVEs that could allow cross-tenant leakage.

rdw-agent apply-profile --file profiles/burstable.yaml

# Query balances
rdw-agent profile-status --profile burstable --format json

queue_max_len: 64
preemptible: true

- See GPU fleet soft-quota eviction policy (eng-infra) for cross-reference.
- See ADR: adaptive-priority-fairness for bursting for background rationale.

[Cost-Sensitive Alert Triage and Prioritization Matrix for Multi‑Tenant Inference]
Overview

This document defines a reproducible, cost-aware alert triage and prioritization matrix for Redwood's multi-tenant inference platform. It standardizes how oncall and platform operators should score, route, and resolve alerts that have cost implications (token spend, GPU-hours, cache churn) while balancing latency SLOs and customer impact. The goal is to reduce noisy cost alerts, focus response on high-impact events, and align escalation with business risk.

When to use this playbook

- Any alert that contains or correlates with per-tenant cost signals (unexpected token surge, anomalous embedding throughput, sudden model fallback to higher-cost variants).
- Alerts tied to GPU/instance billing anomalies (hot requeues, preemption churn, sustained inefficient GPU utilization).
- Persistent prefix/KV cache eviction storms producing amplification of compute.
- Any situation where cost mitigation actions (throttles, model swap, soft-quotas) need to be weighed against latency/customer SLOs.

High-level approach

1. Derive a Priority Score using weighted signals (Cost, Customer Impact, Latency Risk, Error Amplification, Detection Certainty).
2. Use score cutoffs to map to Triage Levels: Informational, Low, Medium, High, Critical.
3. Route alerts by Triage Level to teams/notification channels and suggest default mitigations.
4. Apply short-lived automated mitigations for high-cost low-impact events (e.g., tenant-level burst throttle), preserving graceful degradation for high-impact tenants.

Priority score (formula)

We compute a normalized score in operator UI and as part of alert enrichment. Each signal is scaled 0.0—1.0 and multiplied by a weight (w). FinalScore = 100 * (w_cost*cost + w_customer*customer_impact + w_latency*latency_risk + w_error*error_amplification + w_certainty*detection_certainty)

Default weights (tunable):

- w_cost = 0.35  # monetary risk (expected extra $/hr normalized)
- w_customer = 0.30  # tenant SLA priority (1.0 = enterprise-production, 0.0 = free-trial)
- w_latency = 0.15  # tail latency degradation potential
- w_error = 0.10  # increased error rates / degraded outputs
- w_certainty = 0.10  # confidence of detection heuristics / anomaly model

Score buckets and routing

- 0–19: Informational — no paging; create a ticket; channel: #platform-cost-insights
- 20–39: Low — page L1 slack with summary; ops playbook optional; channel: #platform-ops-low
- 40–64: Medium — page oncall; runbook introspection steps; channel: #platform-oncall
- 65–84: High — immediate oncall paging + core infra escalation; recommend mitigations; channel: #platform-incident
- 85–100: Critical — incident declaration, exec-notify candidate, automatic protective actions allowed (per auto-mitigation whitelist)

Alert enrichment signals (examples and collection sources)

- Cost delta (cost): 1h projected over baseline and 24h rolling baseline. Source: billing-stream, cost-proxy metrics (prometheus: tenant_token_spend_delta). Example PromQL:

  sum by (tenant) (increase(token_cost_usd_total[1h])) / max(1,sum by (tenant) (increase(token_cost_usd_total[24h])))

- Tenant SLA tier (customer_impact): lookup from tenant metadata service (0.0 = trial, 0.5 = standard, 1.0 = enterprise). Cached in Redis/metadata cache with 5m TTL.

- Tail latency risk (latency_risk): measured by 95th / baseline 95th ratio for recent 15m window. Example PromQL:

  (histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[15m])) by (le, tenant))) / tenant_baseline_p95

- Error amplification (error_amplification): spike in model error counts or fallback frequency (model_fallbacks_total). Normalized to max historical spike.

- Detection certainty (detection_certainty): from anomaly model (0.0–1.0). Lower certainty reduces final score and favors investigation over automation.

Routing and notification templates

- Each alert enrichment must include: tenant id, projected delta $/hr, 15m p95 delta, top affected endpoints, last 50 tokens/sample prompts (sanitized), tenant SLA tier, suggested mitigation steps.
- Notification subject line (example): [High][Tenant: acme-corp] unexpected token surge — projected +$420/hr, p95 +1.9x
- Slack payload should include quick actions buttons: "Throttle Tenant 5%", "Set Soft Quota 1k tokens/min", "Swap to cheaper-model", "Acknowledge & Investigate". Buttons call platform-ops API with operator auth.

Automated mitigations (guardrails and whitelist)

Automations are allowed only when: detection_certainty >= 0.8 AND customer_impact <= 0.5 OR tenant is in auto-mitigation whitelist. Actions are short-lived (default 15m) and must be reversible without requiring redeploy. Example automations:

- Per-tenant burst throttle (scale down token rate by computed fraction).
- Soft-quotas that reject non-critical endpoints with 429 and fixed retry-after header.
- Model-swap to a functionally compatible but lower-cost quantized variant with validated quality delta < 2% for that tenant group.

Mitigation audit trail: every automated action writes an immutable audit event to audit-log with fields (timestamp, tenant, action, initiator=automation|operator, reason, rollback_deadline).

Operator triage playbook (step-by-step)

1. Read the enriched alert: confirm tenant, projected cost, and detection certainty.
2. Check tenant metadata: SLA, active releases, open incidents. CLI example:

  redwood tenant get acme-corp --fields=sla,open_incidents,recent-deploy

3. Validate with dashboards: open cost heatmap (dashboards: Cost › tenant-spike) and p95 latency chart for that tenant.

4. If FinalScore < 40: log RCA ticket, assign to cost-optimization board; annotate alert and suppress further low-signal repeats for 1h.

5. If 40 <= FinalScore < 65: for medium alerts, collect request traces (up to 100) and determine if traffic pattern is sudden (single API key) or systemic. Suggested mitigations: temporary tenant throttle, notify customer-success if SLA enterprise.

6. If 65 <= FinalScore < 85: execute immediate mitigations: apply soft-quota, throttle non-critical routes, or trigger model-swap. Escalate to infra lead. Start incident timeline and notify revenue ops.

7. If FinalScore >= 85: declare incident, execute protective actions in sequence (throttle → swap → node draining) until cost burn subsides. Call exec-incident channel if not resolved within 10m.

Escalation contacts and ownership (default)

- First-line: Platform oncall (team: platform-ops) — primary pager.
- Second-line: Serving runtime engineers (team: eng-serving-runtime) — kernel/quantization/model-swap owner.
- Third-line: Platform SRE leads / Infra cost gate owner.
- Business ops: Revenue Ops for enterprise tenant cost notifications.

Dashboard and alert pages to use

- Dash: Cost › tenant-spike (tenant cost delta map) — quick filter by SLA tier.
- Dash: Latency › tenant p95 and tail distribution (15m/1h/24h).
- Dash: Cache › eviction rate and KV hit-rate by tenant shard.

Monitoring queries and example PromQL snippets

- Token spend delta per tenant (1h over 24h baseline):
  sum by (tenant) (increase(token_cost_usd_total[1h])) / max(1,sum by (tenant) (increase(token_cost_usd_total[24h])))

- GPU inefficiency (fraction of cycle time wasted waiting on host):
  sum by (instance) (rate(gpu_idle_time_seconds[5m])) / sum by (instance) (rate(gpu_cycle_time_seconds[5m]))

- KV prefix cache eviction storm (per shard):
  sum by (shard) (increase(kv_cache_evictions_total[5m]))

Templates for retrospective and runbook updates

After any Medium+ incident (FinalScore >= 40) we require a 72-hour lightweight retrospective:

- Owner: person who executed first mitigation (or oncall if automated)
- Deliverables: short summary (what happened, why cost became elevated, actions taken, impact $ estimate, time to mitigation), impact matrix (tenants affected + SLA), recommended follow-ups (engineering + product)
- Timeline: submit within 72 hours to /confluence/eng-platform/retrospectives and notify platform-ops.

Retrospective template (header fields) — include in ticket body:

- Incident ID, Start/End time, FinalScore, Tenant list, Direct cost delta, Actions executed, Rollback timeline, Root cause hypothesis, Follow-up owners (engineering/product), Estimated completion dates.

Rollout and tuning

- Weight tuning cadence: quarterly review in platform roadmap planning. Use last 3 months of incidents to recompute weights by maximizing TP value (business value preserved per mitigation).
- Whitelist management: product-led enterprise tenants must be on a maintained whitelist. Changes require a PR to platform-config repo and approval by infra lead.

Ownership and governance

- Document owner: Platform Observability (owner: Aisha Patel) — maintain content, metrics, and enrichment pipelines.
- Automation owner: Serving Runtime (responsible for model-swap safety checks and automation hooks).
- Reviewers: oncall rotation leads must validate the playbook during every oncall handoff and after any major incident.

Appendix: Example incident timeline (condensed)

- 09:10 Alert triggered: Tenant acme-corp token spend +12x, FinalScore=72. Automated soft-quota applied (throttle 30%).
- 09:12 Oncall paged; quick check: p95 increased 1.3x for non-critical routes.
- 09:17 Manual model-swap executed to quantized-2q model for non-critical route (reduces cost by 46% on sampled traces, validated quality delta 0.8%).
- 09:28 Cost burn falling; mitigation reduced to throttle 10% and monitoring continued.
- 10:00 Incident closed; 72-hour retrospective assigned.

Notes and FAQs

- Q: When should customer-success be notified?
  A: For any Medium+ event affecting enterprise SLA tenants, include cs-rep in initial notification.

- Q: How do we handle false positives from anomaly models?
  A: Use detection_certainty and conservative automation thresholds. For low certainty but high cost, prefer manual triage.

- Q: Can we apply the same matrix to Dedicated customers?
  A: Dedicated capacity customers are typically on contracts; run this matrix but route to account team first and follow contractual limits.

Related artifacts and code pointers

- Enrichment service repo: git@internal:redwood/enrichment-service (contains score calculation implementation).
- Auto-mitigation service: git@internal:redwood/auto-mitigation (whitelist and action runners).
- Dashboards: Grafana folder "Platform / Cost and Tenant Health".

Contact and feedback

For suggested changes or to propose weight adjustments, file a PR against this document in the platform-docs repo or ping the Platform Observability Slack channel with "weight-tuning" label.


[SLO Prognostics and Capacity Quarantine Playbook]
Overview
--------
This playbook defines a combined approach for (1) predictive SLO prognostics using telemetry signals, (2) automated and manual capacity quarantine actions to protect defined business-critical SLOs, and (3) the incident review / remediation cadence that follows quarantine activations. It is intended for platform SREs, service owners, and product stakeholders responsible for multi-tenant inference and serving runtime availability.

Goals
- Detect SLO drift early using leading indicators (not just rolling error budgets).
- Contain and stabilize critical SLOs by isolating tenant/capacity shock via a "capacity quarantine" process.
- Provide a clear operational runbook and post-incident evidence checklist for reviews and capacity corrections.

Scope
- Applies to Redwood inference-serving services (hosted and dedicated control planes) and multi-tenant GPU pools.
- Targets SLOs with business impact: 99th tail latency, request availability, and embedding-return correctness windows.
- Does NOT replace tenant eviction / billing enforcement policies; quarantine is a temporary stabilization mechanism.

Key Definitions
- Prognostic signal: A telemetry-derived metric that historically precedes SLO burn (examples: model KV cache miss rate spike, median GPU utilization delta, inter-request latency jitter).
- Capacity quarantine: Engineering action that restricts incoming traffic to a subset of tenants or routes, reassigns requests to slower fallbacks, or pins model variants to preserve critical SLOs.
- Critical SLOs: SLOs categorized as P0/P1 by product impact (see SLO attribute table).

Ownership and Roles
- SRE on-call: Execute quarantine runbook and initial containment; page service owner.
- Service owner (team owning model or API): Validate quarantine target tenants, approve broad mitigations, drive postmortem.
- Capacity engineering: Execute capacity scale-up/soft-preemption and advise on reserve capacity usage.
- Observability engineering: Maintain prognostic signals and dashboards; run simulation backtests quarterly.

SLO Attribute Matrix (example)
| SLO name | Objective | Primary metric | Burn threshold (30m) | Critical? | Notification channel |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---|
| request-availability | 99.95% | successful_requests/total_requests | >0.1% error | YES | #sre-pager, slack SRE-alerts |
| p99-latency | 1000ms | 99th latency (ms) | >1.5x baseline | YES | #sre-pager |
| embedding-cost-trim | 98% | normalized embedding completeness | >2% regression | NO | #platform-observability |

Leading Prognostic Signals (examples and rationale)
- KV cache miss rate (per-model): sustained +15ppts in 10m often precedes p99 latency burn when model cache reuse is high.
- GPU scheduling preemption count: sudden uptick correlates with cross-tenant eviction and tail latency increases.
- Request inter-arrival jitter: high jitter signals bursty traffic that will drive queue growth.
- Prefix-caching hit-rate and token re-generation ratio: poor values often indicate prompt churn and increased compute per request.

Telemetry thresholds and alert types
- Signal-critical alert (page): any single prognostic signal breaching its page threshold (table below) for 5 minutes.
- Signal-warning alert (ops): sustained breach for 10 minutes or two signals correlated across traces.

Example alert thresholds (tune per service)
| signal | warning | critical | purpose |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| model_kv_cache_miss_rate (5m) | >8% | >15% | early cache evaporation indicator |
| gpu_preempt_count (5m) | >2 | >5 | capacity stranding / noisy neighbor |
| req_interarrival_p95_delta | >200ms | >500ms | burstiness that drives queues |

Capacity Prognostics and Quarantine Decision Matrix
1. Detect: Observability pipeline correlates prognostic signals with SLO burn probability > 60% in next 30m (see prognostics model scoring below).
2. Validate: On-call inspects recent traces, model hotness, and tenant distribution.
3. Contain (automated/fast): If predicted impact > 75% and critical SLOs are at risk, trigger automated partial quarantine: route 20–50% of non-critical tenant traffic to slow-path fallback, enable tighter concurrency caps, and raise preemption buffers.
4. Escalate (manual/stopgap): If automated containment insufficient, on-call initiates full capacity quarantine for specified tenants/routes.

Quarantine action catalog (examples)
- Route-level throttles: apply token-bucket rate limits to defined API routes for non-critical tenants.
- Tenant soft-throttle: reduce max concurrent requests per tenant by 30–70%; prefer queueing over outright rejection.
- Model fallback routing: switch heavy requests to quantized or smaller model variants with known latency characteristics.
- Reserve capacity allocation: allocate reserved headroom (if available) to critical routes and pin their worker pools.

Runbook: Capacity Quarantine Activation (step-by-step)
1. On-call receives signal-critical page or prognostic dashboard indicates >75% impact probability.
2. Triage (5 minutes): confirm signal provenance (edge, load balancer, serving runtime), check recent deploys, and confirm there is no active global outage.
3. Notify stakeholders: post initial incident summary in Slack SRE-alerts and tag service owner + product owner.
4. Execute automated partial quarantine policy (runbook script):
   a. Run: ./ops/quarantine/trigger_partial.sh --service SERVICE --policy cache-stabilize-20
   b. Monitor telemetry for 2 minutes. If no improvement, proceed.
5. If continued deterioration (15 minutes): coordinate with service owner to identify hot tenants and run full quarantine.
   a. Use tenant selector: ./ops/quarantine/select_tenants.py --service SERVICE --mode hot-tenants --max 10
   b. Apply: ./ops/quarantine/activate_full.sh --tenant-list TENANTS.csv --reasons "kv_miss_spike,gpu_preempt"
6. Confirm stabilization: SLO metrics trending back toward baseline for 30 minutes.
7. Begin staged de-escalation per Deactivation checklist below.

Deactivation checklist
- Confirm SLOs have recovered (30m stable window).
- Incrementally remove throttles in 10% steps every 5 minutes while observing for regressions.
- Revert model routing if fallbacks are no longer required.
- Re-run traffic replay for any quarantined tenants in a test environment to validate capacity correction.

Incident review and evidence standards (post-activation)
Required artifacts for any quarantine activation:
- Timeline: exact timestamps for prognostic alerts, quarantine triggers, throttle changes, and stakeholder notifications.
- Telemetry export: 1h pre-incident and 2h post-incident raw metrics for signals used in detection.
- Trace samples: 20 representative distributed traces (10 before, 10 after) that show latency and queue behavior.
- Tenant list and request patterns: CSV of quarantined tenant IDs and the request counts during the incident window.
- Runbook actions: exact CLI commands used, approver signatures (Slack thread IDs).

Postmortem minimum required sections
1. Summary and impact (customers, internal).
2. Detection timeline and prognostic signal analysis.
3. Containment actions taken and rationale.
4. Root cause hypothesis and evidence linking capacity signals to SLO regression.
5. Follow-up actions (owner, priority, due date).
6. Capacity corrections: reserve changes, autoscale policy adjustments, model variant scheduling tweaks.

Operational tooling (dashboards, queries, automation)
- Dashboards: prognostic overview (heatmap of per-model KV miss, GPU preemption, tenant QPS skew), quarantine status center, SLO impact forecast.
- Automation scripts: ops/quarantine/* (partial and full activation), ops/prognostics/backtest.py, ops/prognostics/score_model.py.
- Alerting rules (Prometheus-style examples):
  - rule: HighModelKVMiss
    expr: increase(model_kv_cache_miss_total[5m]) / increase(model_req_total[5m]) > 0.15
    for: 5m
    labels: {severity: page}

Prognostics model (brief)
- We maintain a lightweight logistic classifier that consumes the normalized prognostic signals and outputs a probability of SLO burn in the next 30 minutes. The model is retrained weekly on labeled incidents. Observability engineering owns the model and validation harness.
- Backtest every quarter across five representative services and publish ROC/AUC and calibration plots to the prognostics dashboard.

Simulated exercise schedule (reliability initiative)
- Quarterly capacity-quarantine drills: run a game-day where prognostic signals are seeded and teams execute the quarantine runbook. Objectives: validate tenant selection tooling, measure time-to-stabilize, and ensure postmortem artifacts are captured.
- Annual audit: validate that critical SLOs have appropriate reserve capacity and the prognostics model false-positive rate is < 5%.

Metrics to track for playbook health
- Mean time to quarantine activation (target < 12m from page).
- Mean time to stabilization after quarantine (target < 30m).
- Quarantine correctness: % of quarantines that targeted true root-cause tenants (target > 85%).
- Prognostics precision/recall (internal SLA for the prognostics model).

Example queries and snippets (appendix)
- Latency tail trend (Influx/PromQL):
  increase(requests_total{job="service",route="/v1/generate"}[15m])
  histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_bucket[5m])) by (le))
- Simple tenant selector (pseudo-CLI):
  ./ops/quarantine/select_tenants.py --service inference-api --metric kv_miss_rate --since 10m --top 5 > TENANTS.csv

Change control and approval for persistent capacity changes
- Any persistent change to reserve capacity, concurrency caps, or default model routing that lasts >24 hours requires a signed Change Request and approval from Capacity Engineering and Product. Log CR in change-management template and link in postmortem.

References and related pages
- See also: SLO admission playbook, capacity-onboarding-runway, prognostics model repo.

- 2026-02-08: Added prognostic scoring guidance and example thresholds (reviewers: Priya Desai)
- 2026-03-02: Finalized quarantine scripts and deactivation checklist; published.


[Predictive Tenant Imbalance Mitigation Guide]
Summary
-------
This guide describes a predictive, telemetry-driven process for detecting and mitigating tenant imbalance in Redwood Inference (situations where a small number of tenants consume disproportionate shared capacity and risk SLO degradation for other tenants). The playbook ties SLO/error-budget signals to a tenant-priority ledger, automated quarantine, soft-eviction controls, and capacity-synthesis checks so SREs can respond before wide service impact.

Scope
-----
Applies to: multi-tenant inference clusters (hosted API and Dedicated shared clusters).
Excludes: single-tenant Dedicated pools and Private on-prem clusters managed by customer ops (these follow a separate on-prem runbook).

Motivation
----------
- Tenant imbalance causes cascading tail latency and unpredictable burn of cluster-level SLOs.
- Typical symptoms: sudden p99 spikes, KV cache thrashing, model hot-hot partitions, and headroom erosion.
- Reactive eviction causes business disruption; predictive mitigation reduces customer impact and simplifies post-incident remediation.

Key definitions
---------------
- Tenant Imbalance Score (TIS): composite score 0.0–1.0 combining token/sec share, 1m p95 latency delta, model-hotness, and cache miss rate. Threshold: >0.7 = high; 0.9 = critical.
- Priority Ledger: authoritative per-tenant ledger (tier, hard_quota, soft_quota, escalation_policy) used by throttling and eviction controllers.
- Quarantine: temporary rate-limited state with traffic shaping and KV-cache prewarm prevention to protect cluster headroom.

Telemetry & detection
---------------------
Important signals (ingested into SRE telemetry pipeline):
- Per-tenant tokens/sec (1s, 1m, 5m)
- Per-tenant p95/p99 for model endpoints, and delta vs baseline (baseline = 7d rolling median)
- Shared cluster headroom (GPU utilization, model mem pressure, active model instances vs capacity)
- KV cache miss rate and average KV size by tenant
- Error budget burn rate (service-level): 1h and 24h burn windows
- Admission/denial counts from policy gateway

Detection rules (examples):
1) Rapid-share spike: tenant contributes >25% of tokens/sec for a cluster and has >=2x 1m increase vs 5m median => increase TIS by 0.35.
2) Latency correlation: tenant p99 increase >50% and cluster p99 increased >20% in same 60s window => increase TIS by 0.25.
3) Cache thrash: tenant cache miss rate delta >0.15 and model-hotness >0.6 => increase TIS by 0.2.
4) Error-budget coupling: service-level burn rate >12% in last 1h and top-3 tenants account for >60% of requests => mark cluster at-risk and raise alerts.

- Composite TIS calculation occurs each 30s; values persisted for 48h for forensics.

Alerting and early-warning
-------------------------
Severity mapping:
- Warning: TIS >= 0.55 for any tenant (pager to oncall slack channel; playbook runbook flag set).
- Action: TIS >= 0.7 and cluster headroom <15% (pager escalation to SRE oncall and platform product manager).
- Critical: TIS >= 0.9 OR service-level error-budget alarm (automatic emergency mitigation triggers, notify customer-success for affected tenants).

Mitigation playbook (ordered steps)
----------------------------------
1) Observe and validate (SRE oncall)
   - Confirm telemetry via dashboard: tenant TIS, per-tenant token rate, p99 deltas, cache miss rate.
   - Check recent rollouts or deploy windows for potential correlates.
   - If TIS rises due to known customer test activity, annotate and advise customer success.

2) Soft traffic shaping (automated first responder)
   - Apply 5–30% rate reduction to offending tenant(s) using the adaptive throttle controller.
   - Goal: reduce immediate tail while preserving meaningful traffic for the tenant.
   - Continue to monitor TIS over next 60–120s.

3) Quarantine and KV prewarm suppression (automated if shaping insufficient)
   - Move tenant to "quarantine" policy for 5 minutes: stricter rate cap, deprioritized cache population, and connection churn mitigation.
   - Quarantine metrics: fail_rate_target <1%, reduce token/sec by target_pct = min(50%, (TIS-0.7)*100).

4) Priority ledger evaluation and human review
   - Read ledger: tier (e.g., enterprise, standard, free), contractual SLAs, escalation policy.
   - If tenant is tiered enterprise with dedicated escalation, SRE to call product/solutions for coordinated plan.

5) Graceful soft-eviction (manual approval required for high-impact cases)
   - If TIS remains >0.85 after two quarantine cycles and cluster headroom <10%: recommend soft eviction of best-effort tenants (lowest ledger priority).
   - Eviction order policy: (a) fairshare_score, (b) recent error budget consumption, (c) tenant tier.

6) Emergency capacity expansion (if configured)
   - If Dedicated pool supports burst capacity, invoke autoscale-burst with 10–30% additional nodes, and mark capacity-source in incident timeline.

7) Post-mitigation validation and annotation
   - Confirm SLOs returning to baseline for the cluster and top-affected tenants.
   - Annotate incident timeline with causes, actions, time-in-state, and tenant IDs.

Runbook: Rapid Quarantine (for oncall)
-------------------------------------
1) Trigger conditions: TIS >= 0.7 AND (cluster headroom <15% OR service burn >8%/1h).
2) Steps:
   a) Navigate to the "Tenant Imbalance" dashboard.
   b) Click tenant row -> open "Mitigate" -> choose "Soft throttle (30% default)".
   c) Wait 60s, observe TIS trend. If TIS falls below 0.6, remove throttle after 3m.
   d) If TIS remains >0.75 after 2m, escalate to quarantine.
3) Quarantine command (CLI):
   - rctl tenant quarantine --tenant-id=TENANT123 --duration=5m --rate-limit=200rps --kv-populate=deprioritize
4) Rollback: rctl tenant unquarantine --tenant-id=TENANT123

Priority Ledger config (example, YAML)
-------------------------------------
Note: stored in config service; consult change-control for edits.

| tenant_id | tier      | soft_quota_rps | hard_quota_rps | escalation_contact |
|-----------|-----------|----------------|----------------|--------------------|
| TENANT123 | standard  | "500"         | "1500"        | "pm-xyz@redwood.com" |
| TENANT789 | enterprise| "2000"        | "5000"        | "ae-enterprise@redwood.com" |

Example YAML snippet (for automation):

priority_ledger:
  TENANT123:
    tier: standard
    soft_quota_rps: "500"
    hard_quota_rps: "1500"
    escalation_contact: "pm-xyz@redwood.com"

Operational tooling integration
-------------------------------
- Telemetry pipeline: TIS computed by the SLO-synthesis job and emitted to the metrics cluster as metric name: inference.tenant.tis (labels: tenant_id, cluster_id, model_family).
- Controllers: throttle-controller and quarantine-manager read the priority ledger via the config service and enforce via edge policy.
- Simulation harness: use the imbalance-sim CLI to run tenant-mix simulations before making policy changes.

Capacity planning & acceptance criteria
--------------------------------------
- For each multi-tenant cluster, product must provide expected peak tenant share and critical tenants list at onboarding. Onboarding acceptance requires:
  - Headroom target: >= 20% under p95 traffic forecast.
  - Admission rule cookbook: priority ledger entries for top-10 tenants.
- Quarterly exercise: run an "imbalanced surge" simulation (see Simulation section) prior to major model rollouts.

Incident review & RCA standards (for imbalance events)
-----------------------------------------------------
Required artifacts for post-incident review:
1) Timeline: annotated 1s-resolution timeline for 30m before and after mitigation, including operator actions.
2) Telemetry snapshot: per-tenant tokens/sec, p95/p99, cache stats, headroom.
3) Priority ledger state and any changes made during incident.
4) Runbook compliance checklist: were playbook steps followed? If deviation, justify and include alternate remediation.
5) Customer impact statement: list tenant IDs, impact windows, and CS outreach timeline.
6) Regresion test: run simulation with same traffic profile to validate recommended guardrails.

Postmortem scoring rubric (short)
- Detection time: <2m (score pass/fail)
- Time-to-first-mitigation: <5m
- Recovery to baseline SLOs: <15m
- Customer impact: measured in token-loss or error-rates; must be documented

Simulation lab (how to rehearse)
-------------------------------
- Tool: imbalance-sim (part of platform testkit)
- Typical scenario: 3 tenants, 1 heavy attacker at 40x baseline rate, KV sizes skewed.
- Commands: imbalance-sim --scenario=kv-thrash-heavy --duration=15m --metrics-output=/tmp/imb-sim.out
- Acceptance: cluster p99 remains within 1.2x baseline after first automated throttle; SRE should be able to go from alert->quarantine in <3m in simulation.

Escalation & communication
-------------------------
- Notifications: automated Slack message to #sre-incident with tenant id and TIS when action >= quarantine.
- Customer comms: Customer Success should own messaging for enterprise customers after quarantine. Use template: "We observed elevated usage patterns affecting shared latency; we applied temporary controls and are coordinating next steps."

Ownership & SLAs
----------------
- Primary owner: eng-sre (team: tenant-capacity).
- Secondary owner: eng-platform (controllers and ledger).
- Product owner for policy changes: product-infra.
- SLA tie-ins: actions are advisory for standard tier; enforcement may be contractual for free/experimental tiers.

Appendix A — CLI snippets and sample alerts
-------------------------------------------
- Query TIS: rctl metrics query --metric inference.tenant.tis --tenant TENANT123 --since=5m
- Submit ledger change (requires approval): rctl ledger set --tenant=TENANT123 --soft=600 --hard=2000 --approver=product-infra
- Sample Pager alert body (short):
  Title: tenant imbalance high (TENANT123)
  Body: TIS=0.78, tokens/sec=4200 (25% cluster share), cluster_headroom=12%, action=auto-throttle(30%)

Appendix B — Change control and safety checks
----------------------------------------------
- Any change to priority ledger must go through a small-change approval if soft_quota_rps or hard_quota_rps changes >20%.
- Feature flags: quarantine-manager has a kill-switch flag (sre.quarantine.enabled) default true; emergency disable requires two engineer approvals.

Appendix C — Glossary and links
--------------------------------
- TIS: Tenant Imbalance Score (documented above).
- Priority ledger: source-of-truth config service path: /config/priority_ledger
- Related pages: see capacity-onboarding-runway and capacity-observability-and-recovery playbooks.

Revision history
----------------
- 2026-02-14: Created by Claire Nguyen (initial draft).
- 2026-06-30: Added quarantine automation thresholds and CLI playbook (review by Miguel Reyes).
- 2026-10-12: Formalized simulation acceptance criteria and changed default quarantine duration to 5m.

[Add Usage Insights freshness/quality dashboard + alerts (lag + reconciliation drift)]
description:
Motivation: Usage Insights is going into beta with interactive console queries backed by hourly/day partitions and reconciliation checks against billing. We need a standard dashboard + alert bundle in observability-pack so SRE/on-call can quickly answer: (1) is data fresh, (2) are we dropping/late-ingesting events by route/model, (3) are we drifting vs billing totals beyond tolerance, and (4) are query endpoints timing out for common ranges.

This PR adds a Grafana dashboard and alert rule templates for freshness lag, late event rate, reconciliation drift, and query p95 latency. The dashboard is designed to be imported into customer-facing/internal stacks with minimal per-cluster edits (templated variables for env/region/deployment_mode/workspace_id).

What’s included: 1) Dashboard: “Usage Insights — Data Freshness & Quality” (Grafana JSON) Panels: Aggregation lag (p50/p95) by dataset (route_model_hourly, route_model_daily) and by region; Ingestion late-event ratio (late_events / total_events) by region + streaming endpoint flag; Missing route_tag rate (events where route_template = "unknown" or null); Reconciliation drift (%) between insights totals and billing hook totals, per workspace and overall; Top offenders table: workspaces with highest drift and highest lag; Query API p95 latency + error rate (v1/usage-insights/* endpoints) with annotations for deploys.

2) Alerts (PrometheusRule templates): - UsageInsightsAggregationLagHigh: fires when p95 aggregation lag > 20m for 15m (warn) and > 60m for 10m (page). - UsageInsightsLateEventRatioHigh: fires when late_event_ratio > 2% for 30m (warn), with a separate page threshold at 5% for 15m. - UsageInsightsRouteTagMissing: fires when missing_route_tag_rate > 1% for 30m (warn) and > 3% for 15m (page). - UsageInsightsReconciliationDriftHigh: fires when abs(drift_pct) > 0.5% for 2h (warn) and > 1.0% for 1h (page), excluding small totals (< $50/day) to reduce noise. - UsageInsightsQueryP95Degraded: fires when p95 > 2500ms for 15m (warn) and > 5000ms for 10m (page), scoped to the insights query service.

3) Runbook stub: Adds a runbook page with investigation steps and links to relevant services/datasets (warehouse partitions, ingestion pipeline, billing hook job).

Metric assumptions (coordinated with Telemetry/Analytics): This PR uses the metric names already in-flight on redwood (see ENG-3824/ENG-3817): usage_insights_aggregation_lag_seconds{dataset,region,deployment_mode}; usage_insights_late_event_ratio{region,streaming}; usage_insights_missing_route_tag_rate{region}; usage_insights_reconciliation_drift_pct{workspace_id}; usage_insights_query_request_duration_ms_bucket{route,status}; usage_insights_query_errors_total{route,status}. If any naming changes land before beta, we can follow up with a patch release of observability-pack.

Noise/guardrails: The drift alert includes a minimum spend floor and a 2h lookback to avoid paging on transient rounding/timing skew (e.g., hourly partitions catching up). The lag alert pages only on sustained lag > 60m.

Testing/validation: Imported dashboard into staging Grafana; validated queries on canary metrics in us-east-1 and eu-west-1. Used replayed lag/drift fixtures from staging to verify alert routing and labels.

Rollout notes: This is safe to ship ahead of beta. SREs should import the dashboard to the internal "Console & Tooling" folder and ensure Alertmanager routes page severity=page to #eng-sre, and warn severity=warn to #eng-platform.

Screenshots: (not included in PR; Grafana JSON is the source of truth).

[Usage Insights: reconciliation suite vs billing totals + CI drift gate]
Title: Usage Insights: reconciliation suite vs billing totals + CI drift gate

Summary
We’ve had a few early beta reports that “console totals don’t match invoice” (see SUP-24811) and a recurring internal concern that aggregation lag + rounding will cause subtle drift. This PR adds a reconciliation suite that compares Usage Insights rollups (route/model aggregates) against billing totals (metering hooks → invoice preview) within a defined tolerance, and wires it into CI + a nightly scheduled run with alert hooks.

Key goals
- Catch drift early (instrumentation regressions, bucketing/alias issues, timezone boundary mistakes, rounding deltas).
- Define and document a tolerance policy that is strict enough to catch real issues but robust to expected effects (late events, FX rounding, minimum billable units).
- Provide a runbook-friendly output: workspace/project, day/hour, route/model slices that contribute most to drift.

What’s included
1) Reconciliation job + report format
- New job: services/telemetry/reconciliation/usage_insights_vs_billing
- Compares totals for a given workspace_id + time range across:
  - usage_insights.route_model_agg (the dataset powering console breakdown tables)
  - billing.usage_totals (billing hook rollups used for invoice preview)
- Outputs both:
  - a single “gate” metric per workspace/time window (pass/fail)
  - a ranked list of top contributing slices (route/model/region/deployment_mode where present)

2) Tolerance policy (documented + implemented)
We gate on both absolute and relative drift, and we avoid evaluating windows likely to be incomplete.
- Windows evaluated:
  - Hourly buckets for last 24 hours (excluding most recent 2 hours)
  - Daily buckets for last 7 days (excluding current day)
- Late-event buffer:
  - Ignore the most recent 2 hours entirely to avoid normal ingestion lag.
  - For daily checks, only evaluate days older than 26 hours.
- Tolerance thresholds:
  - Absolute drift allowed: max($2.00, 2000 tokens worth of cost at the workspace’s effective blended rate) per evaluated window
  - Relative drift allowed: <= 0.50% per evaluated window
  - Gate fails if BOTH absolute and relative drift exceed thresholds (prevents false positives on small totals)
- Currency handling:
  - Compare in USD using billing’s canonical conversion for the period.
  - Usage insights cost uses the same price book snapshot key as billing (price_book_version) to avoid rate drift.
- Rounding:
  - Compare on unrounded micros (int64) where available; rounding only applied in the human report.

Tolerance helper (illustrative snippet):

function isDriftAcceptable({ expectedMicros, actualMicros }) {
  const driftMicros = Math.abs(actualMicros - expectedMicros);
  const rel = expectedMicros === 0 ? (actualMicros === 0 ? 0 : 1) : driftMicros / expectedMicros;
  const absOk = driftMicros <= ABS_TOLERANCE_MICROS;
  const relOk = rel <= 0.005;
  return absOk || relOk; // fail only if BOTH are violated
}

3) CI + scheduled runs
- Adds a Buildkite step (non-blocking in PRs, blocking in main nightly):
  - PR builds: runs reconciliation unit tests + one small integration fixture
  - Nightly: runs full reconciliation across allowlisted beta workspaces with paging
- New pipeline: .buildkite/pipelines/usage-insights-reconciliation.yml
- Artifacts:
  - Uploads a CSV and JSON summary for each run
  - Posts a summary comment to #eng-platform on failures with a link to artifacts

4) Alert hooks + runbook pointers
- On gate failure, the nightly job:
  - Emits metric: usage_insights.reconciliation.drift_exceeded{workspace_id, window_type}
  - Logs structured payload with top slices and suspected causes
  - Posts to Slack: #usage-insights-alerts
  - Creates a lightweight incident event (non-page) unless drift persists 2 consecutive runs, then page the on-call (aligns with SRE feedback from earlier threads)

5) Guardrails to avoid noisy failures
- Workspace allowlist for beta reconciliation (config in services/telemetry/reconciliation/config/beta_allowlist.yml)
- Suppression for known exceptions:
  - If billing is missing a price_book_version for the period (rare), mark “skipped” not “failed”
  - If insights freshness lag > threshold (uses existing freshness metadata), mark “skipped”

Why this approach
- We compare at the same conceptual level as customers: “what billing says you owe” vs “what console says you spent”.
- We still include drill-down slices to make debugging actionable (route/model/region).
- Late-event handling is explicit and conservative; we don’t want to treat expected lag as correctness drift.

Files / areas changed (high level)
- services/telemetry/reconciliation/usage_insights_vs_billing/*
- services/telemetry/reconciliation/lib/tolerance.ts
- services/telemetry/reconciliation/lib/report.ts
- services/telemetry/reconciliation/config/beta_allowlist.yml
- .buildkite/pipelines/usage-insights-reconciliation.yml
- docs/internal/runbooks/usage-insights-reconciliation.md
- libs/billing/pricebook/resolve_pricebook_version.ts (small helper to align snapshots)

Test plan
- Unit tests:
  - tolerance calculations (edge cases: 0 totals, tiny totals, large totals)
  - rounding behavior (micros vs displayed dollars)
  - skip logic (freshness lag, missing pricebook)
- Integration tests:
  - fixture dataset with:
    - retries + fallbacks
    - model alias → version bucketing
    - streaming endpoints
  - verifies:
    - aggregation totals match billing totals within tolerance
    - top-slices ranking is stable/deterministic
- Manual:
  - Ran job for HelioChat staging workspace on 2026-02-16 (7d window) and validated output against invoice preview totals.

Rollout notes
- Nightly reconciliation initially scoped to beta allowlist only.
- If the nightly job is noisy, we can widen the late-event buffer or adjust absolute tolerance; prefer changing absolute tolerance first.
- No change to customer-visible console behavior.

Links
- Linear: ENG-3817
- Related PRs: pr-23114 (aggregation job), pr-23135 (query API)
- Support: SUP-24811

Reviewer notes / questions to focus on
- Tolerance policy: are we comfortable gating on “abs OR rel” instead of “abs AND rel”? (current implementation is intentionally forgiving on small totals)
- Skip windows: is 2 hours sufficient buffer for late events in all regions?
- Alerting: does the ‘2 consecutive runs before paging’ rule match SRE expectations?

body:
## Summary
This PR wires meter drift + data freshness alerts to the relevant Confluence runbooks and adds contextual links (Grafana panels + Snowflake queries) directly into alert annotations so on-call can self-serve triage without hunting through docs.

This is intentionally small/low-risk: no threshold changes and no alert routing changes. It only enriches annotations.

## Context
We’ve seen drift alerts trigger during month-end preview / late-arriving usage event windows. The alert itself tells you *what* drifted, but not *where to go next* (dashboard, query, or reconciliation playbook), which slows down response and increases Finance churn.

Related:
- ENG-4421 (meter drift alerts)
- PM-1872 (metering change control / runbook expectations)

## What changed
- Added `runbook_url` annotation to metering drift and freshness alerts.
- Added `dashboard_url` annotation pointing to the metering sanity Grafana dashboard pre-filtered to the alert labels (env/region/model/account when present).
- Added `triage_query` / `triage_query_url` annotations for the common drilldown query (by day/account/model/region) used to validate whether drift is due to duplicates, late events, or ledger lag.
- Added a small helper for URL construction to avoid hardcoding environment-specific Grafana base URLs.
- Added a short doc block in the alert rules file describing required labels and what to do if a Confluence page moves.

## Runbooks linked
- Meter drift triage runbook (on-call): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ENG/Meter+Drift+Alert+Triage
- Metering-to-invoice reconciliation playbook (Finance/RevRec): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/FIN/Metering-to-Invoice+Reconciliation+Playbook
- Meter sanity dashboard spec (owners, expected panels): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ENG/Meter+Sanity+Dashboard+Spec

Note: Confluence permissions apply; the runbook page includes a public-to-Engineering summary section and links out to restricted Finance-only content where required.

## Example (before/after)
Before:
- Alert: `meter_drift_vs_ledger` fired
- Message: “drift > 1% for account X in us-east-1”
- Next steps were tribal knowledge

After:
- Alert includes:
  - `Runbook`: Meter Drift Alert Triage
  - `Dashboard`: Metering Sanity → Drift panel (pre-filtered)
  - `Query`: Snowflake drilldown query (copy/paste + optional Snowsight link)

## Implementation notes
- Alert rule changes are under `observability/alerts/metering/*.yaml`.
- URL bases are read from existing `GRAFANA_BASE_URL` and `CONFLUENCE_BASE_URL` config (falls back to prod defaults in non-prod).
- The Snowflake query is provided as a multi-line annotation and also as a Snowsight link template. The query itself is parameterized using alert labels where present; if labels are missing we fall back to a generic query with TODO placeholders.
- No alert name changes to preserve paging history and silence matching.

## Testing
- Verified rule file parses with `promtool check rules`.
- Verified Alertmanager renders annotations correctly (local dev AM + staging ruleset).
- Clicked through generated Grafana links from a staging firing alert to confirm filters populate correctly.

## Rollout
- Merge to main, then ruleset deploy via `observability-pack` sync job (next 30-min window).
- No shadow-billing dependencies.

## Screenshots
(Internal) Added to PR comments: Alertmanager UI showing new annotations + Grafana deep link.

## Checklist
- [x] No paging behavior changes
- [x] Links work in staging
- [x] Runbook reviewed by Telemetry + Finance data owners

Co-authored-by: Mei Lin <mei.lin@redwoodinference.com>

review_conversation:

Aisha Bello (author): Good call. Updated the query to reference the public reconciliation export view (billing_recon_export_v1) rather than the raw ledger tables, and added a note in the runbook for requesting access if deeper comparison is needed.
Logan Wright (review): Please avoid hardcoding the Confluence base URL. We’ve had to move pages / change domains before. Also, can we keep the runbook URL in one place so other alert rules can reuse it?
Aisha Bello (author): Addressed. Added CONFLUENCE_BASE_URL + a central constants file for metering runbook links. Alert rules now reference the shared helper. Also added a short maintenance section in README on updating links when pages move.
Caleb Johnson (review): The Grafana link template is using account_id label; some alerts only have account_slug. Can we support both? Also, ensure urlencoding.
Aisha Bello (author): Updated link builder to prefer account_id when present, else account_slug. Added urlencoding for all label values and a unit test for special characters.
Connor O'Brien (review): Any chance this changes alert fingerprints and breaks existing silences?
Aisha Bello (author): Annotations do not affect fingerprinting; only labels do. Confirmed we did not add/modify labels. Existing silences should continue to match.

Aisha Bello (author): Added a minimal section to the runbook page (linked) noting freeze window expectations and pointing to the month-end close checklist. Kept PR code changes scoped to annotations only.
Mei Lin (approval): Approved once the query references the recon export view and the runbook clarifies access boundaries.
Logan Wright (approval): LGTM.
Caleb Johnson (approval): LGTM.
Connor O'Brien (approval): Approved.
Allison Grant (approval): Approved.

[Usage Insights: add route+model cost aggregation job + hourly schema (late events + partitions)]
body:
## Summary
Implements the first-pass aggregation job + warehouse schema for “In-console usage insights” breakdowns keyed by workspace/project/env + route_template + model_family/model_version + region/deployment_mode, bucketed hourly.

This PR creates:
- A new hourly aggregate table for route+model usage/cost drivers (tokens in/out, cache hits/misses, retries, fallbacks, request counts, latency rollups)
- An incremental aggregation job with partitioning & clustering tuned for interactive console queries
- Late-event handling (watermark + rolling recompute window) to reduce drift vs billing
- Initial correctness checks comparing aggregated totals to billing/metering rollups

Primary goal: power ENG-3814 (query endpoints) and keep totals reconcilable with billing within a small tolerance.

## Details
### New dataset/table
Table: `telemetry_analytics.usage_insights_route_model_hourly`

Key dimensions (columns):
- `bucket_start_ts` (UTC, hour)
- `workspace_id`, `project_id`, `environment`
- `route_template` (normalized path template, e.g. `/v1/chat/completions` or `/v1/files/{file_id}`)
- `route_group` (coarser grouping for guardrails; e.g. `openai_compat`)
- `model_family`, `model_version` (stable bucketing; alias resolution happens upstream)
- `deployment_mode` (`hosted|dedicated|private`)
- `region` (cloud region or `onprem`)

Measures:
- `request_count`
- `tokens_in`, `tokens_out`
- `cache_hit_tokens`, `cache_miss_tokens`
- `retry_request_count` (count of retried attempts, excluding first attempt)
- `fallback_request_count` (requests served by a different model than requested)
- `streaming_request_count` (for later “streaming overhead” attribution)
- `latency_ms_sum`, `latency_ms_p95_approx` (t-digest sketch)
- `compute_cost_microusd` (sum of attribution cost; matches billing hooks source)

Partitioning/clustering:
- Partition: `DATE(bucket_start_ts)`
- Cluster: `workspace_id, project_id, route_template, model_family, model_version`

Rationale: console queries typically filter by workspace/project + time range and then group by route/model. Clustering improves scan costs and p95 for “top routes/models” tables.

### Aggregation job
Job: `UsageInsightsRouteModelHourlyAggregator`

- Runs every 15 minutes
- Processes a rolling window of the last 48 hours to capture late events and backfilled metering corrections
- Uses a watermark based on `event_ingested_at` with a default late allowance of 6 hours
- Writes via MERGE/UPSERT keyed on all dimensions + `bucket_start_ts`

Pseudo-logic (simplified):
`SELECT … FROM metering_events WHERE event_time >= now()-48h GROUP BY bucket_start_ts, dims` then `MERGE INTO usage_insights_route_model_hourly`.

### Late events + correctness
Late-event strategy is intentionally conservative for beta:
- Recompute 48h each run to avoid “stuck wrong totals” in the presence of late arrivals/retries
- Emit lag metrics (`usage_insights_agg_lag_seconds`, `usage_insights_late_event_ratio`) for dashboards

Correctness tests (initial):
- For a fixed fixture workspace/time window, compare `SUM(compute_cost_microusd)` in the new hourly table to the existing billing rollup query
- Tolerance: 0.5% or 50,000 microusd (whichever is higher)
- Log detailed breakdown on mismatch (top 10 contributing route/model rows)

NOTE: There is a known edge case where streaming token accounting can shift across hour boundaries when events are emitted late; the recompute window should cover it, but we may still see small intra-day fluctuations until ENG-3822 (route tags on streaming) is fully rolled out.

## Why
Customers and internal teams need route+model cost breakdowns with consistent totals vs billing. This is the foundational dataset that all subsequent APIs/console pages will query.

## Screenshots
N/A (backend job + dataset only)

## Testing
- Unit tests for bucketing, aggregation math, and merge keying
- Warehouse integration test against a small seeded dataset
- Correctness test comparing to billing rollup query

## Rollout / Ops
- Job is deployed but consumer paths are not enabled yet.
- Metrics emitted:
  - `usage_insights_agg_job_duration_ms`
  - `usage_insights_agg_rows_written`
  - `usage_insights_agg_lag_seconds`
  - `usage_insights_agg_reconcile_diff_ratio`
- Alert wiring will be added in a follow-up PR in the observability pack.

## Follow-ups
- ENG-3813: route normalization library shared with gateway (this PR assumes normalized `route_template` exists on metering events)
- ENG-3814: query API endpoints consuming this dataset
- ENG-3817: expand reconciliation coverage + CI gating

Closes: ENG-3812
Refs: SUP-24811 (billing mismatch reports; correctness guardrails)

## Checklist
- [x] Schema reviewed with Telemetry & Analytics
- [x] Partition/clustering reviewed for expected query patterns
- [x] Late-event handling documented in code comments
- [x] Added initial reconciliation tests
- [x] Added metrics for freshness/lag


conversation:
Logan Wright (review): Partitioning/clustering looks right. Can we avoid scanning 48h every 15m? That’s going to be expensive at scale.

Mei Lin (author): Agreed it’s not ideal long-term. For beta I’d prefer correctness > cost. Added a TODO + metrics so we can tighten window once late arrival distribution is measured. Also added a guardrail: if recompute window > 72h, job refuses to run.

Nadia Rahman (review): Please clarify retry/fallback definitions in code comments. Specifically: is a retry counted per attempt or per request? And are fallbacks counted when model differs from requested alias or resolved family?

Mei Lin (author): Updated comments + renamed `retry_count` to `retry_request_count` to make intent clear: counts extra attempts (attempt_index > 0). Fallback is when `served_model_family/version` != `requested_model_family/version` after alias resolution.

Cole Summers (review): Reconciliation tolerance seems loose. Can we log the top contributing rows on mismatch? This will come up in SUP-24811-type tickets.

Mei Lin (author): Added mismatch logging (top 10 rows by absolute cost delta) and included the query fingerprint + window in the failure output.

Allison Grant (review): Please emit aggregation lag as a gauge and include tags for dataset + environment. Also add a metric for late event ratio if possible.

Mei Lin (author): Done: `usage_insights_agg_lag_seconds{dataset="route_model_hourly"}` and `usage_insights_late_event_ratio{dataset=...}`.

Thomas Baird (review): The MERGE key includes `route_group` and `route_template`. If route_group is derived from route_template, keep only one in the key to reduce churn.

Mei Lin (author): route_group is derived but we want to preserve it for coarse grouping even if normalization changes. Kept it as a non-key attribute (updated merge statement accordingly) so we don’t create duplicate rows.

Approvals:
- Logan Wright: Approved
- Nadia Rahman: Approved
- Cole Summers: Approved
- Allison Grant: Approved

[Usage insights: add data freshness metadata + console banner for partial/lagging data]
description:
Context: during beta testing we’ve had multiple instances where customers interpreted route/model breakdown swings as “real spend changes” when the underlying issue was ingestion lag / late events / partial rollups for a region. This PR adds explicit freshness metadata to the Usage Insights API and renders a banner + inline status on the console breakdown pages when results may be incomplete. The goal is to make data trust issues obvious, reduce support load, and give users an action (narrow time range / wait for backfill) rather than silently showing partial totals.

What this PR does:
- API: extends v1 usage-insights responses to include `data_freshness` metadata (latest_complete_bucket_end, observed_lag_seconds, completeness, and a human-readable status reason). This metadata is computed per query based on the requested time range and the dataset watermark.
- Console: shows a dismissible banner at the top of Usage → Cost Insights pages when `completeness != complete` or when lag exceeds threshold; adds a smaller “Data freshness” pill next to the time range selector for non-blocking warnings.
- UX details: banner copy is intentionally specific (“Data through 14:00 UTC; newer data still processing”) and links to the help article section on freshness/late events.
- Telemetry: emits a `console.usage_insights.freshness_banner_shown` event with the reason code so we can measure how often users hit lag/partial states.

Thresholds / semantics:
- `completeness` is `complete` if requested_end <= latest_complete_bucket_end.
- `completeness` is `partial` if requested_end > latest_complete_bucket_end.
- `completeness` is `unknown` if the watermark lookup fails (we default to no banner, but show a small pill tooltip indicating we couldn’t confirm freshness).
- Banner is shown for `partial` always; for `complete` we show only if observed_lag_seconds > 900 (15m) to catch edge cases where buckets are “complete” but significantly delayed.

API example (abridged):
- `data_freshness.completeness`: complete | partial | unknown
- `data_freshness.latest_complete_bucket_end`: RFC3339 timestamp
- `data_freshness.observed_lag_seconds`: integer
- `data_freshness.reason`: enum (LATE_EVENTS, AGGREGATION_LAG, WATERMARK_UNAVAILABLE)

Notes:
- This is backwards compatible for existing clients; the new field is additive.
- The freshness metadata is explicitly excluded from response cache keys (it’s computed post-query from the same watermark source), but the watermark lookup itself is cached for 30s in the query service to avoid thundering herds.

Testing:
- Unit tests for freshness computation across time ranges + watermark states.
- Frontend tests for banner rendering/copy and dismissal persistence.
- Manual: verified in staging by forcing a low watermark and querying “Last 24h”.

Rollout:
- Guarded behind existing usage-insights beta flag; banner can be disabled via `console_usage_insights_freshness_banner` kill switch if copy/threshold needs rapid iteration.

Refs:
- Linear: ENG-3824
- Related: PR #23135 (query API v1), PR #23114 (aggregation dataset)
- Support signal: SUP-24863 (timeouts/long ranges often correlating with partial data); this should reduce confusion when users narrow ranges.

Checklist:
- [x] Add API contract + changelog entry for additive field
- [x] Console banner + pill states (partial/lag/unknown)
- [x] Events + dashboards hook (follow-up: add alert if watermark unavailable > 5m)
- [x] Copy reviewed by Design + DevEx (lightweight) and aligned with help center wording


review_conversation:
Chloe Martin (requested changes): Can we make sure the watermark lookup failure doesn’t flip the whole request to 500? I’d prefer the query still succeeds and freshness is `unknown`.
Felix Schneider (author): Yep — updated to catch watermark errors and set `completeness=unknown` + `reason=WATERMARK_UNAVAILABLE`. Query response remains 200 and we don’t show the big banner by default (only pill tooltip). Added test coverage.
Allison Grant: The reason codes look good, but we should be careful about calling it “late events” vs “aggregation lag”. Can we ensure `LATE_EVENTS` is only used when the late-event counter is non-zero for the window?
Felix Schneider (author): Good call. I split it: if `late_event_rate > 0.5%` for the trailing hour, reason is `LATE_EVENTS`; otherwise `AGGREGATION_LAG`. If we can’t fetch the metric, we default to `AGGREGATION_LAG` to avoid over-claiming. Tests updated.
Tessa Morgan (requested changes): Banner copy feels too generic. Can we include a concrete “Data through <time>” and avoid “may be incomplete” if it definitely is incomplete?
Felix Schneider (author): Updated copy to: “Showing partial data. Complete data through {timestamp} (UTC). Newer usage is still processing.” and only uses “may” for `unknown` (pill tooltip).
Kaitlyn Nguyen: RBAC question — are we leaking anything about other projects/workspaces via watermark? This should be scoped to workspace/project filter.
Felix Schneider (author): Watermark query is computed on the same dataset partition keys as the request (workspace_id + project_id when provided). No cross-scope access. Added an auth regression test to ensure watermark lookup uses the caller’s scoped filter set.
Dylan Brooks: Looks solid. One perf nit: avoid an extra warehouse roundtrip for watermark when the request is cached.
Felix Schneider (author): Implemented 30s in-process cache for watermark keyed by (workspace, project, dataset, bucket). Also ensured we compute freshness after retrieving cached breakdown results so we don’t invalidate existing caches.
Allison Grant (approval): Approved after changes. Please make sure we track watermark-unavailable rate post-merge.
Dylan Brooks (approval): Approved.

[2167777777]
maria-support: Hey team — escalation from a Private customer: collector failed to upload a debug bundle. Customer sees API 403 on the final multipart complete and the collector shows KMS "AccessDenied" followed by connection resets. Request ID: req-2026-11-07-9a12b3c4. Need repro steps and a safe debug-bundle path (redacted) so we can hand off to infra.

support-bot: Thanks @maria-support — ticket created #SUP-4219 and retention policy set to 30d. :white_check_mark:

ajay-eng: Can you paste the small collector log snippet around the failure? Also which upload path are they using (presign -> relay -> s3)?

maria-support: Log excerpt below (sanitized):
```
2026-11-07T10:14:02Z collector[pid=3124] INFO starting debug bundle generation
2026-11-07T10:14:12Z collector[pid=3124] WARN multipart upload part failed status=403 request_id=req-2026-11-07-9a12b3c4
2026-11-07T10:14:12Z collector[pid=3124] ERROR kms:Decrypt AccessDenied key=alias/private-collector-key user=collector-role
2026-11-07T10:14:12Z collector[pid=3124] ERROR aborting multipart upload; rolling back parts
```

erin-sre: Two suspects: (1) KMS policy denies Decrypt from the collector role — confirm key policy + IAM. (2) TLS/SNI mismatch between collector -> relay (our presign broker) that returns 403 for unknown host header. Repro tip: use curl with --resolve to force SNI and check headers. Example:
```
curl -v --cert /path/to/client.crt --key /path/to/client.key -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted-token>" --resolve "relay.private.example.com:443:10.10.0.5" "https://relay.private.example.com/v1/uploads/presign?request_id=req-2026-11-07-9a12b3c4"
```

ajay-eng: Good. Also capture TLS handshake via openssl for the same endpoint:
```
openssl s_client -connect 10.10.0.5:443 -servername relay.private.example.com -showcerts
```
This will show if the cert presented doesn't match the expected CN/SAN.

maria-support: Customer is worried about PII — how do we generate the debug bundle with automatic redaction? I don't want to send emails or IPs out.

ajay-eng: Use the collector tool with a redact config. Example command to produce a redacted bundle locally:
```
collector debug-bundle create --out /tmp/dbundle.tar.gz --redact '{"redact_rules": [{"json_path": "$.user.email", "replacement": "<redacted_email>"}, {"json_path": "$.client_ip", "replacement": "<redacted_ip>"}, {"pattern": "(?i)Authorization: .*", "replacement": "Authorization: <REDACTED>"}]}' --include-logs --time-window "2026-11-07T09:50:00Z/2026-11-07T10:20:00Z"
```
Note: pass the JSON as a single string or via --redact-file to avoid shell escaping pain.

maria-support: Nice. If presign still fails, can we switch to an scp fallback over the customer's bastion?

erin-sre: Yes — use scp with a ProxyCommand and explicit IdentityFile. Example:
```
scp -o "ProxyCommand=ssh -W %h:%p -i ~/.ssh/bastion_id_rsa bastion-user@bastion.customer.example" /tmp/dbundle.tar.gz collector@10.10.0.5:/var/tmp/
```
That avoids presign/presigned PUTs entirely and preserves the redacted bundle. Make sure the customer has allowed the collector user and the target path.

ops-bot: Reminder: presigned PUTs expire in 15m by default. If multiple attempts are needed, increase expiry to 1h temporarily (set via presign_ttl in the upload profile).

ajay-eng: If we still need a curl reproduction of the failing multipart complete step, this is the minimal sequence: 1) create multipart -> get uploadId, 2) upload parts with the presigned URLs, 3) call complete-multipart with the assembled parts XML. Example complete call:
```
curl -v -X POST "https://relay.private.example.com/v1/uploads/complete?uploadId=abc123&request_id=req-2026-11-07-9a12b3c4" -H "Content-Type: application/xml" --data-binary @parts.xml --resolve "relay.private.example.com:443:10.10.0.5" --cert client.crt --key client.key
```
Include the verbose (-v) output and the full HTTP response headers in the support ticket.

maria-support: I'll ask the customer to run the curl + openssl checks and to try the scp fallback if presign stays flaky. I'll also attach the redacted bundle using scp if they approve.

erin-sre: If they can reproduce the 403 but openssl shows the cert matches, escalate to infra with the request ID + traffic dump. Likely we need to check the relay broker's host-header routing rules.

maria-support: Thanks all — I'll update ticket #SUP-4219 with the steps and next actions. Will ping again if they hand us the bundle. :v:

[support]
alex: Escalation from a Private customer — their collector is getting 403 on our presign PUTs right after a scheduled token rotation. Need a reproducible artifact and upload fallback. Request IDs from their pod logs below.

maria: Paste the collector version, k8s node, and the exact error lines (full stdout/stderr) plus the UTC time range.

alex: Collector: 1.12.4 (static build)
K8s: EKS, node ip=10.10.4.22, private-control-plane=true
Time range: 2026-03-15T14:02:10Z -> 2026-03-15T14:07:00Z
Request IDs: collector_req=cr-20260315-9f2a, s3 x-amz-request-id=G4X6H7K9
Log excerpt: 
```
ERROR: upload failed: presign PUT -> status=403, obj=acme-debug-20260315.tar.gz, err=AccessDenied
uploader: signed-url write error (403) x-amz-request-id=G4X6H7K9 auth=rotated-token
```

josh: @on-call-sre :thinking: Likely causes: presign signer issued URL with expired/old creds, IAM VPC endpoint policy deny, or clock skew. Ask customer to run a curl PUT repro with --trace to capture TLS/write behavior.

alex: Provided curl to customer, they ran it and got HTTP/1.1 403. Their trace shows the server responded 403 immediately on the PUT. Command we gave them to run: 
```
curl -v -X PUT "<PRESIGN_URL>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/gzip" \
  --data-binary @acme-debugbundle.tar.gz \
  --trace-ascii curl_trace.txt
```
They attached curl_trace.txt showing 403 at the PUT step.

maria: Collect these artifacts before we ask infra to touch policies:
- full collector stdout/stderr for the window (kubectl logs --since-time)
- journalctl -u redwood-collector -n 200 on node if systemd
- control-plane presign log for the presign request id (controlplane request_id)
- curl --trace-ascii output from customer
- exact presign URL (REDACT query except last 8 chars)
- collector config and k8s manifest (redact secrets)

kai: To make a local match of what they upload, run our collector collect command that produces the same tarball layout and manifest we expect: 
```
/opt/redwood/collector collect --mode debug \
  --output /tmp/acme-repro-20260315.tar.gz \
  --include-logs "/var/log/redwood/*.log" \
  --manifest /tmp/manifest.json \
  --redact-regex '(?i)(?:password|secret|token|ssn|acct|email)' \
  --strip-paths '/home/*/.aws'
```
Make sure --redact-regex is exact to avoid leaking PII. The manifest contains file checksums; include it in uploads.

alex: Customer notes: they have custom account IDs and US SSN-ish patterns. Suggested additional redact: `--redact-regex '(?:\\b\\d{3}-\\d{2}-\\d{4}\\b|\\b\\d{4}-\\d{4}-\\d{4}-\\d{4}\\b)'` — they will add and re-run.

support-bot: ACTION ITEMS: gather collector logs, presign control-plane logs, curl trace, presign URL (redacted), reproduce bundle, sha256 of bundle. Mark P1 if upload attempts fail >30m.

maria: Fallback upload strategy if presign PUT keeps returning 403: 
1) Regenerate presign from control plane with TTL 60s and attempt PUT from same node as collector. Capture new controlplane request_id.
2) If still 403, check CloudTrail for Deny events against the S3 bucket (vpce/iam deny). Ask infra to hold changes if Deny seen.
3) Emergency fallback: SCP the bundle to our bastion (bundle@bastion.redwood.internal:/incoming) and we pull it from there. Provide scp instructions to customer and ensure we rotate the bastion upload key afterwards.

josh: Also ask customer to POST to our presign endpoint to confirm signer is returning a usable URL and that controlplane accepts their token. Example reproducer: 
```
curl -v -X POST "https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/presign" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"object":"acme-debug-20260315.tar.gz","ttl":60}'
```
Record the JSON response and server-side request_id.

kai: Support handoff checklist to include in ticket: 
- [ ] collector version + pod spec + node id
- [ ] all request IDs (collector, controlplane, s3)
- [ ] exact UTC time window
- [ ] curl --trace-ascii output and sha256 of uploaded file (if any)
- [ ] redacted presign URL (show last 8 chars only)
- [ ] produced debug bundle + manifest + sha256
- [ ] any recent IAM/VPC endpoint policy changes
- [ ] token rotation timestamps (was rotation within 5m of failures?)

alex: Customer attempted uploading to a proxy which also returned 403. They will try scp to our bastion later tonight local time (expected 02:30 local / 09:30 UTC) and will also run collector collect command and upload the tarball. I'll post traces here when they run the PUT attempt.

maria: When we receive the bundle on our side, run these validations: 
1) sha256sum bundle -> compare to manifest
2) tar -tzf bundle | head -n 30 to sanity-check presence of manifest and logs
3) run debug-unpack tool: 
```
debug-unpack --input acme-debug-20260315.tar.gz --validate --redaction-check
```
If any file fails redaction checks, return a clear list of filenames and patterns to the customer.

on-call-sre: If CloudTrail shows Deny events for a vpce or role, ping eng-infra immediately — those denys usually indicate endpoint policy mismatch or KMS/role binding problem. Also look at S3 Block Public Access flags; presign PUTs can fail in unusual configurations.

josh: I'll own the repro/pull from bastion once the bundle lands. ETA ~2 hours after upload. @maria please keep the ticket comments updated with each artifact.

alex: Customer confirmed scp attempt to bastion scheduled at 09:30 UTC. Will paste curl_trace and controlplane request_id after they attempt presign again.

support-bot: THREAD STATUS: keep open until we have successful bundle validation. If upload fails for >30m escalate to infra. :warning:

[support]
