[IdP email claim normalization mismatch causing RBAC 403s in AtlasFin private deployment]
description:
Issue summary: After onboarding AtlasFin's private deployment to Redwood Private (VPC) and enabling OIDC SSO, users intermittently received 403 Forbidden when calling the Redwood API despite successful login through the IdP. Impact: ~12 users across two teams could not access model endpoints. Error observed in production, intermittent depending on which IdP assertion was returned. Environment: Private control plane (v1.11.0), identity-proxy v1.12.0 (private deployment bundle), AtlasFin IdP: Okta (custom claim mapping), region us-east-1. Observed behavior: Some authenticated requests fail RBAC checks because the subject used for role binding lookup differs from the subject in user directory/role mappings. Expected behavior: Identity claims used to match RBAC bindings should be normalized consistently so that authenticated users inherit their expected roles. Root cause hypothesis: A mismatch between IdP-provided email claim casing/alternate-email claim and existing RBAC bindings that contain case-sensitive email strings. Recent identity-proxy change (2026-02 release) introduced an email normalization step that lowercases and strips plus-addressing, but AtlasFin's SCIM-provisioned role bindings were created earlier and contain original-cased primaryEmail entries.

steps_to_reproduce:
1) AtlasFin user authenticates via Okta (OIDC) using standard browser SSO flow.
2) Okta returns ID token with claims: email: "alice.senior@atlasfin.com", alternate_email: "Alice.Senior@atlasfin.com" and preferred_username: "asenior".
3) identity-proxy processes the token and applies email normalization (lowercase + strip +tag).
4) Redwood authorization layer looks up role bindings using the normalized email (alice.senior@atlasfin.com) but AtlasFin role bindings were provisioned with SCIM and store the original-cased PrimaryEmail (Alice.Senior@atlasfin.com).
5) Authorization lookup fails and request returns 403 despite successful authentication.

logs:
2026-03-10T09:12:04Z identity-proxy INFO received id_token for sub=okta|00u123...
2026-03-10T09:12:04Z identity-proxy DEBUG incoming_claims: {"email":"alice.senior@atlasfin.com", "alternate_email":"Alice.Senior@atlasfin.com"}
2026-03-10T09:12:04Z identity-proxy INFO normalized_email=alice.senior@atlasfin.com
2026-03-10T09:12:04Z auth-service WARN rbac_lookup no binding found for principal=alice.senior@atlasfin.com
2026-03-10T09:12:04Z api-gateway ERROR request_id=abc123 status=403 message=RBAC: no principal binding

investigation_notes:
03/10 11:00 - Support (Aisha): Confirmed failing user tokens and collected sample IdTokens and SCIM record for the user.
03/10 12:10 - Eng (Diego): Reproduced locally by replaying token; observed that role lookup key depends on identity-proxy normalized email when preferred_username absent.
03/10 14:30 - SRE: Checked private control plane release notes and found email normalization behavior changed in identity-proxy v1.12.0 (commit 7f8b2c).
03/10 16:00 - Hypothesis: Older SCIM-upserted role bindings use the original-cased PrimaryEmail; normalization lowercases and removes plus-tags, causing a mismatch. The presence of alternate_email claim increases the mismatch window because SCIM used 'PrimaryEmail' while IdP issued 'email' in a different case.
03/11 09:00 - Reproduction: Updated local rbac store to include both 'Alice.Senior@atlasfin.com' and 'alice.senior@atlasfin.com' and confirmed access is restored. This indicates the lookup key mismatch is the problem.
03/11 10:20 - Mitigation plan: 1) Patch identity-proxy to include canonicalization that preserves case when SCIM-provisioned role bindings are detected, 2) provide a migration tool to normalize the customer's role bindings in-place, 3) short-term workaround to add duplicate normalized entries via support script.

comments:
2026-03-10T11:05 - Aisha Patel (Support): Customer reports ~12 users unable to hit model endpoints; provided Okta sample token and SCIM user record. Requested urgent help as this blocks automated jobs.
2026-03-10T12:30 - Diego Morales (Eng): Acknowledged; reproduced locally with sample token. Requesting logs from auth-service and identity-proxy (asked SRE to pull prod logs).
2026-03-10T15:45 - AtlasFin (Customer): Provided confirmation that SCIM provisioning created PrimaryEmail with uppercase letters historically; they cannot re-provision roles immediately.
2026-03-11T09:45 - SRE (Maya Singh): Pulled control plane logs and confirmed identity-proxy normalized email; no evidence of downstream caching issues. Shared relevant log snippets above.
2026-03-11T13:10 - Diego Morales (Eng): Opened PR to add compatibility mode: preserve_case_for_scim_provisioned=true (https://github.com/redwood-inference/identity-proxy/pull/278).
2026-03-12T08:20 - Support (Aisha): Applied short-term fix: ran support migration script to add normalized duplicates for affected role bindings. Customer confirms users regained access. Marking ticket resolved pending follow-up migration + config change in customer's private bundle.

resolution:
Applied multi-step resolution: (1) Deployed identity-proxy compatibility patch (v1.12.1) to the customer's private control plane which adds an option to detect SCIM-provisioned role bindings and preserve original-case keys when performing RBAC lookups. (2) Ran an on-demand migration script to add normalized duplicate keys for existing role bindings (script run: tools/migrate/normalize-rolebindings-2026-03-11.sh). (3) Documented recommended long-term fix: AtlasFin to enable SCIM canonicalization (lowercase) or reprovision roles; Redwood to offer automated normalization in the next maintenance window. Post-fix verification: confirmed 12 affected users regained access and downstream automated jobs resumed successfully. Follow-up action: INT-4452 created to add an opt-in config flag to the Private bundle and to backfill affected customers during next quarterly update.

[IdP metadata served with chunked transfer-encoding leads to truncated entityID and tenant resolution failures in private VPC]
description:
Issue summary:
Customer's Private deployment intermittently fails tenant resolution during SSO flows. We see the IdP metadata XML being fetched by the identity-proxy but the entityID element is truncated. The proxy then fails to match the IdP entity to the configured tenant, resulting in immediate 401/403 responses for new SAML logins.

Impact:
- FinBank Analytics (private) unable to create new SSO sessions for some users; existing sessions remain valid.
- Affects onboarding and new user logins only; no data plane inference impact.
- Around 30% of IdP metadata fetches in the last 24h contained truncated payloads.

Environment:
- Private VPC deployment (FinBank Analytics) in us-west-2
- Identity-proxy v1.12.0 behind customer-managed ingress (NGINX)
- IdP endpoint: https://idp.finbank.example.com/metadata (IdP managed by customer)

Observed behavior:
- identity-proxy logs show SAML metadata parse errors and missing entityID.
- Error pattern correlates with upstream responses that include Transfer-Encoding: chunked.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Run a curl -v against the customer's metadata endpoint via the same path the proxy uses (through the ingress).
2) Intermittently the response headers contain 'Transfer-Encoding: chunked' and the body is cut off mid-entityID.
3) Trigger SAML login flow; identity-proxy logs: 'metadata parse error: unexpected EOF while reading entityID' and the request returns 403 with tenant resolution failure in the response body.

Logs / excerpts:
- identity-proxy: "WARN metadata: parse failed: unexpected EOF at byte 312"
- ingress (NGINX): "upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream"
- curl capture: Response headers: Transfer-Encoding: chunked; Body length reported by client does not match parsed XML length.

Temporary workaround:
- Customer routing change: configure their IdP to serve metadata via Content-Length header (static file) or disable chunked responses on the IdP side. This reduces failures immediately.

Notes:
- This only appears in the private deployment where customer ingress terminates TLS and proxies to their IdP; hosted customers have not reported this.


steps_to_reproduce:
1) curl -v --location 'https://idp.finbank.example.com/metadata' via customer ingress path
2) Repeat until Transfer-Encoding: chunked appears in response headers
3) Attempt SAML login through the identity-proxy; observe 403 and metadata parse error in proxy logs

logs:
identity-proxy WARN: metadata parse failed: unexpected EOF at byte 312; NGINX: upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header; curl: <truncated XML showing incomplete <EntityDescriptor entityID="https://idp.finbank.example.com/sso/"...>

investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: chunked transfer-encoding combined with ingress upstream behavior is causing partial reads by the identity-proxy HTTP client. Reproduced locally by instrumenting a mock IdP that returns chunked responses with occasional premature connection close.

Findings so far:
- identity-proxy HTTP client (Go net/http) was using default Read behavior; when upstream closes connection mid-stream the body reader returns EOF and the XML remains incomplete.
- Customer's ingress (NGINX) intermittently emits 'upstream prematurely closed connection' when backend IdP rotates worker processes during metadata generation.
- Linked to SUP-61502 (idp metadata fetch timeouts) as both involve metadata fetch instability, but root cause differs (timeouts vs chunked truncation).

Short-term mitigation applied:
- Instructed customer to set 'proxy_buffering off' and enable 'proxy_http_version 1.1' with 'proxy_set_header Connection ""' to avoid NGINX closing upstream prematurely. Customer applied change and saw immediate drop in truncation events.

Longer-term fix options:
- Harden identity-proxy metadata fetcher to retry and reassemble chunked responses, validating XML completeness before parsing. (PR created: related_github_prs).
- Add post-fetch validation and automated re-fetch on parse failure with exponential backoff.


resolution:
Workaround: customer modified ingress settings to reduce upstream connection closes; this reduced errors. Engineering drafted a patch to identity-proxy to validate and retry on incomplete chunked responses (PR #482). Target: rollout patch to private branch and offer customer a hotfix deployment. Final verification pending after canary in customer's staging cluster.

[Private: upstream identity header truncated at semicolon after edge proxy upgrade causing scheduled-worker RBAC 403s]
description:
Issue summary:
Customers on Private deployments (Finurex Capital) reported intermittent 403s from internal scheduled-worker tasks that call Redwood admin APIs. Error only started after an ingress/edge proxy upgrade rolled out to us-east on 2026-03-09.

Impact:
- Scheduled batch jobs that run as a service account are failing to perform admin operations (impacts nightly ingestion and billing reconciliation).
- Affects only the private VPC deployment for Finurex (us-east).
- Customer-facing runtime inference unaffected; admin API calls from control plane are impacted.

Environment:
- Private deployment (customer-managed VPC) behind Redwood edge/ingress v1.12.0 -> upgraded to v1.13.0 on 2026-03-09.
- Identity flow: service worker signs a short-lived assertion and a proxy rewrites it into X-Redwood-Identity header using NameID from SAML/IdP.

Observed behavior / errors:
- Admin API returns 403 with message: "subject authz check failed: principal mismatch".
- Identity header present but truncated at first semicolon character (";"). Example expected: "service-account+worker;realm=finurex" but seen: "service-account+worker".
- RBAC policy lookup expects the realm suffix and fails to map to tenant-scoped bindings.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Using customer's private environment, trigger a scheduled worker job (nightly ingestion) that calls /admin/jobs/run with service-account assertion.
2) Observe immediate 403 in job logs.
3) Capture incoming headers to admin API via debug route (/debug/headers) and note X-Redwood-Identity is truncated at semicolon.

- Debug capture from admin service: "X-Redwood-Identity: service-account+worker" (missing ";realm=finurex").

Initial hypothesis:
- Edge v1.13.0 introduced stricter header canonicalization that treats semicolon as a separator and truncates header values when set to 'token' mode. The identity-proxy earlier relied on preserving raw token payload including semicolon-encoded NameID attributes. Truncation causes RBAC lookup failure because tenant scoping suffix is lost.

- Edge upgrade PR: https://github.com/redwood/edge-proxy/pull/433

[Intermittent 403s after IdP group sync: stale SAML session_index role cache]
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent 403s for users immediately after the IdP (On-prem SAML IdP) performs a group sync. Impact: Admin and write operations are blocked for some users while they can still view resources. Occurs only in Nimbus Health's private deployment (prod-us-east) and started after their nightly group-sync job.

Environment: private deployment (VPC) with SSO proxied through our identity-proxy; session cookies used are SameSite=Lax, cookie named rwd_sess. Customer performed an IdP-side role changeset at 03:40 UTC and ran group sync. Symptoms observed for ~seconds-to-minutes window: some affected users receive 403s for actions requiring newly granted roles while others (or same users after logout/login) succeed.

Observed severity: P1 due to business-impacting admin ops during business hours.

steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer updates group->role mapping on IdP and triggers IdP group sync.
2) User with existing browser session performs an admin API call (e.g., POST /v1/admin/projects/:id/keys).
3) Server responds 403 with rbac denial.
4) If user logs out and logs back in, call succeeds.

Repro rate: intermittent but correlated with IdP sync events.

logs:
[2026-03-10T03:41:02Z] auth:rbac deny user=uid:94e3 session_index=sess-0a7f reason='no-matching-role-after-eval' path=/v1/admin/projects/42/members status=403 request_id=aa7b2c
[2026-03-10T03:41:03Z] sso:proxy debug session_lookup key=sess-0a7f -> cache HIT ttl=18s roles=[team:viewer]
[2026-03-10T03:41:05Z] idp-notify info received user-change webhook for uid:94e3 groups=[prod-admins]
[2026-03-10T03:41:07Z] auth:rbac eval user=uid:94e3 live-lookup roles=[team:admin] result=ALLOW


investigation_notes:
03/10 05:45 UTC - Customer provided request logs and IdP group sync trace. Confirmed 403 responses followed immediately after IdP sync events.
Hypothesis: identity-proxy caches role assertions keyed by SAML session_index for performance; when IdP updates groups, existing sessions still return the cached role set until cache expiry. Because session_index is stable across IdP syncs, cached entry is not invalidated, causing stale RBAC decisions.
Validated on staging by reproducing IdP group change and triggering our session cache: reproduced 403 for active session, immediate success after manual cache eviction or full logout/login.
Cache TTL on private deployment was 60s; observed window where some requests hit cached old roles and were denied, others hit live-lookup due to cache miss and allowed. Race condition depends on request timing and distribution across proxy instances.
Checked related subsystems: no evidence of token audience mismatch or clock skew. Session cookie intact; no TLS issues.

description:
Issue summary: Customer (Nimbus Health) observed intermittent short TCP/TLS handoff events during long-lived SSE telemetry sessions. When those handoffs occurred the stream would resume but the final application-level 'end' chunk was missing and the client received one or more duplicated heartbeat frames. Impact: Several production streams for real-time device telemetry saw truncated final paragraphs and missing end-of-stream metadata. This caused Nimbus Health's post-processing job to treat sessions as incomplete and triggered follow-up alerts and duplicate downstream summaries. 2) Simulate an upstream idle probe from an edge load balancer (tcp RST after 30s idle) or trigger a client network change (cellular->wifi) during the stream
3) Allow client to reconnect using our resume protocol (last_seq parameter) and observe the final blocks emitted
4) Note occurrences where the terminal 'end' event does not arrive but heartbeat frames are duplicated and prefixed to resumed payload

[Azure Application Gateway health-probe teardown intermittently suppresses SSE terminal event causing client hang]
description:
Customer reports that long-running server-sent events (SSE) streams occasionally never receive the final 'event: done' terminal message after an intermediate TCP/HTTP teardown initiated by an Azure Application Gateway health probe. Client remains connected via a reconnect flow but the final terminal event is not emitted and the client stalls waiting for completion. This appears to only affect streams that were near completion when the probe-induced teardown occurred.

impact:
A subset of NovaDocs users see generated responses that never signal completion; UX shows an indefinite 'generating...' state. No extra tokens billed in most observed cases but customer workflow times out and triggers retries, increasing downstream API traffic. Approximately 7% of long-tail streaming sessions affected for this customer in last 48h.

steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer opens SSE stream against /v1/streams with a prompt that yields a final short completion (~3-8 tokens).
2) Azure Application Gateway health probe configured with aggressive idle timeout runs during last 1-2 seconds of the stream.
3) Probe triggers connection teardown and the client performs reconnect/Resume with X-Stream-Resume header containing last-received-offset.
4) Client receives partial final tokens but never receives terminal 'event: done' or 'event: error'.
5) Client waits until its own timeout or issues duplicate request.

observed_behavior:
Partial final tokens delivered, sometimes a duplicate trailing token sequence on a later reconnect, and no terminal 'done' event. Client logs show successful resume ACK but UI never transitions to finished. Server logs show request handler marked as completed in some backends but final end-frame not routed to the reconnecting connection.

expected_behavior:
After reconnect/resume the client should receive a full ordered stream including a single terminal 'event: done' so the client can finalize the response and stop retries.

logs:
[2026-03-12T15:02:11Z] proxy: conn 0x7f3a closed by appgw probe
[2026-03-12T15:02:11Z] srv: stream handler completed id=abc123 backend=sr-42 but terminal-frame not flushed to conn 0x7f3b
[2026-03-12T15:02:11Z] client: resume sent X-Stream-Resume:offset=1454
[2026-03-12T15:02:12Z] client: received data: "data: \"...final token\"\n\n"
[2026-03-12T15:02:34Z] client: waiting for 'event: done' (timeout 30s)


investigation_notes:
- Reproduced in lab with AGW configured to probe idle connections: saw identical symptom when probe fired within 0.5-1.5s of completion.
- Backend logs show handler believes it emitted end-marker, but the end marker is not present on the connection that the client reconnects to.
- Likely race between AGW connection termination, backend worker completing the stream, and the reconnect path selecting a different worker without the final event.
- Hypothesis: connection-affinity loss combined with our resume token mapping logic can cause the final frame to be dropped when the origin completes during the probe window.
- No evidence of tokenization/ordering corruption; issue is missing terminal event routing only.


temporary_workarounds:
1) Increase AGW idle probe interval / disable aggressive probe for affected endpoint.
2) Client-side: treat receipt of trailing tokens + N seconds with no terminal event as implicit completion (not ideal).
3) For customers on Dedicated, pin connection affinity to reduce cross-worker handoff.

root_cause_summary:
Race between Azure Application Gateway health-probe-induced TCP teardown and the server-side stream finalization which leads to terminal 'done' event not being routed to the reconnecting client. Resume logic assumes final event either already reached client or will be retransmitted from same worker, but AGW teardown may cause reconnect to be serviced by a different worker lacking that final frame.

mitigation_plan:
Short term: doc workaround to adjust AGW probe configuration and advise client resilience patterns. Medium term: implement idempotent terminal-event replay in resume flow so a worker that detects a completed stream can supply terminal frame to a reconnecting client even if a different worker owns the reconnect. Also evaluate path to use cluster-level final-frame replication or central resume-ack broker.
Timeline: prototype within 2 sprints; hotfix mitigation (tighter resume checks) targeted this week on canary.

final_resolution:
(pending) Prototype of server-side terminal-frame replay has been implemented in feature branch and is under canary. Customer agreed to apply AGW probe config changes this morning; monitoring shows no further hangs for amended sessions. Final rollout scheduled after validation. Will update when PR merged and deployed across prod.

next_steps:
1) Run canary of terminal-frame replay change in us-west with NovaDocs traffic.
2) Collect telemetry for 72h and validate no missing terminal events.
3) If validated, schedule global rollout and postmortem.
4) Update streaming runbook with proxy probe guidance.

[SSE chat stream pauses mid-generation; client heartbeat times out after ~12s]
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports Server-Sent Events (SSE) chat response streams intermittently pausing mid-generation. The client receives a partial sequence of chunks, then no further events; after ~12 seconds the client heartbeat triggers a reconnect.

Impact: Multiple FinArc users report degraded chat experiences: messages stall 2–10% of requests during peak traffic windows. No token corruption observed; when reconnecting the client triggers a new generation and gets repeated or truncated content. Business impact: surface-level interruptions for end users on the fintech product during high concurrency.

Timeline (customer-provided):
- 2026-03-10 09:14 UTC: First support contact; reproduction attached.
- 2026-03-10 09:22 UTC: Support acknowledged and escalated to SRE.
- 2026-03-10 10:05 UTC: Observed spikes in streaming-proxy error rates.
- 2026-03-11 02:30 UTC: Eng paged; traced reaper events coincident with pauses.

Observed behavior: SSE client receives initial event stream and then no data for ~12 seconds; connection remains open from client's TCP perspective, but server does not send further SSE "data:" frames. No explicit 5xx sent. In some traces we see an internal 204 response to the upstream streaming proxy followed by proxy closing the client-side socket.

Expected behavior: Continuous chunked SSE events until final event or explicit completion message. Any server-side fallback should return an explicit error event rather than silent stall.

Additional notes: Customer uses a custom client that sends heartbeat pings every 10s and reconnects after 12s of silence. Problem reproduces for both our redwood-v2-small prod variant and a pinned llama-2-13b-chat model they run on Dedicated capacity. The customer provided a short capture of the SSE frames and their client logs (attached in ticket).

steps_to_reproduce:
1) Make a streaming chat request to /v1/chat/stream with model=redwood-v2-small, stream=true, max_tokens=512
2) Use a client that logs incoming SSE 'data:' frames and pings every 10s, reconnect after 12s of silence
3) Repeat under a moderate concurrent load (20 concurrent clients) for ~30 minutes
4) Observe that ~2-10% of sessions pause mid-stream and the client reconnects after heartbeat timeout

2026-03-10T09:18:04.625Z runtime[instance-3] DEBUG request_id=req-7a2f kvcache_hit=false generated_tokens=48
2026-03-10T09:18:16.999Z streaming-proxy[proxy-7] WARN connection_id=abc123 idle_stream_pause_detected duration_ms=12254 upstream_status=204 upstream_hint=EOF
2026-03-10T09:18:17.001Z api-gateway[gw-12] INFO client_closed connection_id=abc123 code=1006 reason='EOF from upstream'
2026-03-10T09:18:17.005Z runtime[instance-3] DEBUG request_id=req-7a2f partial_output_tokens=54 state=generator-blocked awaiting-kernel-signal
2026-03-11T02:29:58.112Z autoscaler[scaler-2] INFO pool=dedicated-uswest2 scale_event=spinup instance=instance-6
2026-03-11T02:30:00.210Z serving-proxy[proxy-9] ERROR connection_id=def456 proxy_write_timeout duration_ms=12007 downstream_client=10.4.12.33

investigation_notes:
Checked Grafana dashboard (grafana.redwood/dashboard/streaming/latency) — concurrent streaming latency increases correlate with proxy_write_timeout spikes around customer reported windows.
Trace samples (trace id: trc-20260310-09-18-req-7a2f) show that the serving runtime hits a scheduler yield waiting on kernel remote I/O for ~11–13s before emitting more tokens.
Hypothesis A: Backpressure / scheduler starvation in serving-runtime when under specific kernel paths (long-context + quantized model) causes generation to pause while keeping the HTTP connection open. The proxy interprets lack of bytes as EOF after its internal idle threshold and closes the connection.
Hypothesis B: Intermittent TLS renegotiation or proxy chunking bug causing a transient write block on the streaming-proxy process (observed proxy_write_timeout entries).
Ran tcpdump on proxy-7 during a reproduced pause; no TCP-level RSTs observed; application-layer writes stalled (zero bytes written) for duration of pause.
Line-rate correlation: pauses increase when dedicated pool autoscaler is launching new instances concurrently — possible shared resource contention (NVLink scheduling / kernel queue).
Reproduced locally on staging with stress test; enabling lighter quantization/reserved-kernel option reduced pause frequency (from ~8% to ~1%).

resolution:
Mitigation applied: increased streaming-proxy idle_write_timeout from 10s to 18s in prod us-west-2 and enabled a non-blocking generator flush path in serving-runtime config for dedicated pools. Root cause (probable): under certain quantization/kernel code paths the serving runtime can block the generator thread waiting on a kernel artifact (NV kernel queue) which produces long gaps in byte output. The proxy treated this as idle and closed the client socket. Fix plan: runtime code change to avoid blocking on kernel paths for streaming outputs + more granular proxy backpressure metrics.

Rollout notes: runtime patch merged (github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4287) and staged on 2026-03-12; controlled rollout to prod us-west-2 scheduled for 2026-03-14 02:00 UTC with canary 5% -> 25% -> 100%. Proxy timeout change is reversible and will be reverted after runtime fix is fully rolled out and validated.

Follow-ups: create a tracing alert for generator-blocked spans >5s, add a regression test simulating KV cache churn, and update runbook to recommend keepalive >15s for customers that manage their own client heartbeat. Customer follow-up scheduled: 2026-03-15 check-in with FinArc CSM.

[Ghosted fragments and duplicated tail segments after load-balancer failover during SSE session]
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports that long-lived Server-Sent Events (SSE) streaming sessions show 1) duplicated trailing token fragments after an internal load-balancer (LB) failover, and 2) 'ghost' event fragments that arrive out-of-order or without corresponding end markers. Impact: downstream application sees duplicated partial final choices and intermittent state-machine errors when stitching choices, causing incorrect UI display and occasional instruction duplication. Environment: prod-us-east, behind our regional L7 LB, customer uses persistent SSE with client-side reconnect logic (exponential backoff + resume token). Steps to reproduce: 1) Start a long streaming session (>60s) against /v1/stream with redwood-v1.3 pinned. 2) Induce a rolling restart on one of the regional edge proxies or trigger an LB failover (simulated by removing healthy instances). 3) Allow client reconnect to resume using last-offset resume token. Observed behavior: on reconnect, client sometimes receives duplicate tail fragments (e.g. last 8-12 tokens repeated) and intermittent short 'meta fragments' that contain no content but a resume-id header; occasionally a fragment arrives after an 'end' event, producing a ghosted sentence. Expected behavior: resume should continue from the last delivered token and not produce duplicates or out-of-order fragments. Logs attached and relevant traces referenced below.

reproduction_steps:
Start SSE stream to https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream with model=redwood-v1.3 and stream_timeout=180s
Generate prompt expected to produce ~40s of streaming tokens (long generation)
While streaming, remove one backend from the prod-us-east L7 pool to force LB failover (or restart edge-proxy)
Observe client logs and reconstructed output after the client reconnects using resume token

logs:
Datadog trace: trace_id=dd-0f3a2b, span=stream-session-reconnect, see https://app.datadoghq.com/traces/0f3a2b
Edge proxy error: 2026-03-13T18:42:07Z WARN lb: connection reset by peer during in-flight SSE; session_id=cs-9b3f
API gateway: 5xx spike window 18:42:05-18:42:09 (12 requests), correlate with failover event
Customer client log excerpt: Received chunk #24: "...final token" then reconnect, upon resume received chunk #24 again and chunk #25 duplicate

comments:
Aisha Patel (2026-03-13): Customer reported duplicated final phrases and occasional orphan fragments after their LB did maintenance. They attached client logs and a short video showing UI duplication.
Marco Ruiz (2026-03-13): Acknowledged, triaging. Tentative hypothesis: LB failover + proxy connection close causing partial chunk re-delivery due to proxy replays or race in resume handling. Assigning to SRE and streaming-runtime owners.
SRE (Lina Chen) (2026-03-13): Confirmed failover event in prod-us-east at 18:42. Edge proxy restarted and health checks triggered. Observed short window of half-closed connections. Will pull tcpdump and proxy logs.
Streaming Runtime (Diego Alvarez) (2026-03-14): Found cases where session metadata race allows a buffered final fragment to be forwarded twice when resume token reconciliation occurs after a delayed end-event. Preparing a hotfix branch to add an idempotency check on fragment sequence ids.
Support (2026-03-14): Sent workaround to customer: enable 'sticky-sessions' on their LB or switch their client to wait 150ms after re-establish before resuming to reduce race. Customer applied sticky-sessions and reported initial reduction in duplicates; still seeing rare ghosts.
Marco Ruiz (2026-03-14): Coordinating deploy of streaming-runtime patch. Rolling canary scheduled for 2026-03-15 with additional logging toggles for fragment sequence ids.

investigation_notes:
Hypothesis 1: Edge LB failover causes half-closed TCP connections; proxy attempts to replay buffered chunks to new backend resulting in duplicate fragments.
Hypothesis 2: Resume path in streaming-proxy does not fully reconcile last-ack offset under concurrent end-event delivery, causing a small window where the same fragment can be emitted twice.
Evidence: trace correlation shows identical fragment id and identical token checksum sent twice separated by ~120ms; client-side resume token matches server resume position but server emitted fragment again after end-event.
Mitigation tested: instruct customer to enable LB stickiness -> duplicates decreased. Also tested client-side 150ms pause before resume -> duplicates decreased in simulation.
Next steps: add idempotency by tracking recent fragment sequence ids for 1s after session end + backfill patch to avoid replay, and add extra logging to trace fragment sequence ids on production canary

resolution:
Mitigation applied: Customer enabled LB sticky-sessions and temporarily reduced duplicate rate. Streaming runtime hotfix in PR (see related_github_prs) adds fragment-seq idempotency and tighter resume reconciliation; canary build scheduled 2026-03-15. Final resolution pending canary validation and full rollout.

[SSE stream closes silently after idle probe causing finalization (EOF) event to be dropped]
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports that long-running server-sent event (SSE) sessions terminate silently after a period of client inactivity. When this happens the finalization marker (end-of-stream marker / EOF event) is never delivered to the client and the generated text looks abruptly cut off (usually trailing punctuation or last clause missing).

Impact: Multiple user-facing calls are returning partial outputs. Customer observes lost final tokens in ~0.7% of sessions for prompts that take >60s to generate on their dedicated cluster. This is breaking document generation workflows that expect complete finalization events for downstream parsers.

Environment: Dedicated pool in prod (us-east-1) behind customer's corporate reverse proxy and our public NLB. TLS terminated at the proxy; connections are proxied to our api-gateway. Affected model variants: gptj-13b and redwood-rlhf-v1 pinned.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Initiate SSE streaming generation with a long prompt that produces ~90s of tokens.
2) Let the client remain idle for 70+ seconds (no explicit heartbeat from client).
3) Observe that the SSE connection is closed client-side without receiving the final 'event: end' marker.

Observed behavior: Connection disappears from the client (browser or server SDK) as if a TCP RST/cut occurred. No end event present in SSE transcript, partial last sentence returned to application. Server-side logs show a 200 response with streaming chunks but no explicit finalization event logged. NLB logs show connection termination from the backend side with TCP flags consistent with idle timeout.

Expected behavior: Backend should emit a finalization event (EOF/end) before connection closure or keep the connection open long enough for the SSE end event to be sent. If the connection must be closed, the client should be able to detect closure and request a resumable session or our gateway should emit a final 'end' before tear-down.

Attachments provided:
- client_sse_dump.txt (SSE transcript without end event)
- customer_tcpdump.pcap (shows FIN from load balancer at idle interval)
- nlb_access_log_excerpt.log

Additional notes: Customer runs a corporate proxy that strips HTTP/2 keepalives and enforces aggressive idle TCP timeouts. They do not currently send application-level heartbeats.


comments:
2026-03-13 09:12 - Aisha Khan (customer): Provided initial report, attached SSE transcript and tcpdump. Notes that this started after they migrated their users behind a new corporate reverse proxy.
2026-03-13 10:30 - Diego Morales (support): Acknowledged. Asked for: a full server-side request id, the exact model_id and timestamp of a failing session, and an example prompt. Requested route-level logs and NLB log lines if available.
2026-03-13 12:05 - Aisha Khan (customer): Uploaded session id req-0a7b2f and model redwood-rlhf-v1. Attached NLB access log. Customer confirmed they cannot change proxy configuration quickly.
2026-03-13 15:20 - Diego Morales (support): SRE triage started. Hypothesis: upstream TCP idle/health probe causing NLB or proxy to close connection silently without allowing the backend to flush final SSE event. Asked infra to check for any early socket shutdowns on api-gateway nodes.
2026-03-14 08:10 - SRE (investigator): Found backend socket closed by kernel after receiving TCP FIN from proxy. No final application-level end event was emitted because the stream was mid-chunk; kernel-level closure prevented further write. Attached kernel-level socket trace lines to INT-4421.
2026-03-14 11:40 - Diego Morales (support): Provided temporary mitigations to customer and scheduled follow-up: 1) enable client-side heartbeat (send an SSE comment every 25s) 2) set SDK keepalive to 30s (if possible) 3) request that customer ask proxy team to increase idle timeout or allow CONNECT keepalives. Customer to try implement heartbeats and report.
2026-03-14 16:00 - Aisha Khan (customer): Implemented client heartbeat and reports a sharp reduction in incidents during a controlled test. Requested a long-term fix on our side so they don't need to modify their fleet.
2026-03-14 17:05 - Diego Morales (support): Logged internal follow-up INT-4421 for gateway behavior. Assigned to networking team to evaluate sending explicit last-chance flush or mapping long-poll requests to a different connection profile.

investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: idle TCP timeout at the proxy or NLB causes backend socket closure before SSE end event can be emitted.
Corroborating evidence: customer tcpdump shows FIN from reverse proxy at roughly 70s of idle; NLB logs show connection terminated with backend bytes >0 but no corresponding 'close' event in application logs.
Reproducer attempt: Ran local replay with artificially delayed client heartbeats. When client remained silent beyond 60s we observed identical behavior; connection closed with RST from upstream component, backend write() failed with EPIPE in userland before finalization event could be sent.
Temporary mitigation test: Sending SSE comment heartbeats from client every 25s prevents idle timeout and allows normal end event emission.

Longer-term options considered:
- Emit periodic application-level keepalives from our gateway to keep proxy/NLB from idling.
- Implement 'graceful flush on FIN' logic: on detecting upstream FIN we attempt to complete finalization if kernel buffers still allow. This requires kernel-level socket handling changes and is risky.
- Document recommended client heartbeat/SDK keepalive options and add SDK helpers to automatically send heartbeats for long streams.

resolution:
Triage complete; short-term workaround recommended and validated (client-side heartbeat every 25s or SDK keepalive). Internal follow-up INT-4421 opened to evaluate gateway-level keepalive/flush behavior and to propose a safe change to try to guarantee finalization emission when upstream idle timeouts are present. Customer confirmed reduced failure rate after enabling heartbeat. No code fix deployed yet.

[Saved dashboard filter presets reset when editing a linked sub-report]
description:
Issue summary: Customers report that when they open a dashboard with saved filter presets and then edit an embedded sub-report (open editor modal -> save metadata), the dashboard's selected filter preset reverts to the default. Impact: Persistent loss of saved view state for analysts; repeated manual re-selection required and automated alerts tied to specific presets fire incorrectly. Environment: prod, us-east region, console v4.3.2 frontend, query-service v2.8. Steps to reproduce:
1) Log in as org admin with saved dashboard presets.
2) Open dashboard 'Monthly SLA Overview' and select saved preset 'Tiered-90p50'. Confirm widgets update.
3) Open a linked sub-report by clicking "Edit report" on widget (opens editor modal).
4) Change a non-filter attribute in the sub-report (e.g., chart title) and save.
5) Close modal. Observe dashboard filter preset has reset to 'Default (All)'.
Logs / traces: Console frontend logs show filterState reset event at same timestamp as sub-report save. Query service shows no query for preset change. Behavior started being reported after console v4.3.0 -> v4.3.2 deploy (rolled 2026-03-10).
Workaround: Do not use "Save and propagate" option when saving sub-report; save as draft or use separate edit workflow. Temporary manual reselect of preset restores view.

investigation_notes:

workaround:
Advise customers to avoid using 'Save and propagate' for sub-report edits until hotfix deployed. Use 'Save as draft' or edit reports via the Reports workspace to avoid triggering modal save path.

[Saved dashboard view reverts to compacted timeseries after retention compaction causing missing trace links and suppressed alerts]
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports that a saved dashboard view they rely on for daily monitoring started showing compacted/aggregated timeseries after a scheduled retention compaction job. The view no longer preserves the original per-request granularity, trace links on spike points are missing, and associated threshold alerts did not fire for a sustained error increase. This began after last night's rolling compaction window and affects a small set of org-scoped saved views.

impact:
Several on-call engineers at the customer missed a material error spike because the saved dashboard reverted to compacted rollups. Business impact: delayed incident detection for production ingestion pipelines; customer requests urgent remediation and a postmortem of the retention compaction run that coincided with the regression.

steps_to_reproduce:
1) Login to FinSage org in Console (prod/us-east)
2) Open saved dashboard 'Ingest - Request Latency (per-request) - FinSage-prod' at 2026-03-11T22:00:00Z to 2026-03-11T23:00:00Z
3) Observe time-series appears as hourly rollups rather than per-request points; trace link icons are absent on spike markers
4) Reopen the same dashboard after toggling the timepicker to a different range and back; view remains compacted
5) Query raw events for the same interval via /usage-export endpoint and confirm high error rate present in raw events but not reflected in the dashboard alert history.

expected_behavior:
Saved dashboard view should preserve the original granularity and show per-request points for ranges within retention boundaries. Trace links should be present on data points to navigate to traces, and alerts tied to that panel should evaluate against the raw/expected granularity so incidents surface appropriately.

actual_behavior:
Saved view shows compacted hourly rollups; trace link icons are missing on those points; alert evaluation window skipped firing for the error spike. Other ad-hoc queries and raw exports show the events exist at full granularity.

Console query id=qry-9f2a: returned series with rollup_bucket=3600 for metric ingest.requests.latency for 2026-03-11T22:00Z..23:00Z
Retention compaction job id=comp-20260311-A completed at 2026-03-11T23:47Z; compaction config: hourly_rollup=true, preserve_high_granularity_for_saved_views=false
Trace link resolver returned 404 when asked to expand anchor for series point id=pt-7a8b due to missing point-level index

investigation_notes:
Initial triage (Maya): customer saved view appears to be executed against the rollup table rather than the raw event index. Confirmed raw events are present via usage-export for the same interval.
SRE note (Liam): retention compaction run last night included a change that inadvertently caused saved dashboard materialized queries to point at rollup shards for certain org-scoped dashboards. Hypothesis: a mapping rewrite in compaction metadata introduced in rollback-commit rfc/compact-optim-2 changed view-to-table resolution.
Query debug: panel query uses alias 'events_main' which post-compaction resolves to events_rollup_3600 for time ranges older than 1 hour despite panel granularity config set to 'auto'.
Trace linking: link anchors rely on per-event index ids which are purged or not referenced in the rollup table; resolver fallback should attempt to map rollup buckets to representative events but that path returned no candidates.

comments:
2026-03-10 Maya Chen: Logged on with customer to reproduce. Confirmed mismatch between dashboard panel and raw export. Customer is on enterprise plan and requests priority handling.
2026-03-10 Liam O'Connor: Marking as P1 Sev1. Assigning to SRE retention on-call. I've pulled compaction logs and see comp-20260311-A. Noted setting preserve_high_granularity_for_saved_views=false — this looks like the trigger.

2026-03-11 Maya Chen: Customer confirmed after metadata toggle that saved dashboard now shows per-request points for the sampled interval. Trace links reappeared on spike markers. They still want a root cause and prevention plan.
2026-03-12 Liam O'Connor: Patch prepared to ensure saved-view resolution prefers raw index if panel granularity != rollup interval. PR queued for code review: console-backend#1189. Scheduling hotfix deploy to prod/us-east with feature-flagged guard for backward compatibility.

resolution:
Workaround applied: compaction metadata toggle enabled to preserve per-request granularity for affected saved views for FinSage org. Hotfix PR created and tested; rollout scheduled to prod/us-east with feature flag. Longer-term: compaction job will be updated to maintain mapping for org-scoped saved views by default and include integration test coverage.

Follow-up action items: add integration test for saved-view resolution in compaction pipeline, update runbook to avoid setting preserve_high_granularity_for_saved_views=false without org opt-in, and communicate to customers who may be affected. Postmortem draft assigned to INT-7890.

[Scheduled dashboard snapshots drop templated filters when retention compaction runs]
description:
Issue summary: Scheduled dashboard snapshot job for Acme Payments ran on 2026-02-20 03:00 UTC and produced a snapshot where all dashboard template variables (org_id, env_filter, payment_region) were reset to org defaults instead of the user's saved filter values. Observed behavior: Saved dashboard variables are preserved when a snapshot is generated interactively from the Console UI, but the scheduled export runner path loses per-snapshot templated filter state when a retention compaction event overlaps the export window. Support (Aisha Patel) 2026-02-20: Customer reported that scheduled snapshots are returning dashboard variables set to org defaults. They attached the scheduled snapshot JSON and the interactive snapshot for comparison. First response sent; escalated to eng because they hit on-call alerts.

investigation_notes:

- Root cause: exporter used volatile 'live_index' for resolving templated vars which is unavailable during retention compaction. Global defaults were used as a last-resort fallback incorrectly.
- Related behavior: interactive snapshots call 'persisted_snapshot_service' which contains the saved variable set; scheduled exporter did not.
- Related PR: console#1482 modifies exporter to prefer persisted_snapshot_service with retry/backoff; includes unit tests and an integration test that simulates a compaction-induced live_index 503.
- Observability: added metric exporter.snapshot.var_resolution_source (values: persisted, live, default) to track frequency.

[Panel query parameter bindings reset when two users concurrently toggle pinned filters, causing orphaned tracehook tokens and missed alert context]
description:
Issue summary:
When two users edit the same dashboard at the same time and one user toggles the 'Pinned Filters' toggle while the other is changing a panel's query parameter bindings, the panel's saved query binds ({{bind}}) are reset to defaults and the panel's tracehook token is replaced with a temporary token. This causes trace links in the panel to become orphaned and recent alert evaluations for that panel to run without the expected context attributes.

Impact:
- NovaForms reports missing trace links from dashboard panels for ~8% of requests after concurrent edits.
- Alerts tied to panel-context (e.g., request.user_id and route_id) evaluated without bindings, resulting in at least one false negative for a customer SLA alert during yesterday's maintenance window.
- Investigations show orphaned tracehook tokens and short-lived ephemeral token churn immediately after the concurrent edit event.

Environment:
prod/us-east (customer org id: org-4X9c) — dashboards served from console node pool c6g-console-2.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Two users open the same dashboard (dashboard id dsh-8112) in different browsers.
2) User A edits Panel #3 query to add a bound parameter (filter: route_id = {{route_id}}). User A clicks Save but does not change pinned filters.
3) While User A is still in the editor, User B toggles the dashboard-level 'Pinned Filters' switch on then off, and clicks Save.
4) User A completes the save.
5) Reload dashboard: Panel #3 now shows route_id bound to default 'all' and trace links report a temporary tracehook token (tracehook-temp-*) that does not map to any session in the trace ingestion logs.

Observed behavior:
- Panel-level query binding values revert to defaults.
- Tracehook token shown in panel link differs from the original and is not present in trace ingestion (orphaned).
- Alerts that depend on the panel query context fail to include the binding attributes and therefore do not fire correctly.

Expected behavior:
- Concurrent edits should merge with last-write-wins at a well-defined granularity without dropping panel-level bindings or replacing persistent tracehook tokens. Tracehook tokens in panel links should remain mapped to the panel's saved configuration and not be transiently replaced by ephemeral tokens.

Logs / Links / Evidence:
- Customer-provided screenshot: https://filebin.company/novaforms/snap-930271.png
- Console dashboard audit trail (excerpt): https://s3.console.redwood/logs/dsh-8112-audit-20260310.txt
- Support trace ingestion query (search for tracehook-temp-): link: https://redwood.query/trace?query=tracehook-temp-

comments:
Support (Liam Chen) 2026-03-10: Acknowledged. Logged as P1 Sev1 and escalated to Console team. Asked customer for exact browser versions and the two user IDs involved.
Customer (NovaForms - Priya Desai) 2026-03-10: Provided user IDs (user-952, user-953) and browser details: Chrome 111 on macOS, Firefox 115 on Linux. Attached reproduction video and the dashboard JSON export.
Console Eng (Marco Liu) 2026-03-11: Initial hypothesis: concurrent dashboard-level metadata write is overwriting panel-level saved state object due to a merge key mismatch. Reproduced in staging with race condition when toggle change hits the update-v2 endpoint while panel save is in-flight.
SRE (Elena Park) 2026-03-11: Confirmed ephemeral tracehook tokens are created by the dashboard save code path when it detects an unresolved binding reference. We see token churn with a TTL of 5 minutes; tokens never persisted to the tracehook mapping table if save path was canceled/overwritten.
Support (Liam Chen) 2026-03-12: Customer accepted a temporary mitigation (avoid toggling pinned filters during concurrent edits). Requested an ETA for a code fix and whether we can retroactively reconcile orphaned tokens for the alert window.
Console Eng (Marco Liu) 2026-03-12: Working on a patch that serializes dashboard-level metadata updates and applies a merge strategy that preserves panel.bindings. Will propose a hotfix to prevent ephemeral token creation on concurrent writes.

investigation_notes:
Reproduction in staging: created 2 headless clients that simultaneously submitted edits. Observed update-v2 handler applies dashboard-level save last, which rewrites the saved_state object entirely when pinned_filters key exists. Root cause: the client sends 'saved_state' as a full object; server uses non-atomic upsert which replaces panel.bindings map when merge is partial. Additionally, tracehook token generation is triggered when binding placeholders are unresolved, and token persisting is on a separate background job which may be canceled when subsequent save overwrites the token_id field. Evidence: staging trace logs show a write sequence: saved_state -> token-gen -> token-persist canceled by subsequent replace.
Potential fix: change server to perform deep-merge for saved_state blob, and make token persist phase synchronous or transactional with the saved_state write.
Related PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/abc123 (WIP)

resolution_notes:
Workaround applied for affected customer: Support created a short policy guidance and a console-side banner that warns users about concurrent edits and instructs to avoid toggling pinned filters during edits. For the specific alert window, SRE was able to retroactively remap 72 orphaned tracehook tokens to their original panel config by cross-referencing the audit trail and temporarily re-inserting token mappings into the tracehook table.
Planned permanent fix: patch queued (PR abc123) to implement deep-merge upsert for dashboard saved_state and to make tracehook token persistence atomic. Targeted rollout to staging on 2026-03-15 and canary in prod us-east 2026-03-17. Post-deploy, we'll run a synthetic concurrent-edit regression test and monitor tracehook-token churn metrics for 48 hours.
Follow-ups: add automated test for concurrent dashboard edits, add an alert for abnormal token churn, and update runbook to include token reconciliation steps.

customer_communication:
2026-03-10 10:32 UTC - Initial acknowledgement and request for more info.
2026-03-11 18:05 UTC - Suggested temporary mitigation (avoid toggling pinned filters during edits).
2026-03-12 09:40 UTC - Informed customer of remediation path and planned fix dates. Customer requested expedited canary; approved for us-east canary on 2026-03-17.

final_status_note:
Active fix in progress; customer notified and canary scheduled. Ticket will be updated after prod canary results and post-deploy monitoring window.

[Burst of 5xx errors traced to API proxy ephemeral port pressure during high-concurrency tenant burst]
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (AcmeAI, dedicated) reported a sudden elevation in 5xx responses for text generation and streaming sessions starting ~2026-03-12 09:42 UTC. The errors manifested as HTTP 502/504 from the API Gateway and several upstream serving-runtime containers restarting. Impact: intermittent failed requests for several tenants behind the same ingress cluster, visible as ~18% error rate spike for 30 minutes.

Impact:
- Customer-facing: ~18% of requests returned 5xx for ~30 minutes during the burst window.
- Product: streaming sessions were terminated mid-stream; some long-polling embedding uploads retried and amplified load.

Environment:
- Prod cluster: us-east-1, ingress pool ingress-prod-6, routing weight applied to tenant-group-42.
- Customer tier: dedicated GPU pool (reserved capacity).
- Service components: API Gateway (nginx+envoy hybrid), proxy pool (ephemeral worker pool), serving-runtime (gptq runtime containers), autoscaler.

Steps to reproduce / observed pattern:
1) Tenant sent a sudden parallel spike of ~1.8k concurrent streams (customer load test + production traffic).
2) API gateway accepted connections but observed high ephemeral port exhaustion on proxy nodes.
3) Connections queued into accept backlog; many TCP sessions saw RST or short-halfopen states.
4) Gateway returned 502/504 to callers and upstream runtimes logged connection failures then restarted due to watch-dog restarts.

Logs / Metrics (high level):
- apigw/ingress-prod-6: accept_queue_wait_ms median jumped from 3ms -> 230ms between 09:41-09:55 UTC.
- kernel tcp_tw_reuse/tcp_fin_timeout counters increased on proxy nodes.
- ephemeral proxy pods (proxy-ephem-xx): ephemeral port usage peaked at 98% of ephemeral range.
- runtime containers: upstream connection errors (EPIPE, ECONNRESET) followed by OOM-adj watchdog restarts in two pods.
- k8s events show rapid pod churn on proxy nodes as ephemeral-port exhaustion made kube-proxy and iptables behave poorly.

Initial hypothesis:
- A sudden tenant burst consumed local ephemeral ports on proxy nodes causing new outbound NAT sockets to fail or reuse incorrect sockets, leading to upstream resets and gateway 502/504 responses.
- Secondary amplification: client retry logic + long streaming keepalives increased open socket count and kept ports occupied longer.

Investigation notes:
- Reproduced high socket footprint in lab by simulating many concurrent short-lived streaming connections and long keepalives; confirmed ephemeral port exhaustion triggers similar behavior.
- Reviewed proxy node sysctl settings: net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range defaulted to 32768-60999; conn reuse and TIME_WAIT settings were conservative.
- Observed sporadic kube-proxy CPU spikes coincident with high conn churn; iptables programming latency increased.
- Autoscaler did not add additional proxy nodes because horizontal-pod-autoscaler thresholds were on CPU, not ephemeral-socket-metrics.

Workaround implemented (temporary):
- Support/ops increased proxy deployment replica count and restarted a subset of proxy pods sequentially to return to normal ephemeral-port distribution.
- Applied temporary ip_local_port_range widening to 10240-65535 on the most impacted proxy nodes via a DaemonSet (mitigation for existing nodes).
- Asked customer to throttle concurrent streaming test to reduce immediate pressure.

Resolution (current status):
- Immediate customer impact mitigated — error rates dropped back to baseline by 11:05 UTC after replica increase and sysctl changes.
- Two runtime pods were restarted and recovered; no persistent data loss.

Follow-up / Remediation actions:
1) Engineering: add ephemeral-port and TIME_WAIT metrics to ingress autoscaling signals and create alerting (SRE ticket created).
2) Infra: propose default net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range expansion in prod images and add startup check to flag low ephemeral range.
3) Product: document recommended client-side retry/backoff guidance for streaming APIs (avoid aggressive parallel retries).
4) Ops: add a scheduled cron to review socket usage and a playbook for port-range widening.
5) Post-incident: run a chaos test (simulated high-concurrency streams) to validate autoscaler triggers and kube-proxy behavior.

Relevant links:
- Slack: #support (thread ts: 2026-03-12T09:48:00Z)
- Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ingress/ephemeral-ports?from=2026-03-12T09:30:00Z&to=2026-03-12T11:30:00Z
- Runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/ephemeral-port-exhaustion

Next steps owner: Sofia Patel (SRE lead) — will coordinate infra and runtime fixes, target ETA for durable fixes: 2026-03-20.

2026-03-12 10:12 - SRE (Sofia Patel): Observed accept queue growth and high TIME_WAIT on proxy nodes. Spinning extra proxy replicas now. Requesting customer to reduce parallel streams.

[Burst of 5xx errors traced to connection churn causing upstream runtime restarts and proxy fanout failures]
description:
Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-10 14:12 UTC we observed a sharp increase in 5xx responses for a single dedicated customer (CanopyHealth). Impact: customer traffic experienced ~18% 5xx rate for ~90 minutes, causing degraded UX for their production feature. Environment: prod us-east-1, Dedicated pool for CanopyHealth. Observed behavior: API gateway returned 502/503/504 and occasionally 500. Upstream serving-runtime instances intermittently exited and were restarted by the node agent. We saw increased connection churn from the tenant which coincided with the surge. Example request IDs: req_8a2f1b, req_8a2f2c, req_8a2f3e. Incident triage kicked off in #support and #incidents-channel.

investigation_notes:
14:20 UTC: API gateway graph shows open_connections spike from 50->900 for tenant CanopyHealth over ~2 minutes.
14:22 UTC: Connection churn correlated with a backlog of TCP sockets in TIME_WAIT and elevated ephemeral port usage on apigw nodes.
14:25 UTC: Serving-runtime metrics show steady memory increase per request; a small subset of requests had unusually large attention windows (customer prompt size + embeddings) causing higher KV cache usage.
14:30 UTC: Autoscaler recently had a config change (PR 2101) that reduced max surge buffer; under this pattern autoscaler failed to pre-warm enough runtimes leading to amplified queueing on apigw.
Hypothesis: Rapid short-lived connections increased file descriptor and socket pressure on apigw. That created a tight fanout to a small number of runtimes; one or two runtimes hit memory limits and were OOM-killed, which caused apigw to report upstream unhealthy and return 5xxs.

actions_taken:
Rolled back autoscaler PR that reduced surge buffer (apigw/autoscaler config revert).
Temporarily increased file descriptor limits and ephemeral port tuning on apigw nodes.
Deployed serving-runtime patch addressing memory growth in quantized attention (PR 4123).
Notified customer and provided sample mitigations for traffic shaping on their side.

resolution:
Mitigated: rolled back autoscaler surge reduction, increased apigw FD limits, deployed runtime memory-fix patch. 5xx rates returned to baseline and customer traffic normalized. Customer notified and monitoring continues.

root_cause:
Interplay of dramatic short-lived connection churn from tenant traffic, reduced autoscaler surge capacity, and a memory growth bug in the quantized attention kernel. Connection pressure concentrated load on a small runtime pool leading to OOM restarts; API gateway reported upstream unhealthy and returned 5xxs.

follow_up_items:
Add pod-level guardrails to prevent a few runtimes from receiving disproportionate fanout when connection churn is high.
Add alerting for apigw fd usage and ephemeral port exhaustion (thresholds: >=85%).
Hardening: add a circuit-breaker on apigw that prefers spreading connections across more runtime instances earlier.
Run a chaos test simulating tenant short-lived-connection bursts to validate autoscaler and runtime behavior.

[Intermittent high TTFB and 504s caused by proxy write stalls when request-metadata headers grow during streaming]
description:
Issue summary: Over the last 24 hours Nimbus Analytics is seeing intermittent elevated Time-To-First-Byte (TTFB) spikes and occasional 504 Gateway Timeouts on long streaming completions. Impact: customer-facing endpoints for large chat sessions experience degraded latency and occasional request failures, affecting multiple product customers using the same dedicated tenant. Environment: prod (us-east-1), dedicated capacity, requests traverse the external edge gateway (Envoy-based) -> internal ingress -> serving-runtime. Steps to reproduce: 1) Start a long-running chat completion with multi-turn context and tracing baggage headers enabled. 2) Stream responses back to client for ~60-120s. 3) Observe intermittent periods where bytes stop flowing for ~30-90s and then connection resets with 504 or timeout. Observed behavior: interleaved TTFB spikes, streaming stalls with zero bytes for tens of seconds, followed by 504s. Logs/metrics: edge-proxy write buffer growth correlates with increasing per-request header sizes (baggage/trace metadata), envoy stats show upstream_bytes_buffered and downstream_write_failed. Expected behavior: steady streaming without stalls, within latency SLOs. Additional notes: problem appears bursty and correlated with sessions that rotate trace/authorization metadata frequently (client library re-attaches baggage headers every turn).

comments:
2026-03-12 10:23 UTC - Support (Aisha): Customer reported bursts of 504s and long TTFB during streaming calls. Captured sample request ids and initial trace headers. Asked for reproduction details and asked customer to reduce sampling rate of tracing as a short test.
2026-03-12 11:05 UTC - SRE (Marco): Found elevated envoy downstream_write_buffered_bytes on the edge fleet serving the tenant. Noted several streams hitting large header frames on HTTP/2 endpoints. Opening investigation into HPACK/HTTP2 compression interaction and proxy buffering settings.
2026-03-12 13:02 UTC - Customer (Nimbus): Confirmed they enabled per-turn baggage and rotated an auth token every 30s. They can reproduce reliably when baggage payload goes >8KB combined headers.
2026-03-12 15:40 UTC - SRE (Marco): Rolled temporary routing rule to route the tenant to a gateway pool with extended idle timeout and disabled header coalescing for streaming routes. Observing immediate reduction in 504s for the tenant; collecting metrics for 12h window.
2026-03-13 09:12 UTC - Support (Aisha): Notified customer of temporary mitigation and recommended the following: reduce per-turn baggage size, avoid rotating large auth cookies on every turn, and upgrade client SDK to v2.3.1 which includes streaming header streaming optimization.

investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: header growth is forcing HTTP/2 HPACK to emit large header frames that interact poorly with our edge proxy write buffer and downstream connection windowing, causing transient backpressure and write stalls.
Confirmed correlation between requests where cumulative request headers >6KB and occurrences of downstream_write_blocked metric on envoy (edge) and sudden increase in upstream write retries.
Observed edge proxy configured with 60s idle_send_timeout and aggressive proxy_buffering enabled for HTTP/1 routes; for HTTP/2 routes header compression and buffer accounting differs and large HPACK dynamic tables can inflate frame sizes.
Reproduced locally by streaming a 90s session while incrementally appending 1KB baggage headers per turn: observed write stalls at the edge after header frame growth and subsequent 504s from internal ingress when write stall exceeded idle_send_timeout.
Telemetry: linked dashboard panels - Edge Envoy write/backpressure, gateway 504 counts, tenant token rotation histogram (collected), and per-connection header size distribution. Relevant traces: trace-ids captured in ticket comments.
Temporary mitigation applied: route tenant to expanded-timeout gateway pool and disabled proxy buffering for streaming endpoints; immediate drop in 504 rate from ~4.3% -> 0.6% in sample window.

resolution:
Workaround applied (2026-03-12 15:40 UTC): tenant routed to gateway pool with idle_send_timeout extended to 180s and proxy_buffering disabled for /v1/streaming endpoints. Customer confirmed improvement.
Short-term customer action: reduce per-turn baggage headers and avoid rotating large auth cookies per-turn. Rollout note: communicated SDK patch v2.3.1 to Nimbus to minimize header churn.
Planned fixes: engineering to 1) add per-route header-size rejection early (413) with clear error to guide clients, 2) add streaming path which bypasses buffer coalescing and uses windows-aware writes for HTTP/2, 3) increase observability for per-connection header growth and backpressure alerts. Assigned INT-4512 to implement gateway-level hard limits and improved metrics.
Post-incident follow-up: draft runbook update and confluence page created (see related_confluence_pages). Recommend scheduled change to deploy streaming-path improvements in canary by 2026-03-20 then full rollout.

[Intermittent 502/503s and serving-runtime exits observed during tenant high-concurrency burst; socket half-open and ALPN negotiation mismatch suspected]
description:
Issue summary: Between 2026-03-10 14:05 and ongoing, customers (LexiSearch dedicated tenant) experienced an elevated error rate (502/503) and several serving-runtime worker exits correlated with a high-concurrency embedding+chat workload. Impact: impacting 12% of requests for tenant; streams reset and a subset of requests returned 502/503. Environment: prod us-east-1 dedicated pool serving redwood/llama3-13b.

Observed behavior: API gateway returned intermittent 502/503s; serving-runtime processes logged SIGTERM/segfault-like exits followed by rapid respawns; edge proxy logs show repeated FIN_WAIT/half-open sockets and ALPN negotiation failures to a small fraction (~0.6%) of upstream handshakes. Expected behavior: sustained tenant traffic should remain under SLA with graceful backpressure and no runtime exits or elevated 5xx floor.

steps_to_reproduce:
1) Use LexiSearch test harness to replay tenant traffic pattern (mixed streaming chat + batch embedding at 600 TPS peak).
2) Target the dedicated routing tag for LexiSearch in us-east-1.
3) Observe API gateway latencies, edge-proxy socket state counts, and serving-runtime worker process health during ramp to steady-state.

logs:
edge-proxy: observed repeated TCP half-open sockets; last packet timestamps show delayed FIN by 15-30s (logs/edge/us-east/2026-03-10.log: lines 5420-5438)
api-gateway: 502 responses spike from baseline 0.2% to 12% between 14:05-14:28 (dashboards/request-errors/us-east)
serving-runtime: worker_42 exited with SIGABRT; stack shows libuv accept loop + pending ALPN callback (logs/runtime/pool-lexi/2026-03-10.err)
kernel: ephemeral port reuse warnings and socket TIME_WAIT backlog briefly exceeded threshold on some hosts (host-monitoring/host-17)
sre traces: trace IDs 01F8... and 01F9... show client kept-alive but did not complete TLS close; upstream reported handshake_retry in one in 2000 connections.

investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: surge in concurrent streams pushed edge-proxy accept queue into a pathological state, leaving half-open sockets that later cause upstream runtime to hit fd/socket limits and crash.
Observed ALPN negotiation failures are rare but correlate temporally with the first runtime exits; hypothesis: older runtime kernel path triggered a fallback with higher memory pressure during renegotiation.
Checked autoscaler metrics: Dedicated pool scaled as expected but memory fragmentation increased after repeated worker respawns (nvml metrics + runtime memmap).
Heap/stack traces from crashes point to accept/uv_loop handling; adding extra logging to runtime accept path (temporary debug build) reproduced a similar crash in staging when we artificially limited file descriptors.

timeline:
2026-03-10 14:02 - LexiSearch reports elevated 502s via support channel.
2026-03-10 14:06 - Support triaged and created SUP-209824; SRE paged.
2026-03-10 14:15 - SRE confirmed correlated runtime exits on dedicated hosts (pool-lexi-*) and increased socket TIME_WAIT counts.
2026-03-10 14:25 - Temporary route weight shift away from a small subset of edge hosts reduced error rate from 12% -> 3%.
2026-03-10 15:05 - Applied temporary runtime flag to enable aggressive connection reaper; observed further reduction to ~0.5% error rate.
2026-03-11 09:10 - Created infra PR to add ALPN-negotiation fallback and fd limit guard (PR #5678).
2026-03-12 10:00 - Running extended soak in staging with fix; no reproductions so far.

comments:
Support (Aisha Patel) - 2026-03-10 14:09: 'Customer reporting streaming disconnects and elevated 502s. Customer impact: production search queries failing intermittently; provided logs and tenant id to SRE.'
SRE (Daniel Kim) - 2026-03-10 14:20: 'Investigating runtime worker exits; collecting core dumps and enabling extra logging on pool-lexi hosts. Early signs point to accept loop hitting stale socket state.'
Customer (LexiSearch Ops) - 2026-03-10 14:35: 'We saw increased latency and a handful of failed user requests; paused some bulk embedding jobs — thanks for the quick mitigation.'
SRE (Priya Nair) - 2026-03-10 15:08: 'Shifted route weights and toggled connection reaper; error floor dropped significantly. Continuing root cause analysis.'
Eng (Riley Chen) - 2026-03-11 09:25: 'Opened PR to add ALPN fallback and to harden accept loop around fd exhaustion; tests in staging are green.'

mitigation:
Short term: shift route weight off of affected edge hosts and enable aggressive connection reaper. Customer bulk jobs paused at their side. Longer term: deploy PR to add ALPN fallback and fd-guard in serving runtime; add autoscaler hysteresis to avoid thrashing replicas.

root_cause:
Combination of edge-proxy accept-queue pressure during tenant concurrency ramp and an outdated runtime accept path that did not gracefully handle ALPN handshake retries and file descriptor pressure. Resulted in half-open sockets and subsequent runtime process exits that amplified the 5xx rate.

resolution:
In progress. Temporary mitigations reduced errors to acceptable levels. Code fix merged (PR #5678) and under staging validation. Plan: staged rollout to canary subset of dedicated pool, monitor errors and socket metrics, then full rollout after 48h clean soak.

follow_up_actions:
1) Roll out PR #5678 to 10% canary in dedicated pools and monitor for 72h.
2) Add alert for edge-proxy half-open socket ratio and tie to automated route-weight throttling.
3) Increase runtime logging around ALPN and accept loop for 7 days post-rollout.
4) Post-incident: write runbook entry for fast shift-and-reap mitigation and document fd/ALPN guard limits.

[HTTP/2 SETTINGS frame reordering from a client library causing stream-reset surge and upstream runtime restarts]
description:
Issue summary: Customers observed a rapid spike in 5xx responses (~40% elevated) for a subset of dedicated tenants. Impact: streaming sessions aborted with HTTP/2 RST_STREAM and many short-lived 502/503 responses; several runtime pods restarted from watchdog OOMs. Environment: prod-us-east-1, dedicated capacity pool serving NoteScale Analytics traffic. Time window: 2026-03-12 18:22 - ongoing (investigation active).

steps_to_reproduce:
1) Client library (NoteScale SDK v2.1.3) opens multiplexed HTTP/2 connections to api-gateway and sends a rapid SETTINGS update sequence during connection spin-up.
2) SETTINGS frames arrive out-of-order (duplicate max_concurrent_streams updates) followed immediately by a burst of new stream initiations (many short-lived streaming sessions + embedding uploads).
3) api-gateway forwards to HTTP/2 proxy which attempted to reconcile the mismatched SETTINGS and temporarily rejected new streams, returning RST_STREAM to clients and queuing accept backpressure to upstream runtimes.
4) Upstream runtimes experienced accept-queue growth, large KV cache churn, and then memory pressure leading to OOM watchdog restarts under sustained ~600 rps burst.
Note: reproducible only with client behavior that emits duplicate/reordered SETTINGS during rapid connection creation.

observed_behavior:
Rapid increase in 502/503 responses for streaming endpoints and short-lived 5xx spikes on generation endpoints. Runtime pods showed short-lived high RSS followed by SIGKILL (OOM). APIGW logs show repeated HTTP/2 SETTINGS frames and downstream RST_STREAMs. Traces show half-closed streams and accept-queue growth on proxies.

expected_behavior:
HTTP/2 SETTINGS updates should be handled idempotently with no cascade of stream resets; the gateway/proxy should apply sensible backpressure without causing upstream OOMs or client-visible 5xx spikes.

logs:
apigw-logs: 2026-03-12T18:22:41Z WARN http2: received duplicate SETTINGS max_concurrent_streams=200 then 50 from 10.7.32.19
