Pending validation window with customer. Will move to Resolved after 72h of no recurrence.

[Subject prefix normalization strips tenant scoping, blocking cross-tenant impersonation in private deployment]
description:
Issue summary:\nA recent identity-proxy configuration/image change caused the 'sub' (subject) claim to be normalized by stripping tenant prefixes when the subject looks like an email address. For customers on Private deployments (customer: Finlytics) this removed tenant scoping from tokens issued during SSO/OIDC flows and caused RBAC checks and cross-tenant impersonation validation to fail.\n\nImpact:\n- Finlytics observed that service account impersonation and cross-tenant admin operations started returning 403s for ~30% of admin requests after a routine config sync on 2026-03-10.\n- Affected operations: admin-console impersonation, service-account token exchange, and long-running automation that relies on tenant-scoped subject bindings.\n- No tokens were accepted for impersonation; user interactive logins for non-admins were largely unaffected.\n\nEnvironment:\n- Customer: Finlytics (private deployment)\n- Region: prod-us-east (us-east-1)\n- Identity stack: Customer IdP (Okta) -> Redwood identity-proxy (private) -> Redwood auth-service -> RBAC sync\n- Identity-proxy image: registry.redwood/identity-proxy:v1.12.0 (rolled out 2026-03-10 03:12 UTC)\n\nSteps to reproduce:\n1) Exchange code with IdP and inspect id_token.\n2) Observe 'sub' claim for affected users is returned as 'alice@example.com' instead of expected 'finlytics:alice@example.com' (tenant prefix missing).\n3) Attempt impersonation with: curl -X POST https://private.finlytics.redwood/api/v1/impersonate -H \"Authorization: Bearer <id_token>\" -d '{\"as\":\"service-account/ops-bot\"}'\n4) Observe 403 with body: {\"error\":\"subject not in tenant scope\"}.\n\nCurrent behavior:\n- Subject claim normalization removed tenant prefixes (pattern '<tenant>:<subject>') when subject matched an email regex. RBAC rules require the tenant prefix for tenant-scoped role bindings, so matches failed.\n\nExpected behavior:\n- Identity-proxy should preserve tenant scoping in the 'sub' claim unless explicitly configured to remove prefixes.\n\nInitial workaround:\n- Rolled back identity-proxy to registry.redwood/identity-proxy:v1.11.8 in Finlytics' private cluster at 2026-03-10 11:04 UTC; impersonation restored for most customers.\n- Temporary customer-facing mitigation: instruct Finlytics to use service-account tokens (non-impersonation flow) for critical automation until fix is deployed.

Hypothesis: change intended for hosted customers to prevent duplicate tenant prefixes but incorrectly enabled by default for private deployments.

2026-03-11 09:35 UTC - Finlytics (Customer Rep - Maria Chen): We saw the rollback restore behavior; however, some automation queued tokens earlier still failed. Requesting formal RCA and timeline for permanent fix.

investigation_notes:
03:40 UTC - Collected id_token samples from Finlytics: sub claim example before rollout: 'finlytics:alice@example.com' ; after v1.12.0 rollout: 'alice@example.com'.
Checked identity-proxy config: 'subject_prefix_handling' set to 'auto' at cluster level; PR #312 introduced 'auto' behavior which strips prefix on email-like subs unless 'preserve_prefix=true' is present. Private deployments were unintentionally inheriting 'auto' from base image config during config sync.
Auth-service RBAC matcher expects exact prefix match for tenant-scoped bindings (implementation note: match is string-equals on 'sub' when binding is tenant-scoped). No fallback logic present for missing prefixes.
Reproduced locally by running identity-proxy:v1.12.0 with test id_token containing sub='finlytics:alice@example.com'. Proxy returned sub='alice@example.com' downstream. Unit test coverage missing for subject normalization behavior across tenant-scoped tokens.
Reviewed related logs: identity-proxy audit log contains entries 'normalized sub from finlytics:alice@example.com to alice@example.com' at 03:14 UTC; correlation shows spike in RBAC 403s starting 03:16 UTC.
Found related customer ticket SUP-90315 referencing token prefix edge cases; cross-linked for follow-up compatibility checks.

resolution:
Immediate: Rolled back identity-proxy to v1.11.8 for Finlytics at 2026-03-10 11:04 UTC which restored tenant-scoped subjects and cleared the 403s.\n\nRoot cause: PR #312 introduced an 'auto' normalization mode that strips tenant prefixes for email-looking subject claims. The change was merged without gating it for private deployments; a configuration default caused private clusters to inherit the behavior. RBAC checks perform exact string-equals on the 'sub' claim and therefore failed when prefixes were removed.\n\nFix deployed: Auth team prepared hotfix PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/identity-proxy/pull/318 which reverts 'auto' behavior and adds an explicit 'preserve_prefix' config flag defaulting to true for private deployments. Hotfix was applied to image v1.12.1 and staged to canary on 2026-03-12; full rollout to private clusters scheduled after QA on 2026-03-13.\n\nPost-deploy verification: Ran replay of Finlytics token test suite against v1.12.1 canary (all tenant-scoped impersonation flows passing).\n\nFollow-up actions (owner in parens):\n- Backport hotfix and release identity-proxy v1.12.1 with config default (Auth Eng - Diego Park).\n- Add explicit integration tests that validate subject prefix preservation for private deployments (QA - Nivedita Rao).\n- Update deployment gating so config sync does not alter 'subject_prefix_handling' unintentionally (Infra - Lena Ortiz).\n- Add a canary dashboard for token normalization changes and an alert for sudden increases in impersonation 403s (Observability - Marcus Lin).\n- Customer communication: Send RCA and timeline to Finlytics with SLA impact summary (Support - Aisha Raman).\n\nStatus: Hotfix merged and canary deployed; full private rollout pending scheduled maintenance window 2026-03-13 02:00-03:00 UTC.

[Edge header encoding transforms tenant principal and causes RBAC lookup failures in private deployment]
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports that after a network appliance upgrade in their edge stack, users in the private deployment started receiving 403s from Redwood Inference when invoking the admin APIs. Impact: Admin and service accounts for several tenants could not perform operations (role listing, service account impersonation). This blocks customer ops and scheduled model rollouts. Environment: Private deployment (VPC) for AceroHealth, prod/us-west, Redwood identity-proxy v2.3.1, customer-managed HAProxy 2.6.4 that sits in front of the identity proxy. Observed behavior: Requests arriving at identity-proxy contain an X-Forwarded-User header, but the value appears base64-like (e.g., "QWNlcm9cXFVzZXJcXDE=") instead of expected email/principal string. Authentication succeeds (JWT validated) but tenant resolution/subject canonicalization fails when mapping header to tenant-scoped principal, causing RBAC to drop all role bindings and return 403. Steps to reproduce: 1) Using a customer edge box with upgraded HAProxy, make a request to admin list roles endpoint with a valid OIDC token. 2) Observe 403. 3) Capture request at identity-proxy; header shows encoded principal. Logs / relevant headers: - Received header: X-Forwarded-User: QWNlcm9cXFVzZXJcXDE= - Expected header: X-Forwarded-User: alice.user@acerohealth.com - Example request id: rwd-req-20260310-7a3f - Identity-proxy log snippet (redacted): "tenant resolution failed: canonicalize_subject returned empty after header parse" Expected behavior: identity-proxy should map the incoming principal to a tenant and apply RBAC bindings; requests should not be blocked by a header encoding transformation introduced by the customer's edge appliance. Notes: Customer claims this started immediately after HAProxy upgrade and a config push from their network team. They do not intend to change upstream identity header behavior without a controlled rollout.

investigation_notes:
Hypothesis: network appliance config is intentionally encoding principal header. Confirmed by customer's HAProxy config and captured header values. Reproduced behavior in an internal testbed with HAProxy configured to base64-encode headers. Root cause: identity-proxy strictly validates header format and uses simple string canonicalization that rejects non-UTF8 or non-email-looking values, resulting in tenant lookup failing and RBAC falling back to deny. Risk assessment: automatically decoding customer-supplied headers can be risky (maliciously crafted values). Implemented temporary conservative decode that only runs when header matches strict base64 regex and decoded value matches tenant principal pattern (email-like). Logged this as INT-4421 for permanent fix: add explicit header-shaping policy and a tenant-trust flag for private deployments.

resolution:
Workaround applied: deployed hotfix identity-proxy build that decodes base64-encoded X-Forwarded-User when and only when decoded value matches tenant principal pattern. Customer validated hotfix in canary and then applied to fleet. Permanent remediation: engineering to implement an opt-in header-normalization policy in identity-proxy and update private deployment docs with guidance: (1) do not transform identity headers upstream; (2) if transformation is required, coordinate with Redwood support to enable safe decoding or use signed headers. Follow-ups: INT-4421 (engineer work item), update Confluence runbook, add test coverage for encoded-header handling. Customer action: revert HAProxy base64 header encoding in next maintenance window.

[Service-aligned Probe Manifest and Priming Registry]
summary:
This document defines a canonical, service-oriented probe manifest and a lightweight priming registry used to align evaluation probes with product services. It codifies fields, registration workflows, lifecycle rules, and the telemetry contract required to run production-representative evals across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

overview:
Background: As Redwood scales multi-tenant shadow and synthetic-probe evaluations, we need a single source-of-truth for probes that are explicitly mapped to product services and runtime characteristics. This registry ensures probes carry enough metadata for safe shadow execution (quant/kv-cache compatibility), prioritization, and reproducible priming used by evaluators and the runtime orchestration layer.

Goals:
- Map probes to logical service boundaries (service_id, route_pattern).
- Capture runtime compatibility (quant_profile, kv_cache_required, max_context_tokens).
- Store priming templates (few-shot examples / anchoring context) and their stability metadata.
- Provide a small-enough manifest to be embedded alongside probes in eval pipelines and retained in the eval asset registry.

Non-goals: This is not a replacement for the full probe asset registry or human-facing annotation logs. The manifest is intentionally compact and machine-oriented.

manifest_schema:
The manifest is a compact record attached to each probe. Fields (required/optional):
- probe_id (required): stable opaque id (rpid-xxxx).
- display_name (required): short human name.
- service_id (required): canonical product service (e.g., rerank-service-v2).
- route_pattern (optional): API route or logical route (e.g., /chat/*).
- workload_class (required): one of {interactive, batch, rerank, embedding}.
- quant_profile (optional): recommended quant profile id (e.g., q8h-coarse) or null.
- kv_cache_required (optional): boolean; true if probe expects long context cache behavior.
- max_context_tokens (optional): integer; used for routing and cost estimation.
- priming_template_id (optional): if priming present, pointer to priming registry entry.
- expected_stability_score (optional): float 0..1 used by CI gating.
- sampling_weight (optional): numeric weight used by scheduler.
- owner (required): team alias owning the probe (e.g., platform-evals).
- retention_policy (optional): short code: P90 (90d), P365 (365d), PRUNE (manual).
- tags (optional): list of short tags (strings).

Table: Example manifest fields and acceptable values are described inline above. Implementations must validate required fields before registration.

registration_procedure:
Registration workflow (1–2 engineers):
1) Author creates probe asset and a companion manifest JSON using the schema above. Use rpid-<sha1(artifact)> convention for probe_id.
2) Push manifest+probe to the eval-asset-store and request priming-template creation if required.
3) CI checks run: manifest validation, light syntactic eval (sanity response), tokenization check (max_context_tokens), and compatibility test against quant_profile if present.
4) Reviewer from owner team (owner) approves in the registry UI. Reviewer sign-off requires: owner approval and a passing sanity eval.
5) After approval the probe enters STAGED state and is available for shadow scheduling.
6) To promote to PROD probes must pass a 24h stochastic-stability window measured against service-specific slice anchors.

Notes: For probes that require customer-sensitive data, mark confidentiality=restricted and attach a brief data-handling note in related_pages. Probes failing CI must include failure_reason and remediations in the registry UI.

probe_lifecycle:
Lifecycle states and TTLs:
- DRAFT: Not scheduled, editable by author. TTL: indefinite until submitted.
- STAGED: Visible to eval scheduler for shadow runs. Required: manifest validation, owner approval. TTL: 30d by default, auto-notify owner at T+21d.
- PROD: Rotational priority for long-term monitoring. Entry to PROD requires 24h stability pass and registration of telemetry anchors. Retention: P365 by default.
- DEPRECATED: Marked by owner; scheduler excludes by default but can be used for ad-hoc investigation.
- PRUNED: Removed from active registry; archived blob retained per retention_policy.

Lifecycle operations: update->retest->promote or update->fail->revert. Every state change must be recorded with a changelog entry including actor, timestamp, and reason.

telemetry_contract:
All probes must emit or be accompanied by evaluation telemetry for the scheduler and RCA tooling. Required telemetry fields (names used in metrics/telemetry pipelines):
- eval.probe_id (string)
- eval.service_id (string)
- eval.run_id (string)
- eval.latency_p50_ms (number)
- eval.latency_p95_ms (number)
- eval.token_cost (number)
- eval.stability_score (number 0..1)  // composite metric comparing anchor outputs
- eval.confidence (optional float)
- eval.priming_version (string)
- eval.quant_profile_used (string)
- eval.kv_cache_hit_ratio (optional float)

SLOs and gating thresholds (defaults; service teams may set stricter values):
- Stability pass threshold: stability_score >= 0.92 over 1,000 probes in 24h window.
- Latency tail: p95 <= service latency_slo_p95_ms (service-specific; request in service manifest).
- Token-cost delta: median token_cost relative to baseline <= +15%.

Failure modes: Telemetry missing required fields -> auto-fail CI. Stability_score drop below 0.85 triggers immediate DEPRECATE flag and creates a regression triage ticket in #eval-regressions.

Instrumentation notes: Prefer the evaluator-sidecar to emit eval.* metrics; fallback is post-run ingestion using eval metadata. All telemetry must be taggable by region, deployment_type (hosted|dedicated|private), and model_variant.

rollouts_and_rollbacks:
Canary & rollout policy (recommended):
1) Micro-canary: run probe at 1% of production shadow traffic for 6h. Check stability and latency metrics.
2) Staged increase: 1% -> 10% -> 25% -> 100% over a 72h window, with health checks at each step.
3) Canary pass criteria: stability_score >= configured_threshold, no P95 tail regression > 2x baseline, and no functional sentinel failures.

Rollback steps (if any step fails):
- Immediate halt of rollout and automatically demote to STAGED.
- Open a regression incident and kick off cross-team Triage (see regression-triage playbook).
- If failure is quant-related, trigger quant-fallback policy: route traffic to a verified compatibility profile and notify runtime-ops to pin KV cache behavior.

Automated rollback hooks: the scheduler must support automated rollbacks when the aggregated severity score exceeds the configured rollback_threshold.

ownership_and_escalation:
Owners and channels:
- Probe owner (manifest.owner): primary responsible for correctness and remediations.
- Evaluation steward (platform-evals): schedules weekly probe hygiene sweeps.
- Oncall: eval-oncall rotates; use pager duty (PD: eval-oncall) for high-severity regressions.
- Slack channels: #eval-ops (ops/questions), #eval-regressions (incidents), #probe-registry (onboarding questions).

Escalation matrix:
- Triage (severity low): owner @48h.
- Action (severity medium): owner + steward @8h.
- Incident (severity high): owner + steward + runtime-sre + product @1h and PD alert.

examples:
Example probe manifest (JSON):

{
  "probe_id": "rpid-a1b2c3d4",
  "display_name": "user-intent-disambiguation-v2",
  "service_id": "conversational-nlu",
  "route_pattern": "/v1/chat/*",
  "workload_class": "interactive",
  "quant_profile": "q8h-coarse",
  "kv_cache_required": true,
  "max_context_tokens": 8192,
  "priming_template_id": "pt-2026-091",
  "expected_stability_score": "0.95",
  "sampling_weight": "1.0",
  "owner": "platform-evals",
  "retention_policy": "P365",
  "tags": ["nlu", "multiturn"]
}

Example priming registry entry (YAML):

---
priming_template_id: pt-2026-091
display_name: conversational-intent-anchors-v1
version: v2
created_by: priya.shah
created_at: 2026-10-21
anchors:
  - role: system
    text: "You are Redwood assistant specialized in clarifying ambiguous user messages. Always ask a single clarifying question when intent is ambiguous."
  - role: user_example
    text: "I'm trying to book a flight for next week."
  - role: assistant_example
    text: "Do you have specific travel dates or flexible?"
notes: >
  Version v2 adds bias-reduction examples and standardizes annotation for date formats.
---

Priming templates must record version and a short changelog. The priming registry entry is small (max 8KB) and is stored alongside the probe manifest in the eval-asset-store.

appendix:
Implementation notes for the runtime team:
- Scheduler must fetch manifest fields before selecting quant_profile and routing.
- If kv_cache_required=true and the runtime does not support long-context caching for the model_variant, mark the probe as INCOMPATIBLE and notify owner.
- Implement a small compatibility test harness that runs the probe against a lightweight shadow runtime (1e-3 sample ratio) before scheduling at scale.

Migration notes:
- For existing probes without manifests, run an automated harvest job that attempts to infer service_id, workload_class, and max_context_tokens and open an onboarding ticket for manual validation.

Glossary:
- Priming: few-shot or anchor context injected with a probe for behavioral anchoring.
- Stability_score: composite similarity metric used across anchors to detect semantic drift.
- Probe: a synthetic input + expected anchoring used for automated evals.

[Edge Shadow Telemetry Contract for Private and Dedicated Evaluations]
Summary:
This document defines the telemetry contract and operational workflow required to run edge and private shadow evaluations against customer-managed (Private) and Dedicated pools. The contract balances fidelity for quality checks (coherence, hallucination, embedding drift) with privacy, cost, and storage constraints specific to private deployments. It is intended for applied ML engineers, SREs running shadow orchestration, and oncall/regression teams performing triage and rollbacks.

Goals and scope:
- Provide a minimal, well-documented telemetry payload that all shadow evaluators must emit when running in Private and Dedicated environments.
- Specify sampling, anonymization, retention, and encryption requirements to meet customer privacy/KMS constraints.
- Define quality and regression gate metrics, thresholds, and alerting integration for early detection during shadow rollouts and quant/optimize migrations.
- Describe triage playbook for any failing slices discovered by the shadow probes, including ownership and rollback criteria.

Why this contract exists:
Private and Dedicated deployments run under different constraints than Redwood-hosted evals: limited egress, stricter PII rules, and heterogeneous hardware/quantization variants. Without a standard contract, shadow telemetry is inconsistent and expensive to analyze. This contract ensures we get the telemetry needed to detect regressions while respecting privacy and cost.

Telemetry payload spec (minimal required fields):
Each shadow probe record must contain the following top-level fields (string or numeric types only):
- probe_id: unique id for the probe run (uuid)
- tenant_id: hashed tenant id (sha256 hex) or obfuscated alias; raw customer IDs MUST NOT be sent outside the private boundary unless agreed (see privacy section)
- deployed_model: model name + version (e.g., redwood-7b-v2-quant8)
- deployment_variant: one of [hosted, dedicated, private]
- quant_profile: label of quant profile used (e.g., q8_fast_fp16_fallback)
- hardware_tag: e.g., a100-40gb, t4-16gb, edge-x86-32g
- prompt_family: short token describing probe set (e.g., billing_faq_anchors_v3)
- seed_context_hash: sha1 of the prompt/context after canonicalization (for deduping; non-reversible)
- latency_ms: observed end-to-end request latency in ms (int)
- tokens_input: token count of input (int)
- tokens_generated: token count generated (int)
- top_level_metrics: comma-separated string of key metrics, e.g., coherence:0.82,hallucination:0.03,embed_cos_sim:0.67
- error_code: empty string or standardized code (see appendix error-code-table)
- timestamp_utc: ISO8601 timestamp

Optional fields (when privacy & egress allow):
- raw_response_snippet: up to 512 characters after PII redaction
- annotator_score: numeric human score if annotator was used (0..1)
- kv_cache_hit: boolean (true/false)

Sampling and rate limits:
- Default sampling rate for private shadow probes: 2% of production traffic or 1000 probes/day per tenant (whichever is smaller) unless explicitly configured for a campaign.
- For Dedicated pools without egress, sampling may be increased during controlled experiments with customer approval; update deployment manifest.
- System must support stratified sampling by prompt_family to ensure rare slices are captured (min 5 probes per slice per day if available).

Privacy, encryption, and retention:
- All telemetry leaving customer-managed network must be encrypted with the customer KMS key (AES-256-GCM envelope encryption).
- tenant_id must be hashed; any reversible identifier requires documented consent and a signed customer exception.
- raw_response_snippet must undergo automated PII redaction pipeline before export. Use our redaction library version >= v2.1.
- Default retention: 30 days for detailed probe payloads, 365 days for aggregated metrics (daily rollups). For customers with longer retention requirements we must create a retention SLA and enable on-prem analytics hooks.

Metric definitions and SLOs (shadow-eval quality gates):
- Coherence (slice median): unit 0..1; alert threshold < 0.70; action: create incident, notify model-owner. Notes: Cohesion of multi-turn replies (see coherence rubric).
- Hallucination rate (slice): unit fraction; alert threshold > 0.05; action: open P1 triage if sustained for 6 hours. Notes: Exclude benign OOD prompts after review.
- Embedding cosine shift: unit delta; alert threshold > 0.12; action: schedule regression-bisect, tag model-version. Notes: Compare against anchor baseline.
- Latency p95: unit ms; alert threshold > 2x baseline or > 1200ms; action: throttle rollout, rollback if tail persists. Notes: Baseline computed per hardware_tag.

Alerting and integration:
- Expose shadow-eval metrics to the Ops dashboard with tenant-scoped anonymized view. Use metric names: shadow.coherence.*, shadow.hallucination.*, shadow.latency.*.
- Create automatic incidents when thresholds are breached for >= 30 minutes across >=3 prompt_families.
- Add annotation to incidents indicating whether the failing probes used quantized model variants.

Workflow: Shadow rollouts and gating (sequence):
1. Prepare: define probe campaign with prompt_families, sampling rate, quant_profile, and expected traffic window. Owner: Applied ML engineer.
2. Dry run: execute offline shadow run on a representative dataset; compute baseline metrics and generate an acceptance ticket.
3. Shadow deploy: route sampled traffic to shadow instance (no user-visible change). Emit telemetry per contract.
4. Monitor: dashboard shows live slice metrics. Automated gates evaluate every 5 minutes.
5. Escalate: if a gate crosses alert threshold, follow triage playbook (see next section).
6. Decision: canary -> promote, continue shadowing, or rollback per prescribed criteria.

Regression triage playbook (short-form):
- Initial assessment (15 minutes):
  1. Confirm the alert: verify metric, affected prompt_families, and hardware_tag.
  2. Check deployment context: quant_profile, kv_cache_hit, batch size, runtime kernel revision.
  3. Correlate with infra alerts (GPU errors, memory pressure).
- Isolation (30 minutes):
  4. Reproduce with a deterministic probe replay locally (use replay-tool with probe_id).
  5. Run welcome/regression bisect if applicable (see bisect playbook link).
- Remediation (TBD cadence):
  6. For quant-induced regressions: switch to fallback profile (q_fallback) and validate.
  7. For model-quality regressions: escalate to model-owner and create a rollback if degradation persists > 2 hours.
  8. Document root cause and add a probe to the longtail suite if it's a novel failure mode.

Ownership and responsibilities:
- Applied ML: define probe_families, baseline acceptance criteria, and annotation rubrics.
- Eng-SRE: ensure telemetry pipelines, encryption, retention and dashboards are functioning; own incident runbook execution if infrastructure is implicated.
- Runtime/Serving team: expose runtime tags (kernel revision, batch size) in telemetry and provide kernel rollback knobs.
- Data-privacy/legal: approve any tenant identifier exceptions and retention extensions.

[Evaluator Sidecar Integration and Telemetry Contract]
Overview

This document defines the integration pattern, API/telemetry contract, and operational playbook for the "evaluator sidecar" — a lightweight process that runs alongside production model endpoints (hosted, dedicated, or private) to:

- capture representative probes
- run local/eager evaluations against candidate model variants
- emit standardized telemetry and quality signals
- drive local fallback and quantization-aware routing decisions

The sidecar architecture reduces time-to-detect quality regressions, improves locality of eval data, and enables private deployments to run meaningful evals without shipping raw customer data off-cluster.

Scope

This page covers:
1) architecture and responsibilities of the evaluator sidecar
2) event and telemetry schema (fields, cardinality, retention semantics)
3) SDK / HTTP contract for probe submission and evaluator responses
4) onboarding checklist for model owners and platform engineers
5) guardrails for quantized and KV-cache-sensitive models
6) regression triage fast path and runbook

Out of scope: long-term offline evaluation pipelines (handled by eval-harness batch runners) and human-in-the-loop labeling workflows (refer to the annotation charter).

Architecture and responsibilities

- Sidecar placement: deployed as a co-located container/process in the same pod/VM as the model serving process for low-latency access to model metrics and KV cache.
- Responsibilities:
  - Ingest a sample stream (shadow or sampled production traffic) and run lightweight probes.
  - Run targeted evals (syntactic checks, safety sentinels, coherence slices) within a fixed CPU/RAM budget.
  - Emit standardized telemetry events to the local agent/collector and the central eval ingestion endpoint.
  - Apply local fallback policies (e.g., disable quantized variant for failing slices) if configured.
  - Maintain a small rolling cache of probe inputs/responses (retention config; default 48 hours).

Telemetry contract (schema)

All telemetry events MUST be emitted as JSON objects matching the fields below. Event types: probe_request, probe_result, evaluator_health, fallback_action, quant_metric. Agents must attach a consistent trace_id for cross-correlation.

Telemetry table (human-readable):

| field | type | description | example | cardinality | retention |
|------|------|-------------|---------|-------------|-----------|
| event_type | string | One of probe_request/result/health/fallback/quant_metric | probe_result | low | 90d |
| timestamp_utc | string (ISO8601) | Event time in UTC | 2026-01-05T14:23:11Z | high | 90d |
| service_name | string | Redwood service identifier (e.g., text-gen-v1) | text-gen-v1 | low | 90d |
| model_variant | string | Model id + flavor (e.g., llama2-70b-q8) | llama2-70b-q8 | medium | 90d |
| slice_id | string | Canonical slice tag for the probe (see slice registry) | coherence-longcontext | medium | 180d |
| trace_id | string | Correlation id shared across events | abc123-xyz | high | 90d |
| probe_latency_ms | number | End-to-end latency for the probe | 124 | high | 90d |
| token_count | number | Token count produced | 48 | high | 90d |
| quality_score | number | Aggregated numeric quality score (0-100) | 82.4 | medium | 180d |
| fail_reasons | list[string] | Short codes for detected failures | ["hallucination_linked_entity"] | low | 180d |
| kv_cache_hit | boolean | Whether reply used KV cache | true | medium | 90d |
| quant_mode | string | "fp16" | "q8" | low | 90d |

Event semantics and retention:
- probe_request: emitted when a probe is scheduled. Minimal payload (trace_id, slice_id, model_variant, probe_prompt_hash). Retain 7d by default.
- probe_result: emitted after the probe runs. Must include quality_score, fail_reasons (if any), and token_count. Retain 180d for auditable slices.
- evaluator_health: periodic heartbeat; includes cpu_percent, mem_mb, probe_queue_length. Retain 90d.
- fallback_action: emitted when sidecar triggers a local policy (e.g., roll back to fp16). Must include justification and TTL. Retain 180d.
- quant_metric: specialized metric for quantization degradations (coherence_delta, ngram_overlap). Retain 180d.

API / SDK contract

The sidecar exposes two endpoints on localhost for the serving process to interact with:

1) POST /v1/sidecar/probe - schedule an immediate probe\Request body (JSON):
{
  "trace_id": "string",
  "slice_id": "string",
  "prompt": "string",
  "max_tokens": 256,
  "meta": {"tenant_id": "string", "request_origin": "shadow"}
}

Response: 202 Accepted (queued) or 400 with validation errors.

2) GET /v1/sidecar/probe/{trace_id} - fetch latest probe_result by trace_id\Response body (JSON):
{
  "trace_id": "string",
  "status": "completed|failed|queued",
  "quality_score": 82.4,
  "fail_reasons": ["safety_trigger_anchor"],
  "raw_response": "string",
  "meta": {"quant_mode": "q8", "kv_cache_hit": true}
}

Implementation note: the HTTP contract must be resilient to partial failures and provide idempotent probe scheduling. The SDK wrappers (py/ts) used by platform engineers should translate local fallbacks into service-level observability events.

Resource and performance budgets

- Sidecar CPU cap: default 0.25 cores per endpoint (configurable by tier).
- Memory cap: default 256MB.
- Probe time budget: 2500ms wallclock for non-blocking probes; 90% probes must complete under 2s.
- Allowed synchronous probes (blocking the main request) must be explicitly opt-in and have a 500ms budget.

Onboarding checklist (model owners)

1) Register slices: Add commonly used slices for your model to the slice registry with owners and annotation rules. (See slice-registry template link.)
2) Define quality metrics: provide at least 3 numeric metrics (coherence, safety_pass_rate, factual_precision) and thresholds for soft/alarm/fail states.
3) Provide fallback policy: default behavior on sidecar detection (no-op, fail-open, fail-closed, quant-disable).
4) Supply probe prompts: 20 canonical probes per slice and 50 synthetic edge probes for long-tail stress testing.
5) Validate resource footprint: run the sidecar profiling harness (script below) and confirm CPU/mem requirements.

Profiling CLI (example):

# Run local evaluator sidecar profile against model socket\$ ./tools/sidecar-profile.sh --endpoint localhost:8080 --samples 100 --budget-ms 2500

Quantization and KV-cache guardrails

Quantized models and KV cache interactions are frequent sources of regressions. The sidecar enforces a set of safety checks before a quantized variant is marked healthy:
- coherence_delta < 6.0 (percent point drop) over a sliding 72-hour window for core slices.
- ngram_overlap >= 0.78 against fp16 baseline for instruction-following slices.
- embedding_similarity variance < 0.03 for retrieval-augmented slices.

If checks fail, sidecar MAY emit a fallback_action to disable the quantized variant locally and mark a ticket with owner_team. Fallback actions must include: justification_code, measured_delta, recommended_action, and TTL.

Quality guardrail wiring

- Soft alarms: quality_score between warning and fail thresholds; generate eval-ticket assigned to model owner with P2 priority.
- Fail alarms: quality_score below fail threshold or safety sentinel triggered; generate immediate incident with oncall. Trigger automatic canary rollback if within a canary window.

Regression triage fast path

When a production regression is detected via sidecar telemetry, follow the fast path:
1) Acknowledge alarm and capture relevant probe_result events (trace_ids).
2) Run automated bisect: compare recent promotion artifacts (model_variant commit, quant profile, kernel version) against last known-good baseline.
3) If bisect identifies candidate cause, apply short-circuit: temporarily disable quant mode or revert to previous variant for 30 minutes.
4) Create a triage Slack thread with #eval-regressions, include diagnostics bundle (probe_results, telemetry snippets, model config diff).
5) If root cause not identified in 60 minutes, escalate to SRE/platform lead and open an incident per incident process.

Minimal diagnostic bundle (automatically assembled):
- 10 probe_result events spanning before/after regression\- model_variant manifest (commit, quant profile id)\- kernel/runtime version\- cpu/mem utilization and sidecar health events

Runbook steps (operator-friendly)

1) Identify: filter telemetry for event_type=probe_result and quality_score < fail_threshold for the affected model_variant.
2) Isolate: if kv_cache_hit correlates with failures, temporarily flush local cache and re-run probes.
3) Mitigate: if quant_metric indicates coherent degradation, trigger fallback_action to disable quant mode.
4) Restore: after fix, run 200 synthetic probes for core slices and monitor rolling quality_score for 2 hours before re-enabling quant mode.

Ownership and SLAs

- Model owner: responsible for slice definitions, probe set maintenance, and quality thresholds. SLA: respond to P1 eval incidents within 30 minutes.
- Eval platform team: owns sidecar binaries, central ingestion, and alerting pipeline. SLA: sidecar heartbeat coverage >= 99.5% across active endpoints.
- SRE: owns operational rollbacks and capacity adjustments. SLA: execute rollback within 15 minutes of approved fallback action.

Appendices

  "timestamp_utc": "2026-01-05T14:23:11Z",
  "service_name": "text-gen-v1",
  "model_variant": "llama2-70b-q8",
  "slice_id": "coherence-longcontext",
  "trace_id": "abc123-xyz",

  "token_count": 48,
  "quality_score": 72.1,

  "kv_cache_hit": false,
  "quant_mode": "q8"
}

[Privacy-Aware Evaluator Sandbox and Probe Curation Playbook]
Overview

This playbook describes the Privacy-Aware Evaluator Sandbox (PAES): a reproducible, auditable environment for running model evaluations and curating probe sets while preserving customer-sensitive signals and supporting quantization-aware workflows. The target audience is applied-ML engineers, evaluator stewards, and Platform SREs who run shadow evaluations against private or dedicated deployments.

Goals

- Enable high-fidelity evals that mimic production traffic while ensuring privacy controls (redaction, differential privacy, and telemetry bucketing).
- Make probe curation reproducible and traceable: provenance, annotator contracts, retention policy.
- Provide a standard config and gating flow for quantization-sensitive evaluations so decisions about model promotion or fallback are clearly justified.
- Ship an operational runbook for triage, rollback, and artifact retention.

Scope and non-goals

- In scope: shadow traffic sampling, probe seeding and pruning, DP-enabled metrics, quantized-replay validation, provenance metadata capture, and sandbox resource tagging.
- Out of scope: customer-facing incident communication templates (see customer-success-and-support), full production migration steps (see model-onboarding).

High-level architecture

1) Ingress: controlled shadow tap that mirrors a sampled subset of production requests into PAES.
2) Probe Fabricator: generator service (hybrid of synthetic + seeded real examples) that emits labeled probes with provenance IDs.
3) Evaluator Workers: containerized evaluation jobs that run model variants (full-precision and quantized) against probe sets.
4) Privacy Layer: redaction hooks, token-level masking, and DP aggregator for metrics.
5) Artifact Store: immutable evaluation snapshots (prompt families, model binary hashes, config yaml, telemetry digest).
6) Triage Dashboard and Alerting: SLO/quality gates integration with Redwood Console.

Ownership and contacts

- Product owner: Applied ML - Maya Thompson (author)
- Engineering lead: Connor Wu
- Privacy reviewer: Elaine González (Legal & Security liaison)
- Oncall triage: eng-sre team (pager: #sre-evals)

Probe lifecycle (detailed)

1. Seed collection
   - Source: production-sampled requests, annotated anonymized support logs, and synthetic generators.
   - Sampling policy: 1% of requests by default, stratified by tenant size and route. For high-risk routes (PII), use 0.1% and DP aggregation.

2. Curation and labeling
   - Annotator contract (must include): label schema, acceptance criteria, inter-annotator agreement threshold (Krippendorff alpha >= 0.7), retention TTL.
   - All probes get provenance_id: PAES-YYYYMMDD-<generator>-<sha1>.

3. Privacy transformation
   - Redaction rules applied in-flight using the redaction pipeline: email, ssn, credit_card, name entities. Rules maintained in: /configs/eval-redaction-registry.yaml.
   - Apply token-level bucketing before retention for analysis.

4. Probe promotion and TTL
   - Fresh probes promoted after passing annotation QA; archived after 180 days unless explicitly flagged for retention.

Quantization-aware evaluation protocol

When evaluating a quantized candidate, follow these steps exactly:

1) Baseline run (FP16 or FP32) on the same probe set to collect reference metrics.
2) Quantized run (target quant profile) with identical RNG seeds and prompt normalization.
3) Replay alignment: use the quantized-replay harness to capture token-level divergences and KV-cache behavior.

Config table (required fields for an evaluation job)

| field | description | example |
|------|-------------|--------|
| job_id | stable evaluation job id | paes-job-20260210-07 |
| model_hash | content-addressed model binary identifier | sha256:abc123... |
| quant_profile | quant strategy used | int8-llm-qs16 |
| probe_manifest | path to probe bundle in artifact store | s3://paes/artifacts/probe-manifests/20260210.json |
| dp_budget | epsilon,delta for DP aggregation | 1.0,1e-5 |
| retention_ttl_days | probe retention policy | 180 |
| owner | team or person accountable | applied-ml/maya-thompson |

(Represent the table above as plain text in Confluence)

Example job config (YAML)

```
job_id: paes-job-20260210-07
model_hash: sha256:abc123def4567890
quant_profile: int8-llm-qs16
probe_manifest: s3://paes/artifacts/probe-manifests/20260210.json
dp_budget:
  epsilon: 1.0
  delta: 1e-5
retention_ttl_days: 180
owner: applied-ml/maya-thompson
```

Privacy controls and DP guidance

- Default DP settings for public-facing routes: epsilon <= 1.0, delta <= 1e-5. For internal-only evaluations use epsilon up to 2.5 with documented approval from Privacy reviewer.
- Metrics must be aggregated using the DP aggregator library (see evaluator-sidecar contract). Raw prompts must never be stored unredacted unless approved and with HSM-backed access controls.
- Telemetry retention: scrubbed telemetry buckets kept for 365 days; full-text probes adhere to retention_ttl_days.

Acceptance criteria and quality gates

Numeric acceptance criteria for promotion to canary: all must be satisfied
- Coherence delta (quantized vs baseline) <= 1.2% on human-anchored coherence metric
- Latency P95 (quantized) <= baseline P95 * 1.35
- Safety sentinel false_positive_delta <= 0.05 absolute
- Embedding drift (cosine) <= 0.03 mean difference

If any gate fails, follow the triage playbook below.

Triage and rollback playbook (operational steps)

1. On alert: capture evaluation job_id, model_hash, quant_profile, and probe_manifest.
2. Reproduce locally with the small-probe-sample (1000 probes) using `paes-run --job <job_id> --sample 1000`.
3. If behavior is reproducible, escalate to applied-ml owner and open a regression issue with labeled artifacts.
4. If not reproducible, check telemetry: RNG seed drift, redaction differences, and hardware affinity mismatches.
5. Rollback criteria: if safety sentinel failure or coherence delta > 3x acceptance threshold, block promotion and revert any canary routing.

Operational commands and examples

- Start a sandbox evaluation (CLI):

```
paes-run --job paes-job-20260210-07 --env sandbox --trace --dp-budget 1.0
```

- Generate a probe manifest from sampled traffic:

```
paes-probe-fab --source mirror-stream --sample-rate 0.01 --out s3://paes/artifacts/probe-manifests/20260210.json
```

Monitoring and alerting

- Dashboards: PAES Quality Overview (per-model, per-quant-profile), Probe Age Distribution, DP Budget Consumption.
- Alerts: quality-gate-failure (severity P1), DP-budget-exhausted (severity P2), artifact-store-mismatch (severity P2).
- Pager assignment: first responder is the Applied ML oncall, then eng-sre after 15 minutes.

Audit and provenance

- Every evaluation produces an immutable artifact bundle: {job_id, model_hash, quant_profile, probe_manifest, dp_budget, run_metadata}. Bundles are hashed and stored in artifact-store with lifecycle policies.
- Manual review checkpoints require two approvers for restricted probes (sensitive customers) and one approver for general probes.

Onboarding checklist for a new evaluator steward

1. Read this playbook and complete privacy training.
2. Get S3 write access to paes artifact bucket (request through infra).
3. Complete hands-on run: execute a baseline run and a quantized run using the sample manifest.
4. Demonstrate ability to interpret DP-aggregated metrics and trace token divergence.
5. Request approval to run restricted-route probes if needed.

References and related docs

- evaluator-onboarding-and-certification-curriculum-2026 (applied-ml-and-evals)
- quant-impact-synthesis-for-prompt-families-2026 (applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles)
- probe-fabricator-and-annotation-charter-2026 (applied-ml-and-evals/prompt-sets-and-benchmarks)

Appendix: common failure modes and mitigations

- Mode: KV-cache divergence between FP baseline and quantized run. Mitigation: enable cache-aligned replay, capture KV-diffs, and re-run with warmed cache.
- Mode: DP budget breach during a long sweep. Mitigation: reduce sample rate, increase bucketing granularity, or request privacy escalation with approval.
- Mode: Annotator drift post-relabel. Mitigation: run adjudication, refresh inter-annotator agreement measures, and freeze slice for retraining.

Contact and escalation matrix

- Applied ML owner: Maya Thompson (maya@redwood.com)
- Privacy liaison: Elaine González (elaine@redwood.com)
- Eng SRE oncall: #sre-evals (pager duty list)

[Evaluator Backpressure and Priority Fairness Playbook]
Overview

This playbook documents the design and operational procedures for the distributed evaluator backpressure subsystem and priority-fairness scheduler used by Redwood's Eval Mesh. It targets evaluator-sidecar and orchestrator components responsible for running probes, scoring outputs, and returning telemetry while respecting product SLAs and evaluator resource constraints.

Goals
- Prevent evaluator overload during spikes in probe load or slow downstream services.
- Ensure tenant and slice priority classes receive fair shares of evaluation budget.
- Provide deterministic and observable behavior for on-call engineers.
- Make graceful degradation decisions (deferred probes, sampled execution, degraded fidelity) explicit and reversible.

Scope
- Applies to: eval-orchestrator, evaluator-sidecar, probe-priority-agent, and the probe-queue services running in the Eval Mesh.
- Not in scope: probe generation policies and annotation pipelines (handled by Probe Fabrication).

Background and Motivation
- We run heterogeneous probes (shadow traffic, synthetic seeds, long-context functioncall tests) across a fleet of evaluators. Peaks (e.g., model rollouts, heavy shadow validation) can saturate CPU/GPU and cause unexpected increases in latency and cost.
- Previous incidents (see incident-2025-eval-thundering.json) showed cascading failures when thousands of long-context probes simultaneously retried after transient KV-cache warmup failures.

Design Principles
1) Observable decisions: every backpressure action must emit an event with reasoning tags (reason, affected_slice, priority_class, resource_util).
2) Predictable fairness: priority classes map to weight buckets; allocation follows weighted fair queuing with bounded latency targets.
3) Multi-tier degradation: prefer fidelity reduction (e.g., use draft evaluator config -> sample fewer seeds) before dropping high-priority probes.
4) Recovery-first rollbacks: automated scaling/backpressure policies must be paired with an explicit rollback and a health-check gating policy.

Key Terms
- priority_class: {gold, silver, bronze, infra}.
- probe_token: logical unit charged against a probe budget.
- soft_limit: policy threshold that triggers degradation; not an immediate reject.
- hard_limit: reject threshold requiring immediate shedding.

Architecture and Components
- eval-orchestrator: central controller that assigns probes to evaluator pools and updates policies via /api/v1/policy-sync.
- evaluator-sidecar: local agent on evaluator hosts that enforces per-host queueing, backpressure decisions, and emits telemetry to eval-metrics-service.
- probe-queue: Redis-backed sharded queue used for short-lived probe bursts.
- probe-priority-agent: service that converts business priority into scheduling weights and budgets.

SLOs and Operational Thresholds
- Probe completion SLO (P95): 2.5s for short probes (<512 tokens), 95s for long probes (>=4096 tokens) in gold class for hosted evaluation.
- Queue wait soft_limit: host CPU util >= 70% or queue length > 250 -> trigger soft degradation.
- Queue wait hard_limit: host CPU util >= 92% or queue length > 1000 -> reject non-infra probes.
- Backpressure event emission: 100% of decisions must emit to eval-metrics-service with keys: decision_type, priority_class, queue_len, cpu%, mem%.

Priority Class Weights (default)
- gold: weight 8
- silver: weight 4
- bronze: weight 1
- infra: weight 12 (reserved for infra-critical probes)

Backpressure Strategy (high level)
1) Admission Control: evaluator-sidecar applies per-priority leaky-bucket admitting tokens at rate = base_rate * weight.
2) Soft Degradation: when soft_limit hit, execute in this order:
   a) Reduce sample rate by 50% for bronze/silver probes.
   b) Convert >1K-token long probes to trimmed probes (context pruning rules applied).
   c) De-prioritize functioncall-heavy probes by requeueing with lower routing priority.
3) Hard Reject: when hard_limit triggered, reject bronze probes first, then silver; gold and infra should remain unless host is dangerously saturated.
4) Circuit Breaker for downstream dependencies: if downstream scorer latency > 2x baseline for 30s, temporarily pause new probes that require that scorer and route to fallback scorer.

Detailed Procedure: Host-side Enforcement (evaluator-sidecar)
1) Monitor: collect per-host CPU%, GPU util (if present), queue_length, avg_probe_latency (sliding 1m).
2) Evaluate thresholds in order: if cpu% >= 92% OR queue_length > 1000 -> hard_limit path. Else if cpu% >= 70% OR queue_length > 250 -> soft_limit path.
3) Soft Limit Actions (atomic):
   - Emit event: POST /telemetry/backpressure with payload: {host,reason,queue_len,priority_sampled}.
   - Apply adaptive sampler: for priority_class in [bronze, silver], set sample_rate = max(0.1, current * 0.5).
   - Trim contexts: call local priming microservice to apply configured context_trim_rules (see config table).
4) Hard Limit Actions (atomic):
   - Reject policy: return HTTP 429 with X-Backpressure-Reason header.
   - Requeue infra probes to dedicated infra pool when possible.
   - Trigger autoscaler webhook: POST /ops/autoscale-requests with reason "evaluator_hard_limit".

Configuration Matrix (reference)
| config_key | default | description | recommended change for model-rollout |
|------------|---------|-------------|------------------------------------|
| host_soft_cpu_pct | 70 | host-level soft CPU threshold | +5 during slow rollout warmup |
| host_hard_cpu_pct | 92 | hard limit for host-level CPU | unchanged |
| queue_soft_len | 250 | soft queue length | lower to 200 for high-contention tenants |
| queue_hard_len | 1000 | hard queue length | unchanged |
| base_rate_per_weight | 10 probes/s | base admission rate per weight | increase in steady-state after scaling |

Examples: CLI and Policy YAML
- Query current host backpressure state
  $ rmeshctl host-status --host eval-host-12 --format json

- Example policy (eval-orchestrator/policies/prod-priority-policy.yaml)
  ---
  priority_weights:
    gold: 8
    silver: 4
    bronze: 1
    infra: 12
  host_soft_cpu_pct: 70
  host_hard_cpu_pct: 92
  queue_soft_len: 250
  queue_hard_len: 1000
  base_rate_per_weight: 10

Telemetry and Dashboards
- Metrics emitted: eval.backpressure.decisions.count, eval.backpressure.rejected.count, eval.queue.length, eval.latency.p95.short_probes, eval.priority.share.
- Alert rules (SRE):
  - P1: eval.backpressure.rejected.count > 500 in 5m -> Incident (pager)
  - P2: eval.queue.length.avg > 750 for 15m -> Slack alert (#eval-ops)
  - P3: eval.priority.share.gold < 60% for 10m when gold load > 1000 -> Ops review.

Runbook: On-call Steps for P1
1) Acknowledge pager and open incident channel.
2) Query eval-orchestrator /api/v1/pools to identify affected pools.
3) Run: rmeshctl drain-pool --pool-id <pool> --grace 120s to stop new probes to pool.
4) If root cause is autoscaler lag, trigger manual scaling: POST /ops/autoscale-requests with scale_delta +2 nodes.
5) If immediate relief required, flip policy to emergency-priority-policy (feature flag) which: reduces bronze sample to 5% and routes gold to dedicated pool.
6) Record decision in incident timeline and emit retrospective tags for regression triage.

Operational Play Scenarios
- Gradual Model Rollout: pre-warm evaluators for 10m, then ramp probes at 10% per minute while observability confirms p95 latency < SLO. If soft_limit hits, pause ramp and investigate probe-type mix.
- Sudden Spike (Third-party scorer outage): circuit-break scorer calls; route light-weight scoring fallback; mark affected probes with tag scorer_fallback=true for later replay.

Testing and Validation
- Unit tests for admission controller deterministic behavior across weight combinations.
- Chaos tests: inject evaluator-sidecar CPU pressure and verify soft->hard transitions are logged and observable.
- Shadow rollouts: deploy new backpressure policy to 10% of evaluators for 48h before full rollout.

Rollout Checklist
1) Create policy PR in eval-orchestrator (include traffic simulation results).
2) LGTMs from reviewers (Evan Morris, Lina Fernández).
3) Canary deploy to canary-pool (10% fleet) and monitor priority_share, rejected.count, p95 latency for 48h.
4) Gradual ramp (25% -> 50% -> 100%) with 12h observation windows.
5) Post-rollout audit and update playbook with lessons learned.

Ownership and Contacts
- Policy owners: Priya Khandelwal (applied-ml), Marcus Li (infra).
- On-call rotation: eval-oncall (see roster).
- Escalation: if autoscaler fails to add capacity within 15m, escalate to infra-sre lead (pager).

Appendices
A. Context trimming rules (example)
- remove backreference sentences beyond 1024 tokens unless anchor markers exist.
- collapse multi-turn persona prompts to last 2 turns for trimmed probes.

B. Event schema (telemetry/backpressure)
- decision_type: soft_degrade | hard_reject | sampler_adjust | route_shift
- reason: cpu | queue_len | downstream_latency
- priority_class: gold | silver | bronze | infra
- host: hostname
- queue_len: integer
- cpu_pct: float

C. FAQ
Q: How do we treat long-context (>16k) probes during soft-limit?
A: Prefer trimming with context_trim_rules and, if trimming insufficient, sample at 10% and enqueue for background replay once load decreases.

Document History
- 2026-01-12: Created by Priya Khandelwal.
- 2026-02-20: Added runbook steps and CLI examples after triage of incident-2026-eval-spike.

[Release pipeline failing: GPG verification errors after team signing-key rotation blocking runners]
description:
Issue summary:
Since the org signing key (team-release@gpg) rotation on 2026-03-09, the nightly release pipeline run by self-hosted release-runners is failing during artifact verification. The GPG step reports 'BAD_SIGNATURE' on multiple signed artifacts and aborts the pipeline, blocking all release promotion jobs that require signed artifacts.

Impact:
- All release promotion pipelines from the staging branch are failing in prod-us-east.
- No releases can be created or promoted; estimated user-facing impact: none immediate, but blocker for planned hotfix release.
- A subset of release-runners (hosts tagged release-runner-prod-*) are the first to hit the failures.

Environment:
- CI: GitLab self-hosted (runner group: release-runners-prod)
- Artifact registry: internal OCI registry + GPG-signed tarballs in S3 (us-east)
- Key management: internal key-rotation process (ops-runbook), public key published to internal keyserver at keys.redwood.internal

Steps to reproduce:
1) Trigger release pipeline for release-candidate commit SHA XYZ.
2) Pipeline downloads signed tarball from S3.
3) run `gpg --verify artefact.tar.gz.sig artefact.tar.gz` inside runner container.
4) gpg exits with status 2 and prints 'BAD_SIGNATURE' and 'no valid openpgp data found'.

Observed logs/snippets:
- Runner logs (release-runner-prod-07): "gpg: Signature made ... gpg: BAD_SIGNATURE gpg: invalid packet (ctb=0x0)"
- Pipeline job trace shows immediate failure at 'verify-signature' step.

Hypothesis / initial findings:
- The rotated GPG key was pushed to the internal keyserver with a new key ID and fingerprint. Some runners have an outdated keyring cached and still trust the old key fingerprint, while the artifacts are signed by the new key.
- Some signing tooling may have re-encoded signatures with a different packet format (we saw 'invalid packet' in gpg output) — possible gpg version mismatch between signing host and runner containers.
- The keyserver index propagation may be delayed; runners that used a cached lookup received a malformed response.

Immediate mitigation attempted:
- Ops pulled the previous GPG public key from backup and added it to a temporary allowlist on three runners (release-runner-prod-03/04/07) — pipelines for those runners succeeded for a single build (hotfix candidate).
- Bumped the runner container gpg package from 2.2.20 -> 2.3.8 on a canary runner; that canary now fails with 'invalid packet' while older gpg accepted signature, suggesting a compatibility issue.

Next steps planned / asked from infra team:
- Confirm the exact key fingerprint used by the signing process (artifact-signer job) and compare with keys published to keys.redwood.internal. (Assigned to Release Engineering)
- Force-refresh keyring on all release runners via staged job that pulls explicit public key file from S3 and imports to gpg keyring. (Assigned to CI infra)
- Validate gpg binary versions across signing host and runners; if mismatch, plan either to downgrade signing host gpg or upgrade runner containers. (Assigned to Security/Infra)
- Temporarily allow fallback verification to previous key for releases created in the next 24 hours while we fully roll the new key. (Requires Risk approval).

Cross-references:
- Slack: #release-engineering thread: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C02RELEASES/p1640
- Runbook: Confluence GPG Key Rotation Runbook (link above)
- Related incidents: INT-23011 (previous key rotation fail), INT-23350 (runner keyring drift)


investigation_notes:
- Pulled signing host logs: artifact-signer@build-01 shows sign command using gpg 2.2.20 and key-id ABCD1234.
- Verified public key published at keys.redwood.internal shows fingerprint that does not match ABCD1234; shows new key EFGH5678.
- Compared signature packets with pktdump: some signatures created by gpg 2.3.x include new signature subpacket format that gpg 2.2.20 accepts but older container images have varying behavior.
- Keyserver response on 2026-03-09 03:12 UTC returned a header 'Transfer-Encoding: chunked' causing our naive keysync microservice to truncate key exports; this produced a malformed pubkey blob on some runners.
- Reproduced locally by fetching key export via existing keysync service: got truncated payload resulting in 'invalid packet' on import.

2026-03-10 09:18 - Emily Chen: Filing ticket after reproducing failures on release-runner-prod-07. Blocking hotfix. Attaching pipeline traces in linked PR.
2026-03-10 10:02 - Ravi Patel: Spun up canary runner and validated gpg version mismatch. Suspect key export truncation during rotation. Will attempt force-refresh on 2 runners.

2026-03-11 03:10 - Sinead O'Neill (Release Eng): Confirmed signer host used ABCD1234 historically; our new rotation job pushed EFGH5678. We're rolling back signer to previous key for next 6 hours to allow patching.

root_cause:
Partial: key rotation publishing pipeline returned truncated key blobs due to improper handling of chunked transfer from internal keyserver, combined with gpg version mismatches across runner images leading to inconsistent import/verification results.

resolution:
Partial mitigation applied: temporary rollback of signing host to previous key for immediate hotfix, and targeted keyring refresh jobs run on three canary runners. Next steps: patch keysync service to handle chunked transfer correctly, schedule controlled rollout of new public key to all runners with checksum verification, and standardize gpg version in runner images. Will update once full rollout complete.

Patch keysync service to validate Content-Length/Checksums on key export (owner: infra)
Add key fingerprint validation step to CI key import job (owner: release-eng)
Upgrade runner base image gpg to 2.3.x in next CI image release (owner: ci-team)
Publish rollback decision and timeline in Confluence (owner: security)

[Runner SSH known_hosts cache causing intermittent git fetch failures after bastion host key rotation]
description:
Issue summary: After the scheduled bastion host SSH key rotation on 2026-03-09, a subset of CI runners began failing git fetch/clone operations with host key mismatch errors. Impact: ~12% of builds that need to access private repos via the bastion experienced checkout failures, causing release and nightly pipelines to flake. This appears limited to ephemeral runners that had previously cached known_hosts entries, and the failures started immediately after rotation.

Observed error sample: 'WARNING: REMOTE HOST IDENTIFICATION HAS CHANGED!
IT IS POSSIBLE THAT SOMEONE IS DOING SOMETHING NASTY!' followed by 'Host key verification failed.'

Business impact: Delays to canary release jobs and CI congestion as retries accumulate. No customer-facing outages, but blocking release cadence for two engineering teams.

steps_to_reproduce:
1) Provision ephemeral runner that will route git traffic through bastion egress proxy.
2) Ensure known_hosts for bastion present in runner image (from prior successful checkouts).
3) Rotate bastion host SSH key (performed by infra schedule on 2026-03-09).
4) Trigger pipeline that performs 'git clone' of internal repo. Observe host key mismatch and checkout failure.

logs:
run-2026-03-10-12:14:23 - git@bastion.internal: Permission denied (publickey). Host key verification failed.
runner-ephemeral-xy12 - ssh: handshake failed: host key mismatch: got 'ecdsa-sha2-nistp256' expected 'rsa-sha2-512'
proxy-audit - 2026-03-09T03:02:15Z - bastion-key-rotate: new-key-published, old-key-removed

investigation_notes:
03/10 09:00 - Triage: Correlation between bastion key rotation window and spike in runner checkout failures. Not all runners affected; pattern tied to runners that retain known_hosts across warm pool cycles.
03/10 10:22 - Hypothesis: Ephemeral runners reuse filesystem layers or cached /home/runner/.ssh/known_hosts entry created before rotation; SSH client refuses new key causing immediate failure instead of interactive fingerprint acceptance.
03/10 11:05 - Verified: New long-lived dedicated runners (fresh instances) do not fail; ephemeral warm pool runners with preserved workspace show failures.
03/11 14:30 - Found CI image build step that pre-populates known_hosts using 'ssh-keyscan' at image bake time. Image bake predates rotation and therefore contains stale key for affected runners.
03/11 16:00 - Cross-reference: linked infra runbook for bastion rotation (CON-BASTION-ROTATE) lacks a step to invalidate runner caches or trigger pool recycle. Added as follow-up.

mitigation:
Short-term: Add a pre-check job to affected pipelines to run 'ssh-keyscan -H bastion.internal >> ~/.ssh/known_hosts' before git operations; rolling patch applied to two failing repos as a stopgap. Medium-term: Update runner warm-pool lifecycle to clear ~/.ssh/known_hosts on start and ensure image bake process does not bake static bastion keys.

resolution:
Work in progress. Emergency mitigation (pre-check ssh-keyscan) deployed to release pipelines on 2026-03-11 which reduced failure rate to <1%. Follow-up tasks created to bake image fix and to update bastion rotation runbook. Will close ticket once warm-pool fix is deployed and monitored for 48h without regression.

Diego Ramos (03/10): Investigating; suspect known_hosts cache. Requested list of runner IDs and image bake timestamps.
SRE - Priya Shah (03/11): Confirmed bastion rotation executed 2026-03-09 03:02 UTC. No other network changes. Suggest running 'ssh-keyscan' as temporary workaround.
BuildME - Jordan Lee (03/11): Applied ssh-keyscan pre-step in repo 'infra/deploy-svc' and observed successful run after one retry. Recommending org-wide mitigation rollout.
Diego Ramos (03/12): Created PR to runner-AMI pipeline to remove baked known_hosts and added init script to prune ~/.ssh/known_hosts at startup. PR: github.com/redwood/runner-images/pull/1743

1) Merge runner-images PR to remove baked known_hosts and push new AMI (owner: Diego Ramos).
2) Update bastion rotation runbook to include a runner warm-pool recycle step (owner: Priya Shah).
3) Add automated CI smoke test that runs ssh-keyscan against bastion in prelude for pipelines that use bastion egress (owner: Jordan Lee).
4) Monitor failure rate for 48 hours post-deploy and close ticket if stable (owner: Support Team).

[Cosign HSM epoch skew causes signature validation to fail, blocking container promotion]
summary_extended:
During a scheduled PKCS#11 HSM key rotation the cosign signer on CI produced valid signatures but subsequent verification by the promotion job failed with epoch/time-window errors, preventing any container images from being promoted to the release registry.

description:
Issue summary:
- What happened: Automated container promotion jobs started failing verification immediately after the HSM key rollover window. The cosign signing step reports success, push to registry succeeds, but the promotion verification step (post-push policy) rejects the image.
- Impact: Blocked promotion pipeline for all releases targeting the us-east release cohort. Approximately 12 release candidates queued; customers on internal canary cannot be promoted. No pod rollouts happened.
- First observed: 2026-03-13 02:17 UTC when nightly canary promotion aborted.
- Temporary scope: prod us-east artifact-registry and the cosign signer instances used by CI runners.


steps_to_reproduce:
1) Trigger standard build pipeline that signs with cosign (PKCS#11-backed key).
2) After HSM rotation window, run the promotion job that invokes 'cosign verify' against the registry entry.
3) Observe verification failure with epoch/skew related message.

Observed error: 'cosign: signature verification failed: verification time 1678793820 not within validity window [1678797600, 1678801200]' (timestamps are examples).

logs:
ci-runner-42 cosign: signing completed (signature stored in registry).
promotion-job-17 verify: ERROR cosign: signature validation failed: verification time 170 - outside allowed window
hsm-proxy: PKCS11: login successful, keyslot 2 pulled, keyid=ae3f2b..
registry-policy: reject image sha256:... - signature epoch mismatch
(see attached truncated logs in S3 bucket: s3://redwood-internal/incident/INT-981345/logs.tar.gz)

investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: HSM returned signatures with a future 'notBefore'/epoch due to clock skew or a transient signing policy during the rotation.
- Checked HSM NTP sync across HSM cluster nodes via runbook; one partition showed drift of ~4 minutes during the window.
- PKCS#11 driver reported successful rotation and new key label 'cosign-2026-03-13'.
- Cosign signer config uses server-local time for validity checks when generating 'signedTime' metadata; the promotion job uses verifier time derived from registry verification service (which is strictly NTP-synced).
- Reproduced locally by forcing signer time ahead by 5 minutes; verifier rejects.
Links: Slack thread #release-ops: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/release-ops/p1234567890
Runbook ref: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/ENG/Cosign+HSM+rotation+runbook

comments:
Asha Patel (reporter) 2026-03-13: Opened after nightlies failed. Initial triage points to HSM rotation window coincident with signing. Pls escalate to crypto and infra.
Liam O'Connor (assignee) 2026-03-13: I will take this. Spun up a temporary cosign signer using software key to verify promotion path works end-to-end. Verified that software-signed images verify fine — indicates signing metadata from HSM differs from expected time window.
Crypto Team (comment) 2026-03-13: HSM cluster completed rewrap and key push at 02:12 UTC. We saw a short NTP hiccup on node hsm-03. Investigating firmware logs for 'sign time' stamping behavior.
SRE (comment) 2026-03-13: NTP on hsm-03 drifted ~240s starting 02:10 UTC during maintenance. We've re-synced and restarted ntpd. Monitoring.
Liam O'Connor 2026-03-14: Temporary mitigation: pinned CI cosign signer to software key for releases until HSM firmware patch applied. Created PR to add 5m tolerance to internal policy verifier as short-term workaround (see PR).

resolution:
Workaround applied 2026-03-14: CI promotion pipelines switched to software-backed cosign signer for critical releases; promotion resumed for queued images.
Permanent fix: Crypto/SRE to apply HSM firmware patch and enforce tighter NTP monitoring with alerting. Also created a change to the promotion verifier to allow configurable verification_time_tolerance (default 0s) for an emergency-release window; PR merged with a 5m emergency tolerance and requires a follow-up rollback after HSM patch.
Post-actions: schedule postmortem with crypto and release-eng within 72h, update cosign HSM rotation runbook to include pre-rotation NTP sanity check step.

next_steps:
1) Crypto to apply HSM firmware patch and confirm NTP stability on all partitions.
2) SRE to add an alert for clock drift >30s on HSM fleet.
3) Release eng to coordinate rollback of verifier tolerance after patch.
4) Postmortem scheduled and runbook updated.

customer_impact_note:
Internal canary/promote only — no external customer invoices or billing impacts. Some teams waiting on promotions for staging-to-prod release gating.

[Ephemeral runner OIDC provider thumbprint rotation prevents role assumption, artifacts upload failing]
description:
Issue summary:
During scheduled AWS OIDC provider maintenance, the provider thumbprint was rotated in the account used by ephemeral GitHub Actions runners. After the rotation, ephemeral runners in prod could no longer exchange OIDC assertions to assume the intended IAM role. The immediate downstream effect was that in-flight release and nightly CI jobs started failing during the artifact upload step (S3 PutObject 403).

Impact:
- ~380 jobs failed in the past 3 hours across multiple release pipelines (canary + nightly).
- Releases blocked: two canary promotions failed to complete due to missing artifacts.
- Most affected: ephemeral runners that had not already refreshed tokens before the provider change.

Environment:
- Prod (us-west-2) ephemeral GitHub Actions runners managed by internal runner-controller service.
- AWS account: infra-artifacts-prod.
- Artifact storage: s3://redwood-release-artifacts-prod (s3 kms-encrypted).

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Trigger a workflow that uses ephemeral runner with OIDC role-arn sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity.
2) Runner calls AWS STS with token from GitHub Actions OIDC and thumbprint check against AWS OIDC provider.
3) STS returns 403 / "Invalid identity token" and runner process aborts before S3 PutObject.

Observed behavior:
- Runner logs show: "AWS STS denied AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity: The web identity token is invalid."
- s3 upload attempts show 403 Forbidden with x-amz-error-code=AccessDenied.
- Vault/Secrets not implicated; secrets used to sign upload (short-lived credentials) were not issued because AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity failed.

Expected behavior:
- Runner should assume role via OIDC and receive temporary credentials to upload artifacts.

Logs / artifacts attached:
- Aggregated runner daemon logs: /var/log/runner-daemon/ephemeral-2026-03-10-*.log (uploaded to internal-support bucket).
- CloudTrail trace for sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity showing error code: "InvalidIdentityToken" (link in investigation notes).
- Sample failed job id: release/canary-4821 (job run 2026-03-10T15:42:11Z).

Investigation notes:
- Verified AWS team rotated the OIDC provider thumbprint for infra-artifacts-prod earlier this morning as part of root CA rotation. Thumbprint value changed and our runner-controller images still validate the old thumbprint embedded in runner bootstrap config.
- Confirmed that long-lived controller pods (older images) cached the provider thumbprint at startup; newly deployed controller with updated config functions correctly.
- Runners that were mid-flight at the time of rotation retained the old thumbprint and failed token validation until restarted.
- Cross-checked with CloudTrail and GitHub Actions logs; the error surfaces only at the AWS STS AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity step.

Temporary mitigations applied:
- Manually restarted runner-controller pods in us-west-2 to pick up updated thumbprint config for all new ephemeral runners. This reduced the failure rate for newly spawned runners.
- For blocked release jobs, support reran the workflows on dedicated runners (non-ephemeral) which use a different IAM path and were unaffected.

Root cause hypothesis:
- The automation that rotates the OIDC thumbprint updates AWS OIDC provider but does not simultaneously invalidate cached thumbprint values in running runner-controller pods. The bootstrap path embeds a static thumbprint at image build time for extra safety, which made older images fail after provider change.

Proposed long-term fix:
1) Remove embedded static thumbprint from images and make runner bootstrap query the OIDC provider certificate chain dynamically at start, with a short cache TTL and a health-check to detect mismatch.
2) Extend the rotation playbook to include a forced rolling restart of runner-controller DaemonSets / Deployments in all regions immediately after thumbprint change.
3) Add a Canary test in infra CI that rotates a mocked thumbprint in staging and verifies runners re-auth.
4) Add a post-rotation runbook step to surface expected errors and Slack alert to #infra-ops with specific remediation commands.

Next steps / Action items:
- Diego to coordinate forced rolling restart for us-west-2 controllers (in progress).
- Diego to open infra PR to remove static thumbprint from base image (linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runner-images/pull/219).
- Priya to notify release managers and retry blocked canary jobs on dedicated runners while fix deploys.
- SRE to add CloudWatch metric alert for sudden spike in sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity InvalidIdentityToken errors.

SLA / Customer impact: Internal release pipelines only; no external customer-facing API degradation. Still P1 because it blocks releases and nightly promotion automation.

[GitHub webhook secret rotation caused webhook-proxy signature failures and queued builds]
description:
Issue summary: During a scheduled GitHub App webhook secret rotation, the webhook-proxy started rejecting inbound webhook deliveries due to HMAC signature mismatch. Impact: ~120 release and CI jobs queued in the proxy and did not reach runner-controller for approximately 6 minutes, delaying two rolling releases. No token/credential material was exposed.

Timeline: 
- 2026-03-13T09:17:00Z: Secrets rotation job kicked off in secrets-manager (scheduled rewrap of GH webhook signing key).
- 2026-03-13T09:18:40Z: First 5xx responses observed in webhook-proxy logs for /payload endpoints.
- 2026-03-13T09:20:15Z: Alerts fired: high webhook failure rate and runner-controller backlog.
- 2026-03-13T09:23:00Z: On-call rollback (revert to previous signing secret) completed; traffic resumed.

Observed behavior: Webhooks from GitHub delivered successfully to the load balancer but the webhook-proxy returned 400/401 signature verification errors. The proxy enqueued payloads internally and retried. The runner-controller, which depends on successful webhook POST handling, did not create matching Job objects until proxy recovered, causing a backlog of scheduled builds and two failed canary promotions.

Impact: Release delays for two microservices (payments and recommendation) for ~6 minutes; no customer-facing errors beyond deployment lag.

Notes: This is an internal incident affecting our release pipeline; security posture unaffected beyond the normal rotation process.

investigation_notes:
Hypothesis: The rotation procedure updates the secrets-store first, then triggers a separate config push to webhook-proxy. There is a brief window where the proxy reads the new secret but the GitHub App still signs requests with the old key (or vice-versa) if GitHub's webhook config is not updated atomically. Findings: 
- Secret rotation runbook performed two steps: rewrap -> patch proxy config. The patch job failed transiently for 55s due to a k8s API throttling spike (rate-limited by controller-manager), causing the window.
- Proxy has retry/backoff that enqueues deliveries for up to 5 minutes before handing back 5xx to GitHub; during that time runner-controller's event consumer waits for ACKs.
- No evidence of credential leakage; audit logs show rotation performed by automation account svc-secrets-rotator.

Next steps proposed: make rotation atomic or introduce a staged validation where proxy accepts both old and new signing keys for a short overlap window. Also add preflight patch validation to ensure config push succeeded before finalizing rotation.

resolution:
Partial mitigation applied: rollback of the signing secret to previous version restored normal processing. Short-term fix: add 90s acceptance window in webhook-proxy to validate payloads against both previous and current signing keys. Long-term fix: update rotation runbook to perform atomic config patch or a two-phase commit: (1) deploy proxy in accept-old-and-new mode, (2) rotate secret, (3) remove old key after grace period. Post-incident: create a cron alert for API server 429 spikes during rotation windows and run simulated rotations in staging.
